### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:16:1)


**ויגבה.** אז תראה גבהות השם בעבור המשפט שיעשה בישראל, ותגלה קדושתו בעבור הצדק שיעשה:


*But the Lord of hosts,* etc. Then the excellence of the Lord will be known by the judgment (משפט) which He will have executed on Israel, and His holiness will be revealed by the kindness (צדקה) shown to them.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:1)


**ורעו וגו'.** אז תהיה ארץ יהודה שממה, וירעו בה הכבשים כאילו נהוגים היו להיות שם:


*Then shall the lambs feed,* etc. Judah will then be desolate, and lambs will feed therein, as if they were driven to be there.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:2)


**[כדברם].** מגזרת ארמית וכמוהו דוברו' בים (מלכים א' ה' כ"ג):


כדברם *As if they were driven*.²⁷ Comp. the Chaldee דבר to lead, to drive; and דברת floats (1 Kings 5:25).

footnotes:
²⁷ A. V., After their manner.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:17:3)


**מחים.** הם הכבשים השמנים שיש בהם מוח וכמוהו ממוחים (ישעיהו כ"ה ו'), וחרבות מגזרת חרבן, והנה הוא סמוך ותחסר מלת הארץ, כמו ושכור' (ישעיהו נ"א כ"א) יגון ולא מיין משא חמור להם (שמות א' י"ו כ'), וטעם גרי' יאכלו אנשים נכרים שידורו שם, והנה מחים תאר השם, והם פעולים והגרים פועלים:


מחים *Strong lambs*,²⁸ that have marrow (מוח) in their bones; comp. ממוחים things full of marrow (25:6). וחרבות *And the waste places of;* comp. חרבן destruction. It is the construct state; supply הארץ the land; comp. ושכורת And drunken of SORROW. (51:21). משא ח׳ ל׳ ═ חמר לחם An ass’s LOAD of bread (1 Sam. 16:20). גרים *Strangers,* that will then dwell there. מחים (Adjective,¹ strong lambs) is the objective case; גרים strangers, the subject.²⁹

footnotes:
²⁸ A.V., The fat ones.
¹ Comp. c. iii. note 5.
²⁹ The translation of the passage according to this explanation would be, And in the waste places of the land will strangers eat the fat lambs. This is against the accents which join מחים rather with חרבות than with יאכלו.

**הוי מושכי העון.** הטעם שיחזקו העון:


מושכי העון That fasten iniquity.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:18:2)


**וכעבות העגלה חטאה**, הם מושכים חטאה, והוא שם כמו חטאת, כמו נושא עון ופשע וחטאה (שמות ל"ד ז'), כי גם יהיה תאר השם:


וכעבות העגלח חטאה supply הם משכים And draw sin as if it were with a cart rope. המאה is here a noun; it is the same as חטאת sin (comp. Exod. 34:7); it can also be an adjective, signifying a woman that committeth many sins.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:19:1)


**האומרים וגו'.** יתכן היות ימהר פועל יוצא כמו מהרו את המן (אסתר ה' ה'), ויתכן להיות יחישה לבדו יוצא, ובאו שניהם עתידים בלא דבק, וכמוהו אל תרבו תדברו (שמות א' ב' ג'), והטעם מי יתן ותבואנה אלה העתידו' ונראה אם הם אמת:


ימהר Either transitive, let him bring hastily; comp. מהרו (Esth. 5:5), fetch hastily; or intransitive, let him make speed; and only יחישה transitive, let him accelerate. As to two verbs in the future following each other without conjunction, comp. אל תרבו תדברו Talk no more (1 Sam. 2:3).—Let these prophecies be fulfilled, that we may see whether they are true.

### Verse 27

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:27:1)

ינום *He will slumber*; נום signifies a sleep of a less profound kind than ישן. He will not slumber, much less will he sleep.

### Verse 28

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:28:1)


**אשר.** כצר, כמו חרבות צורים (יהושע ה' ג'), כי משקלי השמות משתנים:


כצר *Like flint*; comp. צורים flint³⁹ (Jos. 5:3); the form of the noun varies.⁴⁰

footnotes:
³⁹ A. V., Sharp.
⁴⁰ From the same root two nouns can be constructed of different forms, but having the same meaning, like צר and צור flint; there is, according to I. E., no standard for the inflexion of the noun as there is for the verb : all verbs are conjugated after פעל.

וגלגליו The wheels of his chariots; they⁴¹ are known. סופה ═ כסופה כמוץ. As the chaff of the storm.⁴² They will come as quickly as the chaff driven by the storm.

footnotes:
⁴¹ It is not clear whether the wheels or the chariots are to be understood; in the first case this remark is quite superfluous; in the second it is perhaps to explain the omission of of his chariots as easily supplied by the reader.

**שאגה. וינהום.** מלה זרה בעבור שאות הגרון ירחב, ויבוא העתיד על משקל יפעל, שהיה עי"ן הפועל אחד מהגרון, רק אם היה לו לומר כן לא יתכן להיותו כלל על משקל יפעול:


וינהום *And he shall roar*. Irregular form; because regularly the guttural letter widens the vowel, and causes the form of the future to be like ⁴³,יִפְעַל the second radical of the verb פעל being a guttural; in the conjugation tables, however, no notice is taken of this property, else we should not have in the paradigm the standard form of the future ויפליט

⁴³ Instead of יִפְעוֹל. See Zahoth, on the Kal.

יִפְצוֹל *And he lets escape*.⁴⁴ He lets escape the prey, as I think, in order to see whether there is any one to deliver it.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:30:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:1)


**וינהום עליו.** על ישראל:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:30:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:2)


**כנהמת ים.** כי אז יחשך אור העולם וכתוב חשכת מים (תהלים י"ח י"ב):


*Like the roaring of the sea,* etc.; *behold darkness*. For the light shall then be withheld from the earth. Comp. darkness of water⁴⁵ (Ps. 18:12).

footnotes:
⁴⁵ When great storms stir up the sea, clouds usually cover the sky and conceal the heavenly luminaries. The figure of the roaring of the sea is therefore followed by that of darkness.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:30:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:3)


וטעם **ונבט לארץ** כי בארץ יהיו ולא בים, ויבוא החשך דרך משל על מצוקות הלב, יש אומרים כי ונבט מבנין נפעל והקרוב אלי שהוא מבנין הכבד הדגוש, והוא שב אל ישראל כאשר אמרתי במלת עליו:


*And if he look unto the land,* etc. For they⁴⁶ will be on the land, not on the sea. *And behold darkness*. Darkness is here a figure for the distress of the heart. ונבט According to some it is Niphal, And it is looked; but I think it is Piel, And he looks, and its subject is Israel, the same to whom reference is made in the word עליו, as I have already stated.

footnotes:
⁴⁶ They, the hostile armies, whose attack is compared to the roaring of the sea, will be on the land—that is to say, will reach the inhabitants of the land, the Israelites—and cause them harm and distress; they will not be like the roaring of the sea, for that does not hurt the people on land.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 5:30:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/5:30:4)


**צר ואור.** יש אומרים השמש והירח ואחרים אמרו הירח והשמש, כי הירח צר כנגד השמש, ור' אדוניה אומר שיחסר אות ה"א כאילו אמר צהר, כי אותיות יה"וא פעם הם יתרים גם ימצאו חסרים, והנה טעה כי ה"א איננה מאותיות המשך ולא יעלם [צ"ל תעלם] רק באחרונה שהיא תמורת אל"ף במבטא, והנכון בעיני להיות כמשמעו להיות צר כמו צר ומצוק מצאוני (תהלים קי"ט קמ"ג), או יהיה תואר השם, והטעם כי תחשך ארץ ישראל מפאת הצר, גם מפאת האור שיחשך בעת הריסותיה כי יעלה איך וכסה אור השמש:


צר ואור According to some, Sun and moon; according to others, Moon and sun, because the moon is small (צַר) if compared with the sun; R. Adonim thinks that ה is omitted, צהר═צר light; for the letters א ה ו י are sometimes present in a word when they are superfluous, and at others omitted where they properly form part of the root; but he is mistaken, because ה does not belong to the vowel letters, and cannot be dropped except at the end of a word, where it replaces א. I take צר literally; it has here the same meaning as in Ps. 119:143, namely, distress, or—being an adjective—distressed. Palestine will be darkened by distress as well as by the sun, which will cast a gloom over her at the time of her destruction; for a mist will rise and hide the sun.

**בעריפיה.** כמו יערף מזבחתם (הושע י' ב') וקרוב מגזרת וערפתו (שמות י"ג י"ג):

## Chapter 6


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:1)


**בשנת מות.** הקדמונים אמרו שמלת מות צרע', כי בעת שנכנס אל ההיכל להקטיר היה הרעש, גם הוא נכון, ויתכן להיות כמשמעו, כי בשנה שהתנבא מת עזיהו, ואין טענה בימי עזיהו (ישעיהו א' א'), אחר שהיה חדשים, וזאת היא תחלת נבואת ישעיהו:


*In the year that King Uzziah died*. Our sages said that died is here used for became a leper;¹ and Talmud Babli Nedarim, 64: There are four persons who, though living, may be counted as dead: the poor, the blind, the leper, the childless. for when Uzziah entered the temple to offer the incense,² the earthquake³ took place. This may be true; but מות can also be taken literally; in that case the death of Uzziah must be placed in the same year in which Isaiah became prophet; no objection can be raised from In the days⁴ of Uzziah (1:1), since even months might have passed between Isaiah’s initiation as prophet and the death of Uzziah. This chapter contains the first prophecy of Isaiah.

footnotes:
¹ Comp. Rashi, ad locum,
² On that occasion, Uzziah was struck with leprosy (2 Kgs. 15:5, and 2 Chr. 26:20, 2 Chr. 26:21).
³ At which, as some believe, Isaiah hinted by the words, And the posts of the door moved. See Rashi on ver. 4. The earthquake, which took place during the reign of King Uzziah, is mentioned Amos 1:1, and Zac. 14:5. Compare also Seder Olam, Amos prophesied before, Isaiah during the earthquake.
⁴ In the days (1:1) appears to mean in the midst of the reign of, since ימים sometimes signifies years. Ibn Ezra anticipates this objection and refutes it by referring to the literal meaning of ימים days, which may of course be applied to a part of a year. Thus the words in the days of Uzziah admit the supposition, that Isaiah commenced his prophetical career in the last year of the reign of Uzziah.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:1:2)


**רם ונשא.** תאר הכסא לא כאשר אמרו רבים, והטעם שהוא למעלה מהחיות כאשר אפרש בספר יחזקאל:


*High and lifted up*. Attributes to throne (כסא), not, as many thought, to the Lord. The throne⁵. עולם העליון the highest world, described as spiritual, indivisible, and unchangeable; *b*. עולם התיכון the middle world, or היכל the divine temple, described as being of a mixed nature, containing bodiless forms, and also bodies, but of a pure and unchangeable substance; *c*. עולם השפלות the lowest world, the earth and the fulness thereof, consisting of bodies of all description. The forms and bodies of the middle world are contained in ten spheres : sun, moon, and five planets in seven spheres, the large body of stars in the eighth, the Zodiac in the ninth, the tenth is the throne.—The angels inhabit the middle world. See I. E. on Ps. 8:4, and on Dan. 10:21. is above the Hajoth⁶ as I shall explain on Ezekiel.⁷

footnotes:
⁵ The throne כסא הכבוד is, according to I. E., the sphere or force (גלגל) that encompasses and moves all the remaining spheres. The whole Universe is divided into three parts; a
⁶ חיות lit. living beings, signify a certain class of angels, frequently mentioned by Ezekiel (1:5, 13, etc.).
⁷ The commentary of Ibn Ezra on Ezekiel, promised by underlinehim/underline repeatedly, is not known.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:3:3)


קדוש תאר השם והקדושה בעצם ולא תשתנה כנגד המקומות, והשם הראה לו זאת הנבואה בעבור שיתקדש מטומאת השפה, כי השם קדוש וכן משרתיו ושלוחיו:


*Holy*. An adjective. Holiness is an essential attribute of the Lord; it is therefore the same in every place. God showed Isaiah this vision, that he might purify himself from the uncleanness of the lips; for the Lord is holy, and so also should be His servants and messengers.

אף על פי שהוא קדוש קדוש כבודו מלא הארץ שהיא למטה, והמפרש מלא כל הארץ הדרים בה כמו (תהלים כ"ד א') ליי' הארץ ומלואה, לא אמר כלום, והעד וימלא כבוד יי' את כל הארץ:


*The whole earth*, etc. Although He is holy above, still His glory filleth the earth below. He who explains מלא כל הארץ that which filleth the whole earth, that is, its inhabitants, and compares it with וּמְלאׇׁהּ and the fulness thereof (Ps. 24), is mistaken.⁹ Comp. ה׳ את כל הארץ וימלא כבוד And the whole earth will be full of the glory of the Lord. (Num. 14:21)

footnotes:
⁹ Ibn Ezra does not show why this explanation is wrong; nor does he give any opinion of his own as to what form מְלאׁ is; the quotation, Num. 14:21, only shows that a phrase like the glory of the Lord filleth the whole earth, is correct; but he fails to prove the identity of this quotation with הארץ כבודו מלא כל. In his commentary on Num. 22:18, however, he explains בֵּיתוֹ מָלֵא כסף ═ מְלאׁ ביתו כסף and quotes מלא כל הארץ as a parallel.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:5:1

**ואומר. נדמיתי.** נכרתי מהיותי עם חברת הקדושים, כמו ודמיתי אמך (הושע ד' ה'), ויש אומרים מלשון דמי (תהלים ס"ב ו'), גם הוא נכון:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:2)


טעם**איש טמא שפתים.** לפי דעתי שהנביא גדל עם ישראל שהיו טמאים במעשה ובדיבור, והנה למד מדיבורם, והעד ויסרני מלכת בדרך העם הזה (ישעיהו ח' י"א) על כן אמר ובתוך עם טמא שפתים אנכי יושב:


*A man of unclean lips*. The prophet was a man of unclean lips, I think, because he grew up with the Israelities, that were unclean in deeds and words, and he learnt their way of speaking; comp. And he warned me not to go the way of this people (8:11); therefore he says, And in the midst of a people of unclean lips I am dwelling.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:5:3)


וטעם **כי את המלך יי' צבאות ראו עיני** שהוא קדוש ופחדתי להקדישו בעבור טומאת שפתים, ואף על פי שאמר ראו עיני במראות נבואה ראה כן:


*For mine eyes have seen the king*, who is holy, and whom I was afraid to anctify because of the uncleanness of my lips. Although he says, Mine eyes have seen, etc., it is but in a prophetical vision that he saw Him.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:1)


**ויעף.** כאשר הוא [הע"ין] קמוץ ויקרא בחטף הוא מגזרת עוף, וכאשר פתוח הוא מגזרת עיף:


ויעׇף *Then flew*. As written here, with a short kamez under ע, it is derived from עוף to fly; but ויעַף (Jud. 4:21), where the ע has a pathah, is derived from עיף to be weary.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:2)


**רצפה.** גחלת כמו עוגת רצפים:


רצפה *A live coal*. Comp. רצפים coals (1 Kings 19:6).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:3)


וטעם **במלקחים** כדרך בן אדם:


*With tongs*. As men use to do.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:6:4)


וטעם **המזבח** בעבור שהאש היא טהורה לא זרה:


*From off the altar*. Where the fire is holy, where there is no strange fire.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:1)


**ויגע וגו'.** טעם 'זה', על האש שימצא בלשון זכר:


זה *This*, namely, הׇאֵשׁ the fire; אֵשׁ is used also as a masculine noun.¹²

footnotes:
¹² I. E. does not refer זה to רצפה, because the former is masculine, the latter feminine; he supplies therefore הָאֵשׁ the fire, which, though generally used as a feminine noun, is sometimes constructed with the masculine form of an adjective; comp. אש להט flaming fire (Ps. 104:4).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:7:2)


**וסר עונך.** הוא עון הדיבור שהוא מדבר התולים כדרך אנשי דורו:


*Thy sin*. The sinning by words; for he spoke frivolously, like his fellow-men.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:1)


**ואשמע.** אומר לשרפים על כן מלת לנו:


*For us*. He speaks now to the seraphim; therefore he says, for us (plural).¹³

footnotes:
¹³ For us is, according to Ibn Ezra, equal to for myself and you, the Seraphim; by this interpretation he avoids referring the plural for us to God.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:8:2)


וטעם **הנני שלחני** אחרי שטהרו שפתי אני ראוי להיות שליח ולא הייתי כן בימים הראשונים, על כן אמרתי מזאת הפרשה תחלת נבואת ישעיה:


*Here am I, send me*. Since my lips are pure, I am fit to be the messenger, but I was not before. From these words I infer that this chapter contains Isaiah’s first prophecy.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ He declares that he was before unfit for bearing the message of the Most Holy.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:9:1)


**ויאמר. שמעו שמוע.** יש אומרים אח' שנגזרה הגזרה השם לא יקבל תשוב' למנוע הרעה נגזרת בעולם הזה, ויאמר רבי משה הכהן כי הטעם על מה שיועיל להן מעצו' טובות שימלטו בעבור', וזה היה נכון לולי מלת ושב ורפא לו, והראשון הוא הנכון:


*Hear ye, indeed*, etc. Some assert that God does not accept the repentance of the sinner, when his earthly punishment is already decreed, to cancel the sentence. R. Moses Hakkohen is of opinion that this passage describes the benefit the people will derive from listening to the good advice of the prophet; that they will be delivered from their afflictions.¹⁵ This is, however, contradicted by Lest they return and be healed. The first explanation is the right one.

footnotes:
¹⁵ R. Moses Hakkohen explains the verse thus: Listen to the words of the prophet, and you will not suffer any of the threatened evils; but this opinion is rejected by Ibn Ezra on account of the following verse, which is the continuation of this, and leaves no doubt about its meaning; according to his opinion the prophet says, Hear ye indeed, but understand not; it is of no use, because it is too late.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:1)


**השמן.** יש אומר שמלת השמן שם הפועל כמו הקטר יקטירון כיום (שמואל ב' ט"ו) וכן השע כמו להשע, וזה לא יתכן בעבור מלת פן, רק הכל ציווי, וידענו כי אין כח בנביא להשמן הלב רק הוא בדבו' וכמוהו רבים:


השמן *Make fat*. According to some it is infinitive, like הקטר To burn incense (1 Sam. 3:16); and הׇשַׁע likewise, like הׇרַע To do evil (Lev. 5:4); but this cannot be so, because of the conjunction פן lest.¹⁶ They are all rather imperative forms. We know that the prophet cannot make the heart fat; he shall only declare their heart to be so; there are many instances like it.

footnotes:
¹⁶ Since the part beginning with lest is the secondary sentence, the preceding must be the principal one; and השמן ,השע, the verbs of the principal sentence, cannot be Infinitives.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:10:2)


**השע.** מגזרת לא תשעינה (ישעיהו ל"ב ג'), כטעם טח, וכן תרגום ארמית. והיה ראוי להיותו על משקל הרף, והשתנה בעבור אות הגרון, או יהיה מהפעלים השניים הנראים:


הׇשַׁע *Shut*. Comp. תשעינה Will be shut (32:3). In Chaldee, this word שעה has the same meaning.¹⁷ The imperative Hiphil ought to be הֶשֶׁע like הֶרֶף, but the guttural letter ע causes the alteration; the form הָשַׁע can also be derived from a verb (שעע) ע״ע

footnotes:
¹⁷ Comp. Lev. 14:42, 43, and the Chaldæan translation.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:11:1)


**ואומר.** ביקש הנביא לדעת עד מתי תעמוד זאת הרעה שלא יבינו ולא ישובו, והנה התשובה עד שתהיה הארץ שממה:


*How long*. The prophet wants to know how long this misfortune shall last, that the people shall not understand nor repent. The answer is, Till the land be desolate.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:12:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:12:2

העזובה *The forsaken land*.¹⁸ Adjective or participle passive Kal.

footnotes:

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:1)


**ועוד** יש אומר כי עשרה מלכים יעמדו עוד על יהודה טרם הגלות וזה טעם **ושבה והיתה לבער**כמו ובערת הרע (דברים כ"א כ"א), ויש אומרים מגזרת לא תבערו אש (שמות ל"ה ג'). ובאמ' שכן היה מספר המלכים עם עזיהו, ואחרי' אמרו כי עשירית תשאר בארץ, ועל דרך הדקדוק [צ"ל דקדוק] הלשו' עשיריה תאר השם ואיננו כמו עשירית והעד יהיה ישראל שלישיה (ישעיהו י"ט כ"ד), והנה התברר כי זה רמז למלכות:


ועוד בה וגו׳ *And yet in it shall be*, etc. According to some: Ten more kings will rule over Judah before the exile, and then ושבה והיתה לבער it¹ shall again be removed¹⁹: comp. ובערת And thou shalt put away (Deuter. 21:21); others compare לבער with תבערו You shall kindle (Exod. 35:3)—and the number of kings from that time, Uzziah included, was really ten. Some explain, the tenth part will be left in the land. Grammatically, עשיריה is an adjective, the tenth; but different from עשירית the tenth part; comp. שלישיה (19:24) the third. It is, therefore, clear that עשיריה refers to the number of kings.²⁰

footnotes:
¹ The kingdom.
¹⁹ A. V., Shall return and shall be eaten.
²⁰ עשיריה being an adjective, and the feminine noun מלכות being supplied, the phrase ועוד בה עשיריה וגו״ is explained by I. E., But yet in it shall be a tenth reign, and then it shall again, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:2)


**כאלה וכאלון.** שנים אילנים היו בשער שלכת והיו חזקים, והאומרים כי שלכת הפוך מלשכה איננו אמת, גם כן הגוזרי' אותו ממלת השליך כי המדבר כאלה לא ידע דקדוק הלשון:


אשר בשלכת *Which were in Shalecheth*.²¹ Two trees were in the gate Shalecheth, which were exceedingly strong.¹ Those that take לשכת ═ שלכת are wrong, as well as those that derive it from השליך he cast; for whoever is able to say such things has no knowledge of grammar.²²

footnotes:
²¹ A. V., When they cast their leaves.
¹ The gate Shalecheth is mentioned 1 Chr. 26:16; but for the two trees no other authority is known than the oak and terebinth of this verse.
²² שלכת is a form derived from the Piel; but השליך is Hiphil; this is however, no valid objection, since the Piel has often the meaning of the Hiphil.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:3)


וטעם **מצבת בם** שיעמדו עוד ויהיו נצבי' תמיד, ואל תתמה על שהמשילם לאילן והנה כן כי כימי העץ (ישעיהו ס"ה כ"ב):


מצבת בם *Substance is in them*. They will still remain and stand firmly for ever; the comparison of the people with a tree is by no means uncommon; comp. for as the days of a tree, etc. (65:22).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 6:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/6:13:4)


וטעם **זרע קדש מצבתה.** שאלה שיעמדו בה אחר כן הם זרע קדש, וזה רמז לעולים מגלות בבל:


*Holy seed will be the substance thereof*. Holy seed will they be that will remain after that. Those that would come back from the Babylonian exile are here hinted at.

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:1:1)

*And he could not*. Pekah ben Remaliahu is meant; comp. Aram is confederate with Ephraim, in the next verse.¹

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:3:3)


**תעלת.** כמו אשר בתעלה לחכה (מלכים א' י"ח ל"ח), והמי' רצים, ואין הברכה ככה, כי הברכ' מקום חיבור מימי הגשמים'. ורבי' אמרו שנקראת כן בעבור שמימיה מקום [צ"ל ממקום] מבורך:


תעלת *Ditch* (comp. 1 Kings 18:38), where the water is running; while בְרֵכָה pool signifies a gathering of rain water; many derive בְּרֵכָה from בְּרָכָה blessing, its water coming from a blessed place, from heaven.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:1)


**ואמרת. השמר.** מלרע מגזרת שמרים (ישעיהו כ"ה ו') כמו ושקט הוא על שמריו (ירמיה מ"ח י"א), והטעם שב על שמריך, כי לעולם השמר מלשון שמירה הוא מלעיל, והעד אל תירא:


חִשָּׁמֵ֨ר Accent on the last syllable. This word is to be compared with שמרים dregs, lees (25:6.), שמריו ושקם הוא על He has settled on his lees (Jerem. 48:11), and explained, Remain on thy lees (that is remain quiet), for הִשָּֽׁמֶר Take heed has the accent on the last syllable but one; and besides, the following Fear not proves the correctness of this explanation.⁴

footnotes:
⁴ השמר is parallel to אל הירא as השקט to לבבך אל ירך, and all these verbs appear to have a similar meaning, while Take heed, and Fear not are just the reverse in meaning the one of the other. השמר means therefore, according to I. E., remain quiet.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:4:2)

ודמה אלה המלכים לזנבות אודים, כמו אוד מוצל מאש (זכריה ג' ב'), והטעם שהם כמו הנשאר לאוד שיעלה עשן ואין כח לו לבער על כן בחרי אף כי בחרי אפם ידמו לזנבות:


*Tails of smoking firebrands*. The prophet compares these kings to the tails of firebrands—אודים firebrands comp. Zach. 3:2—because they are like the remnant of a firebrand that smokes, but cannot burn; and adds. In the fierce anger because it is by their fierce anger that they are like tails of firebrands.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:6:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:6:2)


**את בן טבאל.** יש אומרים כי הוא בתמורה רמלא והוא בן רמליהו, וזה הבל, [כי] בעבור שהזכיר בתחילה בן רמליהו והוא אומר עם ארם ונמליך מלך, יש אומר הטוב אלינו, ואין מלת אל כי אם כלא, כאילו אמרו את בן טוב לא, והנכון שהוא שם שר גדול מישראל או מארם:


טבאל is by a certain interchange of letters the same as רמלא, and בן טבאל therefore the same as בן רמליהו; this is nonsense, because Ben Remaliahu is mentioned before, and he says with Aram, Let us set a king in the midst of it, the son of Tobel. Others say that טָבְאַל means טׂב אֵלֵינוּ good for us, but אַל can only be taken as equal to לא, and בן טבאל would then be בן טבלא ═ good for nothing; but I conclude that it is the name of some famous prince in Israel or Aram.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:7:1)


**כה.** לא תקום, זאת העצה כי כן הזכיר למעלה יעץ, וכבר הודעתיך כי כל פועל אם לא נזכר השם, הו' בכח הדבור:


תקום *Shall stand*. Supply זאת העצה this counsel; for יעץ he has taken counsel is mentioned above (ver. 5), and I stated already (5:2) that the verb contains implicitly a verbal noun, when it is not directly mentioned.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:1)


**כי.** טעם כי כמו כי עם קשה עורף הוא (שמות ל"ד מ'), אך על פי, והטעם בעבור רצין ופקח הצרים על ירושלם:


כי *Although*, Comp. כי עם קשה ערף הוא Although they be a stiffnecked people. (Exod. 34:9.) This plan will not be realised, although Rezin and Pekah besiege Jerusalem.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:2)


**ובעוד.** כאומר עוד נשארו שנים ויהיה כן, ותוספ' הבי"ת כבי"ת בטרם, ותחלת זה החשבון משנת הרעם שהיה בימי עוזיה שהתנבא עמוס וישראל גלה יגלה (עמוס ז' י"א), וכמוהו ויהי מקץ ארבעים שנה ויאמר אבשלום (שמואל ב' ט"ו ז'):


*And yet*⁷ *threescore, etc*. Comp. the common phrase so and so many years are still left before such and such an event will take place. ב in בעוד is superfluous as in (טרם═)בטרם before. These sixty-five years begin with the year of the earthquake, that happened in the days of Uzziah, when Amos prophesied¹ And Israel will surely go into exile (Amos 7:11). Comp. And it was at the end of forty years (2 Sam. 15:7.)⁸

footnotes:
⁷ A. V. Within.
¹ This is not quite correct, since Amos prophesied two years before the earthquake (Amos 1:1.)
⁸ No mention is there made when the 40 years began, but it is certain that they did not begin with the event recorded immediately before; in the same way the sixty-five years here are not to be counted from the year of this prophecy, but, according to Ibn Ezra, from the year of the earthquake in the reign of Uzziah.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:8:3)


**יחת.** מגזרת החתות (ישעיהו ט' ג') והוא מבנין נפעל, כמו ימם (ישעיהו י"ג ז'), והטעם שיהיה לו רע מעם שיבוא עליו, ויתכן היות יחת מבעלי הנו"ן כמו יגש, וכמוהו תחת גערה במבין (משלי י"ז י') והנה נראה הנו"ן במלת הנחת יי גבוריך (יואל ג' י"א) והטעם שירד מהיותו נחשב לעם:


יֵחַת *Shall be broken;* comp. החתות Thou hast broken (9:3); it is Niphal, like יִמַּס (13:7) Will be melted מֵעָם *By a people*.⁹ Evil shall befall them by means of a people that will come against them. יֵחַת can also be Kal of a verb נחת ,פ״נ to go down, (like יִגַּשׁ he will approach; comp. תֵּחַת It comes down) (Prov. 17:9); הנחת Cause to come down (Joel 3:11), where the נ is not omitted. The meaning of יֵחַת מֵעָם is accordingly: They will go down and be no more considered as a nation.

footnotes:
⁹ A. V. That it be not a people.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:9:2)


**אם לא תאמינו.** תחסר מלת דברו, והטעם בקשו אות, על כן כתיב אחריו ויוסף יי שאל לך אות, והנה יראה כאשר אמר הנביא אם לא תאמינו שלא ענה:


*If you will not believe*. Supply speak, or ask for a sign; wherefore immediately succeeds, And the Lord, etc., Ask thee a sign. But it appears that when the prophet said, If ye will not believe, etc., Ahaz did not answer.

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:10:1)


**ויוסף דבר אל אחז.** על ידי ישעיהו וכמוהו וידבר יי אל מנשה ואל עמו (דברי הימים ב' לג י'):


*Unto Ahaz*. Through Isaiah; comp. And the Lord spake unto Manasseh and unto his people (2 Chr. 33:10).¹²

### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:11:1)


**שאל העמק שאלה.** ציווי אחר ציווי בלא דבק וי"ו, וכמוהו התאחדי הימיני (יחזקאל כ"א ט"ו) ומלת שאלה על משקל יי שמע' (דניאל ט' י"ט), כאילו אמ' שאל והעמק בשאל' שתהיה למטה או הגבה למעלה, ורבי' אמ' שמלת העמק גם הגבה שם הפועל:


העמק שאלה. Two consecutive imperatives without the conjunctive ו; comp. התאחדי הימיני Go thee one way, go on the right hand (Ez. 21:16). שְׁאָלָה Imperative, like שְׁמָעָה hear (Dan. 9:19). Ask, and touch the depth with the question, or ask on high above. Many take both העמק and הגבה as infinitives.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ As infinitives they must be connected with אות a sign, and שְׁאָלָה must then have the same meaning as שְׁאׂלָה grave.—Ask for a sign, that he do anything either below in the depth of the earth or on high in heaven.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:12:1)


**ויאמר.** מתשובת הנביא ידענו כי מחשבת אחז היתה לרעה וטעמו לא ארצ' לשאול ולנסו' כי אדע שלא יוכל לעשות מה שאשאל ממנו:


*I will not ask*, etc. From the answer of the prophet we conclude that the words of Ahaz must be taken in a bad sense: I shall not ask nor shall I try Him, for I know that He cannot do what I should ask Him.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:13:1)


**ויאמר. הלאות.** דבר שלא יוכל לעשותו, והנה טעמו בעבור שאתם מלכים ואין כח באדם כנגדכם תחשבו כי כן השם:


*To weary men*. To make them tired of a thing which they have tried to accomplish, so that they become unable to continue their efforts. Because you are kings, and people cannot resist you, you think the same about the ways of God.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ You think, that in the same way, as men become weary in their resistance against you, God is weary and unable to oppose your plans.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:14:1)


**לכן.** טעם 'הוא' אע"פ שאתם לא תשאלו האות הוא יתננו לכם, והתימה מהאומרים שעל אלהיהם ידבר, והנה האות נתן לאחז ואותו נולד אחרי שנים רבות, ועוד שאמר כי בטרם ידע הנער טוב ורע תעזב האדמ', והנה היתה ארץ אפרים גם דמשק עזובה בשנת שש לחזקיהו, והכתוב אמר מפני שני מלכיה, ורבים השתבשו ואמרו כי עמנואל הוא חזקיה, וזה לא יתכן שאם אמרנו שזאת הנבואה היתה בתחילת מלכות אחז, הנה כל מלכותו שש עשרה שנה וכאשר מת היה חזקיהו בן חמש ועשרים שנה, ואחרים אמרו שהוא בן אחז, ואחרים אמרו שהוא משל למלכות, ואם כן מה טעם לדעת הנער טוב ורע, ומה טעם למהר שלל לקר' אב ואם (ישעיהו ח' ד'). והישר בעיני שעמנואל הוא בן ישעיהו, גם כן מהר שלל, והעד ואקרב אל הנביאה (ישעיהו ח' ג'), גם כן שאר ישוב. וכל אחד מאלה השלשה בנים נקראו [צ"ל נקרא] לאות מה שעתיד להיות, הנה עמנואל שהשם יעזרם ויהיה עמם בצר' שהם עומדים [בה] בעבור שני המלכים, ומהר שלל שבאה עת גלות שומרון, ושאר ישוב ששארית ישראל יעשו תשובה, והנה העד הנאמן על זה הפי', הנה אנכי והילדים אשר נתן לי (ישעיהו ח' י"ח) כמו הילדים אשר חנן אלהים, (בראשית ל"ג ה'), והמפרשים אותם תלמידים יראוני כמוהו במקרא, גם ישעיהו היה לאות ולמופת על מצרים (ישעיהו כ' ג'), ויאמר הגאון כי האות הוא שיהיה זכר, ולפי דעתי שהאות חמאה ודבש יאכל, כי אין מנהג הילדים שיאכלו בעת לדתם:


*Therefore the Lord himself* etc. Though you do not ask a sign, He will give it you. It is to me a matter of surprise that there are those who say the prophet here refers to Jesus, since the sign was given to Ahaz, and Jesus was born many years afterwards; besides, the prophet says, For before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land shall be forsaken; but the countries of Ephraim and Syria were wasted in the sixth year of Hezekiah, and¹⁵ it is distinctly said of whose two kings, etc. Many make the mistake of identifying Immanuel with Hezekiah; they cannot be the same, granting even this prophecy to have been uttered at the beginning of the reign of Ahaz; he reigned only sixteen years, and Hezekiah was at the death of Ahaz twenty-five years old. According to others, Immanuel is another son of Ahaz, and others again take the names (Immanuel, Maher Shalal and Shear Yashub) as symbolical of the kingdom; but if so, what meaning would be in the child’s knowing good and evil and in Maher Shalal calling father and mother? (8:4). I think that Immanuel is the son of Isaiah, as well as Maher Shalal; the latter is proved by And I went unto the prophetess, etc. (8:3). Shear Yashub is similarly related to the prophet (ver. 3); each of the three sons received a name that contained some hint at future events; Immanuel implied that God would help them and be with them during the troubles caused by the two kings; Maher Shalal, that the time for the exile of Samaria had arrived; and Shear Yashub, that the remnant of Israel would repent; this explanation is well borne out by the words, Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me, are for signs and for wonders. Comp. The children which the Lord hath graciously given to thy servant (Gen. 33:5).¹⁶ Those that in the former passage regard children as equivalent to pupils must produce us some analogy from Scripture.¹⁷ Isaiah himself was a sign and an example concerning Egypt (20:3).—The Gaon says that the sign consisted in the child being a male child;¹⁸ but in my opinion the sign was that the child was to eat butter and honey; for it is not usual that children eat these things immediately after their birth.¹⁹ after its birth.

footnotes:
¹⁵ The following is added to show that The land shall be forsaken, can only refer to Syria and Israel; both kingdoms were successively conquered by Assyria in the time of Ahaz and Hezekiah.
¹⁶ This quotation is to prove that the words, the children which the Lord has given me refer to the true children of the prophet, not to pupils, and that they are not used in any other figurative sense.
¹⁷ It is hardly necessary to refer to the great many instances, where the listener or reader is addressed as My son, but Ibn Ezra speaks of the whole phrase, children whom the Lord hath given me, and to take that in a figurative sense is not possible without some analogous examples.
¹⁸ This was foretold by the prophet (ver. 14).
¹⁹ If this be the right explanation, the most important point in the sign is omitted from the text, namely, that the child will eat those things immediately

וידענו כי הקטן בשנים יקרא נער והנקבה נערה, גם כן עלמה והזכר עלם, והנה יתכן להיותה בתולה או בעולה, כי אין בטעם רק כנגד השנים, ועלם יוכיח והנה ודרך גבר בעלמ' (משלי ל' י"ט) ואיננה בתול' כלל, בעבור שאמר בראש לא ידעתים:


We know that a male child is called נער, a female child נערה or עלמה—the feminine of עֶלֶם—whether she be a virgin or not; for עלמה signifies a person of a certain age, like the masculine עלם; and in דרך גבר בעלמה the way of a man with a young woman²⁰ (Prov. 30:19) עלמה is certainly not a virgin; because at the beginning of that passage it is said, which I know not (ibid. 18).

²⁰ A. V. the way of a man with a maid.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:16:1

**כי וגו'.** יש אומרים בן עשרים שנה בעבור דברי משה מבן עשרים (שמות ל' י"ד), אם כן היתה זאת הנבואה אחר שתי שנים במלכות אחז, ויתכן היותו פחות מעשרים:

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:20:1)


**ביום. בתער השכירה.** משל על יציאת מלאך השם והרג מחנ' אשור, יש מפרשי' 'השכירה' הגדולה, ואמרו כי כמוהו גם שכיריה בקרבה (ירמיה מ"ו כ"א), ולפי דעתי שהשכיר' שם כמו בכח האכילה (מלכים א' י"ט ח'), והוא מגזרת שכר שיקח בעל התעד, בעבור שהיה חדה מאד, כי זאת היא אומנותו, וטעם את הראש והזקן ושר ונגיד, כי כן כתוב (דברי הימים ב' ל"ב כ"א):


*Shall the Lord shave with a razor that is hired*. This refers to the angel of the Lord coming forth and destroying the camp of Assyria (37:36). Some take השכירה in the meaning of great; comp. שכיריה (Jer. 46:21) her great ones.²⁵ I think that שכירה is a noun like אכילה the eating (1 Kings 19:8), derived from שכר hire, which the owner of the razor receives; for this instrument, the hired razor, is very sharp; it is his profession.²⁶ *The head, the hair of the feet, the beard*. Every mighty one, all princes and noblemen; it is said so distinctly (9:14)

footnotes:
²⁵ This is the explanation of Rashi; the Targum has here for שכירה the word הריפא sharp, but in Jerem. רברבהא, her great ones.
²⁶ It is the profession of him, that lets out razors on hire, to keep them sharp.

### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 7:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/7:25:1)


**וכל ההרים אשר במעדר וגו'.** שהיו הכרמים שם בתחילה מתקנים יתקנום עתה, כי לא יהיו שם חוחים, וכל כך יתן השם ברכה בכרמי ההר עד שישלחו השור שם, כטעם אסרי לגפן עירה (בראשית מ"ח י"א), והנה אמר כי מעגלה אחת ושתי צאן ירבה החלב, וכרמי [צ"ל ובכרמי] ההר שימלטו לבדם יתן השם ברכה עד בלי די:


*And on all hills, etc*. And all the hills, where vineyards have formerly been carefully dressed, will now again be prepared; for there will be no thorns, and God will give such a blessing on the vineyards of the mountains, that people will send the cattle there; comp. He bindeth his foal to the vine (Gen. 49:4). The prophet says that from one cow and two sheep there will be obtained a plentiful supply of milk; and the vineyards of the mountains, that will alone remain undamaged, will enjoy a boundless blessing from the Almighty.

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:1:1

גליון. According to some related to מגלה scroll; the י of גליון compensates for the omission of the Dagesh in ל; comp. דליו They are poor (Prov. 26:7).¹

That is, in a form cast in the same way as the figure of a man is cast.¹ Others³ take גליון as the singular to גליונים (3:23) a cloth to which the writing was affixed by embroidery. *Maher-shalal-hash-baz*.² The prophet is told to indicate by these words the fall of Samaria.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:1)


**ואעידה.** יש אומרים כי האל"ף תחת ה"א, ואחרים אמרו כי בא עתיד תחת עבר, ויתכן היות ואעידה כמשמעו, שאעיד לי, והנביא עשה מה שצוה השם, ואם לא נזכר:


.⁴ואעידה According to some the א is here instead of ה. And take unto me faithful witnesses. According to others the future is used for the past: And I took unto me faithful witnesses. It may, however, be taken literally,⁵ that I should take as witnesses for me. The prophet did what God commanded, although it is not related in the text.

footnotes:
⁴ ואעידה is future Hiphil of והעידה ;עוד is imperative Hiphil, both with ה parag. and conjunctive ו.
⁵ As future.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:2:2)


**את אוריה הכהן.** היה כהן גדול בימים ההם, גם זכריה היה אדם גדול, ודרך הדרש ידועה על נבואת זכריה הנביא ואוריה הנביא:


*Uriah* THE *priest;* Uriah was then high priest. Zachariah was likewise a great man; what our Sages say about the prophecies of Zachariah and Uriah is well known.⁶

footnotes:
⁶ R. Gamaliel, R. Eleazar, the son of Asaria, R. Josua, and R. Akiba, were once going up to Jerusalem; when they came to Zophim (a place near Jerusalem), they rent their garments; they approached the Temple-Mount and saw a fox coming forth from the place where the Holy of Holies had stood before. The sages burst into tears, but R. Akiba exhibited joy. When they enquired how he could express feelings of gladness at such a sight, he asked them why they wept. What! said they; have we not cause to weep, when we find that the very spot of which the law has said, ‘The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death’ (Num. 18:7), has now become the abode of foxes? (Lam. 5:18.) And for the same reason, returned R. Akiba, do I rejoice. It is written: ‘And I should take for myself faithful witnesses, the priest Uriah, and Zachariah, the son of Berchjah.’ Now, what connection is there between Uriah and Zachariah? The one lived in the time of the first Temple (under Ahaz), the other in the time of the second. No other connection but to show that the prophecy of the one is conditioned by the words of the other. Uriah declared: ‘ For your sake shall Zion be ploughed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins,’ etc. (Mic. 3:12). Zachariah foretold: ‘There shall yet old men and women dwell in the streets of Jerusalem,’ etc. (Zac. 8:4). As long as Uriah’s words were not fulfilled, one might have doubted the truth of the prophecy of Zachariah; but when I perceive how literally the predictions of the one have been verified, I can entertain no reasonable doubt that the promises of Zachariah will be fulfilled likewise. Thereupon his companions exclaimed, Akiba, thou hast given us true comfort. (Talm. Babli Makkoth, 24).

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:6:1)


**יען. מי השלוח.** יש אומרים שהם ירושלם, והנכון מלכות בית דוד שרובי מלכי בית דוד היו צדיקים, ומלכי ישראל היו כלם רעים וחטאים, וטעם השילוח הם כמו גולות מים, או שישלחם אדם, או מים שיגדלו שלחים, כמו שלחיך פרדס רימונים (שיר השירים ד' י"ג):


*The water of the Shiloah*.¹¹ According to some Jerusalem is referred to by these words, but it is more correct to explain them as indicating the house of David, because the majority of the kings of this house were righteous, but the kings of Israel were all bad and wicked. מי השילח, literally: the canal, the water which is conducted by man, or which causes plants (שלחים) to sprout forth; comp. שלחיך Thy plants (Song 4:13).¹²

footnotes:
¹¹ Shiloah is a rivulet that takes its rise in the north-west of Zion, flowing between Zion and the Upper City, and falling into the Kedron, which runs into the Dead Sea.
¹² Shiloah, though a proper noun, may still, like all names, be explained like a common noun. According to Ibn Ezra it is derived either from שלח to send; שילח the water which is sent or conducted by the industry of man through the bordering fields and gardens; or from שלח to make fruitful; שילח the river which waters the valley through which it flows.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:10:2)


**כי עמנו אל.** זה טעם שם בן הנביא:


כי עמנואל. *For God is with us*. Here we have the reason for עמנואל Immanuel being the name of the prophet’s son.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:11:1)


**כי בחזקת היד.** כאשר התחזקה עלי הנבואה כמו היתה עלי יד יי (יחזקאל ל"ז א'):


*For the Lord spake thus to me with a strong hand*, that is: When the prophecy came with force upon me; comp. The hand of the Lord was upon me (Ez. 37:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:11:2)


**ויסרני.** דגשות הס"מך לבלוע היו"ד שהוא פ"א הפועל כמו בטרם אצרך בבטן (ירמיה א' ח'), והנה 'ויסרני' שיורה [צ"ל יורה] על יושר פירושי במלת טמא שפתים (ישעיהו ו' ה'):


ויסרני *And instructed me*. The ס has a dagesh to compensate for the absence of the י, which is the first radical;¹⁹ comp. אֶצָּרְךָ I formed thee (Jer. 1:5).²⁰ *He instructed me*, etc. A proof of the correctness of my view concerning Unclean lips (6:5).²¹

footnotes:
¹⁹ Ibn Ezra had the reading וִיִסְּרֵנִי; if he had וְיִסְּרֵנִי he would certainly not have explained it as future Kal, with ו conversive, and supposed the omission of a radical י; since this word is perfectly regular, being the Piël past with ו conjunctive of יסר.
²⁰ Future Kal of יצר.
²¹ If this instruction was necessary, the prophet must personally have been inclined to go the way of the people.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:12:1)


**לא וגו'.** יוכיח המשכילים שלא יקשרו על אחז וישובו עם מלך אשור, וזה טעם ואת מוראו, הנה הוא דבק עם מלך אשור הנזכר למעלה:


*Say ye not*. The prophet warns the right-minded not to conspire against Ahaz in order to join the King of Assyria; and this is to be understood by And their fear, etc., which refers to the King of Assyria²² mentioned before (ver. 7)

footnotes:
²² The King of Assyria was the object of their fear, and therefore many joined him.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:13:1)


**את.** אחר שאמר 'את' הוסיף 'אתו', וכמהו רבים, או טעמו אתו לבדו תקדישו, שמנהג האדם שיפחד מהקדוש, כמו כי איש אלהים קדוש הוא (מלכים ב' ד' ט'):


אתו *Him* is added, although את is before the noun, as in many instances; or it means Him alone.²³ *You shall sanctify*. That which is holy is usually revered by men; comp. for he is a man of God, he is holy (2 Kings 4:9).

footnotes:
²³ The repetition is explained as a sign of emphasis. Comp. Gen. 47:21; 1 Sam. 25:29; 2 Kings 9:27; Neh. 9:29.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:13:2

**מעריצכם.** שם התואר, או פועל, שהוא מפחידכם באמת:


מעריצכם is either an adjective, Your dreadful one, or participle, who in truth makes you fear.²⁴

²⁴ It is God who causes the terror, not the King of Assyria.

למקדש *For a sanctuary*. For a place whither man is used to go to receive blessing and strength. It is to be connected with לאבן ²⁵.נֶגֶף *For a stone*. For a rock, upon which man is used to go to find shelter.

**צור.** יש אומרים שהוא חסר נו"ן כמו שמור, והנכון שהוא כמו וצרת הכסף (דברים י"ד כ"ה) והנה כמו חתו', והטעם סתום אלה דברי הנבואה והם התעוד' והתורה:


צור According to some נ of the root is dropped; נצור ═ צור keep; but more correctly it is explained, Bind up; comp. וצרת And bind up (Deuter. 14:25). צור has, then, the same meaning as in the parallel phrase, חתום seal.—Do not reveal these prophecies, the testimony and the law.

המצפצפים *That peep*. צִפְצֵף has a meaning similar to רִּבֵּר; comp. אצפצף I shall peep (38:14).

*Surely a people that seeketh unto their God*, etc.²⁸ This is the reply.²⁹ Surely such is a people that seeketh unto his God! sarcastically and ironically said.³⁰ How could one seek unto the lifeless idols for the benefit of the living.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:20:1)


**לתורה ולתעודה.** הלמ"ד כמו אמרי לי אחי הוא (בראשית כ' י"ג), בעבור תורת הנבואה, כי עוד יאמרו כדבר הזה לא נשמע, כי הוא כלילה שאין לו שחר, והטעם לא תצא זאת התעלומ' לאור. ויש אומרים כי טעם 'לתורה' שבועה, וכדבר הזה לא ראינו במקרא:


לתורה ולתעודה *Concerning*³¹³¹ *the law and concerning* *the testimony*. The preposition ל has the same meaning as in לי of me (Gen. 20:13). לתורה ולתעודה Concerning the law and the testimony³² contained in the prophecy.—*They will surely*³³ *speak according to this word*, etc. They will say : We shall not listen to it, for it is like a night that is not followed by a dawn; its secret will never come forth to light. According to some לתורה is an oath, by the law; but we find no analogy to this in Scripture.

³² The words כי עוד are a corruption of והתעודה.
³³ A. V., If they speak not.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 8:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/8:21:1)


**ועבר.** יש אומרים כי הנה ימים באים שהעובר בארץ יהודה והוא מיהודה יהיה נקשה ורעב מפני חיל סנחריב וכאשר יראה כי לא יושיעו מלכו ולא ע"ז שלו, אז יפנה למעלה להתפלל לאלהי השמי', ולפי דעתי שהוא על חיל סנחריב שיעבר בארץ יהודה, וידוע כי מחנה גדול ירעב:


*And they shall pass through it*, etc. Some explain this verse in the following way: Days will come when he that is travelling in Judah, and being himself of the tribe of Judah, will be hardly bestead and hungry through the host of Sennacherib; and when he sees that neither his king nor his idol will help him, then he will turn upwards to pray to God in heaven. I think it refers to the host of Sennacherib when marching through the land of Judah; for when the army is large, it is frequently exposed to hunger.

וכאשר יפנה למעלה ולמטה יראה הכל חשך:

## Chapter 9


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:1:1)


**העם.** אלה הם אנשי ירושלם שהולכים במסילותיה כעור שלא יראה מרוב הצער:


*The people that walk in darkness*. The people of Jerusalem, who in their affliction walk in her streets as if they were blind of both their eyes.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:2:1)


**הרבית.** הם יהודה שנקבצו אל ירושלם, וטעם לו הרבית השמחה כאשר הוא קרי, ואשר הוא באל"ף לא היתה שמחה כמוה, כמו לא היה פחד (תהלים נ"ג ו'):


*Thou hast multiplied the nation*, that is, the tribe of Judah, that assembled again in Jerusalem. לו הגדלת השמחה Unto him thou hast increased the rejoicing;¹ this is according to the Keri; but according to the Ketib,² To whom thou hast never before given so great rejoicing; comp. לא היה פחד There was no such dread before (Ps. 53:6).³

footnotes:
¹ A. V., And not increased the joy.
² Keri (קרי the Chaldæan participle passive of קרא to read) is the reading of the text of the Bible according to the direction of the Massorah (tradition)—that is, according to the vowels, accents, and other signs with which the text is supplemented. Ketib (כתיב the Chaldaean participle passive of כתב to write), the text as it is written, without omitting, supplying, or altering any letter; the vowels to the letters must be supplied by the reader; for those in the text belong to the Keri.
³ Comp. also 23:13, זה העם לא היה. According to Ibn Ezra, לא היה כמוהו זה העם There was not such a people before.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:3:1)


**כי את עול סבלו.** משקלי השמו' משתני':


סבלו *His burden*. The form of the noun varies.⁴, סׂבֶל and סֵבֶל burden.

footnotes:
⁴ Our attention is very often called to this rule, as if the author protested thereby against the minute distinctions drawn by some synonymists in cases of nouns of the same root but of various grammatical structure; as, e.g.

**החתות.** נפתח הה"א בעבור אות הגרון, כמו החלו' (דברים ג' כ"ד), ואין מלה זרה, ותי"ו החתות לנוכח השם, כמו הרבית הגוי:


החתות *Thou hast broken*. The ה has Pathah on account of the succeeding guttural (ח); comp. הַחלות Thou hast begun (Deuter. 3:24); it is a regular form.⁵ The second person refers to God, as in הרבית Thou hast multiplied.

### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:4:1)


**כי וגו'.** יש אומרים סאון מגזרת סאה, שהשם מדד לאשור כפי מעשיו, ויש אומר שהוא הפוך מן אסון, כמו כשב וכבש, והנכון שאין למלה הזאת דומ', והעד סואן שהו' פועל והנו"ן שורש, וטעמו כמו נאקה, ברעש גדול:


סאון. According to some, this word is related to סאה measure, and the meaning of the whole phrase is, God gave to Assyria the full measure according to her deeds. Some say, that by metathesis סאון is said for אסון mishap;⁷ comp. כשב ═ כבש lamb; more correctly it may be said that this word is a hapax legomenon, and from the succeeding סואן, which is a verb (participle Kal), we see that נ is radical; the meaning of סאן is to cry loudly. ⁸

footnotes:
⁷ The meaning of the phrase would then be: For every kind of calamity will burst upon them tempestuously.
⁸ I. E. does not tell us whence he derived his meaning for this hapax legomenon; very probably, however, from its being connected with ברעש, with confused noise. According to this explanation the meaning of the phrase in question is : For all kinds of noise raged furiously.

**ושמלה מגוללה בדמים.** וכל אחד שוכב חלל ושמלתו מגוללה בדמיו או טעמו השמלה שהיתה מגוללה בדמי חללים שהרג, והנה הית' לשרפה, והטעם על מיתת חיל סנחריב ביד המלאך כנשרפים (ישעיהו ל"ז ל"ו):


ושמלה מגוללה בדמים *And garments rolled in blood*. Every one lies slain in his blood. Or the garment which rolled in the blood of murdered people, etc. לשרפה והיתה *It was burned*.¹ This refers to the destruction of the host of Sennacherib, which was burnt by the angel (37:36)

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:5:1)


**כי.** כל זה בזכות הילד שיולד לנו, וידענו כי בבא סנחריב היה חזקיהו בן שלשים ותשע שנה לכן קראו ילד בעת נבואת הנביא, יש אומרים כי פלא יועץ אל גבור אבי עד הן שמות השם ושם הילד שר שלום, והנכון בעיני כי כל אלה שמו' הילד, פלא שהשם עשה פלא בימיו, יועץ כן היה חזקיה ויועץ המלך (דברי הימים ב' ל' ב'), אל גבור שהיה תקיף, אבי עד שנמשכה מלכות בית דוד בעבורו, ועד כמו שוכן עד (ישעיהו נ"ח ט"ו), שר שלום שהיה שלום בימיו וכן כתוב (דברי הימים ב' ל"ב כ"ב):


*For unto us*, etc. All this has come to pass through the merit of the child that is born unto us. We know that at the time of the invasion of Sennacherib, Hezekiah was thirty-nine years old;⁹ at the time of this prophecy he is, therefore, called child (ילד). פלא יועץ אל גבור אבי עד. According to some, these expressions are names of God, and the following שר שלום, the name of the child. I think that all these words are names of the child; he is called פלא wonder, ¹⁰¹⁰¹⁰¹⁰ because God did wonders in his days; יועץ counselling; this is distinctly said of Hezekiah (comp. 2 Chr. 30:2); אל גבור Mighty chief; for Hezekiah was powerful; אבי עד The father of perpetuity, because the reign of the house of David was prolonged through his merits: עַד has here the same meaning as in 58:15. שר שלום Prince of peace because peace was established in his days; comp. 2 Chron. 32:22

footnotes:
⁹ Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he commenced to reign; he was king for twenty-nine years (2 Kings 18:2); fifteen years before his death he fell ill (20:6), and this seems to have happened immediately after the destruction of the Assyrian army. According to I. E. on 8:5, Hezekiah was at the time of this prophecy twenty-nine years old. As to the application of the word ילד to adults comp. Gen. 33:5, 37:30, 44:20.
¹⁰ A. V., Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father.
¹⁰ A. V., Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father.
¹⁰ A. V., Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father.
¹⁰ A. V., Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 9:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/9:6:1)


**למרבה.** דרך דרש הסופרי' כי המ"ם סגור בתוך המלה והיה ראוי להיותו בסוף, רמז לאות השמש ששב הצל לאחור, יתכן היות מרבה שם כמו מעשה, או פועל מהבנין הכבד הנוסף:


למרבה Some remark, after the manner of the Midrash,¹¹, when a final Mem is found in the middle of a word; as such instances are too striking to be easily forgotten, any lesson which may be attached to them will probably retain a firm hold upon the memory. that the use of the final Mem in this word hints at the miracle of the sun’s shadow going backward (38:8).¹² מרבה is either a noun, increase, like מְַעַשֶׂה work, or a regular participle Hiphil, causing to increase.

footnotes:
¹¹ פשט and מדרש (simplicity and research), are the two modes of commentary met with in Hebrew Literature; while the former reads and expounds the Scriptural text before us, the latter does not confine itself to this task, but, introducing extraneous historical, philosophical and moral matter, employs the wording of the text as a framework, or simply as a support to the memory. Notice is, therefore, taken even of the shape of the letters if they deviate in any extraordinary way from their customary form; as, e.g.
¹² In the Yalkut no mention is made of this explanation. Kimchi gives a Midrash explanation to this final Mem, but different from that cited by Ibn Ezra. Neither of them gives any account of the word, which is certainly one of the many instances of Keri and Ketib; according to the Keri it is read למרבה, according to the Ketib להם רבה ═ לם רבה.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:3:1)


**ומה וגו'.** הטעם כל זה עתיהם, והנה מה תעשו ביו' שיפקוד השם עונותיכ':


*And what*, etc. All this you have done, but what do you think to do in future, when the Lord will visit your iniquities?


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:3:2)


**כבודכם.** הוא ההמון:


כבודכם *Your Glory*. Your army.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:4:1)


**בלתי וגו'.** הטעם כל זה עשיתם, לא ימלט רק מי שיכרע תחת אסיר ויפיל עצמו תחת הרוגים כאילו הוא הרוג כמוהם:


All this you have done.⁴ בלתי וגו׳ *Except*⁵ *they bow down*, etc. None will escape except those that will bow down amongst the captives, or throw themselves amongst the slain, as if they were slain with them.

footnotes:
⁴ These words are superfluous, and seem to be a repetition of the same phrase in the preceding verse, a mistake made by some careless copyist.
⁵ A. V., Without me.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:1)


**הוי אשור.** הוא דרך קריאה:


הוי *Oh*. Sign of the vocative.¹

footnotes:
¹ See I. E. on 1:4, and Note 13.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:2)


**שבט אפי.** שהוכחתי בו רבים:


*The rod of mine anger*, wherewith I have chastised many.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:5:3)


**[ומטה וגו'].** והמטה שהוא ביד בני אשור הוא זעמי:


*And the staff*, etc. And the staff that is in the hand of the Assyrians, is the instrument of my indignation.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:6:1)


**בגוי.** ועל עם עברתי, שיש לי עברה עליה [צ"ל עליו]:


*The people of my wrath*. The people with whom I am wroth.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:7:1)


**והוא.** ידמה, כמו כאשר דמיתי (במדבר ל"ג נ"ו), והוא מגזרת דמיון, והטעם לא יחשב כי להוכיח שלחתיו, רק אין לו מחשבה כי אם לעקור את הכל:


ידמה *He meaneth*. Comp. דמיתי I thought (Num. 33:56); דמיון imagination (Ps. 17:12). He does not think that I have sent him to chastise; he only considers how to overthrow every kingdom.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:8:1)


**כי יאמר.** בלבו הנה שבו שרי, שהיו בתחלה שרים, הגם מלכים הם על גוים:


*He will say* in his heart.⁶ *Behold my officers*, etc. Those who formerly were officers, have now, through me, become rulers over nations.

footnotes:
⁶ See I. E. on 3:10.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:9:1)


**הלא ככרכמיש כלנו.** כמו ואכד כלנה (בראשית י' י'), והם שמות מקומות נקראו על שם הבונים כמו מצרים (בראשית י' ו'):


כלנו *Kalno* כלנה ═ Kalneh (Gen. 10:10); for the names mentioned there (Gen. x.) are names of places called after their founders, like מצרים Egypt.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:10:1

**כאשר עשיתי [צ"ל מצאה ידי] לממלכת.** עובדי ע"ז:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:10:2)


**מירושלם.** מסביבות ירושלם והם ערי יהודה הבצורות שתפש:


ופסיליהם מירושלים *And their graven images of Jerusalem*.⁷ Of the country surrounding Jerusalem, of the fortified towns of Judah, which were already in the hands of the Assyrian conqueror.

footnotes:
⁷ A. V., And whose graven images did excel them of Jerusalem.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:11:1)


**הלא וגו'.** זאת הנבואה היא על סנחריב כשר יבא להלחם על ירושלם:


*Shall I not*, etc. This prophecy refers to Sennacherib, when he came to conquer Jerusalem.⁸

⁸ Ibn Ezra refers this passage to Sennacherib’s expedition against Jerusalem Jerusalem was not conquered by him; comp. 1:8.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:12:1)


**והיה כי יבצע.** ישלים וכמוהו ידיו תבצענה (זכריה ד' ט'):

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:12:2

**את כל מעשהו.** להביא חיל סנחריב אל ציון:


*His work*. To bring the host of Sennacherib unto Zion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:12:3)


**על פרי.** כמו פרי מחשבתו [צ"ל מחשבתם] (ירמי' ו' י"ט):

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:1)


**כי.** עשיתי, גבורה:


עשיתי I have acted valiantly. ⁹ Supply גבורה valour.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:2)


**נבונותי.** מהשניים הנראים מבנין נפעל:


נבונותי *I am prudent*. Niphal of בין, verb ע"י.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:3)


**ואסיר.** עתיד והטעם על זמן עומד כמו יעשו עגל בחורב (תהלים ק"ו י"ט):


ואסיר And I was removing. Future for the imperfect;¹⁰ comp. יעשו they made. Ps. 106:19.

footnotes:
¹⁰ See chap. i., Note 43.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:4)


**ועתידותיהם שושיתי.** מגזרת ועתדה בשדה לך (משלי כ"ד כ"ו), הממון שיזמן האדם שימציאנו לעתיד מימיו:


ועתודתיהם *And their treasures*. Comp. ועתדה And prepare it (Prov. 24:26); the possessions which man provides for himself for the days that are to come.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:13:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:13:5)


**ואוריד כאביר.** ואם הוא באל"ף הוא נוסף, והטעם אוריד היושבים בארמון כביר, ויאמר ר' משה ההן כי האל"ף עיקר, כמו אביר הרועים (שמואל א' כ"א ח'), והטעם כגבור:


כאביר Although it is written with Aleph, this letter is pleonastic, and the word means strong, mighty—I subdued those that dwell in strong fortresses.¹¹ According to R. Moses Hakkohen, who takes the א as radical—comp. אביר the chief (1 Sam. 21:8)—it means like a hero.

footnotes:
¹¹ This is against the accents, which join כב׳ר with ואסיר and separate it from יושבים; besides, the construction of the words, the adverb or object כאביר being placed before the verb יושבים, is very unusual; the regular order would be יושבים כביר According to I. E. כַּבִּיר ═ כַּאבִּיר; according to R. Moses Hakkohen כְּאַַבִּיר ═ כַּאבִּיר.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:14:1)


**ותמצא.** לחיל, ממון כמו את החיל הזה (דברים ח' י"ז):


לחיל *The riches*. Comp. החיל the wealth (Deut. 8:17).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:14:2)


**נודד כנף.** פועל יוצא, והנה הכנף פעול, בעבור שהמשילם לבצים והאפרוחים יולדו מהם:


נודד *Moving*. A transitive verb, governing the accusative. כנף *Wing*. This figure is used because the nations have just been compared with eggs, and birds come from eggs.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:15:1)


**היתפאר הגרזן.** כלי הברזל שיחתך בו והוא מגזרת נגזרתי [צ"ל נגרזתי] (תהלים ל"א כ"ב) והנה הטעם כי השם המשילו, ואין למשור רע כי אם וישר במגר' (דברי הימים א' כ' ג'), והוא מפעלי הכפל, על משקל מעוז (ישעיהו כ"ה ד'):


הגרזן. An instrument to cut with. Comp. נגרזתי, I have been cut. (Ps. 31:23.) *Shall the axe*, etc. That is to say, It is God that has given the power to the Assyrians. משוד. Only one parallel is found to this word; וישר, And he cut (1 Chr. 20:3); it is derived from a verb ע״ע (שרר, to cut), after the form of מֽעוֹז, strength. ¹²

footnotes:
¹² מַשוֹר with Dagesh in ש and Pathah under מׇעוֹז ; מ has long Kamez under מ, to compensate for the omission of the Dagesh, because the succeeding letter is a guttural.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:15:2)


ומשל אחר כהניף שבט ואת מרימיו, והטעם כהנפת השבט ותנופת מרימיו, כי עיקר התנופה למרימיו כהרים מטה, ההרמה למרימים לא לעץ:


Another figure is contained in the succeeding ¹³.וחנופת מרימיו כהנפת שבט ═ כהניף שבט ואת מרימיו It is like the shaking of the rod; and this is principally the action of them that lift it up. כהרים מטה. *As the lifting up of the staff*, which is done by the people, not by the wood.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹³ Ibn Ezra read ואת מרימיו, while our editions have את מרימיו. Rashi seems also to have read ואת. I. E. does not at all explain the meaning of את; he ignores it entirely as if ואת מרימיו were the same as מרימיו ותנופת ═ ומרימיו.
¹⁴ A. V., As if the staff should lift up itself, as if it were no wood.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:16:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:16:2)

¹⁵ Verbs פ״י of this class take as a rule a Zeré

### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:17:1)

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:18:1)

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:19:1)


**ושאר.** שלא ימלטו כי אם מעטים עד שיוכל לכותבם נער שאין לו רגילו' בחשבון:

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:20:1)


**והיה.** על מכהו, הוא אשור, וזה לאות כי רבי' מיהודה קשרו:


*That smote them*, the Assyrians. This verse shows, that many of the men of Judah conspired against their king.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:21:1)


**שאר ישוב.** הוא שם בן הנביא, והנה פירש כי טעם שאר ישוב על שאר יעקב והוא יהודה, גם ישוב משרת עצמו ואחר עמו, כמו מתן בסתר יכפה אף (משלי כ"א י"ד), והנה הוא כן, שאר יעקב ישוב אל אל גבור:


שאר יעקב. *The remnant shall return*. This is the name of the prophet’s son, which is to be explained now. Supply יעקב, after the first שאר. The remnant of Jacob, that is Judah, will return; repeat likewise ישוב before אל: The remnant of Jacob will return to the mighty God (comp. Prov. 21:14). The verse, if written in full, would run thus: שאר יעקב ישוב אל אל גבור שאר יעקב ישוב,. The remnant of Jacob will return, the remnant of Jacob will return to the mighty God.

וטעם **גבור** בעבור שהוא יוכל להושיעם:


*Mighty*, who is able to help them.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 10:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/10:22:1)


**כי וגו'.** הטעם אף על פי שיהיו ישראל רבים בימים ההם כחול הים, לא ישאר מהם רק מי שישוב לשם, כי כליון חרוץ גזור מהשם, כמו אתה חרצת (מלכים א' כ' מ'), יבוא כנחל שוטף בצדק:


*For though*, etc. Although Israel should in those days be as numerous as the sand of the sea, only those that will return to God will remain; for destruction, which is decreed—חרוץ, decreed; comp. חרצת, thou hast decreed (1 Kings 20:40)—by God, will come like a river, overflowing with righteousness.

**כי.** מעט מזער, בימים, ויכלה זעמי ואפי בהם על רוב שהשחיתו, ויש מפרש תבליתם מן אחרי בלותי (בראשית י"ח י"ב), על משקל תכליתם [צ"ל תכלית] (תהלים קל"ט כ"ב):


מעט מזער. *A very little*. Supply בימים, of time. *And the indignation*, etc. And mine anger and wrath, on account of their great iniquities will all be spent. תבליתם. *Their iniquities*. According to some, their destruction; comp. בלותי, My old age²¹ (Gen. 18:12). The form of the word is like that of תַּכְלִית (Ps. 132:32)

²¹ חבלית is, according to the first explanation another form for תֶּבֶל (Lev. 20:12); according to the second it is formed from בלה, to wither, as תכלית, from כלה.

## Chapter 11


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:1)


**ויצא וגו'.** רובי המפרשים אמרו כי זה המשיח, והטעם שימות מחנה אשור הצר על ירושלם, ועוד יבא עת גאולת ירושלם השלימה, ולפי דעת רבי משה הכהן שעל חזקיהו רמז, כי הוא דבק עם הפרשה:


The majority of commentators apply this chapter to the Messiah, as if the prophet said, The Assyrian army, which is now attacking Jerusalem, will perish; but besides this partial deliverance, a time of complete redemption will come for Jerusalem. R. Moses Hakkohen refers the chapter to Hezekiah, on account of its being the continuation of the prophecy recorded in the preceding chapter.¹

footnotes:
¹ Ibn Ezra does not directly decide in favour of either opinion, but tries throughout the chapter to show that both views can be fairly upheld. The connection with the preceding chapter, however, which is to recommend the view of R. Moses Hakkohen, is a very feeble support, since the transition from momentary relief to the lasting Messianic redemption, even in one and the same chapter, would be quite natural.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:2)


**חוטר.** מגזרת תרגום מטה:


חטר *Rod*. Comp. חוטרא, the Chaldæan translation of .מטה

**גזע.** כמו זרע:


גזע Seed.²

footnotes:
² A. V., The stem. Ibn Ezra does not give the derivation of the word; in the three passages of the Bible where it occurs, it can be translated either stem, or seed.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:1:4)


**ונצר** כמו סעיף, כנצר נתעב (ישעיהו י"ד י"ט):


נצר *Branch*. Comp. 14:19.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:2:1)

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:3:1)


**והריחו.** פעמים תטעה הרגשת האוזן שתשמע ואין קול, גם העין תטעה שירא' לה הנח שהוא נע, רק הרגשת הריח לא תטעה, והריחו, כאילו יריח הדבר ביראת השם שיש לו, לא ישפוט כאשר יראה לעיניו, ולא כאשר ישמע, כי יתכן להיות עדות העדים שקר:


והריחו *And his enquiry*.⁵ The ear is sometimes deceived in hearing sounds, which are only imaginary; the eye, too, sees things in motion, which in reality are at rest; the sense of smell alone is not deceived. He will properly investigate the question before him by his piety; he will not judge according to what he seems to see or to hear, because the testimony of the witnesses⁶ might be false.

footnotes:
⁵ A.V. And shall make him of quick understanding.—I. E. derives והריחו from הריח, to smell, and explains why this verb has been chosen to signify to enquire, or to investigate properly.
⁶ The witnesses, is either to be taken literally and referred to to hear alone, or figuratively signifying the eye, and the ear, and referred to both to see, and to hear.

ואלה התוכחות והמשפטים הם כמשפט המלוכה:

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/11:5:1)


**והיה וגו'.** והנה הצדק לא יסור ממנו כל ימיו בכל מעשיו:


*And righteousness shall be*, etc. And uprightness will never depart from him in all his doings.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:7:1

**ופרה.** היא גדולה כי העגל קטן ויש אומרים כי הנקבה חזקה מהזכר:


פרה The large cattle; the younger of the breed is called עגל (ver. 6). Some assert that the female of cattle is stronger than the male.⁸

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 11:8:4

יתכן היות ה"א**הדה**תחת י"וד ידו אליה (ירמיה נ' י"ד), והטעם ישלח ידו, או אין לה אחות:
