## Chapter 22


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:1)


**משא גיא חזיון.** ירושלם שהיא מקום הנבואה:


*The valley of vision*. Jerusalem, the centre of all prophecies.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:1:2)


יש אומרים כי טעם **עלית לגגות** לקטר למלאכת השמים, ולפי דעתי שהטעם עלותם לראות החיילות הצרות על ירושלם כי כן מנהג המדינות:


*Thou art wholly gone up to the house-tops*. Some think, they went up in order to offer incense to the host of heaven, but my opinion is, that they went up in order to see the force that besieged Jerusalem, as is generally done under such circumstances.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:1)


**תשואות.** מגזרת שאון [יג ד']:


תשואות *Stirs*. Root שאה to stir; comp. שאון noise (13:4).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:2:2)


**עליזה.** שמחה והטעם כי היתה מלאה אנשים, ונלכדו בשביה ובעה ולא יכלו להלחם:


עליזה *Joyous*.—Jerusalem had been full of men, but they were smitten with captivity and famine, and could not fight.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:1)


**מקשת.** שראו, מרוב הפחד מסרו עצמם ואוסרו:


מקשת אסרו *Because of the bow they were bound*.¹ When they saw the bow of the enemy, they surrendered out of fear, and became prisoners.

footnotes:
¹ A. V., They are bound by the archers.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:3:2)


**מרחוק ברחו.** כמו עם לבבם שלם (דברי הימים י"ו ט'):


מרחוק ברחו ׳ *Which have fled from far*. The relative אשר which is to be supplied; comp. עם אשר לבבם שלם ═ עם לבבם שלם in behalf of those whose heart is perfect (2 Chr. 16:9)



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:1)


**על וגו'.** אלה דברי הנביא:


*Therefore said I*. The first person refers to the prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:2)


**שעו ממני.** הרפו ממני כמו לא תשעה ממני (איוב ז' י"ט):


שעו ממני *Look away from me*. Root שעה to let loose, to turn away; comp. תשעה Thou wilt depart² (Job 7:19).

footnotes:
² See chap. xvii. Note 11.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:4:3)


**אמרר**, השומעים בבכי:


אמרר בבכי *I will embitter by weeping*.³ I will embitter those that listen.

footnotes:
³ A. V., I will weep bitterly. According to I. E., the Piel of מרר is causative, and the object השמעים the bitterness, is to be supplied here.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:1)


**ומבוכה.** מגזרת נבוכים הם (שמות י"ד ג'):


ומבוכה *And of perplexity*. Comp. נבוכים entangled (Ex. 14:3).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:2)


**מקרקר.** מהפך או הורס והנה הוא הפך הקיר כמו ושרשך מארץ חיים (תהלים נ"ב ז'):


מקרקר overthrowing, or pulling down, derived from קיר wall, with a negative sense; comp. ושרשך, and he will take away thy root (Ps. 52:7), derived from שרש root.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:5:3)


**ושוע אל ההר.** יש אומרים כמו ישעו ואין מושיע (שמואל ב' כ"ב מ"ב), ויש אומרים כי השועה תגיע אל ההר:


ושוע אל ההר *And of crying to the mountains*. Some say that this phrase means the same as ישעו ואין מושיע they look, but there is none to save (2 Sam. 22:42); others, their cry will reach the mountains.⁴

footnotes:
⁴ According to the first explanation, שוע is identified with שעה to turn,to look, or to trust; and the meaning of the phrase is, it will be as if they trusted to the mountains, that could not help (see c. 17:7). The second explanation takes שוע in its usual meaning to cry: Their cry will be so loud that it will reach the mountains, that are far away.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:1)


**ועילם.** זאת הנבואה על ביאת נבוכדנצר, וטעם עילם אפילו עילם שהתגבר עליהם נבוכדנצר, הוא ישא אשפה ויבוא על ירושלם:


*And Elam*, etc. In the following the prophet predicts the siege of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar.⁵ *Elam*. Even Elam, that was defeated by Nebuchadnezzar,⁶ was to take up arms against Jerusalem.

footnotes:
⁵ I. E. refers this prophecy to Nebuchadnezzar, and not to Sennacherib; because the siege described here, is to end in the fall of Jerusalem (ver. 14 ); this was in fact the result of the siege of Nebuchadnezzar, while Sennacherib was, by a miraculous destruction of his army, compelled to leave Palestine altogether.
⁶ This statement is perhaps based on Jer. 25:25, 49:34 ff., where the collapse of the power of Elam is predicted; and Ezek. 32:24-25, where the extinction of the power of Elam is mentioned as an accomplished fact. Elam, according to I. E., conquered by Nebuchadnezzar, might be expected to refuse to join him in an expedition against Palestine.7 The Hebrew text has the words אפילו שחם בעלי מדינות though they are in possession of provinces; they have no sense; for why should the inhabitants of Kir in that case not join Nebuchadnezzar? even if we join the following קיר with this phrase: though they are in possession of the provinces of Kir, it is impossible to find any sense in it. If, however, we add רחוקות distant, as is done in the translation, all difficulty is at once removed. קיר אפילו שהם בעלי מדינות רחוקות even Kir, that is a distant country, or, even the inhabitants of Kir, that live in distant countries, and must find an expedition against Jerusalem very hard and troublesome, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:6:2)


**וקיר.** שאפילו שהם בעלי מדינות קיר, כמו וארס מקיר (עמוס ט' ז'), יגלה מגניו על ישראל סביבות ירושלם:


*And Kir*, though being far from Jerusalem;—comp. And Aram from Kir (Am. 9:7)⁸—*will uncover the shield* round Jerusalem against Israel.

footnotes:
⁸ The quotation is probably to prove that Kir is the name of a country, which is situated beyond Syria, and therefore distant from Jerusalem.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:1)


**ויהי.** כ"ף עמקיך לנכח ירושלם:


*Thy valleys*. The second person refers to Jerusalem. שת שתו.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:7:2)


**שות שתו.** הדייק והסוללה וכלי המלחמה:


*They prepare*,⁹ the forts, the trenches, and all the instruments of war.

footnotes:
⁹ A. V., They set themselves in array.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:1)


**ויגל.** וכבר נגלה מסך יהודה והטעם כי ראו בבוא האויב כי אין להן כח לסבול, ויתכן היות ויגל השם:


*And he discovered*, etc. The veil was already taken away from the eyes of Judah, when the enemy was approaching; they saw immediately that they had no strength to resist. The third person ויגל, And he discovered might also be referred to God.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ According to the first explanation, the enemy is the subject; the enemy, by his approach, opened the eyes of Judah, and made them discover their weakness.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:8:2)


**ותבט.** שב אל יהודה שהסתכלו בכלי הנשק:


*And thou didst look*. Judah is addressed.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:9:1)


וראו בקיעי עיר דוד כי רבו, והוצרכו לקבץ את מי הבריכה להיות כמו חומה סביב למקום


*Ye have seen also*, etc. They looked to the fortifications, and found that the breaches of the town of David were many; they were therefore obliged to collect the waters of the pool, that they might serve as a fence round the town.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:1)


**ואת.** והוצרכו לספר הבתים לדעת מספר אנשי המלחמה:


*And ye have numbered*, etc. They had to count the houses, in order to know the number of the soldiers.¹¹

footnotes:
¹¹ It was desirable to know the number of the houses, in order to ascertain how many soldiers the town might be able to keep.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:10:2)


**ותתצו הבתים.** הסמוכים לחומה מחוץ:


*And the houses have ye broken down*. The houses that were near the wall from without.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:1)


**ומקוה.** כמו מקוה מים (ויקרא י"א ל"ו):


ומקוה *And a ditch*. מקוה מים ═ מקוה A gathering of water (Lev. 2:36).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:2)


**ולא הבטתם אל עושיה.** שהוא השם, כי הוא עושה זאת הגזרה להביא נבוכדנצר:


*Unto the maker thereof*. Unto God, who has decreed to bring Nebuchadnezzar against Jerusalem.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:3)


**ויוצרה.** הטעם על הגזרה:


*Unto him that fashioned it*. That fashioned the decree.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:11:4)


ויתכן היות **מרחוק** דבר עם מלת ויוצרה, ויתכן היותו דבר עם לא ראיתם:


מרחוק *Long ago*. Join מרחוק either with ויוצרה, he that fashioned it long ago, or with לא ראיתם, you have not seen for a long time.¹²

footnotes:
¹² The second explanation is not in accordance with the accents; וְיוֹצְרָ֥הּ has a conjunctive, מֵרָח֭וֹק a disjunctive accent.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:12:1)


**ויקרא.** כנוי לגזרה, והנכון שהקריאה היא נבואת הנביאים:


*And in that day did the Lord*, *God of Hosts, call*, etc. That is, God decreed. More correctly, however, this phrase may be referred to the words of the prophet.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ The meaning of the phrase is therefore, And the prophet, in the name of God, declared.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:1)


**והנה וגו'.** הריגה יציאת הרוח, והפך זה וישחטם במדבר (במדבר י"ד ט"ו):


הרג *Slaying*, causing the separation of the soul from the body; הרג is used with reference to cattle instead of שחט, and on the other side וישחטם, And he slaughtered them (Num. 14:16) is used with reference to men instead of ¹⁴.ויהרגם

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:13:2)


**אכול ושתה.** ידבר הנביא מה שיהיו אומרים:


*For to-morrow we shall die*. The prophet foretells what people will say in the days of the siege.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:14:1)


**ונגלה.** זה הדבר ותחסר מלת אני כמו יי במראה אליו אתודע (במדבר יב ו') ויש אומרים כי הם דברי הנביא והראשון הוא הנכון:


ונגלה *And it was revealed*. This thing¹⁵ was revealed. באזני In mine ears.¹⁶ Supply אָזְנֵי the ears of.¹⁷ Comp. נביאכם יי Your prophet, the prophet of the Lord¹⁸ (Num. 12:6). According to some the suffix in באזני refers to the prophet; but the first explanation is better.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁵ The determination of the people, mentioned in the preceding verse.
¹⁶ A. V., In mine ears, by the Lord, etc.

**עד תמותון.** ביד האויב הצר עליכם:

### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:1)


**כה וגו'.** וטעם יי צבאות בעבור הסוכן שהוא ממונה על בית המלכות, וכאילו הוא פקיד על הממון שהוא אצור:


*God of hosts*. This attribute is added, because the treasurer is mentioned, who was appointed over the royal house, and whom some believed to be the master of the money stored up there.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ The hosts are, according to I. E., all creatures on heaven and earth (comp. Gen. 2:1). God of hosts is therefore the true master of the state treasures, not Shebna. Concerning the occasional use of the Tetragrammaton as an appellative governing the genitive צבאות of hosts, see i., Note 45, and I. E. On Exodus 3:15.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:2)


**הסכן.** כמו ערי מסכנות (שמות א' י"א), כמו אוצרות:


הסוכן *The treasurer*. Comp. מסכנות stores (Ex. 1:11).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:15:3)


וטעם **על.** שיתנבא עליו ויאמר לו:

### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:1)


מה לך לשבת פה ומי לך פה ממשפחה שיוכלו לעזור לך:


*What hast thou here?* Why didst thou stop here? *And whom hast thou here* of thy family that could assist thee?


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:16:2)


**כי חצבת לך פה קבר.** כמו כרית, ובורות חצובים (דברים ו' י"א), והטעם שתחשוב בלבך כי לעולם תהיה סוכן, ובירושלם תמות, וכבר תקנת לך שם קבר, והאומר שפיר' קבר כמו ארמון, איננו נכון, והעד שמה תמות:


חצבת *Thou hast hewed*. Comp. חצובים hewed (Deut. 6:11). Thou thinkest that thou wilt always remain treasurer, and that thou wilt die in Jerusalem, and therefore thou hast already prepared a grave for thee.—Those commentators that take gravein the sense of palace are mistaken, as shown by the words there shalt thou die (ver. 18).²¹

footnotes:
²¹ The Targum has אְַתַר place, and אַתְרֵיהּ his place for קבר and קברו and seems to take קבר figuratively for the palace or the place where Shebna hoped to remain till his death.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:1)


**הנה יי מטלטלך.** כפול, מן ויטילו הכלים [יונה א' ה']:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:17:2)


**טלטלה.** אתה שתחשוב כי אתה גבור כטעם והיית לאיש (מלכים א' ב' ב'), והנה הוא כדמות קריאה או טלטלה כטלטול גבר, והראשון קרוב אלי:


גבר *O man*.²² Thou, who thinkest that thou art mighty. Comp. והיית לאיש and show thyself a man (1 Kgs. 2:2). גבר is here the vocative case. It can also mean as the carrying away of a man.²³ I prefer the first explanation.

²² A. V., A mighty captivity.

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 22:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/22:18:1)

צנוף יצנפך צנפה *He will surely bind thee together*.²⁴²⁴ Comp. מצנפת mitre (Ex. 28:4). He will take him, together with all his money and wealth.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁴ A. V., He will surely violently turn and toss thee. According to I. E.: צנף to bind, מצנפת a mitre that is bound round the head.

**ארץ רחבת-ידים.** היא בבל:


*A large country*. Babylon.²⁷

footnotes:
²⁷ According to I. E. this catastrophe of the house of Shebna took place in the days of the Babylonian invasion during the reign of king Jehoiakim or Zedekiah, when Shebna himself was probably no more alive; for Manasseh reigned 55, Amon 2, Josiah 31, Jehoahaz ¼, Jehoiakim 11 years; and to these a part of the reign of Hezekiah must be added. It can hardily be understood why I.E. transfers this catastrophe to a later period and takes Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah, for the son of that Hilkiah, who officiated as high priest during the reign of king Josiah, while the text seems to point at the reign of Hezekiah (comp. 36:22), unless we assume that he is anxious to refer the second part of the chapter to the same period, to which, as he believed, the first part alluded. (Comp. ver. 6).

*There shalt thou die*, etc. There he shall die, with all his horsemen. *The shame of thy lord’s house*. For thou art a disgrace to the house of thy master; or thou wilt then be, etc. This prediction was probably verified in the exile of King Jehoiakim or Jehoiachim; comp. And I will call my servant Eliakim, the son of Hilkiah (ver. 20)

**והצפיעות.** אולי הם הבנות מגזרת יצא צפע (ישעיהו י"ד כ"ט), ואחר שאמר שהוא לאב הנה איש יהודה כבניו והנשים כבנותיו, שהם נמשלים אל כלים קטנים:

The female children are perhaps meant; comp. יצא צפע shall come forth a cockatrice (14:29).²⁹ Since he is said to be the father, the men of Judah are as it were his sons, and the women his daughters. *All vessels of small quantity*. The real reason for this explanation is very likely to be found in the masculine and feminine terminations of the two words צאצאים and צפיעות.

## Chapter 23


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 23:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:1)


**משא צור.** צור היא על הים ונבוכדנצר תפשה:


*Tyre*. A town near the sea; it was conquered by Nebuchadnezzar.¹. 10:11). As to the first siege, it is distinctly stated by Josephus that it was not successful; the result of the second is not mentioned, and some infer from Ez. 29:18, that Nebuchadnezzar did not conquer Tyre. But whether conquered or not, the distress and misery which so long a siege must have entailed upon the inhabitants of Tyre, the loss they sustained in wealth and territories, fully corresponds with the humiliation predicted by Isaiah, Jeremiah and Ezekiel. I. E. refers this chapter to the second and not to the first siege, very likely because the Chaldæans are mentioned in it, according to his interpretation, as the conquerors of Assyria (ver. 13).

footnotes:
¹ Tyre was besieged five years by Shalmaneser, about 720 B.C. (Joseph. Antiq. 9:14), and thirteen years by Nebuchadnezzar, 583—570 (ib


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 23:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:2)


**כי שדד כל בית.** בצור שלא יבא שום סוחר:


כי שרר מבית מבוא *For it is laid waste*, *that there is no house*, *no entering in*. For every house in Tyre is destroyed, that no merchants come there any more.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 23:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:1:3)


**מארת כתים.** אפילו מארץ כתים שהיא רחוקה נגלה להם זה השוד, והזכיר כתים בעבור האניות, והעד וצים מיד כתים (במדבר כ"ד כ"ד):


*From the land of Chittim*. Even from the land of Chittim, which is very far,² this destruction was announced to the ships of Tarshish. Chittim is mentioned, because of the ships which passed the coast thereof.³ Comp. (Num. 24:25)

footnotes:
² Chittim is probably Cittium in the isle of Cyprus, which belonged to Phoenicia.
³ Ships of Tarshish are ships coming from Tarshish; they passed the coast of Chittim (Cyprus), and heard there the news of the calamities of Tyre; because the enemy that besieged Tyre tried at the same time to get Cyprus into his possession, either by hostile attack or by a support given to her revolt against Tyre. The quotation from Num. 24:25, And ships from the coast of Chittim, is only to prove that Chittim was a naval power.

לא היה *There was none like them*.¹⁵¹⁵ Comp. לא היה פחד There was no fear like it (Ps. 53:6). According to others: Would that it were not; for *it founded the kingdom of Assyria for wild beasts*,¹⁶ that is, the Chaldsæans laid Assyria waste, and it became the habitation of wild beasts.¹⁷ לציים For the little wild beasts that live in the land.¹⁸ *They set up the towers thereof* etc. Although they, viz., the Assyrians, have set up the towers for defence, etc.

footnotes:
¹⁵ A. V., Was not. Where no fear was.
¹⁵ A. V., Was not. Where no fear was.
¹⁶ A.V., Till the Assyrians founded it for them that dwell in the wilderness.

¹⁸ The passage in the Hebrew text seems to be corrupt; the word ציים is explained by I. E. on 13:21, 34:14, to mean beasts that live in the wilderness. קטנות שהם is very likely a corruption for השוכנות, that dwell, and ציה desert is left out after בארץ.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 23:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/23:13:4)


**[הקימו בחוניו].** אף על פי שאשור הקימו המקימים בחוניו להלחם כמו עופל ובוחן (ישעיהו ל"ב י"ד), והוא בנין גבוה, והנכון שוי"ו בחוניו שב אל עם כשדים, כאשר הקים בחוניו - עוררו, פועל יוצא כאילו הבחונים עוררו הארמונים עד שהתעררו - שמה למפלה:


בחוניו *The towers thereof*. Comp. בוחן tower (32:14). More correctly, the suffix in בחוניו refers to the people of the Chaldæans: when they, viz., the Chaldæans, set up their towers of siege. עוררו *They raised up*. It is a transitive verb. *The palaces thereof*. It was as if the towers stirred up the palaces, but before they awoke, *he brought her to ruin*, that is, the Chaldæan brought Assyria to ruin.

ויש שואלים והלא התורה אסרה אתנן זונה (דברים כ"ג י"ט) ואיך אמר הנביא כי אתנן צור הזונה יהיה קודש, התשובה הכתוב בתורה הוא האמת וזה שאמר הנביא הוא על דרך משל ואיננה זונה כלל:


Some ask, How can the prophet promise that the hire of the harlot Tyre will be sanctified to the Lord, since the Law prohibits the hire of an harlot to be brought to the house of the Lord? (Deut. 23:19). The reply to this question is, that the Law prohibits the real hire of an harlot, but the prophet uses the words, her hire, in a figurative sense; in reality, he does not speak of an harlot at all.

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:2:1)


**והיה.** כל האדם יהיו שוים ברעה הזאת וכאשר יתחברו שנים כפי"ן היא דרך קצרה וכן הוא האדון כעבד והעבד כאדוניו:


*And it shall be*, etc. All men shall be alike in this catastrophe. כעם ככהן וגו׳. *As with the people, so with the priest*. etc. When two nouns with the prefix כ follow each other, the phrase is elliptical; the complete sentence would be: as with the people so with the priest, and as with the priest so with the people, as with the servant so with the master, and as with the master so with the servant, etc.

E., has not that kind and charitable feeling, which he has who lends without security (מלוה); the former is more liable to hurt the feelings of the poor in taking and giving back the pledge (comp. Dent. xiiv. 10, ff.). The word חנם used by I. E. is translated without security, because it is here the opposite of על משכונו on his security.

⁵ Literally, according to I. E., is confounded.

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:5:1)


**והארץ חנפה.** תורות, שקול הדעת שכל בני אדם משתוי' בו:


תורות *The laws*. The laws which are dictated by common sense, in which all agree.¹⁰¹⁰ are generally distinguished by saying that the former refers to those laws which society would make even without revelation; the latter, to such laws as would not be made without direct command in Scripture. This distinction is not applicable here, because the prophet speaks in this passage of laws that concern all nations. The explanation, however, given here by I. E., does not agree with his remark on Gen. 26:5, where תורה is explained to refer to the law of circumcision. What I. E. means by the laws contained in the natural order of things or by the covenant of the universe is more clearly stated in his commentary on Gen. 26:5, namely, שילך אדם אחרי מעשיו Man shall follow the ways of God displayed in his works. Comp. I. E. on Lev. 19:19.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:6:1

**על כן [אלה].** באלה, חסר בי"ת כמו כי ששת ימים (שמות כ' י"א), ויש אומרים כי תחסר מלת תחת, כמו ונשלמה פרים שפתינו (הושע ל"ד ג'):


באלה ═ אלה By a curse;¹² comp. בששת ═ ששת, in sin (Ex. 20:11); according to others, the preposition תחת, for, is to be supplied; comp. פ׳ שפ׳ ונ׳ תחת ═ ונשלמה פרים שפתינו. And let us bring our lips (that is, the words of our lips, our prayer) instead of bulls (Hos. 14:2).¹³

footnotes:
¹² From this remark it may be concluded that I. E. read אבלה mourneth instead of אכלה.
¹³ A. V., So will we render the calves of our lips.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:6:2)


**חרו.** כמו וחרה נחשתה (יחזקאל כ"ד י"א), כמו נשרפו:


חרו *They are burned*. Comp. וחרה, and may be burnt (Ez. xxiv. II).¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ A. V., And may burn.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:7:1)


**אבל תירוש אמללה גפן.** כי אין זומר ועודר:


*The new wine mourneth*, etc. Because there is none to dress the vine and to dig the ground.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:7:2)


**שמחי לב.** כי היין ישמח לב:


*The merry-hearted*. For wine maketh glad the heart (Ps. 104:15)



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:1)


**שבת משוש תופים.** מבית המשתה:


*The mirth of tabrets ceaseth*, from the feasts.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:8:2)


**שאון עליזים.** כאשר ישתכרו:


*The noise of them that rejoice*, when they are drunk.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:9:1)


**בשיר לא ישתו יין.** בניגון כי אם לצורך כי ימר השכר, ולפי דעתי שמלת ימר מפעלי הכפל כמו יקל [ותקל? בראשית ט"ו ה'] והוא מבנין נפעל:


*They shall not drink wine with a song*, for *the strong drink shall be bitter*. יֵמַר is according to my opinion¹⁵ a verb ע״ע—comp. וָאֵקַל And I was despised (Gen. 16:5)—Niphal of מרר

footnotes:
¹⁵ The grammarian, R. Jonah, is of opinion that יֵמַר is Kal; therefore I. E. adds, according to my opinion.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:10:1)


**נשברה [קרית תהו].** הטעם כל קריה שהולכים יושביה אחרי התוהו:


*The city of vanity*. The city whose inhabitants go after vain things.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:10:2)


**סוגר כל בית מבוא.** כי יצא כל אדם למסלות מרוב הצער:


*Every house is shut up, that no man can come in*. For every one will go out into the streets because of the great trouble.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:1)


**צוחה.** כמו צעקה:


צוחה A crying.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:2)


**על [היין].** מקום היין:


על מקום היין ═ על היין In the place of wine.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., For wine.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:3)


**בחוצות.** בפרהסיא:


*In the streets*. Publicly.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:11:4)


**ערבה.** מגזרת ערב (בראשית א' ה') כמו חשכה:


ערבה *Is darkened*. Comp. עֶרֶב evening.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:12:1)


**נשאר. ושאייה.** שם מגזרת שואה (ישעיהו י' ג'):


ושאיה *And with destruction*. שאיה is a noun derived from שאה to be waste;comp. שואה desolation (10:3).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:12:2)


והנביא אמר נשאר על דרך בן אדם להבין השומעים, וכן טוב משניהם (קהלת ד' ג'):


*In the city is left desolation*. This phrase is used by the prophet improperly; comp. Better is he than both they, who hath not yet been (Eccles. 4:3).¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ Strictly speaking, he who has not yet been born cannot be better; in the same way שַׁמָּה desolation cannot be said to be left; because desolation is the negation of existence. Comp. I. E. on 2:11.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:13:1)


**כי. כנוקף זית.** כנוער זית וקרוב מטעם ונקף סבבי היער (ישעיהו י' ל"ד):


בנקף *As the shaking*. נקף is similar in meaning to ונקף and he shall cut down (10:34).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:13:2)


**כעוללו'.** והטעם מעט, כי אם כלה בציר ישארו עוללו':


*As the gleaning grapes*, that is, only a few; for when the vintage is over, the gleaning grapes are left.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:1)


**המה וגו'.** כל המפרשים הסכימה דעתם כי מפרשת הנה יי בוקק הארץ הוא לעתיד על מלחמת גוג ומגוג, ולדעת רבי משה הכהן שידבר על מלך אשור, ומשתה שמנים (ישעיהו כ"ה ו') על מות מחנה סנחריב ועדיו הוי עטרת גאות (ישעיהו כ"ח א'):


*They shall lift up*, etc. All commentators agree that from the words, Behold, the Lord maketh, etc. (ver. 1), the prophet refers to the remote future, to the war of Gog and Magog;¹⁸ only R. Moses Hakkohen refers this prophecy to the king of Assyria, and finds in a feast of fat things (25:6) the indication of the destruction of the hosts of Sennacherib, which remains the subject of the prophecy until the words, Woe to the crown of pride, etc. (28:1).¹⁹—

footnotes:
¹⁸ Comp. Ez. xxxyiii. and xxxix. Gog is the name of the king of Magog, a country or nation in the north of Palestine (xxxyiii. 15), deriving their origin from Magog, the son of Japheth (Gen. 10:2).
¹⁹ The words of the Hebrew text are—ועדו הוי עטרת גאות And his proof is taken from the words, ‘Woe to the crown of pride,’ but the proof is not at all clear; for granted even that xxviii. refers to the period of the Assyrian invasion, it cannot be concluded that xxiv.—xxvii. refer to the same period, especially since the last verse of xxvii. seems to be the conclusion of a prophecy (comp. 11:15, 16; 19:23—25). The translation is based on the suggestion, that ועדו is a corruption of the original וְעַד or עַד unto.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:2)


**המה.** הנמלטים:


*They shall lift up*, etc., they that escaped, etc.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ The remnant of the army of Sennacherib, after the loss it sustained before Jerusalem. The opinion of R. Moses Hakkohen is continued in this remark.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:14:3)


**ירונו.** הרמת קול ומגזרת ותעבר הרנה (מלכים כ"ב ל"ו) .**מים.** ההולכים בים, וכן מלת צהלו והעד צהלת הסוס:


ירנו *They shall shout*.²¹ Comp. הרנה the proclamation (1 Kgs. 22:36). *They shall cry aloud from the sea*. They that go on the sea, shall cry, etc. צהלו *They shall cry aloud*. Comp. צהלת הסום the neighing of the horse.²²

footnotes:
²¹ A. V., They shall sing. According to I. E., or rather to R. Moses Hakkohen, ידנו and צהלו refer to the cries of anxiety and distress which the remnant of the Assyrian army lifted up. רנן and צהל do not always signify, to sing, as proved by the quoted הָרִנָּה the proclamation after a defeat, and צהלת the neighing of horses.
²² Instead of צהלת הסוס, which is not a biblical phrase, we have perhaps to read מצהלות אביריו the neighing of his strong ones (Jer. 8:16).



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:1)


**על. באורים.** יש אומרת גבולות וכמוהו מאור כשדים (בראשית י"א ל"א), ויש אומר בבקעים, והראשון הוא הנכון:


באורים Some explain it, In the countries; comp. כשרים אור the land of the Chaldæans²³ (Gen. 11:31); others: In valleys. The former explanation is the right one.

footnotes:
²³ The same phrase is also quoted in favour of the second explanation. See Rashi.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:15:2)


**באיי הים.** כבדו את יי כי כבדו מושך אחר [עמו]:


שם *The name*. Supply כבדו glorify; for the verb כבדו in the first half of the sentence refers also to the second. They (ver. 14) can also be explained to refer to the righteous.²⁴

footnotes:
²⁴ With this remark I. E. reverts to the first mentioned opinion, that these chapters (xxiv.—xxvii.) refer to the period of Gog and Magog. According to this opinion the prophet speaks in ver. 14, of the righteous people, that will then receive the reward for their faith in God; ידנו and צהלו retain according to this explanation their usual meaning, they sing. In the following part the commentary is based on this same supposition, while that of R. Moses Hakkohen is only incidentally mentioned, as if to show that it can really be maintained throughout the whole portion from xxiv. unto xxvii.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:1)


**מכנף.** יתכן היות טעם המה הצדיקים ובעבור שהארץ היא עגולה אמר מכנף הארץ, והטעם ממקום רחוק:


מכנף *From the uttermost part*. The word כנף corner, is used here to signify a great distance, because the earth is round.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁵ One is rather inclined to think that, because the earth is round, the expression כנף הארץ the comer of the earth should not be used. Perhaps he means to say, that the corner of the earth is used instead of far off, because we can never reach it.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:2)


**צבי.** פאר או מתרגום ארמית, ומלת ואומר דברי כל גוי, וכן שמענו:


צבי *Glory*. The word is derived from a Chaldaic root.²⁶ *And I said*. Each nation will say so. *Have we heard*, etc. The same.

footnotes:
²⁶ צבה to desire; from this I. E. derives צבי desirable, beauty, glory.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:3)


**רזי.** מגזרת וישלח רזון בנפשם (תהלים ק"ו ט"ו) וטעם פעמים בכל רגע:


רז׳ *Leanness*. Comp. רזון leanness (Ps. 106:15). The repetition indicates that these words are said every moment.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:16:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:16:4)


**בוגדים בגדו.** כי כל אדם בוגדים בגד אחר בגד:


בגדים בגדו וגו׳ *Treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously*, etc. For all people deal treacherously again and again.²⁷

footnotes:
²⁷ The root בגד is here repeated five times; this, according to I. E., indicates the repetition of the same action by the same person, as well as its contagious spreading amongst all classes of people.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:17:1)


**פחד וגו'.** ובעבור זה בא הרע לכל עם והנה כאשר תפחד הנפש, והפחת שהיא כמו בור קרובה, ונלכדה רגלו בפח, מיד יפול:


*Fear and the pit*, etc. And therefore the evil is come to all people; for when any person is in fear, and a kind of pit is near him, and his foot is besides caught in a snare, he must instantly fall.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:18:1)


**והיה. כי ארובות.** כמו חלונות, והטעם גזרות שמים:


*Windows from on high*, etc. A figure for decrees of the Lord.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:19:1)


**רעה.** מגזרת תרועם (תהלים ב' ט') וזאת הלשון ידועה בארמית:


רעה *Is broken*. Comp. תרועם thou wilt break them (Ps. 2:9); a word found frequently in the Targum.²⁸

footnotes:
²⁸ רעע in Chaldee is the same as רצץ in Hebrew.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:19:2)


**פור התפוררה.** כטעם שבר כמו שלו הייתי ויפרפרני (איוב י"ד י"ב) וככה אתה פוררת בעזך ים (תהלים ע"ד י"ג):


פור התפוררה *Is broken asunder*. Comp. ויפרפרני and he hath broken me asunder (Job 16:12); פוררת thou hast divided (Ps. 74:13)



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:1)


**נוע.** הטעם על יושבי הארץ שינוסו ממקום למקום, ויתנודדו כמלונה כי השומר יחליף מקום מלונו:


*The earth shall reel*, etc. The inhabitants of the land will flee from one place to the other, and be moved like the cottage of the watchman; for the watchman changes the place of his abode.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:2)


וטעם **וכבד.** כי יבקשו להתנועע ולברוח ויכבד פשעם עליהם, ויפלו:


*And shall be heavy*, etc. When they will be about to move and to flee, their transgression will be too heavy for them, and they will fall.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:20:3)


**קום.** שם הפעל, וככה ומלך אלקום עמו (משלי ל' ל"א):


קום *To rise*. It is infinitive; comp. אלקום no rising up (Prov. 30:31 ).²⁹

footnotes:
²⁹ It is rather curious to find I. E. referring to אלקום as another instance of the infinitive קום, and not to Ps. 18:39, 36:13, 127:2; Lam. 1:14; Am. 5:2.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:21:1)


**והיה וגו'.** יש רבים שפירשו זה על קדרות המאורות, והנכון שהם שמלאכים שהם עומדים לעזור לגוי ולהיות לגוי אחר לשטנם, וזה מבואר בספר דניאל (דניאל י' י"ג וכ'). על כן אמר ועל מלכי האדמה באדמה, כי מלכות המלכים דבקה עם מלכות המלאכים:


Many refer this prediction to an eclipse of the sun and moon; but more correctly it is referred to the angels, that are ready to assist or to attack a nation. Comp. Dan. 10:13, 20. These words are therefore followed by: the kings of the earth on the earth; for the reign of the kings is in connexion with the reign of the angels.³⁰

footnotes:
³⁰ Those unknown causes that govern the destinies of men and nations are sometimes personified, and represented as the messengers or angels of the Lord. Each nation is therefore said to have its angel above, in whose hand its destiny is placed, and the prosperity or the misfortune of a nation is made dependent on the success or failure of its representative angel above.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:22:1)


**ואספו אספה [אסיר].** כאסיר, כאשר יובא המון האסירים אל בור לסגור עליהם ויעזבום ימים רבים, וכן 'יפקדו' לתת להם מחיה, והטעם כי תמשך זאת הרעה, ויתכן היותו כמו ומימים רבים תפקד (יחזקאל ל"ח ח'), וזאת הפקידה לרעה:


באסיר ═ אסיר As a prisoner. *As prisoners are gathered, etc*. As people who are brought to the prison to be shut in are often left there for a long time before they are visited to be supplied with their food. The idea contained in this simile is, that this evil will last a long time. יפקדו they shall be visited, may also be compared with ומימים רבים תפקד and after many years thou wilt be visited (Ez. 38:8), and explained in an evil sense.³¹

footnotes:
³¹ According to the first explanation, יפקדו means they will be visited to receive their food; according to the second, they will be visited to receive their final punishment.



### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 24:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/24:23:1)


**וחפרה.** טעם הלבנה והשמש כי הם מושלים, והנה מלכי אדמה יבושו גם תקדר השמש והלבנה, אז תראה מלכות השם בהר ציון, אז יהיה כבוד לדבקים בשם, ויש אומרים כי הטעם על עובדי המאורות ואיננו דבק בטעמי הפרשה:


*Then the moon*, etc. Sun and moon, the rulers of heaven, are used here in a figurative sense for the kings of the earth, who will be ashamed; but it is also possible that an eclipse of sun and moon is meant by the prophet. The kingdom of God will then appear on the mount of Zion, and honour will be given to those that remain faithful to God. According to others this passage refers to the worshippers of the heavenly bodies; but this explanation is at variance with the context.

**יצר וגו'.** מי שיצרו סמוך עליך, אתה השם תצרנו בשלום, ויש אומרים שיתכן להיות מלת שלום זכר גם לשון נקבה:


יצר סמוך תצר שלום Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on thee. Others are of opinion that שלום may be used as masculine and feminine.⁴

**כי השח.** מפעלי הכפל כמו הקל ארצה זבולון (ישעיהו ח' כ"ג) והטעם על מדינות הגוים:


השח *He bringeth down*. A verb ע״ע like הֵקַל he afflicted slightly (8:23). *Them that dwell on high*, etc. This refers to the heathens.

ישפילנה ישפילה *He layeth it low*, *he layeth it low*. He will continually lay it low; comp. עזי ומעזי My strength and my fortress (Jer. 16:19).⁶

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:8:1

**אף וגו'.** אלה דברי צדיקים שיקוו השם להראות משפטו בעולם כי הנפש מתאוה לשמך, ויחסר אות למ"ד כאילו אמר לאורח משפטיך:


*We waited for thee, O Lord, even for the way of Thy judgment*,⁷ etc. These are the words of the righteous that hope in the Lord, that He will show His judgment in the universe; for the soul is longing for Thy name. Before ארח path supply the preposition ל for.

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:1)


**נפשי.** רעיון נפשי, שאויתיך בלילה:


נפשי *My soul*, that is, the thought of my soul,⁸ was בלילה אויתיך *I have desired Thee in the night;*

footnotes:
⁸ A. V., With my soul, with my spirit. אויתיך I desired thee, and אשחרך Will I seek thee early, are, according to I. E., the thoughts which fill the soul and spirit of the righteous, and are, therefore, by a kind of metonymy, called their soul and spirit.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:2)


**אף רוחי בקרבי אשחרך.** והנה יש לאדם נפש ורוח כאשר פירשתי בקהלת (קהלת ג' כ"א):


Yea the thought of my spirit *within me*, was אשחרך *I will seek Thee early*. Man has נפש soul and רוח spirit, as I explained in Koheleth.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ In his commentary on Koheleth 3:21, I. E. says that נפש is common to all living creatures, but נשמה is peculiar to human beings alone;—the difference between רוח and נפש is not explained there. On Koheleth 7:3, he remarks that the life of man manifests itself in his vegetable, animal and intellectual nature, or as explained there by I. E. himself, in his appetitive, נפש, sensitive, רוח, and deliberative capacities נשמה.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:3)


**כי כאשר.** יראו משפטיך לארץ ילמדו צדק:


*When Thy judgments are*, etc. When Thy judgments appear on the earth the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:9:4)


**יושבי תבל.** שם מקום היישוב:


תבל *World*. The inhabited part of the earth.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:1)


**יחן.** מפעלי הכפל כמו על כמון יוסב (ישעיהו כ"ח כ"ד), והנה הטעם כי השם יחן על הרשע והוא לא ילמד צדק, והטעם שיאריך לו אולי ילמוד:


יחן *Let favour be shewn*. A verb ע״ע; it is a form like יוסב is turned (28:27).¹⁰—God is merciful to the wicked, but they will not learn righteousness; He has patience with them for a long time, they might perhaps improve.

footnotes:
¹⁰ יחַֻן is future Hophal of יוסב ; חנן future Hophal of סבב.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:2)


**בארץ נכוחות.** במקום שיש שם יושר, יעשו עולה:


*In the land of uprightness*. In the place where the people are upright, they (the wicked) will do wrong.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:10:3)


**נכוחות.** מגזרת נכח כמו טובים ונכוחים (שמואל ב' ט"ו ג'), ולא ישים לב לראות גאות השם:


נבחות *Straightforwardness*. It is related to נכח before (Ex. 26:35); comp. נכחים right (2 Sam. 15:3). *And will not behold*, etc. He does not wish to consider the greatness of God.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:11:1)


**יי וגו'.** הטעם אחר שידך רמה והם לא יחזיון, יחזו שיקנאו לעמך, ויבושו, ותאכל האש צריך, ויש אומר יחזו קנאתך בכלם, והוא דבק בטעם 'אף אש צריך':


רמה ידך בל יחזיון *When Thy hand is lifted up*¹¹ *they will not see*. יחזו ויבשו קנאת עם *But they shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people*; let them show their envy of Thy people, and be ashamed, אף אש צריך תאכלם *And let the fire devour Thine enemies*. Some explain the former phrase thus: Let them see Thy punishment inflicted upon all of them. According to this explanation, the phrase has the same meaning as the words אף אש צריך תאכלם yea, even the fire, which shall devour thine enemies.¹²

footnotes:
¹¹ רמה Is lifted up, that is, does not touch them or does not punish them.
¹² A. V., They shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people; yea the fire of Thine enemies shall devour them.—The Hebrew text has  קנאתך בבלם יחזו, which is perhaps to be altered into יחזו קנאתך בכל עם, since the difference between the two explanations is, that according to the first, עם refers to Israel, according to the second, to all other nations, so that קנאת עם is either the envy of the heathen people at Israel, or the punishment inflicted upon all people, that are enemies to Israel or to God.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:12:1

**יי. תשפות.** תערוך, כמו שפות הסיר שפות (יחזקאל כ"ד ג'):


תשפות *Thou wilt ordain*. Comp. שפות set on (Ez. 24:3).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:12:2)


**כי וגו'.** תמיד אתה עשית לנו מה שלא נדע אנחנו לעשותו:


*For thou also hast wrought*, etc. For Thou hast always done for us what we do not know how to do.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:13:1)


**יי וגו'.** כי גם אנחנו עבדנוך כאשר בעלונו, היו אדונינו, כמו כסף ישיב לבעליו (שמות כ"א ל"ד), ואעפ"כ היינו מזכירים שמך, וטעם לבד בך כי אתה עזרתנו, כאילו אמר אין עזר כי אם בך, על כן יש לנו להזכירך:


*Other lords*, *besides Thee*, *have had dominion*, etc. For we worshipped Thee even when others became our masters. בעלונו *Had dominion over us*, were our masters (בעלים); comp. לבעליו unto the owner of them (Ex. 21:34). *But by Thee only we make mention of Thy name*. Nevertheless we praised Thy name. לבד בך *But by Thee*. Thou hast helped us, therefore we were able to praise Thee.

### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:16:2)


**צקון לחש.** הנו"ן נוסף כנו"ן אשר לא ידעון (דברים ח' ג'), והיא מלה זרה, והיתה ראויה להיותה יצקו, לכן באה חסרת פ"א הפעל כמו והיום רד מאד (שופטים י"ט י"א), והטעם כמו ולפני יי ישפך שיחו (תהלים ק"ב א'):


צקון *They poured out*. The נ is paragogic, as in ידעון they knew (Deut. 8:3); the word is besides irregular; the regular form is יצקו; the first radical is dropped in צקון; comp. ירד═רד he went down (Judg. 19:11). As to the phrase they poured out a prayer, comp. he will pour out his prayer (Ps. 102:1).

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:1)


**הרינו חלנו.** רוח, וכן ילדנו, והטעם כי לא היה בנו כח להנצל, וזה הוא ישועות [בל נעשה], לא נוכל לעשות:


*We have conceived*, *we have been in pain with*, *as we have brought forth*, *wind*.¹⁶ We have conceived, and we have been in pain with wind, and so we have also brought forth wind. We had no strength to deliver ourselves; this is the meaning of the following ישועות בל נעשה we have not wrought any deliverance. We were not able to bring any deliverance.

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., We have been with child, we have been in pain, we have, as it were (כְמוֹ) brought forth wind. According to I. E. the word כמו compares the verbs הָרִינוּ we have conceived and הַלְנוּ we have been in pain, with the verb יָלַדְנוּ רוּחַ we have brought forth, with regard to the object רוּחַ wind, which is common to all of them.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:2)


**ארץ.** בארץ, חסר בית כמו כי ששת ימים (שמות כ' י"א):


ארץ *In the earth*. Supply ב; comp. בששת═ששת (Ex. 20:11).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:18:3)


**ובל יפלו.** יש אומרים שהוא חסר אל"ף, אומרו [צ"ל כמו] ויפלו מאד בעיניהם (נחמיה ו' ט"ז), ואין ויפלו שם כי אם כמשמעו, כאשר אפרש, ולפי דעתי שלא נוכל שלא יפלו:


ובל יפלו Some say, that א is omitted, as in ויפלו (Neh. 6:16); but the latter has its usual meaning (and they fell), as will be explained by me. I explain בל יפלו we could not help their falling.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ According to I. E. the root of יפלו is נפל to fall. ובל יפלו ישבי תבל We could not effect that the inhabitants of the world should not fall; that is, we could not prevent the destruction which threatened to come over a great many of the inhabitants of the world.—A. V., Neither have the inhabitants of the earth fallen.—The passage quoted from Nehemiah ויפלו מאוד בעיניהם is explained by I. E. בשפלים ונפלים ממעלתם they appeared to themselves low and degraded.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/26:19:1)


**יחיו וגו'.** רק מתיך, הכף לנוכח השם, הם יחיו, ולפי דעת הכל שזה רמז לתחיית המתים, ויש אומרים שהוא הפך מתים בל יחיו, כי הנה אדונינו מתו ואנחנו שהיינו חשובים כמתים היינו חיים:


*Thy dead men shall live*. Only Thy dead men shall live; God is addressed. Generally, it is believed, that this phrase contains some reference to the resurrection of the dead.¹⁸ Some explain it as a contrast to They are dead, they will not live, (ver. 14), they, that is, our masters, are dead, but we, who were considered as dead, are living.

¹⁸ Comp. Targum: Thou wilt revive the dead.

**נבלתי.** היו"ד סימן הנביא כי הוא מישראל, וכן הוא, יחיו מתיך ומתי נבלתי יקומון, כאילו קול ישמעו לאמר הקיצו:


*My dead body*. The first person refers to the prophet, who is one of the Israelites, that are considered as dead. Let Thy dead men live, and let the dead of my people rise, as if they heard the cry: Awake, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 26:19:3

**כי טל אורות**, טל עם אורה, הוא טלך, והכ"ף לנוכח השם, ויש אומרים כי אורות צמחים כמו ללקט אורות (מלכים ב' ד' ל"ט), והם צמחים יסבו כנגד השמש והירח:


טל אורות *A dew of light*.¹⁹ A dew acccompanied by light. *Thy dew*. God is addressed in these words. According to others, אורות means herbs; comp. 2 Kings 4:39; it signifies a kind of herb, which turns toward the sun and moon.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ A. V., The dew of herbs.
²⁰ Comp. Plin. Nat. Hist. Lib. XVIII., cap. 36 (Lupinus) cum sole quotidie circumagitur, horasque agricolis etiam nubilo demonstrat. The lupine makes its daily circuit with the sun, and shows the farmer the time even when the heaven is covered with clouds.

**וארץ.** נפתח הוי"ו להורות על ה"א הדעת הנעדר, והארץ תפיל הרפאים ממנה כנפל אשת, ויש אומרים אתה לבדך החיית מתיך, כי תולדת הארץ להפיל המתים בתוכה:


וְהָאָרֶץ ═ וָאָרֶץ. And the earth *Shall cast out the dead*, out of itself. תפיל Shall cast out, shall bear; comp. כנפל אשח As the untimely birth of a woman (Psalm 58:9). Others explain, Thou alone hast given life to Thy dead; for it is the nature of the earth to throw the dead into its midst.²¹

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 27:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:1:3)


**לויתן.**הוא התלי ונקרא בריח בעבור שהוא מבריח מן הקצה אל הקצה:


*Leviathan*. The Theli ; (תלי)² it has the epithet בריח stretching,³ because it stretches from one end to the other. [I think it is a sea monster].⁴

footnotes:
² תלי is the imaginary axis or line through the centre of the earth, and the two points in which the ecliptic and the equator, or the ecliptic and the orbit of the moon meet. The latter is probably meant here. The origin of the word has not yet been fully established. It is generally believed to be the same as in Arabic تالي but the two words, being quite different in meaning, תלי) hanging, تالي following,) are probably not connected with each other. Moreover, if תלי were the same as تالي it would have been written תאלי. It seems more probable and natural to derive תלי from תלה to hang, since it denotes the ends from which the earth is, as it were, suspended. (Comp. תלאי Talm. Bab. Shab. 78; and תולה ארץ על כלימה He hangeth the earth upon nothing (Job 26:7). This axis, being a straight line, is called בריח a bar, which passes in a straight line from one end to the other; but at the same time the attribute עקלתון crooked, is given to it, because the intersections of the ecliptic and the orbit of the moon are not constant, and the three points above-mentioned are therefore not exactly in a straight line. It is likewise connected with the name of תנין dragon; the one end of the line being called the head, the other the tail of the dragon. These names owe their origin probably to the serpentine winding of the orbit of the moon round the ecliptic. R. Jehuda Hallevi compares the axis of the ecliptic with a king, who sitteth on his throne and thence governs the whole country (Cusari 4:25). A similar idea presented itself to the mind of the commentator, who explained נחש בריח by תלי, and signified by this figure the king of Assyria or of Egypt.
³ A. V., Piercing.
⁴ The words in brackets are added, firstly because from the remark of I. E. on Job 26:13, it appears that he explained נחש בריח to be a sea monster; secondly, because it is evident from his remark on נחש עקלתון that a remark to that effect must have preceded.

**ועל לויתן.** גם הוא בים, והוא צורת נחש, כי גם צורת נחש בים, ועקלתון שם התאר:


*Even Leviathan*, *that crooked serpent*. This is likewise an animal that lives in the sea; it is like a serpent, for there are also serpent-like animals in the sea.⁵ עקלתון *Crooked*. It is an adjective.

footnotes:
⁵ The sea-monsters are usually called תנינים; this remark is therefore added, that they are also called נחשים, some of them being serpent-like.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 27:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:5:4)


ולפי דעתי כי **חמה אין לי** איננו דברי השם, ואל תתמה כי בספר הזה רבים כאלה, והנה עד קרוב הרינו חלנו, יחיו מתיך (ישעיהו כ"ו י"ח), ואלה דברי איש יהודה, אחר שהשם אמר אני יי נוצרה לרגעים, פן יפקד עליה אמרו אין אנחנו מדברים בחמה, שאם יבוא האויב לשום הכרם שמיר ושית, הייתי הורג את עצמי, כמו והיה יחזקאל לכם (יחזקאל כ"ד כ"ד) ואת שמואל (שמואל א' י"ב י"א) כאשר עשה ביום הזה (ויקרא ח' ל"ד), והנה במלחמה דבר עם מי יתנני, או יחזק השם שיתן לי עוז ברית, שיהיה השם בשלום עמי, גם האויב, אז ישרש יעקב, והוצרכתי לפירוש הזה בעבור מלת יעשה שלום לי, כי השם עושה שלום לבדו:


I think that God is not represented as speaking in these two verses, as is the case in many passages of this book—we need only refer to the preceding chapter, verses 18 and 19¹⁵—but the men of Judah,¹⁶ after having heard God’s promise, I the Lord will keep it, lest he visit it, are introduced, saying, We do not declare with fury, that if the enemy should come to turn the vineyard into a place of briers and thorns, we should kill ourselves. Comp.¹⁷ And Ezekiel shall be, instead of And I shall be (Ez. 25:24), And Samuel, instead of And myself (1 Sam. 12:11); As he hath done, instead of As I have done (Lev. 8:34); במלחמה in war, is to be joined with מי יתנני who would turn me in this way: If one should come to turn me by war into a place of briers and thorns, etc. או יחזק *Or if He would strengthen my stronghold*, etc., to give me the strengthening promise that He will be in peace with me, and so should the enemy be, then Jacob would take root, etc. I am compelled to explain in this way by the phrase, He will make peace unto me, because it is God alone that maketh peace.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁵ The peculiarity hinted at in this remark seems to consist in the introduction of the dialogue form; ver. 3 is assigned to God, ver. 4 and 5 to Israel, ver. 6 again to God; similarly 26:18—19 is assigned to the people, ver. 20 again to the Lord.
¹⁶ The expression איש יהודה the men of Judah, is perhaps used by I. E. instead of Israel, because the second part of this chapter (comp. ver. 7), refers, according to his interpretation, to the kingdom of Israel.
¹⁷ The passages which follow are instances of the use of the third person instead of the first, as is the case here; through it ═ through myself.
¹⁸ I. E. is not the author of the first opinion, which attributes to God the words, He will make peace unto me, since, as he says, he is compelled to assume, that they are to be assigned to the men of Judah. It is often the case in the commentaries of I. E., that an anonymous opinion, which is supposed to be generally adopted, is followed by the commentator’s own explanation, introduced by a phrase like ואני אומר ,ולפי דעתי but I think, but I say. In this verse the first explanation is perhaps to be assigned to those whose opinion is introduced at the beginning of verse 4, with the words, some say.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 27:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/27:8:3)


**בשלחה.** יש אומר כי היא השחיתה עצמה בכלי מלחמתה, כמו ובעד השלח יפלו (יואל ב' ח') והנכון שהוא מגזרת שלחיך (שיר השירים ד' י"ג) והעד ביום קדים, והנה הוא כן, במדה שמדדה לנפשה, כי מריבה עשתה אפילו עם אנשי כפריה, והם שלחה, על כן הגה השם אותה, כמו אשד הוגה מן המסילה (שמואל ב' כ' י"ג), והנה הה"א תחת יו"ד השורש כמו ידה הדה (ישעיהו י"א ח'):


בשלחה According to some: with its sword.²⁵ The meaning of the sentence accordingly is: Samaria destroyed itself with its own instruments of war. Comp. השלח the sword (Joel 2:8). More correctly, however, it may be compared with שלחיך thy plants (Song 4:13), especially because of the words: on the day of the east wind.²⁶ Samaria was punished with her own measure, she had quarrelled even with the people of her own villages,—which may be considered as her plants (שלחה)—therefore. הגה *the Lord removed*²⁷ *her;* comp. ²⁸הוגה he was removed (2 Sam. 20:13); ה replaces the radical י; as in ידה═הדה he stretched forth (11:8).

footnotes:
²⁵ A. V., When it shooteth forth.
²⁶ The figure the day of the east wind, leads the reader to suppose that there is also a reference to plants, which are damaged by the east wind.
²⁷ A. V., Stayeth.—Being in continual conflict with her neighbours, Samaria was taken away from amongst them.
²⁸ Hophal of יגה.

**שער קטב.** [הכ"ף הראשון] מושך אחר, וכן הוא כשער:


שער קטב. The כ in כזרם refers also to שער: As a destroying wind.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:3)


**קטב.** כמו אהי קטבך שאול (הושע י"ג י"ד):


קטב Destruction. Comp. קטבך thy destruction (Hos. 13:14).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:2:4)


**הניח לארץ [ביד].** הטעם כי השם הוריד אלה הזרמים, והניחם לארץ בידו החזקה:


הניח לארץ *He cast down to the earth*. God sent those storms and caused them to visit the earth. ביד *With the hand*. With His mighty hand.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:3:1)


**ברגלים. עטרת.** באה מלת יחיד, והטעם רבות, וכמוהו רבים:


עטרת *Crown*. Singular form but plural sense; there are many instances of this usage.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:4:1)


**והיתה ציצת נובל.** כאילו אמר זה הציץ שיהיה נובל, כמו בת בבל השדודה (תהלים קל"ז ח'), או ציצת עלה נובל, והוא הנכון:


ציצת נובל The blooming of the blossom which will fade away,⁴—comp. בת בבל השדודה O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed (Psa. 137:8)—or the blossom of the fading plant, and this is better.

footnotes:
⁴ A. V., A fading flower.—I. E. supplies ציץ blossom, or עלה leaf, plant, because of the incongruity of the feminine ציצת and the masculine נובל. There is besides, according to his opinion, a contradiction between a fading flower, and the glorious beauty, which he believes to be in apposition to the former; he explains therefore נובל to have the meaning of a participle future that will fade away, and for a similar reason, השדודה (Ps. 137:8): that will be destroyed. The latter expression is explained by him differently in his commentary on the Psalms (ad locum).

**כבכורה.** היא התאנ' הבכורה בטרם בא פרי הקיץ:


כבכורה *As the hasty fruit.* As the fig that ripens before any of the summer fruit comes.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:5:1)


**ביום וגו'.** והנה זה הפך צבי עטרת אפרים, כי תראה מלכות השם בציון:


*In that day*, etc. This will be just the reverse of the fate of the crown of Ephraim; for the kingdom of the Lord will appear in Zion.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:1)


**ולרוח. ליושב על המשפט.** הם הסנהדרין, והטעם שיחזיקם:


*To him that sitteth in judgment.* To the judges. God will strengthen them. אל השער ═ שערה.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:6:2)


**משיבי מלחמה [שערה].** אל השער. יש אומרים משיביה מהשער, ורבי משה הכהן אמר כי השם יחזק הבורחים, והוא הנכון:


*To the gate*. שערה משיבי מלחמה. Some explain: who turn the battle away from the gates. R. Moses Hakkohen renders the passage thus: (God will give strength to those) who have escaped,⁵ and this is the right explanation.

footnotes:
⁵ According to the first explanation השערה (lit. to the gate) is very strangely the same as מן השער (lit., from the gate). The literal translation of the phrase according to the other opinion is: those who turn the battle to the gate, that is, those who come back in their flight to the gate to defend the town against the besieging army.

*The priest*, whose duty it is to teach; *the prophets*, whose duty it is to exhort the people.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:7:4

**פקו פליליה.** השופטים, והנה פקו פועל יוצא, או תחסר מלת דברי, והוא הנכון, והנו פועל עומד מגזרת ופיק ברכים (נחום ב' י"א), כטעם הנתק הברכים:


פקו פליליה, they pervert judgment; by the subject they the judges are meant, and the verb פקו has a transitive meaning; or the words of the judgment are unstable,⁷ דברי the words of being supplied. I prefer this latter explanation; for פקו is intr.; comp. ופיק ברכים, and the tottering of the knees. (Nahum 2:11.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:8:2)


**בלי מקום.** שאיננו מלא כמו עד אפס מקום (ישעיהו ה' ח'), וכן מלאו קיא ומלאו צואה, והנה ממעל ומתחת:


בלי מקום *So that there is no place*, which is not full, etc.; comp. עד אפס מקום until there be no place, (5:8). קיא צואה Asyndeta. They are covered with filthiness from the top to the bottom.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:9:1

שמועה *Doctrine*. A noun.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:9:3

⁸ I. E. means to say that the plural in the absolute state has sometimes the ending ־ֵי; but he is not of opinion that the two forms of the noun for the absolute and construct state are used promiscuously. Comp. I. E. on 15:1, and ibid.

בלעני שפה *With laughing*¹² *lips.* Comp. לענ derision (Ps. lxxix., 4). The teacher speaks to the child in a laughing and mocking way.

*And with another tongue.* The teacher usually tries to substitute letters which are easy to pronounce for the more difficult ones; in the same manner the prophet must speak, when he rebukes this people.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:12:3

המרנעה *The refreshing.* Comp. מרגוע rest (Job 6:16); both words are substantives. According to the grammarian of Jerusalem¹³ מרגעה is a participle.¹⁴

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:13:1)


**והיה.** והנה חשבו כי דבר השם איננו עקר, רק כאב ביד להרגילם למען לא ילכו אל מצרים כאשר כתוב הוי היורדים מצרים לעזרה (ישעיהו ל"א א') כי הפרשה אחת היא:


*But the word of the Lord was unto them*, etc. They indeed thought that the word of God itself was of no importance; it was only a school-exercise to them.¹⁵ *That they might go*¹⁶ to Egypt. Comp. Woe to those that go down to Egypt, etc. (31:1), a portion of this same prophecy.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁵ The word of God is compared with the lessons in reading and writing given to children. The meaning of the words are in that case immaterial. In the same way the people thought that the divine prophecies were only exercises of style and composition, either for the prophets in delivering, or for the public in hearing, them.
¹⁶ לא in למען לא ילכו of the Hebrew text is superfluous; the following quotation: Woe unto, etc., proves that the words to Egypt, contain the explanation of I. E., not the comment of the people on the words of the prophet.
¹⁷ From c. xxiv. to c. xxxv. is, according to R. Moses Hakkohen, whom I. E. seems to follow, one continuous prophecy concerning the Assyrian invasion and the destruction of the army of Sennacherib.

### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:1)


**כי כרתנו ברית.** עם מות שלא נמות עתה:


*We have made a covenant with death*. We shall not die now.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 28:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/28:15:2)


**ועם שאול עשינו חוזה.** כמו ברית, ויאמר רבי משה הכהן כמו חזו' דרך נבואה, ומה יעשה במלת עשינו חוזה, ולפי דעתי שחוזה הוא הנביא וכן הוא ברית את מות ועם שאול עשינו ברית חוזה, כברית שתעשה על ידי נבואה:


חזה *An agreement*. R. Moses Hakkohen says that חזות (ver. 18) signifies a kind of prophecy; but how can he apply this explanation to the phrase ¹⁸?עשינו חזה I think that חזה means prophet, and explain עשינו חזה to be the same as עשינו ברית חזה We have made a prophet’s covenant, a covenant like that made by divine inspiration.

footnotes:
¹⁸ I. E. says that, although חזות in the phrase וחזותכם את שאול לא תקום (ver. 18) might be explained to signify prophecy, and the whole sentence to mean: And what you prophesied concerning the grave will not be fulfilled, it is impossible to find that sense in the phrase ועם שאול עשינו חוזה, which has evidently the same meaning; חזות and חוזה are therefore explained by the assumption of an ellipsis, to be the same as ברית חזות and ברית חוזה, a covenant of a prophecy and a covenant of a prophet; that is, a covenant like that made by divine inspiration.
