### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:1)


**החשתי וגו'.** אלה דברי השם:


*I have long time,* etc. The first person refers to God.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:2)


**החשתי.** כמו החרשתי, וכן גם אני ידעתי החשו (מלכים ב' ב' ג'):


החשתי *I have holden my peace.* Comp. החשו hold ye your peace (2 Kings 2:3).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:3)


**אתאפק.** כמו להתאפק (בראשית מ"ה א'):


אתאפק *I refrained myself.* Comp. להתאפק refrain himself (Gen. 45:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:4)


**כיולדה אפעה.** אצעק, ואין רע לו, ויש אומרים שהוא כן, כיולדה שהיא יולדת פעה, כן אשום ואשאף, מגזרת אפעה שרף מעופף (ישעיהו ל' ו'):


אפעה *Will I cry.* Hap. leg. According to some it means viper, and כיולדה אפעה וגוי is explained by them as follows : like one that beareth a viper, so shall I be desolate and sighing at once.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:5)


**אשם.** מבנין נפעל מפעלי הכפל:


אשם *I shall be desolate.*²³ It is Niphal of a verb ע׳׳ע (שמם).

footnotes:
²³ A. V., I will destroy.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:14:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:14:6)


**אשאף יחד.** כטעם שואף זורח (קהלת א' ה'), והנה היא שממה בלב עם שאוף בפה, וזה הטעם הוא כנגד שיהיו אנשי העולם חושבים כי אין לו כח להושיע עמו:


אשאף *I shall sigh.*²⁴ Comp. שואף sighing (Eccles. 1:5). אשם Refers to the feeling of the heart, אשאף to the utterance of the mouth. This verse is addressed to those who will assert, that God is unable to help His people.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁴ A. V., I will devour.—According to I. E. the verb שאף signifies the ardent longing shown by frequent short breathing (comp. I. E. on Eccl. i., 5). The meaning of the phrase is accordingly, that God waits long before He punishes the enemies of Israel, but then he shows, as it were, eagerness to help His chosen people.
²⁵ According to R. Moses Hakkohen, from the Babylonian exile; according to I. E. from the present exile. That I. E. had the latter more in view, he indicated by the use of the future שיהיו חושבים they will be believing.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:15:1)


**אחריב.** ואיך יחשבו זה, והלא יראו שאחרי' הרים וגבעות, וכל העשב אוביש, ואעשה מהנהרות איים, שירדו שם בני אדם:


*I will make waste,* etc. How can they think²⁶ thus? Do they not see, that I lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs, and make rivers into islands, that people can dwell therein.

footnotes:
²⁶ The form חשבו is to be emended into the future יחשבו ; as may be inferred from the succeeding future והלא יראו.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:16:1)


**והולכתי וגו'.** ואני מוליך עורים בדרך לא ידעו, כי העור אם היה רגיל בדרך, ילך בה בלי אור, ואני אשי' המחשך כאילו הוא אור להם, ומעקשים למישור יש אומר כי זה רמז לשוב ישראל מבבל:


*And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not;* for ²⁷ even the blind, if accustomed to a path, go there without a guide. *I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight.* Some²⁸ refer this to the return of the Israelites from Babylon.

footnotes:
²⁷ The blind are supposed not to know any way; I. E. thinks it therefore necessary to point out that they sometimes know their way.
²⁸ The Hebrew text has ישוח, which is either a corruption of יש some, or a proper name. Comp. also c. xl. Note 1.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:17:1)


**נסוגו וגו'.** הטעם אני יש לי כח כאשר ארצה, ולא לפסילים:


*They shall be turned back,* etc., for I have the power to do as I like, not so the idols.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:17:2)


**[בפסל].** מושך אחר עמו וכן [הוא] לפסילי המסכה, בעבור מלת אתם:


מסכה *Molten images*.²⁹ The plural פסלי images must be supplied from the preceding phrase, because of the pronoun אַתֶּם ye which follows.

footnotes:
²⁹ The singular may be rendered by a plural form, and also be considered as a plural for the grammatical construction, if the context shows that the word is to be taken in a collective sense. The form of the fem. sing. is often the sign of a collective noun. I. E., however, prefers to explain the construction by the assumption of an ellipsis.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:18:1)


**החרשים וגו'.** השמיעה והמראה עקרה בלב, והנה אלה חרשי לב ועורי לב:


*Ye deaf* etc. Hearing and seeing originate in the heart; those that are deaf and blind in their hearts are, therefore, called here deaf and blind.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:1)


**מי וגו'.** זה הכתוב לעד על יושר פירושי:


*Who is blind,* etc. This verse proves the correctness of my explanation.³⁰

footnotes:
³⁰ As to the prophet’s being mocked by his audience, and the redemption of the Jews from Babylon being at the same time his deliverance from his own personal sufferings and troubles, see Introduction, and I. E. on c. xl. Note 1.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:2)


**החשתי וגו'.** והטעם אתם עורים כי תאמרו כי [אין] עור רק הנביא:


You are blind who say that none is so blind as the prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:3)


**כמלאכי אשלח.** הוא שליח השם, וכן כתיב ויאמר חגי מלאך יי [חגי א' י"ג:


כמלאכי *As my messenger.* Comp. חגי מלאך יי Haggai, the messenger of the Lord (Hag. 1:13).¹

footnotes:
¹ This quotation is to show that the prophet is sometimes called מלאך the angel of the Lord.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:19:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:4)


**מי עור כמשולם.** כמו וירא מצוה הוא ישולם (משלי י"ג י"ג) מגזרת שלם, וכן המשולם הוא הצדיק:


כמשלם *As he that is righteous.*³¹ Comp. ישולם is recompensed (Prov. 11:31) ; שַׁלֵּם to pay (Exod. 22:5); פשלם lit., he who is recompensed, that is, the righteous.

footnotes:
³¹ A. V., Prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:19:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:19:5)


**ועור כעבד יי.** שיעבד השם, ואם איננו נביא:


*As the servant of the Lord,* who, though not a prophet, serves God.



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:20:1)


**ראות.** מלה זרה בעבור התחברות שני משקלי שם הפעל, בא המוכרת והסמוך, וכן הוא, יראו דברים רבים ולא תשמרם הנפש או העין, ואזניה' יפקחו ולא יסגרום, ולא ישמעו, וזה תמה:


ראות *Seeing.* It is an irregular form; it is a combination of the two infinitives, the construct (רְאׁת) and the absolute (רׇאׁה). The meaning of the verse is: they will perceive many words of God, but their soul or eye will not retain them ; their ears will be open, they will not be closed, and still, strange to say, they will not hear.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:21:1)


**יי חפץ וגו'.** זה שלא יביט להראות צדק השם עד שיגדי' תורתו, שיפחדו כל עוזביה, או יהיה זה הכתוב [דבק] עם הבא אחריו, כי השם הראה צדקתו, ושם זה העם האומר על הנביא שהוא עור, שסוי ובזוי:


*The Lord is well pleased,* that they do not see; He will show His justice and exalt His law, so that all those that forsake it shall be afraid. This verse may also¹ be connected with the next, thus : God showed His justice, and made those, that said of the prophet, that he is blind, robbed and spoiled, etc.

footnotes:
¹ The Hebrew text has אז which is a corruption of או or ; for in the succeeding words a second explanation is contained. According to the first explanation the תורה law, that is to be exalted, is the divine law, described in the Pentateuch; according to the second it is the message which this prophet brought from the Lord, concerning the return of Israel from the Babylonian exile.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:1)


**והוא. שסוי.** מבעלי הה"א כמו שוסי' את הגרנות (שמואל א' כ"ג א'):


שסוי *Spoiled.* This is a verb .שסה) ל׳׳ה) Comp. שוסים spoiling (1 Sam. 23:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:2)


**הפח.** שם הפעל, כמו נפיחה, ואם הם שנים שרשים:


הפח *Breathing.* It is infinitive and has the same meaning as נפח, though of a different root (פוח).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:3)


**בחורים.** מגזרת חור פתן (ישעיהו י"א ח'), והטעם שהם אסורים יושבים בתחתית יוצאי השבי:


בחורים *In holes.* Comp. חור hole (11:8). They are imprisoned, occupying the lowest dungeons of all the captives.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:4)


**השב.** בעובר שהוא סוף פסוק, והוא פועל יוצא, השב המשסה:


הׇשַׁב The Pathah is substituted for Zeré because the word is the end of the verse ; השב is transitive, and means restore, namely the spoil.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:5)


**מי בכם יגיד זאת.** כמו זה הנביא שתאמרו שהוא עור, וישמע העתיד וזה לאחור, וזהו מגזרת אל תאחרו אותי (בראשית כ"ד נ"ו):


*Who among you will tell*³² *this,* will tell things like those which the prophet, whom you declared to be blind, proclaimed. לאחור *For the time to come.* Comp. תאחרו you keep me waiting³³ (Gen. 24:56);

footnotes:
³² Our editions have יאזין will give ear; but I. E. reads instead יגיד will tell.
³³ A. V., Hinder me not.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:22:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:22:6)


**לפנים.** מגזרת פנה:


לפנים in former time is derived from פנה it has turned away ; it is gone.



### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/42:24:1)


**מי וגו'.** אז יודה השם ויאמר מי נתננו למשיסה הלא יי זו כטעם זה הוא שחטאנו לו, ולא אבו אבותינו שמוע ללכת בדרכיו:


*Who gave Jacob,* etc. Then the people will confess and say: who has given us for a spoil? Certainly the Lord, it is He (זה═זו this), against whom we have sinned, and in whose ways our forefathers refused to walk.



### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 42:25:1

*Upon him.* Comp. Gen. 49:22.³⁴ עליו upon him, after the plural לא שמעו ,לא אבו they would not, they were not obedient, and צעדה she runs after בנות branches. (Gen. 49:22.) Comp. c. ii. Note 18. Upon every one of our forefathers.

ותלהטהו *And it burned him.* Comp. להט flame (Gen. 3:24).—They will confess that their forefathers were blind with regard to their hearts, and had no understanding.



## Chapter 43


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:1:1)


**ועתה.** אמר הנביא אחרי שאתם מודים, עתה יגאלכם השם:


*But now,* etc. Now, says the prophet, since you have confessed, God will redeem you.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:1:2)


**קראתי בשמך.** מעלה גדולה, כמו ראה קראתי בשם (שמות ל"א ב') והמעלה היא שאתם שלי:


*I have called you by My name.* I have given you a great distinction; comp. I have called by name Bezaleel (Ex. 31:2); and the distinction is further described in the words thou art mine.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:2:1)


**כי וגו'.** הכתוב ידמה השרים לנהרים, גם אש, כמו אש יצאה מחשבון (במדבר כ"א כ"ח), וטעם כי תעבור במים, על מדי ופרס כאשר ילכדו בבל:


*When thou passest through the waters,* etc. The peoples¹ are in Scripture compared with rivers and also with fire; comp. A fire is gone out of Heshbon (Num. 21:28). By the waters and the fire the armies of Persia and Media are meant, that were to conquer Babylon.

footnotes:
¹ The Hebrew text has השרים the princes, but they are compared neither with rivers nor with fire (comp. I. E. on Num. 21:28); the translation is based on the conjecture, that השרים is a corruption of העמים.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:3:1)


**נתתי כפרך מצרים.** שמלכי מדי יעשו להם רעה:


*I gave Egypt for thy ransom.* The Egyptians shall be afflicted by the kings of Media.²

footnotes:
² Media is here identical with Media and Persia. Kambyses, king of Persia, conquered Egypt 625 B.C.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:4:1)


**ואתן אדם.** שאני בראתים כאשר בראתיך:


*Therefore will I give men*, whom I have created, as I have created thee.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:5:1)


**ממזרח.** היא בבל:


*From the east.* From Babylon.¹

footnotes:
¹ According to I. E. on c. 49:12, Babylon is in the north of Palestine; but in reality it may be considered as north-east of Jerusalem.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:5:2)


**וממערב.** היא מצרים ואשור, וכתי' והסב לב מלך אשור (עזרא י' כ"ב):


*From the west.* From Egypt and Assyria.³ Comp. Ezr. 6:22.⁴

footnotes:
³ Assyria is described as in the west of Palestine, and identical with Ethiopia; comp. 18:1, Note 3, and 49:12.
⁴ The words referred to are: And turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of God. It is difficult to find out what I. E. intended to prove by this quotation, since it does not give us the least information concerning the position of Assyria. He means perhaps to show that the name of Assyria was not limited to the kingdom of Nineveh, since in the time of Ezra the latter kingdom had ceased to exist.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:6:1)

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:6:3)


**[בני].** ובנותי, אנשים ונשים:

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:1)


**כל וגו'.** יש אומרים כי נקרא כמו קורא, ואיננו נכון, רק הוא כמשמעו, כל הנקרא בשמי שהם עם יי:


קורא ═ נקרא that calleth, as some explain; but this is wrong. It is to be taken literally.⁵ *Every one that is called by my name,* that is, all that belong to the people of the Lord.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:2)

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:3)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:7:4)


**אף עשיתיו.** הטעם ותקנתיו, ורבי שלמה בעל השירים השקולי' ז"ל פירש בו כי זה אור העולם, ואיננו דבק בטעם הפרשה:


עשיתיו I have established it.⁷—R*.* Salomo, the father of metrical poetry in Hebrew,⁸ explained this verse to contain the principles of the creation of the universe ; but this explanation is not in accordance with the context.⁹

footnotes:
⁷ A. V., I have made him.
⁸ R. Salomo Ibn Gebirol, who is believed to be the first Hebrew poet who wrote whole works in metrical verses. See Zahoth, On Metre.
⁹ According to I. E. this verse is in apposition to בני my sons and בנותי my daughters of the preceding verse, and refers to the Israelites ; the three verbs not differing essentially from each other. According to R. Joseph. Sephardi, Super-commentator of I. E., On the Pentateuch (Gen. 2:4), I. E. refers these three verbs to the creation of matter, the creation of form, and the combination of both. But I. E. cannot be the author of this explanation, because it would overthrow his rendering of ברא, upon which he lays great stress. See c. xl. Note 61, and c. xlv. Note 6.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:8:2)

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:9:1)


**כל וגו'.** ושמא יאמר אדם כי ישראל לא ידעו אלה העתידות, כי הם עורים, שמא יש בגוים ובחכמיהם מי שידע', מי בכם יגיד אלה העתידות, וישמיעונו ראשונות שעברו, שאמרו הם קודם היותם שתהינה:


*Let all the nations be gathered together,* etc. If some should say that the Israelites did not know these future events, for they were blind ; but of other nations and their wise men, some knew them perhaps, the question is put, *Who among them can declare this,* viz. that which shall happen in days to come, *and show us former things,* past events, which they had announced before they took place.

*let them hear,* that is, let the witnesses hear the same,

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:1)


**אתם.** עם ישראל ידבר ועבדי הוא הנביא:


*Ye are my witnesses,* etc. Israel is addressed. *And my servant.* The prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:2)


**כי אני הוא.** זה הייחוד שאי' למעלה ממנו, כי כל יש איננו הוא בעצמו:


*I am he.* This is the sublimest expression of the unity of God; for every other being is different from its real form.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ Every creature is, according to the theory of I.E., produced after and by its abstract form in the spiritual world above, but being subject to accidents, it deviates from its abstract original, from its true and perfect form, and is, as it were, not truly itself. To God alone this is not applicable; He is, therefore, said to be Himself in truth, to be always the same.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:10:3)


**לפני לא נוצר אל.** יש אומרים לפני מעמד הר סיני, ואחרי אחרי המעמד ואין צורך, רק הוא, אין לפני אל וכן אחרי לא יהיה, והטעם כי הוא ראשון ואחרון, ונזכר נוצר עם אל, כי אין אל מבלעדיו כי אם נוצר, ועורי לב יחשבו שיצא מדברי הנביא שהשם נוצר חלילה חלילה, רק לא יבינו האמת:


*Before me, after me.* According to some, before me means before the revelation on Sinai, and after me, after the revelation.¹⁵ But it is not at all necessary to depart from the literal meaning of the words: No God was before me, and none will be after me, because God is the first and last. The expression formed (נוצר) is applied here to the word God, in order to imply that a god besides Him can only be one formed by man. Shortsighted people think, that the expression formed used in reference to the Creator, slipped out of the mouth of the prophet; but this is by no means the case ; such critics do not conceive the true meaning of the verse.¹

footnotes:
¹⁵ This explanation is intended to oppose the inference, which might be made from the words before me, after me, that God is not without beginning and end.
¹ That there is no God besides Him, not even one formed by Him.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:11:1)


**אנכי אנכי.** הטעם אני אנכי פעמים, שלא אשתנה, כהשתנות צבאות מעלה כנגד המוצק, והתחתיים בעצם ובתבנית, על כן אושיע בכל עת:


*I, I.* The word is repeated, as if to say, I do not change as the host of heaven does with regard to its centre, nor as earthly things do with regard to substance and form; I can therefore help at every time.

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:14:1)


**כה.** שלחתי בבלה, יש אומרים כי תי"ו שלחתי רמז לנביא, ולפי דעתי שהוא דבר יי, כי בתחלה כה אמר יי, ואחר כן אני יי קדושכם, והנה הטעם, כל כך באתי במהרה, כאילו שלחתי, וחכם גדול בספרד אמר כי הכבוד ידבר עם הנביא, ושר ישראל הוא, המשולח אל בבל לגאול ישראל:


שלחתי *I was sent.*¹⁶ Some think that the first person I refers to the prophet; but I am of opinion that God is speaking, because this verse begins, Thus saith the Lord, and the next verse, I am the Lord, The meaning of the phrase is: I have come so hastily, as if I were sent.¹⁷ A very learned man in Spain conjectures, that the Divine Glory,¹⁸ the same heavenly prince of Israel¹ that has been sent to Babylon to redeem Israel, is speaking to the prophet.

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., I have sent.
¹⁷ I. E. seems to have read שֻׁלַּחְתּׅי instead of שׁׅלַּחְתּׅי adopted in our printed Bibles.
¹⁸ The angels, according to I. E., being the uncorporeal first emanation from the divine Glory, are also called הכבוד the divine glory.
¹ Comp. Dan. 10:20.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:19:1)


**הנני עשה חדשה.** לכידת בבל, או שימלטו ישראל לבדם, והוא הנכון בעיני, ועוד שאשים במדבר מים, בעבור השבים מהגולה אל ציון:


*A new thing.* The taking of Babylon, or the fact that the Israelites alone will escape; the latter seems the more probable explanation.²² *I will even make,* etc. I shall, besides, produce water in the wilderness for the benefit of those who will return from Babylon to Zion.

footnotes:
²² Because, in the first place, Babylon had been taken before by Sennacherib; secondly, the capture of a town does not appear to be a new thing, since many strongholds had been taken before, and this event could not be called by the prophet a new thing ; while it can more properly be said of the deliverance of the oppressed Israelites, who were in numbers and warfare inferior to all other nations.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:23:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:23:2)


**ולא כבדתני.** בזבחי שלמים ולא בקשתי ממך שתעבדני במנחה:


*Neither hast thou honoured me* (זבחיך) *with thy sacrifices,* with thy peace-offerings.²⁴ *I have not caused,* etc. I have not asked thee to serve me with oblations.

footnotes:
²⁴ The word זבח is used in connection with שלמים to signify peace-offerings (Lev. 3:1), and as a complement of עולותיך, signifying all animal offerings except the holocaust (ib. 17:8), that is, peace and sin-offerings. The word occurring twice in underlinethis/underline passage, is therefore explained to refer each time to a different kind of sacrifice. I. E. refers it first to peace-offerings, probably because of the expression neither hast thou honoured me; believing that sin-offerings can never be an honour to the Almighty; they can only be the symbol of a compensation or a satisfaction for wrongs done as it were against the Almighty; this is properly expressed by the verb הרויתני thou hast satisfied me, or thou hast filled me.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:27:1)


**אביך הראשון.** הוא ירבעם, שבחרו ישראל למלך, לא על פי השם:


*Thy first father hath sinned.* Jeroboam, when chosen by the Israelites, to be their king, without the consent of God.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁵ This statement is not quite correct, since the prophet Ahijah from Shiloh told Jeroboam that God had appointed him to be king over ten tribes (1 Kgs. 11:29—39). The idolatry of Jeroboam should rather be pointed at by I. E.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 43:27:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:27:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/43:27:2)


**ומליציך.** הם השרים מליצי המלך או הלויים מליצי הכהנים, ויש אומרים שאביך הם המלמדים כמו אבי אבי רכב ישראל (מלכים ב' ב' י"א) וישימני לאב לפרעה (בראשית מ"ה ח') אבי כל תופש כנור ועוגב (שם מ"ה ה') והמליצים הם התלמידים, והוא מגזרת כי המליץ (שם מ"ב כ"ג):


ומליציך *And thy interpreters.*²⁶ Either the princes, the interpreters of the king, are meant, or the Levites, the interpreters of the priests. Some explain אביך by thy teachers. Comp. 2 Kgs. 12:13; Gen. 4:21; 45:8, and מליציך by thy pupils. As to מליץ interpreter, comp. Gen. 42:23

footnotes:
²⁶ A. V., And thy teachers.

## Chapter 44


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:1:1)


**ועתה.** שמע את הטוב':


but now hear the good which I shall do unto thee.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:2:1)


**כה.** ויצרך מבטן, רמז ליעקב, כטעם בבטן עקב את אחיו (הושע י"ב ד') ושם אפרשנו, או הוא על דרך משל, ומבטן מיום היותם לעם לשם:


*From the womb.* With this expression the prophet alludes to Jacob (comp. Hos. 12:4; in my commentary thereon I shall explain it),¹ or metaphorically to the time, when Israel was declared to be the people of the Lord.

footnotes:
¹ I. E. takes the expression womb literally, and refers it to the incident recorded Gen. 25:26, in the account of the birth of Jacob and Esau.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:2:2)


**ישורון.** מגזרת ישר, והוא תאר השם, ואפס על משקלו:


ישרון *Jesurun.* It is originally an adjective derived from ישר right; there is no other instance of this form.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:3:1)


**כי אצק וגו'.** כמו שאצק מים על מקום צמא כן אצק רוח קדשי או רוח ישעי,****ונדגש צד"י אצק לחסרון היו"ד, וכמוהו בטרם אצרך בבטן (ירמיה א' ה'):


*For I will pour water,* etc. As I pour water over the place that is thirsty, so will I pour out the spirit of my holiness, or of my salvation, etc. אֶצּׁק *I will pour out.* The Dagesh in צ compensates for the י which is omitted;² comp. אצרך I shall form thee (Jer. 1:5)

footnotes:
² The root of אצק is יצק.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:4:1)


**[וצמחו בבין חציר].** וצמחו רוחי וברכתי כמו חציר, ורבים אמרו על הצאצאים, וכן [הוא] וצמחו כאילו הם יושבים בין החציר, והטעם שיפרו וירבו:


*And they shall spring up.* The pronoun they refers to My spirit, and My blessing, of the preceding verse; according to others³ to thine offspring. בבין חציר *Like grass.* Lit., between the grass, that is, as if they were between grass. They will increase and multiply.⁴

footnotes:
³ Comp. Rashi, ad locum; and Targum Jonathan.
⁴ This remark on בבין חציר is seemingly a continuation of the second explanation of And they shall spring up, but in reality it can also be connected with the first one.5 Comp. Rashi ad locum.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:1)


**זה וגו'.** יהיו רבים, ורבם אוהבי השם לשוב אל ביתו:


*One shall say,* etc. They will be numerous, and the majority of them will be faithful to God, and desirous of returning to His house.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:2)


**וזה יקרא בשם יעקב.** להתפאר לעיני הגוים שהוא מזרע קדוש:


*And another shall call himself by the name of Jacob,* in order to show to all nations, how proud he is of belonging to the holy people.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:3)


**וזה יכתוב ידו.** חסר בי"ת, וכן הוא יכתו' בידו, לבא אל מקדש השם:


בידו═ידו With his hand. *And another shall subscribe unto the Lord,* that he is willing to go to the sanctuary of the Lord.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:5:4)


**יכנה.** כמו יקרא, ורבי' פירשוהו על הגרים כטעם והחזיקו עשרה אנשים (זכריה ח' כ"ג):


יכנה He will surname himself.—Many refer this verse to proselytes; comp. Ten men shall take hold, out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you; for we have heard that God is with you (Zec. 8:23)



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:6:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:6:2)

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:6:3)

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:1)


**אל תרהו.** אין לו ריע, והמחליפים באל"ף איננו נכון במקום הזה, בעבור חסרון היו"ד מהמכתב שהו' שורש:


אל תרהו *Be ye not afraid,* תרהו is hap. leg; those that identify it with תראו are wrong, on account of the absence of the radical י ¹⁰—

footnotes:
¹⁰ This is no good reason at all; since י of ירא to fear can in writing be well omitted in the future Kal; it is read תּׅ־רְאוּ to distinguish it from. תּׅרְאוּ you will see.—According to I. E. א and ה belong to those letters which interchange.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:2)


וטעם **אל תפחדו.** כאשר תבאנ' אלה הצרות אל בבל, אל תפחדו אתם (אלה אתם):

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:8:3)


**הלא מאז** הודעתי אתכם **ואתם עדי**, והנה תראו, **היש אלוה מבלעדי, ואין צור [בל ידעתי]** שלא אדענו כי הוא תוהו והבל [ובוהו] ויש אומרי' שהוא כטעם ויודע בהם (שופטים ח' ט"ז) אנשי סוכות, והנכון הוא רמז להמון מעלה:


*Have I not told thee* of it long ago? *Ye are even my witnesses,* and you will see whether there is a *God beside me; There is no God* בל ירעתי *whom I know not*¹¹ to be vain and powerless. According to some, whom I chastised not; comp. ויודע and he chastised¹² (Jud. 8:16). I think that the prophet speaks here of the host of heaven.¹³

footnotes:
¹¹ A. V., I know not any.
¹² A. V., He taught.
¹³ In that case צור rock, protection, would signify the same as שׂר prince, used by Daniel 10:20. See I. E. on 24:21, Note 30.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:1)


**יוצרי פסל כולם תוהו.** הם ופסיליהם תוהו:


*They that make a graven image, are all of them vanity.* They themselves as well as their images are vanity.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:2)


**וחמודיהם.** שיצירום במשכיות עד שיהיו נחמדים לעין והם הפסילים:


וחמוריהם *And their delectable things.* The objects which they ornament with figures, that they be charming to the eye, namely the idols.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ The word פסילים is not used here by I. E. in its general meaning idols; but in the special meaning assigned to it by I. E., stone images (40:19). The reason that I. E. refers חמודיהם to stone images is to be found in his desire to find system and symmetry in the words of the prophet. The images made of metal and wood being mentioned ver. 12 and ver. 13, the general term חמודיהם must be restricted to stone images, in order to have a complete picture of all kinds of idols.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:3)

footnotes:
¹⁵ A. V., Their own.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:9:4)

לבער *To bum. Then shall it be for a man,* etc. Some warm themselves by the fire, others kindle it, etc. ישיק *He kindleth it.* Comp. נשקה was kindled (Ps. Ixxviii. 21); the meaning of נשק is similar to that of בער to burn.

### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:18:1

**לא.** הדעה בנקבים הקרובים אל המצח, והבינה בנקב האמצעי שהוא בתוך הראש:


לא ידעו ולא יבינו *They have not known nor understood.* The seat of knowledge (רעת) is in those cavities of the brain that are nearer to the forehead; the understanding (בינה) is in the middle one, that is also in the middle of the head.²⁹

²⁹ In his remark on Ex. 31:3, I. E. explains the three expressions ,חכמה ,תבונה, דעת to signify the receptive, discriminative and reproductive faculties of our mind, and assigns to each of them its special place in the brain.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:23:1

### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:24:1)


**כה.** עשה כל, אני עושה כל חפצי, והעד כי נטיתי שמים לבדי:


*That maketh all things,* which I desire; you may infer it from the fact, that I, by myself, stretch forth the heaven.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:24:2)


**מאתי.** מכחי, כי אין השם גוף, וכתוב מי אתי והנה הוא כמו לבדי, ודע כי הכתוב אמר נוטה השמים ורוקע הארץ כי עמידתם תמיד בשם:


מאתי *By myself.* Lit., from myself, that is, by my strength; for God is incorporeal.³⁹ It is written in two words, מי אתי. who is with me, which is the same as I alone. Consider well the words of the text: who *stretcheth*⁴⁰⁴⁰ forth the heavens and *spreadeth* abroad the earth ; they teach us that it is God who is continually keeping heaven and earth in existence.

³⁹ The literal meaning of the words, That spreadeth abroad the earth from, myself might imply the idea that the earth has its origin materially in God; I. E. refutes this idea by substituting the figurative meaning from or with my strength.

### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:25:1)


**מפר אתות בדים.** הם הבודאים מלבם, וכמוהו בדיך מתים יחרישו (איוב י"א ג') ויותר נכון להיותו מגזרת בדד, כי יש נשמות שיש להם כח להתבודד:


בדים *Liars.* Comp. בדיך thy lies (Job 11:3). More probably בדים is connected with בדד alone, and signifies such, persons as pretend to be able to emancipate their souls from, the influence of the body, which some in reality can do.¹

footnotes:
¹ The more the soul emancipates itself from the body, the closer is its union, with the pure intellect, with the original and fundamental ideas, and the wider and surer its knowledge. This state of emancipation is called by I. E. preparatian for inspiration. Comp. תמונות צורות ומראות בדבר השם ובהיות הנפש מכוונת לכבוד או תתחדש לה when the soul is prepared for the Divine Glory, then it receives new ideas, images, and visions by the word of the Lord. (Abridged Commentary on Exod. 23:21.)

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:25:3)


**משיב חכמים.** הם רואי הכבד והכתף וחכמי העתיד:


*Wise men.* Persons, who divine from the liver or shoulder, and soothsayers.⁴³

footnotes:
⁴³ From the context it may be inferred that by wise men the prophet meant diviners; but since two kinds of diviners ברים and קוסמים have already been mentioned, I. E. refers this general expression to other kinds, which are not included in these two names.



### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:1)


**מקים דבר עבדו.** הוא הנביא והטעם עצמו, ומה הוא דבר הנביא, שתושב ירושלם:


His servant. The prophet himself.⁴⁴ *The word of his servant,* that Jerusalem shall be inhabited.

footnotes:
⁴⁴ I. E. here neglects the rule of the parallelism, which he repeatedly recommends; for that rule demands that עברו and מלאכיו should have the same meaning) and since the latter is a plural, signifying his messengers, עבדו is likewise to be taken in a collective sense, and referred not only to the one prophet who is here speaking, but to all prophets.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:2)


**[תושב].** מגזרת ישיב' כמו תורד (ישעיהו י"ד ט"ו):


תושב *Thou shalt be inhabited.* Root ישב to dwell. Comp. תורד thou shalt be brought down (14:15) from ירד to go down.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:26:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:26:3)


**וחרבותיה.** חרבות כל עיר ועיר, או הה"א סימן ירושלם:


*Her decayed places.* The decayed places of every city,⁴⁵ or of Jerusalem.¹

footnotes:
⁴⁵ The use of the singular her (הָ) after the plural the cities of Judah is explained in this remark. Comp. I. E. on c. 2:11, Note 18.
¹ Although the pronoun her is nearer to the cities of Judah, it may still agree with Jerusalem, which is mentioned first, because it is the most important, and may be considered as the representative, of all the cities of Judah.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:27:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:27:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:27:1)


**האומר לצולה.** כמו מצולה [יונה ב' ד'] במצולת ים [מיכה ז' ט'], וזה הטעם רמז על בבל שהיתה מליאה אדם והון, כמצולת ים:


מצולה═צולה (Jon. 2:4) *The deep.* A figurative expression, signifying Babylon, that was full of men and wealth like the deep of the sea.⁴⁶

footnotes:
⁴⁶ Which is full of water.



### Verse 28

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 44:28:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:28:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/44:28:1)


**האומר.** ולאמר לירושלם תבנה, והנה זאת הראיה גמורה שנבנת' ירושלם בימי כורש, ורמז תוסד על בית השם שצוה שיבנה, וכאשר יסדו ידי זרובבל, צוה כורש שלא יבנה, והנה התברר שלא טעה דניאל בחשבונו, כאשר פירשתי במקומו:


*That saith to Cyrus,* etc. This verse proves that Jerusalem was built in the days of Cyrus; the words thy foundation shall be laid contain an allusion to the fact, that Cyrus ordered the temple to be built, but after its foundation had been laid by Zerubbabel, prohibited its further restoration; it is therefore clear, that Daniel made no mistake in his calculations, as I have already explained.⁴⁷

footnotes:
⁴⁷ All our learned men agree, says I. E. in his commentary on Dan. 9:1, that Daniel made a miscalculation; he thought that the 70 years of exile, foretold by Jeremiah, commenced with the first deportation under king Jehoiakim, and ended with the commencement of the reign of king Cyrus over Babylon, while in truth the exile commenced with the destruction of the temple, and ended during the reign of Darius Hystaspes. I. E. objects to this opinion, and proves, in the form of a dialogue between himself and R. Jehudah Hallevi, that Daniel was right. The exile lasted only till the reign of Cyrus, under whose auspices the foundation of the temple was laid. According to the prophecy of Isaiah not the building, but the founding of the temple (תּׅוׇּםֵר), was to be promoted by Cyrus.

*His anointed.* According to some, the prophet; others think that Cyrus is meant; either explanation is admissible; comp. The Lord hath anointed me (61:1), and Anoint Hazael to be king (1 K. 19:15).

*I*. The support of God or the heavenly prince of Persia is to be understood;¹ comp. Dan. 10:20.

footnotes:
¹ This remark of I. E. is intended to smooth the anthropological expression I (God) will go before thee. Two explanations are given; the first substitutes for I the expression my support; the second assigns these words to the angel, the messenger of God, who speaks of God sometimes in the first, sometimes in the third person. Comp. c. xvi. Note 7.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:2:2

והדורים *The crooked places.* It is the opposite of ישר straight. Some derive it from הדר glory;² it means mountains, and is as to its form either adjective or participle passive.³

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:7:2)


**ובורא חשך.** מגזרת בריאה כטעם גזירה, כי החשך איננו כלום רק העדר האור:


ובורא חשך *And causeth*⁵⁵ *darkness.* ברא has here the same meaning as גזר to decree; for darkness is nothing by itself, it is but the absence of light.⁶

footnotes:
⁵ A. V., And create.
⁵ A. V., And create.
⁶ Darkness is no substance in itself; the verb to create, which signifies to bring a substance into existence (להוציא יש מאין), cannot therefore be applied to it, and the verb ברא, which is used here by the prophet with regard to darkness, means to decree, to order. But God commands that there shall be darkness, is the same as, God commands the light to withdraw. I. E., however, lays rather too much stress on his exposition of the verb ברא.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:7:3)


**ובורא רע.** כמוהו, והנה רע מלחמה הפך שלום או חולי בגוף בן אדם שהוא נלחם עם התולדת, והזכיר זה בפרשה הזאת שהוא יחזק כורש הפך מלך בבל:


The same is to be said¹ war, illness. But I. E. explains that these evils are but a certain relation of existing beings to each other; and finds the verb to decree or to command to be more applicable to them than the verb to create. concerning ובורא רע *And causeth* *evil.* By evil war is meant as the opposite of peace, or the sickness under which man labours, as being at war with his constitution. These antitheses are used to indicate that in the same way God will strengthen Cyrus and weaken the king of Babylon.

footnotes:
¹ The evil seems sometimes to be something real, to which the verb to create might well be applied, as e.g.

### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:12:1)


**אנכי.** ואיך תצוני על בני, וכל העולם שלי הוא, כי אנכי עשיתי ארץ ואדם עליה בראתי אני הוא שידי נטו שמים, וכל צבאם צויתי ונבראו, הטעם משל לדבור, וכן כתיב כי הוא צוה ונבראו (תהלים קמ"ח ה'):


*I have made the earth,* etc. How will you command me concerning my children, when the whole universe belongs to me? I have created earth and man upon it; my hands have stretched out the heavens, and *all their hosts have I commanded,* and consequently they were created. I commanded is poetically said¹⁶ for I spoke as in the verse He commanded and they were created (Ps. 148:5)

footnotes:
¹⁶ I. E. explains I commanded by I spoke, because this verse refers to the creation of heaven and earth and all their hosts, and the verb to command cannot properly be applied to things which do not yet exist.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:13:1)


**אנכי.** וי"ו העירותיהו על כורש:


*I have raised him,* namely Cyrus.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:13:2)


**וכל דרכיו איישר.** ולמה זה, כי הוא יבנה עירי:


*And I will make straight all his ways,* and all this only because He shall build, etc.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:1)


**כה.** יגיע מצרים, גם זה לאות שכורש יבוז מצרים ויהיו נשבים, וידוע כי דרכם על ארץ ישראל, כי היא אמצעית בין עילם ובין מצרים:


*The labour of Egypt,* etc. This verse shows that Cyrus was also to conquer Egypt, and to carry the inhabitants thereof away into captivity; the way, as is well known, led through. Palestine, which is situated in the midst between Elam and Egypt.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ As to the position of Elam, see c. xiii. Note 7. Cyrus did not conquer Egypt, but Kambyses, his successor, conquered it 525 B. C.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:2)


**אנשי מדה.** הטעם הגדולה, כי כל איש מדה יש לו, וכמוהו וחזקת והיית לאיש (מלכים א' ב' ב'):


*Men of measure.* Men of great measure; for all men have a certain measure; comp. show thyself a man═show thyself a brave man (1 Kgs. 2:2).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:14:3)


**ויודו ויאמרו אך בך אל.** וזה היה אחרי שוב הגולה:


*Surely God is in thee.* These are the words which they will confess and declare; this was in fact the case after the return of Israel from the Babylonian captivity.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁸ Comp. I. E. 19:19, note 26.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:15:1)


**אכן.** אז יודו לשם ויאמרו, אמת כי אתה אל מסתתר מהגוי שאין לך חפץ בו, ואתה אלהי ישראל מושיעם, ומפרשים אמרו כי מסתתר כמו נסתר, ונראית בעבור ישראל שהושעתם, וזה איננו נכון בדקדוק, כי מסתתר מבנין התפעל:


*Verily thou art a God,* etc. Then they will confess to God and say, It is true that thou art God who hid himself from the people in which He delighted, and now thou art the God of the Israelites, who helps them. Some say that אל נסתר ═ אל מסתתר invisible God, and explain the verse thus: God, though invisible, revealed himself for the sake of Israel. This explanation, however, is not supported by the rules of Hebrew grammar, מסתתר being Hithpael, and signifying who hid himself.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:16:1)


**בושו.** הלכו בכלימה, החרשים שפסלו הפסילים, והם הלכו בכבוד אל המשלחים בשבילם כי צירים שלוחים וכן ציר בגוים שולח [עובדיה א' א'] והטעם שילכו אל מקומם:


*They shall go with confusion,*¹⁹ etc. They that make the idols, and come with honour to those that send for them, shall go, etc. צירים *Messengers.*²⁰ Comp. ציר an ambassador (Jer. 49:14). הלכו *They shall go.* They shall return to their land.

footnotes:
¹⁹ A. V., To confusion.
²⁰ A. V., Idols. According to I. E. חרשי means the makers of idols, צירים of messengers, that is, for whom messengers were sent from a distance.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:17:1

*Israel is saved by the Lord.* Therefore they will not be ashamed, as those men have been put to shame, that made vain things which cannot help in times of trouble.

עד *Innumerable.*²¹

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:18:1)

*He hath established it,* as the habitation for men and beasts.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:18:2

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:19:1)


**לא וגו'.** והנה לא בראתי הארץ לתוהו, ואיך אומר לזרע ישראל תהו בקשוני, ורבים פירשוהו לא בסתר דברתי על מעמד הר סיני, והנכון בעיני שהוא רמז על אלה העתידות שגילה סודם לנביאו, ונביאו לישראל ולגוים, על כן אמר מגיד מישרים:


*I have not spoken,* etc. I have not made the earth in vain, how then should I say to the Israelites Seek ye me in vain.²² Many refer this verse to the revelation on Sinai;¹ but I refer it to those future events, of which the Lord informed the prophet, and which the prophet announced to Israel and all other nations ; this may be gathered from the words מגיד מישרים I declare things that are right.²³

footnotes:
²² God has not created the earth in vain; he wishes that it shall be inhabited; how then should He ask the Israelites, whose land is desolate and waste, to seek Him, that is, to pray to Him, for the restoration of the country, in vain, that is, without being relieved?
¹ See Rashi ad locum.
²³ According to I. E., the words Things that are right, refer to the predictions concerning the redemption of the Israelites, which is sure to take place as soon as they make up their minds to return to God.



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:20:1)

הקבצו ובאו התנגשו *Assemble yourselves and come, draw near.* These are imperatives.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:20:2)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:22:1)


**פנו [אלי והושעו].** טעם והושעו ותהיו נושעים, והנה הרשות בידכם:


*And be ye saved.* This is the same as and you will be saved; it is in your own power.²⁴

footnotes:
²⁴ The imperative And be ye saved is here used, although the Israelites cannot properly be commanded to save themselves, for it is God who saves them; because the relief sent to them by God is only the consequence of their good actions, which they are here indirectly commanded to do.



### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:1)


**בי.** טעם בי שהוא קיים, וכל מקום ששם שבוע', היא גזירה שנגזר' ולא תבטל:


*By myself,* who am eternal. *I have sworn.* I have made a decree, which will not be undone.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:2)


**יצא מפי [צדקה].** דבר צדקה, כמו צדקה ממני (בראשית ל"ח כ"ו), והטעם דבר אמת:


דבר צדקה ═ צדקה *a righteous word.*¹ Comp. צדקה she hath been righteous (Gen. 38:27).²⁵

footnotes:
¹ This remark is added to explain the discrepancy between the genders of the verb יצא and the noun צדקה.
²⁵ This quotation is adduced to prove that the word צדקה admits also of the meaning truth.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:23:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:23:3)


**כי לי וגו'.** והטעם שאלה העתידות אעשם, עד שתכרע לי כל ברך, תשבע כל לשון להיות לי, כי לי ימשוך אחר עמו כמשפט, וכמוהו ובשמו תשבע (דברים ו' י"ג):


*That unto me,* etc. These things here foretold I shall do, till unto me every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear to belong to me. לי unto me must be repeated before תשבע shall swear ; it is an ellipsis, such as is frequently met with. Comp.²⁶ And shall swear by His name (Deut. 6:13)

footnotes:
²⁶ As to the meaning of נשבע to swear to be faithful to.



### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 45:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:24:1)


**אך וגו'.** אלה דברי הנביא, כאומר לא ידעתי אלה עתידות בדרך חכמה, אך ביי לבדי שאמר לי אלה הצדקות והעוז, והנכון אך ביי לבדו צדקות ועוז, ונכנסה מלת לי אמר, והטעם בשם שדבר עמי:


לי *Unto me.* The pronoun of the first person refers to the prophet. He declares, that he does not know these future events by the aid of his reason, but by the Lord alone, who informed him of these things of righteousness and strength.²⁷ It is more correct to explain the verse thus : Surely in the Lord, alone is righteousness and strength, the words לי אמר are a relative sentence signifying who spoke unto me.

footnotes:
²⁷ Mentioned in the preceding verse, and referring to the faithful fulfilment of the divine promise.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/45:24:2)


**עדיו.** [כמו] ולא שבתם עדי (עמוס ד' ו'):


עדיו *To Him.* Comp. Am. 4:6

## Chapter 46


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:1)


**כרע בל.** עבודה זרה לבבליים, גם כן נבו ויש אומרים שהוא כוכב חמה:


*Bel.* The idol of the Babylonians; the same is the case with Nebo. The latter is explained by some to signify the sun.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:2)


**קורס.** מגזרת (שמות כ"ו י"א) קרסים והטעם ידוע, ואין ראוי לכתבו:


קורס It is connected with קרסים taches (Ex. 26:11); its meaning is well known.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:3)


**לחיה ולבהמ'.** שישא אדם [אותם] עליהם:


*Upon the beasts and upon the cattle,* upon which man is carried. This sentence is therefore followed by the words


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:1:4)

¹ A. V., Your carriages. נשאתיכם is explained by I. E. in an active sense, although it is in fact participle passive Kal of נשא.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:2:1)


**קרסו כרעו.** הנושאי':


*They bow down.* The beasts that carry the idols, bow down.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:2:2)


**ולא יכלו מלט.** עצביהם נפשם, הנשואים, כי גם הם נשבו, ויש אומרים כי כרעו קרסו כל העצבים שהיו בבבל שלא הזכירם, ולא יכלו העצבים למלט משא כי הם בעצמם הלכו בשבי:


*The burden.* Their idols. נפשם *Their souls,*² that is, the persons carried by the beasts, *are gone into captivity.* They were also carried away as captives. Others explain the verse thus : They, that is, all the idols that are left in Babylon, and are not yet mentioned,³ stoop and bow down, and cannot deliver the burden, for they must go themselves into captivity.

footnotes:
² A. V., Themselves.
³ That is all idols worshipped in Babylon besides Bel and Nebo.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:3:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:3:2)

### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:4:1)


**ועד וגו'.** דרך משל, מיום שהיו עם השם עד עולם:


*And even to old age,* etc. This is a figurative expression; it means since the day they had become the people of the Lord for ever.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:4:2)


**אני עשיתי.** ישראל, ולא כאלהי בבל, שהבבליים יעשו אלהיהם, ואני אשאם ואמלטם, ולא כמוהם שלא יכלו למלט משא:


*I have made* the Israelites; I am, therefore, not like the gods of Babylon; the Babylonians make their gods. *And I will carry and deliver* the Israelites; while the idols cannot deliver the burden.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:5:1)


**למי.** ותשוו, אותי ונדמה שנינו:


*And make me equal,* that we two should be similar.—This verse is addressed to the idolaters.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:6:1)


**הזלים וגו'.** עם עובדי עבודה זרה ידבר, הזלים רבים הוציאוהו מגזרת אזל מכלינו (שמואל א' ט' ז'), והוא חסר אל"ף, והנכון שאין רע לו, כי אזל פועל עומד, וטעמו הנותנים זהב מכיסם, והנה בתור' אבנים בכיס (דברים כ"ה י"ג) והנה הוא במאזנים, גם קנה כן טעמו ואין רע לו:


הולים *They lavish gold,* etc. Many compare this word with אזל is spent¹ (1 Sam. 9:7), and assume here the elision of the first radical (א) ; but it is in fact hap. leg.; for אזל is intransitive. הזלים means who give. מכיס *Out of the bag.* The bag is a part of the balance; comp. בכיסך in thy bag (Deut. 25:13). The succeeding בקנה has a similar meaning; it is hap. leg.

footnotes:
¹ Literally: is gone. The literal translation of הזלים accordingly is: that cause to go, that is, that spend. I. E. properly objects that ולים, if participle Kal of אול, has a neuter sense, they that go.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:1)


**ישאוהו. תחתיו.** במקומו:


תחתיו *In his place.*


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:2)


**לא ימיש.** פועל יוצא, לא יוכל להמיש נפשו ממקומו, או הוא פועל עומד והראשון הוא הנכון:


לא ימיש *It shall not move itself.*⁴ ימיש is a transitive verb.¹ It may also be explained to be a neuter verb meaning it shall move, but the former explanation is better.

footnotes:
⁴ A. V. Shall he not remove.
¹ Or, more properly, reflective.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:7:3)


**יצעק.** מושך אחר עמו, וכן הוא ומצרתו יצעק:


The word יצעק One shall cry is to be repeated after ומצרתו and out of his trouble.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:8:1)


**זכרו. והתאוששו.** י"א כמו והוסדו, כמו אשיותיה (ירמיה נ' ט"ו) ואושיא יחיטו (עזרא ד' י"ב), ורבינו האי גאון ז"ל אמר שהוא מגזרת אש, כאילו הוא התחדדו [צ"ל התחררו] והגאון רב סעדיה ז"ל אמר שהוא מאש והטעם הוקדו, כטעם והיה בלבי כאש בוערת (ירמיה כ' י"ט), והשיבו זאת על לב:


והתאששו According to some And be founded ; comp. אשיותיה her foundations (Jer. 1. 15) and אושיא walls (Ezr. 4:12). R. Hai deriving it from אש fire explains והתאוששו be burnt. R. Saadiah derives it also from אֵשׁ, but explains it: be flamed; comp. this word was in mine heart as a burning fire (Jer. 20:9).⁵ *Bring again to mind* this thing.¹

footnotes:
⁵ The difference between the two explanations, that of R. Hai and that of R. Saadiah, is, that the former derives it from אש fire in its literal sense, as a destructive element, the other from אש fire in a figurative sense, as the incentive to actions.
¹ I. E. supplies ואת mentioned in the first sentence. This thing refers to the nature of the idols described in the preceding verses.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:9:1)


**זכרו ראשונות.** שעברו, על כן אמר מעולם, אז תדעו כי אנכי לבדי אל:


ראשנות *The former things.* The things that have passed ; the word מעולם of old is therefore added.⁶ *I am God.* Thus you shall know that I alone am God.

footnotes:
⁶ The literal translation of ראשנות is first things, and can be used to signify the first of the things to come as well as past events.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:10:1

**מגיד וגו'.** כי הגדתי האחרית מראשית, והטעם קודם היותו, כי מי יוכל לבטל גזרותי, כי לעולם עצתי תקום וכל חפצי אעשה:


*Declaring the end from the beginning,* that is, declaring the event before it happens; for who can annul my decree; my counsel stands for ever, and I will do all my pleasure.

*I have spoken* this decree. אביאנה *I will also bring it to pass.* יצרתיה *I have formed it*⁷ by a heavenly decree, *I will also do it* on earth.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:13:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:13:2)


**לא תאחר.** עצמה עמו מבוא, דרך משל, בעבור שהוא פועל יוצא:


לא תאחר *Shall not tarry.* Literally : shall not stay itself with me too long before coming, for תאחר is a transitive verb.⁸ It is a figurative expression.⁹

footnotes:
⁸ עצמה itself, the objective case being supplied.
⁹ The words דרך משל in the Hebrew text are not in their proper place; they should be at the end of the remark, as indicated in the translation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 46:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/46:13:3)


**ונתתי.** מושך אחר עמו וכן הוא, ונתתי לישראל תפארתי או טעמו לישראל שהם תפארתי, והוא הנכון כמו אשר בך אתפאר (ישעיהו מ"ט ג'):


ונתתי And I will place is to be repeated before לישראל. The phrase תפארתי לישראל is therefore to be rendered thus : And I will place my glory in Israel. It may also be explained thus : to Israel, who is my glory; comp. in whom I will be glorified (49:3); the latter explanation is the better.



## Chapter 47


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:1)


**בתולת בת בבל.** הטעם שהיא כמו בתולה, שלא יצאו דמי בתוליה:


*Virgin.* Babylon is like a virgin, that has not yet been deflowered.¹

footnotes:
¹ That is, for a long period; but strictly speaking, Babylon had been conquered before by the Assyrians. See Niebuhr, Gesch. As. and B. p. 179.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:2)


**בת.** כמו קהלת:


בת *Daughter.* It is here figuratively used for people.²

footnotes:
² It is strange that I. E. here explains the expression daughter, after having many times passed it over in silence (1:8; 10:32; 16:1; 22:4 ; 23:10, etc.); even the very same phrase בתולת בת (23:12; 37:22), did not elicit any remark or explanation. The object of his remark here, is probably not only to explain the figurative use of the word בת daughter קהלת═ congregation or people, but also the meaning of the construct state of the two nouns בתולת בת the virgin of the daughter of, while other authorities render them the virgin daughter of, explaining בתולת, in spite of the form of the construct state, to be in apposition to בת. I. E. refers the virgin to the capital and the daughter to the whole country. Comp. his remark on Lam. 1:15. The Chaldæan translation renders these two words by מלכו כנשתא the kingdom of the people.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:3)


**אין כסא.** לא יהיה לך כסא לעולם:


*There is no throne* for thee any longer.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:1:4)

ענוגה *Tender.* It is an adjective similar in form to אדומה red (Num. 19:2)

*Meal.* This is a prolepsis. Comp. And stripped the naked of their clothing (Job 22:6).

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:2:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:2:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:2:4)


**שובל.** הוא השיער היורד על הלחיים, ונקר' על דרך משבולת הנהר (ישעיהו כ"ז י"ב) על דעת ר' משה הכהן, והנכון שאין רע לו, ופירושו כפי מקומו בלא ראיה:


שובל *Locks.*⁴ The hair that hangs down over the cheeks. R. Moses Hakkohen compares שובל with שבלת the channel of the river (27:12),⁵ but I consider it as hap. leg., and its meaning can only be found from the context, without being supported by any. parallel passage.

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:3:1)


**תגל.** מבנין נפע':


תגל *Shall be uncovered.* It is Niphal of גלה .


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:3:2)


**ולא אפגע אדם.** ולא אקבל פגיע' אדם כמו פיוס כמו ואל תפגע בי (ירמיה ז' ט"ז), והנה אם היה אחר מלת פגיעת בי"ת, יהיה הוא הפועל, ויש אומר נקם אקח ממך ולא אפגע אדם, כמו ויפגעו את משה ואת אהרן (שמות ה' כ') שיעמוד לי בדרך, או שיאמר לי אל תעשה, או לא אפגע אדם שלא אשמח:


ולא אפגע אדם *And I shall not accept the intercession of any man.*⁶ פגע means to entreat; comp. אל תפגעי בי entreat me not (Ruth 1:16); when פגע is constructed with the preposition ב, then the noun, to which the ב is prefixed, is the object to the verb.⁷ Some render the meaning of this sentence in the following way: I shall not take vengeance on thee, and I shall not meet a man (comp. ויפגעו and they met, Ex. 5:20) sc. standing in my way, or telling me not to do it, or I shall not meet a man, whom 1 should not cause joy by this.⁸

footnotes:
⁶ A. V., And I will not meet thee as a man.
⁷ I. E. thus distinguishes between פגע governing the accusative, and פגע being followed by the preposition ב; the former has the meaning to accept the prayer of or to be entreated by, the latter: to entreat. In the former case the noun governed by the verb פגע is in reality הפועל, the one that acts (that entreats), in the other case הפעול the object.
⁸ It can hardly be seen, how the reader could supply from the context, or from the signification of the verb פגע to meet, the relative sentence whom I should not cause joy by this, and it is very improbable that the prophet, if he had this sentence in his mind, should have dropped it, leaving it to the sagacity of the reader or hearer to supply it.

footnotes:
¹⁰ The question is, to which noun does the pronoun –ָהּ its in אחריתה refer, since there is no such noun directly preceding. According to I. E. it may refer either to the noun pride which is the true character of the words I shall be a mistress for ever, and can be substituted for them, whenever reference is made to them; or to a word like נחלתי my inheritance (ver. 6), which might easily be supplied from the preceding verse, as well as from the phrase I shall be a mistress for ever, viz., of Israel, the inheritance of the Lord.

¹¹ A. V., None beside me.

E. אפס signifies either the negatives not or none or the preposition beside; in the former case אפס ═ אפסי; in the latter אפסי means beside me; but it does not signify both simultaneously: none beside me. כתמם *In their perfection.* When the evils¹² were complete. תמם is an infinitive.¹³—All these evils came over thee for the multitude of thy sorceries, etc.

footnotes:
¹² It is not clear whether I. E. meant by the evils the threatened punishment of the loss of children and widowhood or the sins of Babylon mentioned vers. 6, sqq. In the former case I. E. would probably have said these evils (הרעות האלה); in the other case it is rather at variance with the words, וכל זה בעבור, All these evils came over thee for, since the cause of the threatened evils is stated already by the word כתמם when they were complete.
¹³ It is the infinitive of תמם with the pronominal suffix –ם their.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:1)


**ותבטחי ברעתך וגו'.** ודעתך, רמז לחכמה חיצונה מכחדת השם:


*And thy knowledge.* The prophet here alludes to that rationalism which denies the existence of God.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:2)


ונקמץ אל"ף **רואני** בעבור היותו מהגרון:


רוֹאׇגׅי *Seeth me.* The א has Kamez, because it is a guttural letter.¹⁴

¹⁴ See I. E. on 41:25 and note 31.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:10:3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:10:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:10:5)

ואפסי *And none.* It has here the same meaning as above (ver. 8). *I am, and none else beside me,* I am wise, and there is none as wise as I am.

¹⁵ A. V., Evil. I. E. supplies יום the day of because of the masculine form of the verb ובא.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:2)


**לא תדעי שחרה.** כלילה שאין לו שחר, והטעם אור:


לא תדעי שחרה *Thou shalt not know its light.*¹⁶ It will be like a night, which is not relieved by daylight; שחר means light.

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., From whence it riseth.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:3)


**הוה.** מגזרת ואתה הוה להם (נחמיה ו' ו'), לרע שיהיה פתאום, וכמוהו והותי במאזנים (איוב ו' ב'):


הׂוׇה *Mischief.* It is derived from הוה to become; comp. ואתה הוה that thou mayest become (Neh. 6:6);¹⁷ it signifies an evil that comes suddenly; of the same root is והותי and my calamity (Job 6:2).

footnotes:
¹⁷ A. V., That thou mayest be. Although the root הוה has the general meaning to become, both in the good sense and in the evil, the noun הוה may still be said to be derived from the same root, and to be used only in the bad sense.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:11:4)


**כפרה.** לתת כופר להסירה או לבטלה כמו ואיש חכם יכפרני' (משלי ט"ז י"ד):


כפרה To put it off by ransom; comp. כפר ransom (Ex. 30:12); or to annul it; comp. יכפרנה will remove it¹⁸ (Prov. 16:14).

footnotes:
¹⁸ A. V., Will pacify it.

### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:1)


**עצתיך.** מלה זרה, כי התחברו יחד סימן היחיד והרבים, וכמוהו והפלא יי את מכותך (דברים כ"ח נ"ט) ואם הוא הפך:


עֲצׇתׇיׅךְ *Thy counsels.* It is an irregular form, a combination of the singular and plural; comp. מֲכּׂתְךְ thy plagues (Deut. 28:59), which shows the same peculiarity in the opposite order.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ The possessive pronoun of the second person feminine is –ֵךְ or –ַיׅךְ the former, if connected with a noun in the singular, the other, if connected with a noun in the plural; the regular forms for the two words are accordingly עֲצָתֵךְ thy counsel, or עֲצוֹתַיׅךְ thy counsels; מַכְּתֵךְ thy plague, or מַכּוֹתַיִךְ thy plagues.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:2)


**הוברי שמים.** אין רע לו, וטעמו חכמי שמי', הם חכמי המזלות, ויש מי שהוציאוהו מגזרת ברור, והטעם שלא יוכלו לדעת חלקי השעו' אם לא יהיה אויר השמים ברור וזך, וזאת היא דרך רחוקה, כי ה"א הוא עיקר, והוא על משקל שומרי החומות (שיר השירים ה' ז'):


הברי שמים *Astrologers.* Some derive הברי from ברר to be clear, because the astrologers cannot know the exact time unless the heaven be clear and cloudless. This is far-fetched ; besides, the ה is radical, and the word is in form²¹ similar to שמרי watchmen of (Song 5:7).

footnotes:
²¹ That is in respect to letters and vowels. Although this is not yet sufficient to establish the identity of two forms, in this case it is sufficient, since the radical and preformative letters can in both words be easily distinguished and found as corresponding to each other.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:3)


**מודיעים לחדשים.** כן חכמתם, כי לא יסתכלו לדעת כל התולדות באויר ובמדינות, רק מעת התחברות המאורות, כי הם עיקר אומנותם, וזה טעם לחדשים:


מודיעים לחדשים *The monthly prognosticators.* This is their wisdom; they look to the stars for the knowledge of changes in the weather, and of events concerning the countries, only at the time of the conjunction of the planets, which is the source of their wisdom, and is here indicated by the word מאשר יבאו עליך ²².לחרשים

footnotes:
²² According to this explanation the literal translation of לחדשים is at each new revolution of the stars.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:13:4)


(רק) **מאשר יבואו עליך.** איננו דבק עם לחדשים, רק עם מלת ויושיעוך, ואם היא רחוקה, וכמוהו אשר אתם יורשים אותם את אלהיהם (דברים י"ב ב'):


*From these things that shall come upon thee.* This phrase is not to be joined with מודיעים לחדשים, but with ויושעוך and save thee, though distant from it; comp. אשד עבדו שם הגוים אשר אתם יורשים אותם את אלהיהם wherein the nations which ye shall possess, served their gods²³ (Deut. 12:2)

footnotes:
²³ The words את אלהיהם are not governed by the nearer ירשים, but by the more remote עבדו.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:14:1)


**הנה וגו'.** טעם אש מחנה האויב, כמו כי אש יצאה מחשבון (במדבר כ"א כ"ח):


*Fire.* The host of the enemy. Comp., There is a fire gone out of Heshbon (Num. 21:28).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 47:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/47:14:2)


**לחמם.** שם הפועל מפעלי הכפל, והוא שלם על משקל לשכב את בת יעקב (בראשית ל"ד ז') והטעם שימותו הם ולא תשאר להם שארית:


לחמם *To warm at.* It is infinitive of a verb (חמם) ע״ע, written in full, and similar in form²⁴ to לשכב to lie (Gen. 34:7).—The meaning of the whole sentence is: they will perish and no remnant will be left of them.

footnotes:
²⁴ The Pathah under ל in לַחמם instead of Hirek as in לִשכב is easily explained by the guttural letter by which the ל is followed; but not so regular is the change of Pathah in the second syllable into Kamez; and a remark of I. E. on this point might have been expected, if he had had the reading לחמָם; and not rather לחמַם.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:4:1)


**מדעתי וגו'.** כאשר ידעתי הראשונות, כן ידעתי כי קשה לב אתה, והוא מדבר למי שאינו מאמין בשם והוא מזרע יעקב, וכאילו גיד ברזל ערפך שלא תסור מדרכך, ומצחך [נחושה] שלא תבוש:


מדעתי *I know.*² As I knew the former things, so I know also that thou art hardened in thy heart. The second person refers to those Israelites who do not believe in God. *And thy neck is of iron.* Thou dost not depart from thy way, as if thy neck were of iron. *And thy brow brass.* And thou dost not blush, as if thy forehead were brass.
