⁷ According to this explanation the words I knew it are understood; and the past tenses ידעת שמעת, are here used instead of the future.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:8:2)


וטעם **מבטן.** כי ידעתיך מעת היותך, והפך זה בטרם אצרך בבטן (ירמיה א' ה') והנה קראו פושע, והטעם על הגזרות, ועוד אפר' זה בתחלת ספר ירמיהו:


*From the womb.* I knew thee¹ since thou camest to existence. In the opposite sense⁸ this expression is used in Jer. 1:5: Before I formed thee in the belly, I knew thee. *And thou wast called a transgressor from the womb.* This refers to the decrees of the Almighty.⁹ I shall fully explain this subject in my commentary on the book of Jeremiah.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹ The accents are against this explanation; they join מבטן with ופשע; ‘And one that transgresseth from the womb, that is a sinner from his earliest youth; while according to I. E. מבטן is joined with קרא לך : Thou art called from thy birth a sinner.
⁸ That is, in a good sense.
⁹ Which fix the destinies of man before he is born.
¹⁰ I. E. alludes here to the contradiction that seems to be implied in the fact, that on the one side the destinies of man are settled before his birth, and on the other side, free-will is conceded to him ; as here the one has been appointed to be a prophet, the other a sinner. I. E. promises to explain it fully in his commentary on Jeremiah, which seems either to have never been written, or if written, not to be known.

**לא פתחה אזנך.** עצמה, דרך קצרה:

¹¹ A. V., Thine ear was not opened.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:10:2

במצרף כסף═בכסף *In the silver refinery,*¹³ I have refined thee, by taking away the dross, that is, the wicked.

¹³ A.V., With silver.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:10:3)


**בחרתיך.** יש אומרים שהוא כמו בחנתיך, ואין רע לו, והנכון שהו' כמשמעו בחרתי לך כור עוני, לא מצרף כסף:


בחרתיך *I have chosen for thee,*¹⁴ Some say that בחנתיך═בחרתיך I have tried thee; in that sense the word is hap. leg.¹⁵ I take it in its usual meaning, I have chosen for thee to refine thee in the furnace of affliction, not in the silver refinery.

### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:11:1)


**למעני.** כי איך יחל, מבנין נפעל מפעלי הכפל, והיו"ד שבלמעני כמו ונשאר אני (יחזקאל ט' ח') והנני יוסיף על ימיך (ישעיהו ל"ח ה'):


יחל *Should be polluted.* It is the Niphal of a verb (חלל) ע״ע; as to the use of the first person in למעני and third person in יחל, comp. ונשאר אני and I was left (Ez. 9:8); הנני יוסיף behold, I will add (38:5).¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ I. E. supplies the personal pronoun אני before יחל, from the pronominal suffix of the first person in למעני and compares then the construction with נשאר אני I am left (Ez. 9:8) and הנני יוסיף (38:5). In all these cases the personal pronoun of the first person is connected as the subject with a verb in the third person singular. Comp. 38:5 and I. E. on 29:14, Note 22.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:2)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:3)


והנה טעם אף כי אני אמת ראשון ואחרון כי אני בראתי הכל:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:13:4)


וטעם **טפחה.**[כמו] אשר טפחתי ורביתי (איכה ב' כ"ב), ויש אומרים שמדד השמים בטפח, ומזה הכתוב למדו המפרשים כי השמים והארץ נבראו יחד לא זה קודם זה ודרך הפשט שאני עשיתים, ובעת שאקרא אליהם למלאות חפצי, יעמדו שניהם לפני כעבדים, וכמוהו למשפטיך עמדו היום (תהלים קי"ט צ"א) כי איך יקרא השם לאשר איננו:


טפחה *Hath put round,*¹⁹¹⁹ Comp. טפחתי I have swaddled (Lam. 2:22). Others explain it: Hath measured with the handbreadth יעמדו יחדיו —.(טֶפַח) *They stand up together.* From this phrase some of the commentators derive their opinion, that heaven and earth were created simultaneously, not consecutively.²⁰ The literal meaning, however, is: I have made them, and when I call them to do My will and desire they stand both before Me like servants; comp. למשפטיך עמדו they stand up²¹ according to Thy ordinances (Ps. 119:91). For else²² how should God call them, when not yet existing.

footnotes:
¹⁹ A. V., Hath spanned. According to I. E. טפח means to put round; but although he appears to reject here the derivation from טֶפַח hand breadth, in his commentary on Lamentations 2:20, he seems to adopt it.
¹⁹ A. V., Hath spanned. According to I. E. טפח means to put round; but although he appears to reject here the derivation from טֶפַח hand breadth, in his commentary on Lamentations 2:20, he seems to adopt it.
²⁰ When a dispute arose between the school of Hillel and that of Shammai about the order of the creation of heaven and earth, R. Shimeon ben Jochai settled the dispute, proving from this verse, I call unto them, that is, unto heaven and earth, they stood up together, that both were created at the same time. (Bereshith Rabba c. i.). Comp. Kimchi ad locum.
²¹ A. V., They continue. This quotation is to show that the verb עמד has also the meaning to stand as a servant, to attend. Comp. לפניו אשר עמדתי before whom I stand (1 Kings 17:1), that is, whose servant I am.
²² That is, if the words I call unto them had not the meaning, I give commands to them, as to my servants, but were the description of their creation, identical with I commanded them to come into existence.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:16:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:16:2)


**לא מראש וגו'.** מבתחלה לא אמרתי זה הסוד וזאת הגזירה בסתר:


*I have not spoken in secret from the beginning* of this plan and this divine decree.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 48:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/48:16:3)


**מעת היותה וגו'.** אמר הגאון מכאן רמז כי הנשמה קודם הגוף, ולא אמר כלום, כי הנה הכתוב אומר בתחילה, עתה נבראו ולא מאז, והטעם כאשר נגזרה זאת הגזרה שיצאה מפי השם, אל המלאכים הם השרים הממונים על המלכיות, כאשר הוא כתוב בספר דניאל (דניאל י' כ') שם הייתי גם אני:


*From the time that it was, there was I*. The Gaon finds here an indication that the soul exists before the body; but he is wrong, because it is said, They are decreed now, and not from the beginning²³ a time anterior to the birth of the prophet, and the pronoun I in the phrase, There am I, to the soul of the prophet. If this were the correct explanation, the prophet implied in these words his adherence to the theory of the pre-existence of the soul. But I. E. properly rejects this explanation, since ver. 7, quoted by him, proves that the words, from the beginning, do not refer to a very remote time, but to a period within the lifetime of the prophet. (ver. 7). The meaning of the sentence is the following: When this decree was made by God unto the angels,²⁴ the representatives of the respective countries (comp. Dan. 10:20), I was also there.

footnotes:
²³ According to the Gaon, the words From the time that it was, refer to a very remote time, indicated in the phrase from the beginning, which precedes, i.e.,
²⁴ The Hebrew text has the words אלה המלאכים these angels, which cannot be properly connected with the words which precede, nor with those that follow. אלה is probably a corruption of אֶל unto. The angels receive from the Almighty the power to act, with regard to a certain event, and this authorisation is called by I. E. The decree of the Almighty. See his commentary on 9:7, and note 13.

²⁵ God had sent me to proclaim the future events; and He sent His angel to verify the words of the prophet. It is however possible, that I. E. connects ורוחו with שם אני ; There was I and His angel.

**אין וגו'.** יש אומרים כי אין שלום לרשעים מישר', ויתכן שיהיה רמז לבבליים, כי זאת הטובה תהיה לישראל, ואין שלום לבבליים:


*There is no peace unto the wicked,* that is, unto the wicked of Israel, as some explain, or unto the Babylonians; for this blessing shall be for Israel alone, but there shall be no peace for the Babylonians.



## Chapter 49


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:1)


**שמעו.** אלה דברי הנביא:


*Unto me,* that is unto the prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:2)


**מרחוק.** היושבים בארץ רחוק, או מרחו' על דבר העתיד:


*From far.* That live far away; or things that will happen in remote future.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:1:3)


**מבט' קראני.** אפרשנו בספר ירמיה:


*Hath called me from the birth,* I shall explain this in the commentary on Jer. 1:2.¹

footnotes:
¹ Comp. c. xlviii. Note 10.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:1)


**וישם פי כחרב חדה.** לדבר צחות, או חדה על נבואתו על בבל, והטעם אע"פ ששם פי כחרב חדה החביאני השם בצל ידו, ולא יכלו לי הבבליים ורשעי ישראל:


*And He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword,* to speak elegantly; or, as was the case in his prophecies against Babylon, to speak sharply; and the meaning of the whole phrase is accordingly : Although God has made my mouth like a sharp sword against the Babylonians, neither the Babylonians nor the wicked men in Israel, could do any harm to me,


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:2)


והנה **החביאני** כמו נדן לחרב, והעד ובאשפתו:


because God hath hid me in the shadow of His hand, which is to the prophet as the sheath to the sword; comp. in His quiver hath he hid me.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:2:3)


**ברור.** זך נראה:


ברור *Polished*, when seen.²

footnotes:
² I. E. adds נראה seen, in order to show more clearly the similarity between the two figures. The prophet is compared with a sword which is sharp to inflict wounds, but is well protected by its sheath from receiving injury, and with an arrow, which is shining when let loose, but is at other times kept well in its quiver.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:3:1)


**ויאמר לי.** השם:


*And said*. And God said. ישראל


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:3:2)


**עבדי אתה [ישראל.** אתה], הוא מזרע ישראל אשר בך אתפאר, או אתה ישראל שאתה נחשב בעיני ככל ישראל, והוא הנכון:


*Israel*.³ That is, Thou art an Israelite of whom I am proud; or Thou art Israel, thou art estimated in mine eyes like all Israelites together. I prefer this latter explanation.

footnotes:
³ A. V., O Israel.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:1)


**ואני.** גם אלה דברי הנביא בעד נפשו:


*Then I said*. Then I, the prophet, said.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:2)


**אמרתי.** בלבי:


*I said* to myself,


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:3)


**לריק יגעתי.** שהוגעתי נפשי להוכיח את ישראל ולא שמעו:


*I have laboured in vain*. I have troubled myself in vain to rebuke Israel; they do not hearken.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:4:4)


**אכן משפטי.** אצל השם שיתן לי שכר על יגיעתי, וככה ופעולתי כמו ולא תלין פעולת שכיר (ויקרא י"ט י"ג):


*My judgment is with God*. He will reward me for my trouble. ופעלתי *And my wages*.⁴ Comp. שביר פעלת the wages of one that is hired (Lev. 19:13)

footnotes:
⁴ A. V., And my work.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:5:1)


**ועתה.** יצרי, השם יצרני להוכיח את ישראל עד שישובו אל השם:


*That formed me*, etc. God formed me, that I should rebuke Israel, till they returned to Him.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:5:2)


**לא יאסף.** השרש שהוא בוי"ו כאשר הוא קרי, וכמוהו הוא עשנו ולא אנחנו (תהלים ק' ג') וחבריהם, והגאון אמר לא יאסף לא ימות, כי מנהגו לפרש כדרך קרי וכדרך כתיב, והנכון מה שאמרתי, רק האל"ף הכתוב הוא תחת וי"ו, כאשר פירש ר' יהודה המדקדק נ"ע:


לא *Unto him*.⁵ The original reading is לו unto him, as the Masorah recommends; comp. Ps. 100:5; there are some more instances of the same kind. According to the Gaon, the meaning of לא יאסף is: Will not die; he generally explains both the Keri and the Ketib;¹ but what I said, is nevertheless right, and לא of the text is the same as לו, as the Grammarian R. Jehudah explained.⁶

footnotes:
⁵ A. V., Not.
¹ Comp. c. ix. Note 2.
⁶ The quiescent letter after Holem (ō) which is also called mater lectionis, is generally ו, but sometimes א, so that לא can sometimes he written for לו. See Two Treatises, etc. ed. John W. Nutt, p. 11 (p. 13 in the Engl. Transl.).

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:3)


והטעם כי לא תשיב ישראל לבדם, רק נתתיך לאור גוים:


Not alone wilt thou bring Israel back, but I will give thee for a light of nations.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:6:4)


**להיות ישועתי.** להשמיעה קודם היותה:


להיות ישועתי. *That my salvation may be*,⁸ that is, that my salvation maybe published before it comes, *unto the end of the earth*

footnotes:

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:1)


**כה וגו'.** גם אלה דברי הנביא וככה הוא, כה אמר השם לי, שאני בזוי נפש אצל הרשעים, והנה לבזה נפש שם התאר:


*Thus saith the Lord*, etc. The prophet continues to speak of himself: Thus says the Lord unto me, who am despised of the wicked men. לבזה *To him who is despised*. בזה is an adjective.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:2)


**למתעב גוי.** פועל יוצא לשנים פעולים, שהנביא ידבר דברים שיתעבוהו בשבילם הגוים, או יהיה למתעב גוי שהנביא יתעב כל גוי:


מתעב It is either a causative verb, meaning: causing to abhor, that is, saying things, for which the nations abhor him; or a transitive verb: abhorring, that is, abhorring all idolaters.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:3)


**לעבד מושלים.** והטעם כפי מחשבת גולי ישראל, או רמז על הבבליים והוא הנכון:


*To a servant of rulers*, that is of the nobles of Israel, as they consider themselves, or of the Babylonians. The latter rendering is preferable.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:4)


**מלכים יראו וקמו.** הנה כבר רמזתי לך זה הסוד בחצי הספר (ישעיהו מ' א'), ועל דעת רבים כי המלכים כמו כורש כאשר ישמע דברי הנביא, יקום וישתחוה:


*Kings shall see and arise*. I have already alluded to the inference that may be drawn from those words (40:1). Most of the commentators explain this sentence thus: Kings, like Cyrus, will rise and worship, when they hear the words of the prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:5)


**למען יי.** כי נאמן בדברו:


*Because of the Lord*. For He remains faithful to His word.—


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:7:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:7:6)


והנה כ"ף **ויבחרך** לעד על יושר זה הפירוש:


The suffix ך in ויבחרך and He chose thee,⁹ shows that this explanation is right.¹⁰

footnotes:
⁹ A. V., And he shall choose thee.
¹⁰ The use of the pronoun of the second person, proves according to I. E. that the prophet himself is addressed, and that he is personally to receive compensation for the contempt and scorn with which the people received his prophecies. See I. E. on 40:1.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:8:1)


**בעת רצון עניתיך.** גם זה עד על הרמז, ורבים אמרו כי כ"ף עניתיך שב אל כורש, והנה אין הפרשה דבקה, ורבי משה אמר כי בי"ת בעת רצון בבי"ת במרחב יה (תהלים קי"ח ה'), ואיננו רחוק:


בעת רצון עניתיך *In an acceptable time I have heard thee*. This expression is likewise a proof of the correctness of my opinion.¹¹ Many, in opposition to the context, refer the pronoun thee to Cyrus. R. Moses thinks that the preposition ב in בעת רצון has the same meaning as in במרחב יה (Ps. 118:5), namely: with. It is not at all unlikely that his opinion is right.

footnotes:
¹¹ See preceding note. The meaning of the phrase according to I. E. is: In the time of favour, viz., for the Israelites, when their redemption was prepared, I have also heard thee, the prophet, and decreed to cause thee to be honoured by all.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:9:1)


**לאמר.** רמז על ישראל שהתנבא הנביא קודם הגאולה:


*That thou mayest say*, etc. This shows that the prophet announced this to the Jews before they returned from the Babylonian exile.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:9:2)


**ובכל שפיים מרעיתם.** ימצאו מרעיתם:


*And their pastures in all high places*. And they shall find their pastures, etc.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:10:1)


**לא וגו'.** בשובם אל ציון:


*They will not*, etc. When they return to Zion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:10:2)


**שרב.** כמו חורב, והיה שרב (ישעיהו ל"ה ז'), והמכה לשמש, כמו יומם השמש לא יככה (תהלים קכ"א ו'):


שרב *Heat*. Comp. 35:7. *Nor the sun smite them*. Comp. The sun shall not smite thee by day (Ps. 121:6)



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:11:1)


**ושמתי כל הרי לדרך.** שישפלו ההרים והמסלות ירומו, והנה הם בשפלה:


*And I will make all my mountains a way*, etc. The mountains will be lowered, and the paths which are low will be exalted.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:11:2)


ובאה מלת **ירומון** עם מסילות כמו אם תמצאו את דודי (שיר השירים ט' ח'), והעיקר אחר שהכל לשון רבים לא יחושו לאמר על נקבות בלשון זכרים, ויש אומרים כי טעם כל הרי שהשבים יהיו רבים עד שילכו על ההרים, ויפרשו ירומון על השבים כאילו הוא כן ועל מסלותי ירומון:


As to the use of the masculine plural ירומון, together with the feminine מסלות, comp. תמצאו ye (daughters of Jerusalem) find (Song 5:8). The origin of the seeming irregularity is to be found in the indifference of the Hebrews as to the use of the plural masculine for the feminine, so long as the idea of plurality is clearly expressed.¹² Others explain the verse thus: Those that will return, will be so numerous, that they will have to walk high on the mountains.¹³ According to their opinion ירמון means: they—that will return—will be high, as if the prophet said: they will walk high on my paths (ועל מסלתי)

footnotes:
¹² According to this remark, the distinction between the masculine and feminine is in the plural often neglected; Comp. the third person plural past, and the second person plural past with a pronominal suffix.
¹³ That is, the roads between the mountains will not be wide enough for all the people that will return; part of the people will therefore be compelled to walk on the mountains on both sides of the road.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:1)


**הנה.** מרחוק יבאו, ממזרח:


*From far*, from the east.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ The phrase From far, is explained to refer to The east, because north and west are directly mentioned, and Sinim is supposed by I. E. to be in the south. Where three sides are mentioned, it may be expected, that the fourth will likewise be found.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:2)


**[מצפון].** היא בבל:


*From the north*, from Babylon.¹

footnotes:
¹ Babylon is here described to be in the north; but in his remark on 43:5, I. E. says, that it is in the east. It was perhaps north-east of Palestine. See c. xliii. Note 2a.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:3)


**ומים.** אשור כאשר הוא כתיב והסב לב מלך אשור (עזרא ו' כ"ב):


*From the west*. From Assyria. Comp. Ezr. 6:22.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁵ See I. E. on 43:5, and Notes 3 and 4.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:12:4)


**מארץ סינים.** מפאת מצרים אולי הסנה מזאת הגזירה:


מארץ סינים *From the land of Sinim*. A land near Egypt. The name סינים is perhaps connected with סנה bush.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ This remark seems to be intended as a hint where to place the land of Sinim, indicating that Mount Horeb is a part of it; because simply to say, that סינים means perhaps bushes would be quite superfluous, and moreover, I. E. would in that case rather have said והוא מגזרת סנה it is derived from סנה ‘bush,’ than הסנה מזאת הגזרה, the word סנה is of the same root.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:13:1)


**רנו וגו'.** דרך משל, או רננת שמים להיות האויר זך והארץ לתת צמח וכן ההרים:


*Sing*, etc. This is a figurative expression; or¹⁷ the purity of the air is to be considered as the singing of the heavens, the productiveness of the fields and gardens as the singing of the earth, and the singing of the mountains can be explained in a similar way.

footnotes:
¹⁷ According to the second explanation the expression must also be figurative; the difference between the two explanations is, that according to the former the nouns heaven, earth, mountains, are used here in a figurative sense, signifying all classes of people; according to the latter the verb sing has a figurative meaning.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:14:1)


**ותאמר.** קודם הגולה היתה אומרת ציון, כי יי שכחה, וטעם ציון כנסת ישראל:


*But Zion said* before the redemption,¹⁸ that the Lord forgot her. *Zion*. The congregation of Israel.¹

footnotes:
¹⁸ The Hebrew text has קודם הגולה but it may be inferred from the context, that I. E. meant here קודם הגאולה before the redemption.
¹ By this remark I. E. probably intends to say that Zion here is not the representative of the kingdom of Judah alone, but of all the tribes of Israel, so that this prediction might as well refer to the redemption from the Babylonian exile as to the period of Messiah. See I. E. on 40:1.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:1)


**התשכח.** בעבור שהשם שם בתולדת כל הנקבות לרחם על ילדיהן אמר כן:


*Can a woman*, etc. This is mentioned, because God has given to woman a natural disposition to have pity on her children.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:2)


**עולה.** כמו עולל, וכן עול ימים וזקן (ישעיהו ס"ה כ'):


עולל═עול *Sucking child*. Comp. Jer. 6:11; Is. 65:20.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:3)


**מרחם בן בטנה.** הטעם כפול:


*That she should not have compassion*, etc. Repetition of the same idea.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:15:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:4)


**גם אלה תשכחנה.** גם יש נשים אכזריות שתשכחנה בניהן, ויתכן שתשכחנה אלה:


גם אלח תשכחנה *Yea, they may forget*. There are cruel women, that forget their children or themselves;¹⁹ or there are women that forget these,¹

footnotes:
¹⁹ This is the translation according to the Hebrew text או עצמן; the question, however, is not whether they forget themselves, but whether they forget their children. It is possible that עצמן is a corruption of עולליהן their sucking children.
¹ According to the first explanation the pronoun אלה these is the subject of the sentence, and refers to the women; according to the second to the sucking child and the son of her womb.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:15:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:15:5)


**ואנכי לא אשכחך.** וטעם עולה כי על הקטן תרחם יותר כי אין בו כח:


yet will I not forget thee. Her sucking child is mentioned, because the mother has usually more compassion for the little one that has no strength.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:16:1)


**הן.** אמר הגאון כי על כפים העבים, ולפי דעתי שהכתוב דבר על לשון בני אדם, כי על כפים חקותיך שאראה אותך תמיד, והעד חצי פסוק כמשפט:


*I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands*. According to the Gaon, the clouds are meant by the palms of my hand;²⁰ but I say it is an anthropomorphism, meaning: I shall see thee continually; the second part of the verse, the parallelism of which divides it into two similar halves, confirms the correctness of this explanation.

footnotes:
²⁰ Comp. Rashi ad locum (second explanation), and I. E. on Job 36:34.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:17:1)


**מהרו וגו'.** הנה באו בניך, ויצאו ממך כל מהרסיך:


*Thy children*, etc. Thy children have come, and all thy destroyers shall go away from thee.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:1)


**כלם.** המ"ם סימן בניך, ויאמר רבי משה הכהן ז"ל כי טעם כלם על בניך ועל מהרסיך, והטעם על הרשעים, ויפרש יצאו כמו פועל עבר ואין צורך:


*All of them*. All of thy children.²¹ R. Moses Hakkohen explains the expression thus: Thy children as well as thy destroyers, that is, the wicked, gathered themselves, etc. According to this explanation the future יֵצֵאוּ is used instead of the past יׇצׇאוּ.²² But it is not necessary to assume this irregularity here.

footnotes:
²¹ According to I. E. the pronoun them (–ׇ ם in כֻּלׇּם) refers to thy children of the preceding verse, though separated from it by the sentence thy destroyers and they that made thee waste shall go forth of thee.
²² The sense of ver. 17 and ver. 18 accordingly is: Thy children make haste, even thy destroyers, etc., that had gone away from thee, all of them now come back unto thee, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:2)


**חי אני.** והנה גזרה שלא תבטל כאשר אני חי כן זה יהיה אמת:


*As I live*. The decree shall not be annulled; as truly as I am living, it will be acted upon.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:18:3)


**ותקשרים ככלה.** כקישורי כלה בצואר:


כקשורי כלה ═ ככלה As the ornament of the bride round her neck.²³

footnotes:
²³ A. V., As a bride doeth. I. E. supplies the noun קשורי ornament, from the preceding verb ותקשרים and bind them. He repeatedly mentions the rule, that every verb implies a verbal noun: so here the noun קשורים is contained in the verb; to this rule another must be added, which is here made use of, namely the rule of ellipsis: מושך עצמו ואחר עמו. A word, mentioned in one sentence, or in one part of the sentence, is sometimes meant for the next likewise.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:19:1)


**כי [חרבתיך].** תחת חרבותיך, וכמוהו האתן בכורי פשעי [מיכה ו' ז'], ונשלמה פרים שפתינו (הושע י"ד ג'), או כי עד הנה היו כן:


תחת חרבותיך ═ חרבותיך Instead of Thy waste places.²⁴ Comp. פשעי for my transgressions (Mic. 6:7); פרים instead of calves (Hos. 14:31.) The verse can also be explained thus: They were thy waste places before, but now,

footnotes:
²⁴ A. V., Thy waste places. I. E. supplies the preposition תחת instead of, because the second person fem. תצרי does not agree with the plural חרבותיך ,שממתיך.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:19:2)


**תצרי מיושב.** מרוב היושבים, והם כלם בניך, על כן (טעם) ורחקו מבלעיך:


*Thou shalt be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants*, by reason of the multitude of inhabitants, all of whom are thy children; because they that swallowed them up, will be far away.



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:20:1)


**גשה.** לשם בשבילי:


גשה לי *Give place unto me*. Lit. Go thither for my sake. Comp. גש הלאה stand back (Gen. 19:9)



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:1)


**ואמרת.** וגלמודה, יושבת בדד, וכמוהו יהי גלמוד (איוב ג' ז'), ושורש המלה מארבע אותיות והוא תאר השם:


נלמודה *Desolate*. Remaining lonely; comp. גלמוד solitary (Job 3:7). It is an adjective, of a quadriliteral root.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:2)


**סורה.** שם התאר שסרה ממקומה, ולא יתכן היותו פעול, כי סר איננו מהפעלים היוצאים:


וסורה *And removing to and fro*. It is an adjective, and not a participle passive;²⁵ for סור to depart is a neuter verb.

footnotes:
²⁵ Comp. Rashi ad locum.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:21:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:21:3)


**ואלה איפה הם.** שתי מלות כטעם איו:


איפה *where*. It is a compound of two words אי and פה



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:1)


**אשא אל גוים ידי.** כאדם שישא ידו ויראהו, וכן ארים נסי והטעם שאודיע זאת הישועה:


*Behold, I will lift up My hand*, etc. As a man lifts up his hand, that he may be seen. This phrase as well as that which follows: *And set up my standard*, are the same as I shall make known this my salvation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:2)


**והביאו.** הגוים בניך:


*And they shall bring thy sons*. By they the Non-Israelites are to be understood.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:22:3)


**בחוצן.** כמו גם חצני נערתי (נחמיה ה' י"ג):


בחוצן *In their lap*.²⁶ Comp. חצני my lap (Neh. 5:13)

footnotes:
²⁶ A. V., In their arms.



### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:23:1)


**והיו מלכים אומניך.** כמו אומן את הדסה (אסתר ב' ז'), זה דרך משל לרוב הכבוד שיהיה להן:


אומניך *Thy nursing fathers*. Comp. ויהי אמן and he brought up (Est. 2:7). It is a figurative expression for the great honour which will be shown to Israel.



### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:1)


**היוקח וגו'.** דברי הנביא ידבר בעד ישראל, שהיו אומרים איך יצאו ישראל מיד הגוים:


*Shall the prey*, etc. These words are put into the mouth of Israel by the prophet. How is it possible, the people ask, that Israel should be delivered from the power of the heathen nations ?


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:2)


**היוקח מגבור.** המלקוח שלקח והוא השבי:


המלקח *The prey*, which he has taken, that is, the captives.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:24:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:24:3)


**ואם שבי צדיק ימלט.** בעבור צדקתו, אחר שלקחו הגבור:


ואם שבי צדיק ימלט *Or shall the righteous*²⁷ *captive be delivered*, because of his righteousness, after having been taken by the mighty.

footnotes:
²⁷ A. V., Lawful.



### Verse 25

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:25:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:1)


**כי כה אמר יי.** השבי, שלקח הגבור, יוקח ממנו:


*The captive of the mighty*. The captive which the mighty man has taken, will be taken away from him.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:25:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:2)


**עריץ.** כמו גבור, והוא תאר השם כמלת אימים (בראשית י"ד ה'), הנה הוא יוצא:


עריץ *The terrible*. It is an adjective with transitive meaning: causing terror; comp. אימים (Gen. 14:5).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:25:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:25:3)


**ועוד [את יריבך אנכי אריב].** כי אעשה מריבה עם אנשי ריבך, ורבים אמרו כי [יריבך] שרשו מבעלי היו"ד בראשונה, ואחרים אמרו שהוא הפוך, ויאמר הירושלמי כי תחסר מלת אשר כאילו אמר ועם אשר יריבך, וישם היו"ד שהוא לעתיד, והנה שכח ריבה יי את יריבי (תהלים ל"ה א'), והכלל שהי' מלה זרה:


Moreover, *I will contend with him that contendeth with thee*. I shall make war against those that attack thee. יריבך *that contendeth with thee*. Some derive it from ירב; others by metathesis from ריב;²⁸ according to the Jerusalemite²⁹ the relative אשר who must be supplied before יריבך, which he explains to be the third person singular masculine future of ריב; he overlooked, however, the parallel instance of יריבי that strive with me (Ps. 35:1).³⁰ In short it is an irregular form.

footnotes:
²⁸ There is in fact no difference between the two views, whether we assume a new root ירב which has the same meaning as ריב, or say that it is the same root, the י having changed its place; in both cases יריב is a noun, meaning he that contendeth.
²⁹ See I. E. on 28:12, and note 13.
³⁰ This form cannot be explained to be the future, since in that case it would be יְרִיבֵנִי he that contends with me, or יְרִיבוּנִי they that contend with me.



### Verse 26

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:26:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:26:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:26:1)


**והאכלתי מוניך.** מגזרת לא תונו איש את עמיתו (ויקרא כ"ה י"ז), ואחרים אמרו סופריך, כמו על ידי מונה (ירמיה ל"ג י"ג) שישראל נמשל לצאן:


מוניך *That oppress thee*. Comp. ולא תגו ye shall not oppress (Lev. 25:17). Others say that it means: thy numberers, comparing it with מונה that telleth (Jer. 33:13), because Israel is compared to a flock of sheep.³¹

footnotes:
³¹ It is true that Israel is often compared by the prophets and poets to a flock of sheep; but in this chapter this is not the case, and the verb מוניך, if taken in this figurative sense, would here be too isolated, and out of place.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 49:26:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:26:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/49:26:2)


**דמם.** מדמם, והוא דרך צחות:


מדמם = דמם *With their own blood*. An ellipsis is as frequently found in poetry.



## Chapter 50


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:1:1)


**כריתות.** גט כריתות:


ספר כריתות Bill of divorcement.¹

footnotes:
¹ The Hebrew text has the words גט כריתות אמכם ובין אשתו. There is no doubt that this passage is corrupt; the original words were perhaps: כריתות אמכם ֗ גט בין איש ובין אשתו; or כריתות ֗ גט ׃ אמכם ֗ ובין אישה the latter suggestion has been adopted for the translation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:1:2)


**אמכם.** ובין אשתו, והנה זה יכחיש דברי ירמיה, ואתן את ספר כריתותיה אליה (ירמיה ג' ח'), והתשובה כי ירמיהו דבר על מלכות ישראל שלעולם לא תקום וכמוהו לא תוסיף קום (עמוס ח' ב'), וישעיהו דבר על מלכות דוד שממנו יהיה משיח:


*Of your mother* and her husband.—This verse seems to contradict the prophecy of Jeremiah, I had put her away and given her a bill of divorce (3:8); but in fact the latter refers to the kingdom of the ten tribes which will never again be established; comp. She shall no more rise (Am. 5:2); but Isaiah speaks of the kingdom of the house of David, which will be restored by Messiah.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:2:1)


**מדוע באתי.** רמז לנביאים שהתנבאו, אולי ישובו ישראל לשם:


*Wherefore when I come*, etc. This verse proves that already prophets have tried to make Israel return to the Lord.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:2:2)


**הן בגערתי וגו'.** הנה ראיה גמורה שלא תקצר ידי מפדות:


*Behold I dry up*, etc. This proves that the power of God will not fail in redeeming Israel.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:3:1)


**אלביש שמים קדרות.** מלבוש קדרות, הטעם על העבים, ויש אומרים על קדרות השמש כאשר תקדר כולה בחצי היום, וכאילו שק כסותם, בעבור שהשק הוא שחור:


מלבוש קדרׂות ═ קדרות *With black cloth*,² that is, with clouds. Some understand it to refer to an eclipse of the sun, when the sky becomes obscure in the middle of the day, and appears as if covered with sackcloth, which is usually black.

footnotes:
² A. V., With blackness. See c. xlix. Note 23.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:1)


**יי וגו'.** אלה דברי הנביא:


*The Lord hath given me*, etc. The first person refers to the prophet.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:2)


**למודים.** מתואר השם, והעד למוד מדבר (ירמיה ב' כ"ד), לשמוע כלמודים. **ולעות** דבוק עם לדעת [ומלת לעות מגזרת עת]. **והטעם יעף.** לב התלמיד כאשר ילמד דברים קשים ויעף וילאה:


למודים *Learning*.³³. It is an adjective; comp. למד מדבר used to the wilderness (Jer. 2:24); כלמדים as the pupils (at the end of this verse).

footnotes:
³ A. V., Learned.
³ A. V., Learned4The noun which is described by this attribute must be supplied; the adjective may therefore be considered as a substantive meaning the pupils. See c. iii. Note 5.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:3)


והנה **לעות.** לשום עת או היא מלה זרה אין רע לה:


לדעת לעות את יעף דבר *That I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary*. The infinitive לעות is governed by לדעת to know; it is derived from עת time, or it is hap. leg.⁵ By him that is weary, the pupil is meant, who has a hard lesson to learn,⁶ of which he soon becomes tired and weary.

footnotes:
⁵ The Hebrew text seems here to be corrupt. The words והנה לעות לשון עת are written twice, and the explanation of the word יעף which should follow that of לעות, is put in the middle. It may therefore be suggested, that the words והנה לעות לשון עת או היא מלה זרה אין רע לה were intended to be substituted for והנה לעות לשון עת, but were by some misunderstanding misplaced, while the original phrase was allowed to occupy its position. The translation has been made according to this supposition.
⁶ The Hebrew text has דברים קיצים, but יצ seems to be nothing but a mutilated ש; and the original form of the phrase probably was דברים קשים difficult things.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:4:4)


וטעם **יעיר וגו'.** כי יי יעיר אותי בבקר בבקר, ופירוש יעירני שיעיר אזני שאהיה שומע כלימודים, והנה אני תלמיד לשם:


*He wakeneth*, etc. The Lord stirreth me up every morning; he stirreth up my ear that I may listen as pupils do; for I am a pupil of the Lord.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:5:1)


**יי וגו'.** אחר שהשם פתח אזני שגלה סודו לי, לא מריתי אני להיות שלוחו:


*The Lord God hath opened mine ear*, etc. Since the Lord hath opened mine ear, and revealed His plan to me, I have not objected to be His messenger.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:6:1)


**גוי וגו'.** לא חששתי אם אני נתתי על שמו גוי למכים:


*I gave my back*, etc. I did not care that I had to expose my back to strokes for the sake of His name.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:7:1)


**ואדני יי יעזר לי על כן לא נכלמתי.** והטעם כי השם יקיי' כל דברי נבואתי:


*I shall not be ashamed*. God will fulfil all the words prophesied by me.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:8:1)


**קרוב מצדיקי.** קרוב הוא העת שאראה אני צדיק בדברי הנבואות, אז אומר מי יריב אתי:


*Near is*, etc. Near is the time, when I shall appear as justified in my prophecies; then I shall say, Who will, etc.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:9:1)


**הן וגו'.** ואחר שהשם עזרני מי הוא ירשיעני, ואלה שהם מרשיעים אותי בפה, והם כולם כבגד יבלו, כטעם יאבדו:


*Behold the Lord*, etc. Since God assists me, who will condemn me ? And all those that condemn me by their words, they will wax old as a garment. יבלו *They shall wax old*. They shall perish.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:10:1)


**מי [בכם].** ידבר הנביא עם אלה:


*Who is amongst you*, etc. The prophet now addresses those same people, that condemn him.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:10:2)


**אשר הלך חשכים.** שב אל ירא השם, שלא יבקש גדולות ותאות העולם, יבטח בשם, ויש אומר כי אשר הלך חשכים [שב אל ירא השם], תאר לעבדו שהוא הנביא, והטעם, מי גם בכם, כמו אין בכם, בעבור שראיתם הנביא אין לו מעלה בעולם הזה, וזה הוא הנכון בעבור הכתוב הבא אחריו:


*That walked in darkness*, etc. The relative pronoun refers to ירא יי him that feareth the Lord. The meaning of the sentence is, Who is among you, etc., that does not run after material honours and pleasures; let him trust in the Lord, etc.⁷ According to others, the words that walketh in darkness, describe His servant, the prophet,⁸ and the meaning of the whole sentence is, Who is among you, etc., that is, there is none among you, that feareth the Lord, because you see the prophet obtaining no honours from the people. This is the right explanation, and it is confirmed by the words which follow.

footnotes:
⁷ According to this explanation, vers. 10 qualifies the term כלם all of them of the preceding verse. If there be among them any one that acts according to the words of the Lord taught by the prophet, he may trust in the Lord, that he will be saved, and will not be involved in the threatened punishment.
⁸ According to this explanation, this verse contains a rhetorical question, establishing the correctness of the term all of them. There is none among them that acts according to the words of the prophet, who is described here to be walking in darkness, that is, to be exposed to all kinds of trouble and annoyance, but who trusts in the Lord that he will surely be relieved of it.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:11:1)


**מאזרי זיקות.** כמו שביבים, מטעם הפרשה, הטעם נפשכם:


זיקות *Sparks*. The meaning of the word must be found from the context.⁹ מאזרי *Who compass* yourselves.¹⁰

footnotes:
⁹ First, it corresponds to אש fire in the parallel phrase; secondly, it is connected with the verb בערתם ye have kindled.
¹⁰ The verb אזר to compass about, governs two accusatives, the one, זיקות sparks, is the thing which is put round, the other, נפשבם yourselves, which is understood, is the thing round which it is put By the omission of נפשכם the verb becomes similar to a reflective verb.

**מידי היתה.** גזרה:


*This*. This decree.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 50:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/50:11:3)


**למעצבה תשכבון.** בעצבון תמותון, כמו וישכב דוד (מלכים א' ב' י') ורבים כן:


למעצבה תשכבון *Ye shall lie down in sorrow*. You shall die in sorrow. Comp. וישכב דוד and David slept, that is, and David died (1 Kings 2:10); there are, besides, a great many instances of the use of the verb שכב in this sense.

### Verse 1

**שמעו.** שב לדבר עם הטובים, המאמינים בדברי הנביא:


*Hearken to me*. The prophet speaks now to the good people, who believe in the words of the prophets.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:2)


וטעם **והביטו** כמו אל תתמהו איך תשוב ציון מלאה בנים כאשר היתה:


*Look*, etc. Be not surprised how Zion can again be filled with her children as before, but look, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:3)


**הביטו אל צור.** כמו הנני עומד לפניך שם על הצור (שמות י"ז ו'):


*Look unto the rock*. Comp. Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock (Ex. 18:6).¹

footnotes:
¹ By this quotation I. E. intends to prove the use of phrases like to stand upon the rock, to look unto the rock in a figurative sense. The phrase quoted from Exodus refers to God, and can therefore by no means be taken in its literal meaning.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:4)


**[חצבתם].** שחצבתם ממנו וזהו אברהם:


*Unto the rock*. Unto the name of the rock,¹ of which you are hewn; that is, unto the name of Abraham.

footnotes:
¹ This is the literal translation of the Hebrew text; but it is possible that the word שם is a superfluous repetition of the word שׇם in the preceding phrase; if that be the case, the translation must be thus: ממנו צור שחצבתם ═ צור חצבתם the rock of which you are hewn, and that is Abraham.

**ואל מקבת בור.** מגזרת ויקב חור בדלתו (מלכים ב' י"ב י'):


מקבת *The hole*. Comp. ויקב and bored (2 Kings 12:10).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:1:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:1:6)

### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:2:1)


**הביטו.** אמר רבי יונה כי תחוללכם פועל עתיד כמו תשובבכם, תחת פועל עבר חוללתכם, ויאמר רבי משה הכהן כי הוא תואר השם, ואם אין על משקלו:


תחוללכם *That bare you*. According to R. Jonah, it is future, like ²,תשובבכם instead of the past חוללתכם. R. Moses Hakkohen believes it to be an adjective, although there is no other adjective of the same form.³

² This word is not to be found in the Bible; very probably another word was intended by I. E.

וַאֲבׇרְכֵהוּ *And blessed him*. The ו has Pathah, because ואברכהו is future: it means, I told him that I should bless him; and so it was. In the same way.

*The Lord shall comfort Zion*, etc. Thus the connection of this verse with the preceding one is explained. *He hath comforted all her waste places*, by the multitude of her children, of her inhabitants.

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:6:1)


**שאו וגו'.** מזה הפסוק למדו אנשי תושיה, כי נשמת האדם עומדת, ודברם אמת, לכן אין טעם הפסוק כן, והשמים הוא הרקיע והארץ היא מיושבת, וישועת השם ואמונתו וצדקתו לעולם עומדת:


*Lift up your eyes*, etc. Philosophers derive from this verse the doctrine of the immortality of the soul of man;⁶ their doctrine is right; but this verse certainly does not contain it. השמים The sky.⁷ הארץ The inhabited part of the earth. Both may perish, but the salvation of the Lord, His faithfulness, His righteousness remains⁸ for ever.

footnotes:
⁶ If all die, and the salvation of the Lord still remains, there must be left something, that is to enjoy that salvation; if the bodies die, the souls are supposed to remain alive. According to I. ⁷ A. V., The heavens.—According to I. E. there are various kinds of heavenly worlds, some of which possess immortality; the sky, (רקיע) is the lowest, the one nearest to the earth.
⁸ I. E. comparing this phrase with a similar one (Ps. 112:3) explains the verb היה by the verb עמד, which more exclusively expresses duration, while היה has also the meaning to become, signifying a single act.

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:10:1)


**הלא.** את היא המחרבת ים, על בקיעת ים סוף המחרבת מי תהום רבה:


*Which hath dried the sea*. This refers to the division of the Red Sea. מי תהום רבה *The waters of the great deep*. Repeat הטחרבת which hath dried before these words.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:10:2)


**השמה.** אשר שמה כמו השבה עם נעמי (רות ב' ו'), והטעם כפול:


השמה *That hath made*. It is in form similar to השבה that hath returned (Ruth 2:6). The second part of the verse is a mere repetition of the idea contained in the first.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:11:1)


**ופדויי.** הטעם עורי זרוע השם, ואז ישובון פדויי השם, וכבר פירשתיו (ישעיהו ל"ה י'):


*And the redeemed*, etc. The connection between this and the preceding verses is: Awake, O arm, etc., and then, when this is the case, the redeemed of the Lord shall return. I have explained this already (35:10)



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:1)


**אנכי מנחמכם.** סימן לנביא עם ישראל:


*I am he that comforteth you*. The pronouns I and you, refer to the prophet and the people respectively.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:2)


**מי את.** על דעת הכל עם ישראל ידבר, ולפי דעתי שהנביא ידבר ברוח הקודש עם נפשו, והעד ואשים דברי בפיך [לקמן ט"ו]:


*Thou*. It is generally believed that Israel is here addressed; but I think, that the prophet speaks to his own soul, in a prophetical spirit;¹² comp. And I have put my words in thy mouth (ver. 16).

footnotes:
¹² That is, the prophet is addressed by God. The quotation which follows proves it, because it cannot be said according to I. E. of the whole nation, And I have put my words in thy mouth.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:12:3)


**חציר.** חסר כ', כמו אש אוכלה הוא (דברים ד' כ"ד):


כחציר═חציר *As grass*. Comp. אש אכלח as consuming fire¹³ (Deut. 4:24)

footnotes:
¹³ A. V., Consuming fire.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:1)


**ותשכח.** כאלו שכחת, ידבר ברוח הקודש אל לבו, שהוא עושך ויש לו כח גדול, שהשמים והארץ ברשותו:


*And forgottest*. It is as if thou didst forget. The prophet, in his prophetical spirit, speaks thus to his own heart. *The Lord thy Maker*, who is omnipotent; for heaven and earth are in His power.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:2)


**המציק.** כאשר אמר גוי נתתי למכים (ישעיהו נ' ו'):


*The oppressor*. Comp. I gave my back to the smiters (50:6).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:13:3)


**להשחית.** להרוג, ואיה עתה חמת המציק:


*To destroy*, that is, to kill men. *And where is*, etc. Where is now the fury of the oppressor.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:1)


**מהר צועה.** מגזרת צועים, וצעוהו (ירמיה מ"ח י"ב), והנה צועה כמו יושב במצור ובמצוק, ואם הוא פועל עומד, והטעם כמו קשור, ומלת להפתח לעד:


צועה *The captive exile*. Comp. צועים oppressors.¹⁴ וצעוהו and they shall oppress them (Jer. 48:2). The literal meaning of the word, though a participle active,¹⁵ is bound; he who is oppressed, and is in distress, is, as it were, bound. This meaning of the word is proved by the words which follow: that he may be loosed.

footnotes:
¹⁴ A. V., Wanderers. Shall cause him to wander.
¹⁵ This remark seems to be out of its proper place in the Hebrew text; its proper place is either after the quotations with which the word is compared, namely after וצעוהו, or at the end after the explanation of the neuter meaning of the word, namely after לעד. The latter order of the words has been adopted for the translation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:2)


**ולא ימות לשחת.** זה הנביא:


*And that he should not die*. The prophet is meant.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:14:3)


**ולא יחסר לחמו.** כמיכיהו (מלכים א' כ"ב כ"ז) וירמיהו (ירמיהו ל"ז) שיאכילום [צ"ל שהאכילום] לחם לחץ:


*Nor that his bread should fail*, as was the case with Micaiah and Jeremiah, who received but scanty food (1 Kings 22:27; Jer. xxxvii.)



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:15:1)


**ואנכי רגע.** יש אומרים שהוא הפוך כמו גוער, ויש אומרים מניח, אחר שהמו גליו, לשון מרגוע (ירמיהו ו' ט"ז), והוא הישר בעיני, או טעמו אניח אני הים, ואני אצוה שיהמו גליו, והטעם משל על המציקים:


רגע *Who stilleth*.¹⁶ Some say that גער ═ רגע who rebuketh, by metathesis; others compare it with מרגוע rest (Jer. 6:17), and render it who giveth rest; I approve of this latter explanation. ¹⁷ויהמו גליו *Whose waves roared*, that is, whose waves have been roaring. The meaning of the verse might also be the following: I am he who stilleth the sea, but I am also he who commandeth that its waves shall roar. Sea and waves are figurative expressions for the oppressors.

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., Who divided.
¹⁷ These words are not directly mentioned in the text; and the remark on it seems to belong to the explanation of the word רגע; but indirectly I. E. intended by the words אחר שהמו גליו to paraphrase the words ויהמו גליו and to indicate that, although placed after רגע they do not express the effect, but rather the cause.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:16:1

**כסיתיך.** להצילך, כי אמר כאשר כונן להשחית [לעיל י"ג]:


*I have covered thee* to protect thee against him, who was ready to destroy (ver. 13).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:16:2)


**לנטוע שמים.** דרך משל, שיתנבא על המדינות שתשובנה לקדמותן:


*To plant the heavens*. A figurative expression for the announcement to be made to the countries that they shall be restored to their former happiness.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:16:3)


**וליסוד.** שם הפועל, ונעלם היו"ד כמשפטו, והנה בא כמו השלם, וכמוהו מניח לו לישון (קהלת ה' א'):


ליסוד *To lay the foundations*. It is the infinitive; the radical י is silent, according to the rule;¹⁸ the word ליסוד is, however, in form similar to the perfect verb;¹⁹ comp. לישון to sleep (Eccl. 5:11)

footnotes:
¹⁸ The י after a Hirek is silent, when it has no vowel of its own.
¹⁹ לִיְסד is fully corresponding to לִשְׁמוֹר; all the letters of the root are written; the Sheva under the second letter is dropped on account of the property of the י mentioned in the preceding note.

*Which hast drunk*, etc. Israel is compared to a man that is drunk, and is not aware of what is done unto him; he lies down in deep sleep.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:17:3)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:17:4)

מצית *Thou hast wrung out*. Comp. תמצו you may milk out (66:11), though of a different conjugation.²⁰ The meaning of this figure is, thou hast received the full measure of evil.

footnotes:
²⁰ בנינים is perhaps a corruption of שרשים or פעלים, for both words are of the same conjugation, namely Kal. They differ in their derivation; the root of מצית s מצה, that of תמצו is מצץ.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 51:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/51:19:2)


**השוד והשבר.** השוד הוא החרב, כי השוד לעולם עם החרב, והשבר הוא הרעב כמו בשברי לכם מטה לחם (ויקרא כ"ו כ"ו), וי"א זוגות באו הרעות:


*Two things*, etc. Desolation and the sword are the same, for desolation accompanies the sword; destruction and famine are likewise the same;²¹ comp. בשברי לכם מטה לחם. and when I have broken the staff of your bread (Lev. 26:26). Others explain שתים In pairs. The evils come unto thee in pairs.

footnotes:
²¹ The verse quoted by I. E. בשברי לכם מטה לחם seems to be in no connexion whatever with the preceding phrase כי השוד לעולם עם החרב; it proves only that שבד and דעב are connected together, but it contains nothing concerning the identity of שוד and חרב. The original Hebrew text probably contained also the words השבר הוא הרעב, to which the quotation which follows refers.

**מי אנחמך.** חסר ב' במי אנחמך, כי האדם יתנחם כאשר יאמר לו מה שאירע לך כבר אירע כן לפלוני:


במי═מי *By whom. By whom shall I comfort thee ?* Man is usually comforted by being told that some other man has met with the same accident.

## Chapter 52


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:1:1)


**עורי.** כל המפרשים הסכימה דעתם, כי זאת הנבואה עודנה לעתיד אע"פ שישוב להזכיר, סורו צאו משם [י"א], וזאת היא תשובת ר' משה הכהן ז"ל, ולא אמר כלום כאשר אפרש, כי אם אמרנו שזאת הנבואה היא על גלות בבל ושוב הגולה, הנה כתוב לא יוסיף יבא בך עוד ערל וטמא, וכתוב כי מי נח זאת לי, כן נשבעתי (ישעיהו נ"ד ט'), והנה היא גזרה לא תבטל כלל:


All agree that this prophecy has reference to the time yet to come, notwithstanding the passage Depart ye, etc. (ver. 11), which is adduced by R. Moses Hakkohen, though in error, as I shall prove, in answer to this opinion. How could this prophecy be referred to the deliverance and return of the captives in Babylon, when it is said, the uncircumcised and unclean shall no more come unto thee (ver. 1.); for this is as the waters of Noah, etc. (54:1); thus have I sworn (ibid.); such expressions characterise an irrevocable decree.¹

footnotes:
¹ Since these prophecies are described as irrevocable decrees, but have not been verified at the return of the Israelites from the Babylonian exile, they are still to be fulfilled, and refer therefore to the days of Messiah.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:1:2)


ובא **יבא** אחרי יוסיף כמו אל תרבו תדברו גבוהה (שמואל א' ב' ג'), ויחסר אות שי"ן, והוא דרך צחות בלשון:


לא יוסיף יבוא *Shall no more come*. As to יבוא and יוסיף following each other without conjunction, comp: אל תרבו תדברו talk no more. The conjunction שֶׁ ² is omitted by poetical license.³

footnotes:
² That is אֲשֶׁר; I. E. says שֶׁ, because he is more used to it than to the full form אשר, although in the Bible the syncopated form is very rare.
³ The omission of the conjunction between words and sentences is often met with in poetry or in poetical prose (oratory), but is very rare in the usual prose.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:2:1)


**התנערי מעפר.** דרך משל, על כן אמר שבי כי היא (הוה) שוכבת בעפר:


*Shake thyself from the dust*. It is a figurative expression. The prophet therefore⁴ continues, Arise, sit down; for Jerusalem is compared to one that has been lying down in dust.

footnotes:
⁴ The word therefore does not refer to the remark immediately preceding, but to the words of the text, Shake thyself from the dust, which imply, that she was lying in the dust.—The words sit down are to be contrasted with the lying in dust.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:2:2)


**התפתחי מוסרי צוארך.** הטעם שלא תהי עוד תחת ממשלת גוי:


*Loose thyself*, etc. Thou wilt be no more under the dominion of another nation.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:3:1)


**כי. חנם נמכרתם.** מכרתי אתכם לגוים, והטעם בלא כסף, וכן אגאלכם חנם:


*You have been sold*, etc. I have sold you to the nations without receiving money for you, and so will I redeem you without giving money for you.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:4:1)


**כי וגו'.** הטעם כמה רעות עברו על עמי (באו) כי בתחלה ירד אל מצרים לגור ושם ענה:


*My people went down*, etc. Many evils came over my people from the beginning; for when, long ago, they went down to Egypt to sojourn there, they were oppressed.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:4:2)


**ואשור באפס עשקו.** כמו בלא דבר, כמו חנם עשקו, הטעם על גלות אשור:


באפס *Without cause*. For nothing. *And the Assyrian without cause oppressed them*. This refers to the exile of the ten tribes.

מה לי פה *What have I here*, any more.⁵ It is an anthropomorphism. It might also mean, what reason have I to be silent,

*that my people is taken away for nought* by Babylon, Edom, and other nations.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:3)


**ומושליו.** הם גדולי ישראל, והנכון שהם כמו על כן יאמרו המושלים בואו חשבון (במדבר כ"א כ"ז):


ומשליו And they that rule over them, that is, the princes of Israel, or His poets; comp. המשלים they that speak in proverbs (Num. 21:27).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:4)


**יהילילו.** בהראות ה"א הבנין:


יהילילו *Hoẇl*.⁶ The ה, the characteristic of the Hiphil, is here not omitted, as is usually the case.

⁶ A. V., Make them to howl.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:5:5)

מתנאץ═מנאץ *Is blasphemed*. The Dagesh in נ compensates for the omitted ת.⁷

⁷ I. E. does not describe this form as a compound of Hithpael and Pual, but as the Hithpolel, which is a conjugation by itself, regularly formed of verbs ע״ו and ע״ע, but exceptionally of other verbs.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:7:1)


**מה וגו'.** אחר שאושיעך, וזה הטעם הנני, מה נאוו מבניין נפעל, מגזרת וכי תאוה הוא לעיני' (בראשית ג' ו'), והאומר כי הנו"ן שורש, אינו אמת, אע"פ שתמצא זאת הלשון בלשון חכמינו:


*How beautiful upon the mountains*, etc. After I shall have helped thee, that is, after I have said, Behold, it is I, then how beautiful, etc. נאוו *Are beautiful*. It is Niphal of אוה to desire. Comp. תאוה desire. He who thinks that נ in נאוו is radical, is mistaken, although the root נאה to be beautiful is found in Rabbinical literature.⁸

footnotes:
⁸ Comp. the phrase לך נאה לשבח It is becoming to praise Thee, which is frequently met with in the Hebrew liturgy.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:7:2)


**מלך אלהיך.** זה הוא הנני:


*Thy God reigneth*. This is the explanation of הנני behold, it is I.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:8:1)


**קול.** צופים שיש וכלם ישאו קול לבשרך:


קול צפיך נשאו קול יחדיו ירננו *The voice of thy watchmen*,¹ *all of them shall lift up their voices, they shall shout*,⁹ bringing good tidings to thee.

footnotes:
¹ That is, the watchmen whom thou wilt appoint for thyself, while the bearers of good tidings mentioned in the preceding verse are appointed by God. The Hebrew text has the words צופים שיש לך watchmen that are unto thee as the explanation of צופיך thy watchmen, but it is difficult to see why this possessive pronoun should require the explanatory paraphrase, more than the very many others in the Bible. The word שיש is perhaps a corruption of שים appoint, an קול צופיך is to be translated accordingly: Let there be the voice of thy own watchmen.
⁹ A. V., Thy watchmen shall lift up the voice; with the voice together shall they sing.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:8:2)


**כי עין בעין.** כי כלם יראו בעינים, ששב יי ציון, וכמוהו אשר עין בעין נראה אתה יי (במדבר י"ד י"ד):


*For they shall see*, etc. For all of them shall see with their own eyes that the Lord has returned to Zion. Comp. That thou, Lord, art seen face to face (Num. 14:14)

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:10:1)


**חשף.** הטעם הראו' גבורתו, כגבור שיהרוג בכח זרועו:


*Hath made bare His holy arm*. He has shown His strength. It is a figure taken from the hero that slays with the strength of his arm.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:10:2)


**כל אפסי ארץ.** ויש אומרים קצות הארץ בלא חבר, רק מהטעם, ואחרים אמרו כי כמהו ואשור באפס עשקו (ישעיהו מ"ז ח'), כאילו אמר באפסו, ועוד כמוהו אני ואפסי [לעיל ד'], ויש אומרים שהאל"ף נוסף, כמו פיסת בר (תהלים ע"ב ט"ז), והנכון בעיני שהוא כמו מי אפסי', ואל תתמ' כי הפסוק ישים יד ורגל ובטן ופה והטעם ידוע, שהמדבר הוא בן אדם וכן השומע, ישים הדברים בדרך משל כאילו הם על צורות בן אדם, להבין השומעים:


אפסי *The ends of*. Some consider this word as hap. leg., its meaning being found from the context. According to others, it is to be compared with באפסו═באפס in his land (ver. 4); ואפסי and my land (47:8).¹¹ To others the א is prosthetic; they compare, therefore, אפס with פיסת a handful (Ps. 72:16).¹² I connect it with מי אפסים waters to the ankles (Ez. 47:3).¹³ It is not in the least surprising that the text attributes to God hand, foot, heart, and mouth; the meaning of such figures is well known. He who speaks, as well as he who is addressed, is a human being; the idea is therefore clothed in such language as can be understood by man.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹¹ The phrase אני ואפסי עוד is according to this explanation, to be translated I and my land shall remain for ever. A. V., I am, and none else beside me. According to I. E. I am, and none besides.
¹² It is difficult to see the connection between פיסת handful and אפסי ends. The latter is perhaps according to this translation to be rendered like מְלׂאׇהּ the fulness of or the inhabitants of.
¹³ The meaning of אפס is according to this explanation, ankle extremity, and אפסי ארץ the extremities of the earth, or the ends of the earth.
¹⁴ This observation is made here by I. E. as if he wanted to refute the opinion of those that try to explain here the arm of the Lord by Messiah.

**סורו וגו'.** אמר רבי משה הכהן ז"ל צאו מתוכה של בבל, והנכון בעיני שמלת סורו סורו טמא, לכל הגולה שהיא בינות הגוים:


*Depart ye* from Babylon, according to R. Moses Hakkohen. I think that these words are addressed to those that are still in exile among the nations.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:2)


**סורו סורו.** פעמים דרך מהירות כמו סורה אדוני (שופטים ד' י"ח):


The repetition of Depart ye is to indicate that it is to be done immediately. Comp. Turn in, my lord, turn in to me (Jud. 4:18).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:3)


**צאו משם.** כל אחד ואחד ממקום גלותו:


*From thence*. Every one from the place of his exile.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁵ שׇׁם there seems to point to one certain place, but since no such place is mentioned before, its meaning must be found from the context. R. Moses Hakkohen, who refers this whole section of the book to the Babylonian captivity, understands by there the city or country of Babylon. I. E. who refers this section to the period of Messiah, understands by the word שׇׁם all the countries whither the Jews came during the exile. It is, however, strange that שׇׁם is explained by I. E. to refer to one country only and to require paraphrasing like מִתּׂכׇהּ, since it could easily be connected with כל הגוים all the nations. The parallelism of the verse (שם═מתכה) perhaps gave rise to this explanation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:4)


**טמא אל תגעו.** שיבדלו מאומות העולם:


*It is unclean, touch not*, that is, keep away from the heathen nations.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:5)


**צאו מתוכה.** כל אחד ממדינת גלותו, כי אין בכל הפרשיות למעלה זכר בבל:


*Go ye out of the midst of her*. Every one shall go out of the country of his exile. Babylon has not been mentioned in any of these chapters.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ That is from c. l., if we are to consider the north (49:12) and Babylon to be the same (see I. E. ad locum); or, if not, from c. xlix., since Babylon is mentioned 48:20.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:6)


**הברו.** בנין נפעל והיה ראוי להדגש בעבור אות הכפל:


הברו *Be ye clean*. It is Niphal. The Dagesh, which usually compensates for the omitted letter, is here left out, because ר is a guttural letter.¹⁷

footnotes:
¹⁷ The root of the word is ברר; the one ר being omitted, a Dagesh in the other is required for its compensation, instead of which the preceding short vowel (Pathah) is produced into the long Kamez: although ר is no guttural letter, it shares this property with the gutturals.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:11:7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:7](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:11:7)


**נשאי כל יי.** הם ישראל נושאי התורה, ויש אומר על הלוים שהם נושאי הארון, והראשון נכון בעיני:


*Ye that bear the vessels of the Lord*. The Israelites, who are the bearers of the law.¹⁸ Some refer these words to the Levites, who are the bearers of the Holy Ark; but I prefer the former explanation.

footnotes:
¹⁸ The Law (תורה) is called here according to I. E. כלי יי the vessels or the instruments of the Lord, because it is the means by which God makes mankind holy and happy.
