### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 52:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/52:13:1)


**הנה ישכיל עבדי.** זאת הפרשה קשה מאד: אמרו תועי רוח שהוא רמז לאלהיה', ויפרשו עבדי הגוף, וזה לא יתכן, כי הגוף לא ישכיל ואפי' כשאדם חי, ועוד מה טעם יראה זרע (יאריך ימים), והוא לא היה לו בן, ועוד יאריך ימים ולא היה כן, ועוד ואת עצומים יחלק שלל, והראיה גמורה כי למעלה, כי הולך לפניכם יי, והם ישראל, ואחר כך רני עקרה, והיא כנסת ישראל, והנה טעם עבדי, כל מי שהיה בגלות מישראל והוא עבד השם, ורבים פירשוהו על משיח, בעבור שאמרו קדמונינו ז"ל [מדרש רבה איכה א' ט"ז] כי ביום שחרב בית המקדש נולד משיח, והוא אסור בזיקי', והנה אין טעם לפסוקים רבים, נבזה וחדל אישי', מעוצר וממשפט לוקח, ויתן את רשעי' קברו, ומה טעם יראה זרע יאריך ימים, והגאון רב סעדיה ז"ל פירש כל הפרשה על ירמיה ויפה פירש וטעם יזה גוים רבים בפיו בדרך נבואתו, כיונק לפניו גם כתב בתחלת ספרו (ירמיה א' י') כי קטן היה כאשר נתנבא, ויי הפגיע בו והוא חטא רבים נשא כי כן כתוב זכר עמדי לפניך לבקש עליהם טובה [שם י"ח כ'], כשה לטבח יובל וכן כתוב ואני ככבש אלוף יובל לטבח [שם י"א י"ט], ופירש ואת עצומים יחלק שלל על ארוחה ומשאת שנתן לו רב טבחי' [שם מ' ה'], והנכון בעיני כי כל הפרשה דבקה כי מה טעם להזכיר ירמיהו אחר הנחמות ולפני הנחמות, והנה ידבר על כל עבד יי שהוא בגלות, או יהיה עבדי כמו ישראל עבדי, וזה קרוב מזה:


The passage which follows offers great difficulties. The Christians refer it to Jesus, and explain my servant to indicate the body. This is wrong; the body cannot be wise, even during the life of man. Again, what is the meaning of he shall see his seed (53:10), he shall prolong his days (ib.)? This was not in fact the case. Again, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong (53:12).²⁰ The best proof,²¹ however, is the circumstance that this passage is preceded by the Lord will go before you, etc., which undoubtedly refers to the Israelites, and is followed by Sing, O barren, etc., which is likewise addressed to the Israelites. *My servant*. The Israelites, who are the servants of the Lord, and are now in exile. Many believe that Messiah is meant by this expression, because our ancient teachers said that Messiah was born on the day on which the temple was destroyed, that he was, as it were, bound in chains, etc.;²² but many verses in this passage cannot be explained on this supposition. Comp. He is despised and rejected of men, he was taken from prison and judgment, and he made his grave with the wicked, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days. The Gaon R. Saadiah refers the whole passage to Jeremiah. His explanation is beautiful; he says: *he shall scatter many nations* by his words, by his prophecy. Comp. Jer. 1:10. *As a tender plant*. Jeremiah was young when he began to prophesy (Jer. 1:6). *And the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of all of us; he took away the sin of many*. Comp. Remember that I stood before thee, to speak good for them, and to turn away the wrath from them (ibid. 18:20). *He is brought as a lamb to the slaughter*. Comp. But I was like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter (ibid. 11:19). *And he shall divide the spoil with the strong*. Jeremiah received presents and gifts from the Babylonian chief of the guard (ibid. 40:5). But I think that this passage must be connected with the chapters that procede and follow. What reason is there for mentioning Jeremiah here after some of the comforting prophecies, and before others of the same kind ? The singular, my servant, is used because the prophet speaks of every one that is a servant of the Lord and suffers in exile, or because ישראל עבדי ═ )עבדי my servant Israel,) refers to the whole nation; the latter reason is more probable.

footnotes:
²⁰ This, if taken literally, was not the case; if in any figurative sense, the whole argument is destroyed which is based on the supposition of a minute coincidence of the facts here predicted with the incidents in the life of Jesus.
²¹ ראיה גמורה means literally a perfect or complete proof. The first proof was a negative one, but the proof introduced with these words is a positive one that the chapter refers to Israel or to the prophet.
²² Comp. Midrash Rabba, Echa 1:16. The passage must be taken in a figurative sense, namely, that on the day on which the temple was destroyed, it was already decreed, by the Almighty that it should again be rebuilt, but that the restoration would be dependent on the return of the Israelites to God and to His word.

**ותארו.** בא על דרך רחבו, וזה דבר ידוע כי כמה גוים יש בעולם שיחשבו כי צורת היהודי משונה מכל הצורות, וישאלו היש ליהודי פה או עין, כן [שמעתי] בארץ ישמעאל ובאדום:


ותארו *And his form*. It is in form similar to רחבו his breadth (Exod. 25:10).²⁴—It is a well-known fact that many people in the world imagine the Jew a being altogether different from his fellow creatures; they ask, Has the Jew a mouth, an eye, etc.? This is the case among Mahometans as well as among Christians.

The meaning of this verse is: God will in future visit those nations that trouble Israel with punishment (comp. (Zech. 1:11, 12), because he thought that so long as the heathen people have peace, Jerusalem would not find mercy.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:6:2)


**הפגיע.** מגזרת ויפגע במקום (בראשית כ"ח י"א):


הפגיע *Hath laid*. Lit. Hath caused to meet; comp. ויפגע and he alighted (Gen. 28:11).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:6:3)


**עון.** במקום הזה כמו עונש כמו אם יקרך עון (שמואל א' כ"ח י') כי לא שלם עון האמרי (בראשית ט"ו ט"ז) ויגדל עון בת עמי (איכה ד' ו'), ויש אומרים מגזרת ואל תפגע בי (ירמיה ז' ט"ז), ויהיה פי' עון כלנו כמשמעו, והטעם כי יפגע בעבור היות שלום בעולם, כטעם ודרשו את שלום העיר [שם כ"ט ז'], לכן מלת עון תבא קשה עם הפגיע בו:


עון Lit. iniquity; here it means the punishment for the iniquity. Comp. עון punishment (1 Sam. 28:10; Gen. 15:16;⁶ Lam. 4:6). Some explain הפגיע he caused to pray; עון has, according to their opinion, the usual meaning iniquity; and the sense of the whole phrase is: God will accept the prayer of Israel, that peace shall be on earth. Comp. And seek the peace of the city, etc. (Jer. 29:7). But עון in this sense, joined with הפגיע בו, is rather an unusual construction.⁷

footnotes:
⁶ The passage referred to is כי לא שלם עון האמרי for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full (A.V.). It requires, however, to be proved that עון in this passage means punishment.
⁷ If פגע ב means to pray to, the meaning of the Hiphil הפגיע ב is, to cause to pray to, and also, to accept the prayer, if the noun governed by the preposition ב is the same as the subject to the verb הפגיע; and הפגיע בר is to be translated, He caused to pray to Himself; if, therefore, the phrase הפגיע בו is followed by a noun in the accusative, this must express either the person who is caused to pray, or the object of the prayer. The accusative עון is neither the one nor the other, since in the latter case, not the iniquity but the atonement for the iniquity, not the punishment, but the cancelling of the punishment, (not עון but כפרת עון) is the object of the prayer.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:7:1)


**נגש.** מבנין נפעל:


נגש *He was oppressed*. It is Niphal.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:7:2)


**ולא יפתח פיו.** ואין צורך לפרש זה, כי כל יהודי כן הוא בגלות, כי בשעה שיעונה לא יפתח פיו לדבר, אף כי הוא הצדיק שבהם לא יתעסק בעולמו כי אם בעבודת השם ולא יכיר שר או גדול שיעמד לו בפרץ בקום עליו אדם, ולא יפתח (לו) פיו והטעם בכל עת:


*Yet he opened not his mouth*. This requires no explanation; for this is the case with every Jew in exile; when he is insulted he dares not reply, especially the pious one who devotes himself only to the service of God, and does not care for worldly prosperity; nor does he know any prince or chief whom to ask for assistance, when oppressed by man. The phrase Yet he does not open his mouth, is repeated to express the continuity of this fact.

**ואת דורו מי ישוחח.** כמו או שיח לארץ ותורך (איוב י"ב ח'), והטעם מי היה מגיד לאנשי דורו שיהיה כן, והוא כבר היה כמו נגזר מארץ חיים:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:8:5

**מפשע עמי.** דברי כל גוי, וזה שהנגע שיהיה לישראל היה מפשעינו, כמו מחולל מפשעינו, והנכון שהוא כן, ומפשע עמי יבא הנגע להם, בעבור מלת למו שהוא כמו להם:


*For the transgression of my people was he stricken*. Every nation will think: Israel was stricken because of our sins; comp. he was slain for our transgressions (ver. 5). The construction of the sentence is: For the transgression of my people plagues came over them. להם═למו To them, that is, to the Israelites.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:9:1)


**ויתן.** יש מפרשים על מתי גלות, ויש אומרים שמלת במותיו מגזרת ואתה על במותימו תדרך (דברים ל"ג כ"ט), והטעם בנין שיושם על הקבר, והנה יהיה במותיו כמו קברו:


Some refer this verse to those Israelites that die in exile; others derive במתיו from במה high place; comp. במתימו their high places (Deut. 33:29), and refer it to the building erected over the grave; so that קברו═במתיו his tomb.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:9:2)


**ואת עשיר.** כמו ואת רשעי', והטעם הגוים שהם עשירים כנגד ישראל, והנכון בעיני, שטעם הפסוק, שכל כך היה ישראל בצער בגלות, שהיה רוצה שימות עם הגוים, כמו תמות נפשי עם פלשתים (שופטים ט"ז ל'), והכתוב אמר ויתן על מחשבתו, כמו וילחם בישראל (יהושע כ"ד ט') על בלק, והעד כי זה מרוב הצער, שאמר על לא חמס עשה כי הגוים יצערו ישראל חנם, ולא בעבור מעשה שעשו, ולא דבור רע שידברו שהוא נכון להתפרש לשני עניני', ואם טען טוען, והלא במות לא תשתנ' במלת על במותימו, ומדוע השתנה במלת במותיו, יש להשיב, כי זאת המלה תבא על שנים משקלים, כמו סריסי פרעה (בראשית מ' ז') וסריסי המלך (אסתר ו' י"ד):


רשע═עשיר *Wicked*.⁸ The heathen nations that are rich in comparison with Israel are meant. I think that this verse describes the trouble of the Israelites in exile, which is so great, that they long to die with the nations; comp. Let me die with the Philistines (Jud. 16:20). As to ויתן he longed to give;⁹⁹ comp. וילחם and he intended to fight (Jos. 24:9). That this longing for death is caused by the great pains, may be inferred from the words which follow: because he had done no violence. The heathen nations oppress Israel without cause; he neither deserves such ill-treatment, by any wrong act nor by any ambiguous, deceitful word. If the objection should be made that בׇּמוׂת does not change in the construct state into בְּמוׂת, as is the case in בְּמׂתׇיו, I answer, that this noun has two forms in the plural, like סריס officer: סׇרִיסֵי (Gen. 40:7); and סְרִיסֵי (Est. 6:14)

**ויי חפץ דכאו.** כמו דברו לשלום (בראשית ל"ז ד'), מהבנין הכבד הדגוש:


דַּכְּאוׂ *To bruise him*. It is in form similar to דַּבְּרוׂ, to speak with him (Gen. 37:4). It is Piel.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:2)


**החלי.** מבעלי הה"א בא על דרך האל"ף, ואף כי שמצאנו תחלואיה אשר חלה יי בה (דברים כ"ט כ"א), והנה חפץ דכאו, לייסרנו בגלות:


החלי *He hath put him to grief*. It is a verb ל״ה, but conjugated like a verb ¹⁰;ל״א comp. תחלואיה אשר חלה the sicknesses which the Lord hath laid upon it (Deut. 29:21). *God was pleased to bruise him*, to chastise him with exile.

footnotes:
¹⁰ The Hiphil of the verb ל״א has Hirek in the second syllable followed by יא, e.g. קרא he called, הִקְרִיא, while the Hiphil of the verb ל״ה has Kamez followed by ה, e.g. קרה he met, הִקְרׇה. This distinction is, however, not always adhered to: so here החלִי, the apocopated form of החלִיא, instead of החלׇה the root being חלה.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:3)


**אם תשים אשם נפשו.** שיתודה ויודה, והטעם אם תשי' נפשו אשמתו לנגדו, השם ירבה בניו, ויאריך ימים שיראה הוא ובניו בישועת השם, והגה ידבר על הדור שישובו לשם בעת קץ ביאת המשיח:


אם תשים אשם נפשו *If his soul shall set his guilt*¹¹ before him, that is, if he will confess and fear the Lord.¹² *He shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days*. He and his children will enjoy the salvation, which the Lord will grant them. This refers to that generation which will return to God, that is, to the law of God, in the days of Messiah.

footnotes:
¹¹ A. V., When thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin.
¹² The corresponding words of the Hebrew text are יראת השם. But they are not required at all for the explanation of the words in question, and are besides, in no grammatical connection with the preceding words. They are superfluous, and are probably nothing more than a repetition of the succeeding יראה, which was wrongly changed into יראת ה׳.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:10:4)


**וחפץ יי בידו יצלח.** הטעם על התורה שישובו הגוים לדת השם:


*And the pleasure of the Lord shall prosper in his hand*. The true religion shall prosper, all nations will accept it.

**יראה.** חפצו או יראה טוב עד שישבע, בעבור כי בדעתו יצדיק רבים, והם הגוים שילמדום ישראל לעשות התורה:


He shall see the reward of his forbearance, and shall find his desire fulfilled; or he shall enjoy prosperity in such a degree that he will be satisfied, because צדיק עבדי לרבים בדעתו יצדיק *By his knowledge he will cause many to be just*.¹⁴ He will teach the nations how to live according to the Law.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:11:3)


וטעם **ועונותם הוא יסבול.** שישתתף ישראל עם צער הגוים ברוב עונותם, לא כאשר עשו הם לישראל, או הטעם שיתפלל לשם בעד הגוים, כטעם ואם משפחת מצרים לא תעלה (זכריה י"ד י"ח), וזה הנכון בעיני, כי הפסוק הבא אחריו לעד:


*And he shall bear their iniquities*. Israel will sympathise with the heathen nations in their misfortunes, which have come upon them for their many sins; although they do not sympathise with Israel in his afflictions. The meaning of the phrase might also be this: The Israelites will pray to God for the other nations, and thereby take away their sins; comp. (Zech. 14:18).¹⁵ I approve of the latter explanation, since its correctness is evidenced by the words which follow.

footnotes:
¹⁵ The passage referred to, And if the family of Egypt go not up, and come not, that have no rain, there shall be the plague, etc. indicates, according to the opinion of I. E., that the Egyptians (and other nations likewise) shall come up to Jerusalem, and tell the Israelites of their distress; the Israelites will then pray for them, or join them in their prayer, and God will send the relief and comfort prayed for.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:12:1)


**לכן וגו'.** כל המפרשים אמרו כי זה הפסוק דרך משל על המתים על ייחוד השם, וטעם רבים כמו גדולים כמו על כל רב ביתו (אסתר א' ח'), והם הנביאים, והעצומים הם האבות, הטעם שיהיה חלק מתי הייחוד עם הנביאים, וידענו כי זה דבר אמת הוא, רק איננו מטעם הפרשה, והנכון בעיני כי הוא כן, לכן אתן לישראל חלק בז ושלל מגוים רבים:


*Therefore will I divide him*, etc. All commentators agree that in this verse the prophet speaks of those that die for the unity of God, explaining the expression ברבים *with the great*—comp. רב chief (Est. 1:8)—to signify the prophets, and understand by עצומים *the strong* the patriarchs. ¹⁶ According to this explanation the meaning of the whole verse is, The merit of those that die for the unity of God, is equal to the merit of the prophets and patriarchs. We know that this is true, but the subject has no connection with the context of this chapter. I explain it as follows: I will certainly give to Israel a portion of the spoil and booty taken from many nations;

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 53:12:10

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:12:10](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/53:12:10)


והנה פירשתי לך כל הפרשה, ולפי דעתי כי הנה ישכיל עבדי הוא שאמר הנביא עליו, הן עבדי אתמך בו (מ"ב א') ויאמר לי עבדי אתה (ישעיהו מ"ט ג') וכן כתוב בדעתו יצדיק צדיק עדי לרבים (ישעיהו נ"ג י"א) וכת' גוי נתתי למכים (ישעיהו נ' ו'), והסוד כאשר רמזתי בחצי הספר והנה כל הפרשיות דבקות זאת עם זאת:


I have thus explained the whole passage, on the supposition that it refers to Israel;¹⁹ but my opinion is, that my servant, mentioned here (52:13), is the same as that of 42:1, 49:3, 53:11, the same who says of himself, I gave my back to the smiters, etc. (50:6). In my commentary on chap. xl., I mentioned briefly the leading principle of my opinion, which considers all these chapters (from xl.) as connected with each other.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ The explanation given in the whole chapter seems to be only a concession made to the general opinion, that these chapters, from xl.—lxvi., have no inner connexion throughout, and that in this portion עבדי my servant refers to Israel. His own opinion is, that the servant of the Lord is the prophet, who was in Babylon in exile with his brethren, illtreated there and insulted not only by the Babylonians, but also by those Israelites, that did not believe in his divine mission, but ultimately, when his words were proved to be true by facts, honoured and respected by all.
²⁰ Comp. I. E. on 40:1, 49:8, 52:13.



## Chapter 54


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:1)


**רני עקרה.** כנסת ישראל עקרה לא ילדה והיא עקרה, והטעם שמעט מספר ישראל:


*O barren, thou that didst not bear*. The congregation of Israel is called barren and a woman that did not bear—the latter attribute being the explanation of the former—because of its small number.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:2)


**פצחי גם צהלי.** פירשתיו:


צהלי ,פצחי. I have already explained these two words.¹

footnotes:
¹ Comp. I. E. on 14:7, 52:9, and 10:30.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:1:3)


**לא חלה.** מגזרת חיל (שמות ט"ו י"ד) וכן הוא, פצחי רנה וצהלי עקרה, אשר לא חלה, ועל דעת ר' משה הכהן ז"ל בבל, ועל דרך האמת כל אומה שיש לה בעל והוא מלך:


לא חלה *That didst not travail with child*. Comp. חיל trembling (Ex. 15:14); repeat עקרה O barren before מבני בעולה .חלה לא *Than the children of the married wife*, that is, than the children of Babylon,² according to the opinion of R. Moses Hakkohen, but I think, that every nation that has a husband (בעל), that is, every nation that has its own king, is meant here by בעולה the married wife.³

footnotes:
² The explanation introduced by the words על דעת רמ״ה ועל דרך אמת, This is the opinion of Rabbi Moses Hakkohen, but I think, refers doubtlessly to the words בני בעולה, the children of the married woman. The opinion of R. Moses Hakkohen is missing in the printed edition of this Commentary.
³ This is again an allusion to the difference of opinion between R. Moses Hakkohen and I. E., regarding the subject of these prophecies (xl.—lxvi.). They both agree in the meaning of the figure; but while the one applies it to Babylon, the other applies it to all countries whither Jews have been dispersed through the Roman exile.

### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:4:1)

לא תחפירי *Thou shalt not be ashamed*. Comp. וחפרה and shall be confounded (24:23). *Fear not*, while being in exile.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:4:2)


**עלומיך.** רמז לגלות עלומים, או רמז לבית ראשון וגם שני, שהיו רעות רבות לישראל מעורבות בימי מלכותם:


*The shame of thy youth*. The exile of the youths is to be understood;⁹ or the phrase refers to the period of the first and second temple,¹⁰

footnotes:
⁹ This is the translation of the words רמז לגלות עלומיך; but עלומיך is rather suspicious; for first, the third person עלומיה is required; secondly, I. E. would not have used the same word in explaining the phrase. From the context we may infer that גלות מצרים the stay of the Israelites in Egypt is meant.
¹⁰ עלומיך, according to this explanation, is thy vigour or the period of thy vigour—that is, the period of the independence of the Israelites, the opposite of אלמנותיך thy widowhood, the period of weakness and bereavement. **אלמנותיך.** חסרון המלכות:


אלמנותיך, thy widowhood, to a later period, when they had been dispossessed of it. when the Israelites were sometimes visited with great calamities. *Thy widowhood*. The loss of thy independence.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:5:1)


**כי וגו'.** מלת בועליך על לשון רבים, וכן עושיך, כמו ישמח ישראל בעושיו (תהלים קמ"ט ב') על דרך מלת אלהים ואדונים, כאשר פירשתי בספר בראשית (בראשית א' א') , והנה טעם בועליך כמו מלכך, (ואלהייך כמו):


בּוֹעֲלַיִךְ ,עשַׁׂיִךְ *Thine husband, thy Maker*. As to the use of the plural,¹¹ comp. בְּעשׇׁיו in Him that made him (Ps. 149:2); אלהים God; אדונים Lord; I have explained this in my commentary on Genesis (1:1).¹² בועליך Thine husband is here used for מלכך thy King. and עשיך thy Maker for אלהיך thy God.¹³

footnotes:
¹¹ בּוֹעֲלַיִךְ ,עשַֹׁיִךְ instead of בּוֹעֲלֵךְ ,עוֹשֵֹךְ.

E. says that the king is the husband of the country; we separate therefore ואלהיך from מלכך, and consider it as the explanation of ועשיך, which is to be supplied; the emended text would be ועשיך כמו ואלהיך.

*The God of the whole earth shall He be called*. All nations will accept the divine Law. Comp. For then will I turn to the people a pure language that they may all call upon the name of the Lord, etc., (Zeph. 3:9)



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:6:1)


**כי וגו'.** בעבור שאמר וחרפת אלמנותיך, שהגוים מחרפים את ישראל שאין להם מלך, אמר השם כאשה עזובה היית ועצובת רוח שעזבה בעלה, והנה בעלה חי, כאשר אמר כי בועליך עושיך, ומלת עצובת שם התואר ולא פעול ואם הוא על משקלו, על כן כתוב קראך יי ואשת נעורים כי תמאס אמר השם, וכן היית:


*As a woman forsaken*, etc. The reproach of Israel’s widowhood, the scorn heaped upon the Israelites by other nations, for not having a king of their own, having been mentioned before (ver. 4), the prophet continues in the name of God: Israel has been, it is true, like a woman that is forsaken, and has grieved at the absence of her husband, but her husband is yet alive, etc.; comp. thy Maker is thy husband, etc., (ver. 5)—עצובת grieved is an adjective, not a participle, which it resembles in form—the text continues therefore, the Lord hath called thee.¹⁴ ואשת נעורים כי תמאס *And like a wife of youth, when she is refused*,¹⁵ thou hast been.

footnotes:
¹⁴ The Lord hath called thee to come unto Him, as the husband calls his wife, after having left her for a short time.
¹⁵ A. V., When thou wast refused.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:7:1)


**ברגע.** בי"ת ברגע נוסף כבי"ת בתחילה, בראשון, ויש מפרש שפירש כי הוא מן רוגע הים (ישעיהו נ"א ט"ו), והעד וברחמים:


ברגע *For a moment*. The preposition ב is here pleonastic as in בתחלה at the beginning בראשונה at first.¹⁶ Some say that the meaning of רגע is rebuke; comp. רוגע who rebuketh.¹⁷ (51:15); their opinion is supported by the parallelism of the verse.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁶ The Hebrew text has בראשון; but since this word has the meaning in the first month, it is to be emended into בראשנה, at first; comp. I. E. on 1:26.—The ב in ברגע may justly be considered as superfluous, since רגע is here used as a noun, and the accusative without the preposition ב would likewise express the duration of time. This is not the case with בתחלה, which without the preposition is a noun, the beginning; with the preposition it is an adverb meaning at first.
¹⁷ A. V., That divided.
¹⁸ By the parallelism רגע is the opposite of רחמים mercy.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:8:2)


**ובחסד עולם.** הפך רגע, הנה הטעם שתעמוד מלכות ישראל לעולם כאשר הוא מפורש בספר דניאל (דניאל ז' כ"ז), והנה יהיו ימי הגלות ואם ארכו, כמו רגע כנגד ימי המלכות שלא יפסקו:


With *everlasting kindness*, etc. This is the opposite of the idea expressed in, I hid my face for a moment. The kingdom of Israel will remain for ever (comp. Dan. 7:27); and the days of the exile, though many, will be like a moment in comparison with the everlasting days of the future happiness.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:11:4)


**בספירים.** אבנים יקרות אדומות, כאשר פירשתי במגילת איכה (איכה ד' ז'):


ספירים *Sapphires*. Precious stones of red colour, as I have explained²³ (Lam. 4:7)

footnotes:
²³ Saadiah is of opinion that ספיר signifies a stone of white colour, because of the expression לבנת הספיר, the white colour of the sapphire (Ex. 24:10). I. E., however, explains the latter phrase, the pavement of a sapphire stone, and infers, by means of the rule of parallelism, that ספיר has the same colour as פנינים, of which the verb אדמו they are red is used (Lam. 4:7).



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:1)


**ושמתי כדכד.** אין רע למלת כדכד במקרא, והיא אבן יקרה:


כדכד *Agates*. It is hap. leg.; it is the name of a precious stone.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:2)


**ושמשותיך.** מגזרת שמש, והם בחלונות [צ"ל חלונות] ישימו בם זכוכית, וזה מנהג ארמוני המלכים:


ושמשתיך *And thy windows*. It is derived from שמש sun. It signifies the apertures, which are closed with glass²⁴ in stately palaces.

footnotes:
²⁴ שמשה is the name of the aperture through which the sunlight (שמש) passes into the house; in the earlier centuries they were not filled at all, or they were closed with oil paper; in the time of I. E. glass windows seem to have been introduced, but only in houses of a grand style. Here still more is promised. Precious, transparent stones shall be used as windows in all houses, and even over the gates. The Hebrew text has: ישימו זכוכיות והן בחלונות; it is rather difficult to find the meaning of these words; in the inverted order they read very well והן זכוכיות ישימו בחלונות and these are transparent things which are put in the windows.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:3)


**[ושעריך].** והם המשמשות על השער:


ושעריך *And of thy gates*.²⁵ And the windows of thy gates.²⁶

footnotes:
²⁵ A. V., And thy gates.
²⁶ The words of the Hebrew text, והם המשמשות על השער, require some emendation. Firstly, there is no noun to which the masculine pronoun והם and these could refer; secondly, שמשות is derived from שמש sun, and not from the verb שמש to serve or to attend; thirdly, the word which they explain is missing; the original words are perhaps the following: ושעריך ֗ שמשות שעריך והן השמשות על השער. The translation is based on this suggestion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:12:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:4)


**אקדח.** אבן יקרה, ואל"ף נוסף והוא מגזרת כי אש קדחה באפי (דברים ל"ב כ"ב):


אקדח *Carbuncles*. A precious stone. The א is prosthetic; comp. קדחה is kindled (Deut. 32:22).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:12:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:12:5)


**לאבני חפץ.** שיש לאדם חפץ בהם, לא ככל האבנים שהם מושלכות אין חפץ בהם:


*To stones that are desired*, that are not like those stones which are thrown about, and are of no value.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:13:1)


**וכל בניך למודי.** כמו תלמידי, והנה המלה תאר השם:


למודי Taught of. It is an adjective,¹ and is used as a synonym of תלמיד pupil.

footnotes:
¹ Comp. c. iii., Note 5.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:13:2)


**ורב.** פועל עתיד בעבור הוי"ו:


ורב *And great shall be*. It is a verb; the ו turns the past into the future.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:14:1)


**בצדקה תכונני.** מבנין התפעל והתי"ו מבולע, והטעם שיעשו ישראל צדק בעולם ולא יעשקו הגוים כמשפט המלכים:


תכנני *Shalt thou be established*. It is Hithpael. The ת is omitted and compensated by the Dagesh in the כ. *In righteousness*, etc. Israel will do justice to all, and will oppress no people, as the heathen nations are used to do.²⁷

footnotes:
²⁷ המלכים the kings of the Hebrew text is perhaps a corruption of המלכות, a general term, used to signify the governments by which the Israelites were kept in a sort of slavery and degradation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:14:2)


וטעם **לא תיראי.** בעבור העושק והחמס יסיר השם המלכות:


*Thou shalt not fear*. For the sin of oppression and violence deprives the state of its power.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:15:1)


**הן וגו'.** אמר רבי יונה הן גור יגור כמו חבור ואמר כי כמוהו נהרסו ממגורות (יואל א' י"ז), והטעם היתכן שיתחבר חבור כי אם ברשותי, והטעם על גוג ומגוג:


גור יגור. According to R. Jonah: they will surely gather together; comp. ממגורות barns,²⁸ (Joel 1:17). The meaning of the whole verse is accordingly: Is it possible, that any alliance should be made except with my permission ? (The alliance between Gog and Magog is here referred to.)

footnotes:
²⁸ Lit., the places where the corn is gathered together.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:15:2)


**מי גר אתך.** פי' מי שהתחבר והיה אתך ושב עליך, אז יפול, והנכון בעיני כי גור יגור כמשפטו, וכן הוא, היתכן שיגור עמך גר בארץ שהוא שלי כי אם ברשותי, מי שירצה לגור עמך בארצי עליך יפול, כמו אל הכשדי' אתה נופל (ירמיה ל"ז י"ג) על פני כל אחיו נפל (בראשית כ"ה י"ג), והטעם שיפול [צ"ל שיפיל] עצמו תחת רשותך:


He who is now thy ally, and will then become thy enemy, will fall.²⁹ I take גור יגור in its usual meaning and explain the verse thus: Can there dwell any stranger with thee in my land, except it be with my will; he who desires to dwell with thee in my land, עליך יפול *must surrender to thee*.³⁰ The verb נפל has here the same meaning as in אל הכשדים אתה נופל thou fallest away to the Chaldӕans (Jer. 37:13); and in על פני כל אחיו נפל he surrendered to all his brethren (Gen. 25:18); namely: to submit to the authority of.³¹

footnotes:
²⁹ This explanation seems to be based on the meaning of the two prepositions אתך and את ;עליך with indicates alliance, friendship; על against, enmity and war.
³⁰ A. V., Shall fall for thy sake.
³¹ In his commentary on Gen. 23:18, I. E. gives three meanings of the verb נפל in the two passages quoted here: 1. His lot or portion fell. 2. He went away. 3. He died. The meaning adopted here to surrender, is not even mentioned there.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:16:1)


**הנה וגו'.** דרך משל:


*Behold, I have created the smith*, etc. It is a figurative expression.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:16:2)


**ומוציא כלי.** מאש ויתקנהו, וגם אנכי בראתי המשחית שישחית כלי החרש:


ומוציא כלי למעשהו *And that bringeth forth a vessel for its work*.³² That bringeth forth a vessel out of the fire, to finish it. *And I have also created the waster to destroy* the instrument of the smith.

footnotes:
³² A. V., An instrument for his work.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:1)


**כל כלי יוצר.** שיוצר עליך, להיותו לא יצלח, רק ישבר, הנה יוצר מהבנין שלא נקרא שם פועלו על משקל יוסר (ויקרא ד' ל"ה):


יוצר עליך That is formed against thee. *Shall not prosper*, to become what it is destined to be; but it will be broken. יוצר *Is formed*. It is Hophal, similar in form to יוסר is taken away, (Lev. 4:35).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:2)


**וכל לשון וגו'.** הנה פירוש זה כל כלי:


*And every tongue*, etc. This is the explanation of any weapon, etc.³³

footnotes:
³³ This same opinion, that the phrase every tongue, etc., is the explanation of the preceding verse, is indicated by I. E. in his remark on ver. 16, at the beginning, It is a figurative expression.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:3)


**תרשיעי.** הטעם שיאמינו הגוים בתורה, וישראל יראום רשעת דתיהם:


*Thou shalt condemn*. All nations will accept the religion of Israel, who will prove to them the falsity of the faiths they have hitherto followed.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 54:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/54:17:4)


**זאת נחלת עבדי יי.** מהשם, על התורה או על ארץ הצבי:

## Chapter 55


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:1)


**הוי.** לשון קריאה, כמו הוי כל צמא, אלה דברי השם לאומות העולם, בימים ההם מי שירצה ללמוד תורה:


הוי *Ho !* It is the sign of the vocative. *Ho, every one that thirsteth*, etc. With these words the Lord will address those who will then be desirous to accept the Law.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:2)


**ואשר אין לו כסף.** והטעם אם אין לו כסף לקנות, שאין לו כסף ללמוד:


*And he that hath no money* to buy, that is, that has not the means required for study.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:3)


**שברו [ואכלו].** הטעם על החכמה, כטעם אכול את המגילה הזאת (יחזקאל ג' א'), כי החכמה לנשמה כמאכל לגוף:


*Buy and eat* the wisdom. Comp.¹ Eat this roll, (Ez. 3:1). Wisdom is demanded by the soul as the food is demanded by the body.

footnotes:
¹ As to the verb to eat being used in a figurative sense, signifying to learn, to perceive.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:1:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:4)


**ולכו.** אלי:


*Come ye* unto me,


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:1:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:1:5)


**והטעם [צ"ל וטעם] ושברו חנם.** ואכולו בלא כסף, וטעם שברו יין וחלב, כי שניהם הם כמו מאכל ומשתה, וכן יודו חכמי הרפואות, וטעם יין וחלב, כי התורה נמשלה בהם:


*Buy* for nothing, *And eat* without paying. *Wine and milk*. Each serves both for food and drink, as medical authorities assert.² Wine and milk are mentioned because the Law is compared with them.³

footnotes:
² The function of the drink is to dissolve the food and to accelerate its digestion; most beverages, according to I. E., are believed to contain no elements of nourishment, but in wine and milk both properties are found, they nourish and accelerate the digestion.
³ Comp. Midrash Yalkut ad locum, and I. E. on Solomon’s Song 2:4.—No other passage of the Bible, however, can be adduced, in which the Law is compared with wine and milk.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:2:1)


**למה וגו'.** שיוגיעו עצמם בחכמות נכריות שלא יועילו:


*Wherefore do you spend money*, etc. Wherefore will you labour in profane science⁴ which is of no use to you.

footnotes:
⁴ By the term חכמות נכריות profane science, as contrasted with the knowledge of the Law, I. E. means hardly anything but speculative philosophy, metaphysics; because all practical sciences, especially the science of nature, is repeatedly recommended by I. E.; comp. his commentary on Exod. 20:1.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:2:2)


**ואכלו טוב ותתענג בדשן.** כמו והיה דשן ושמן (ישעיהו ל' כ"ג) כטעם תענוג הנשמה במות הגוף, או טעמו:


בדשן *In fatness*. Comp. דשן (30:23). *Let your soul delight itself in fatness*, that is, in that happiness which the soul enjoys after its separation from the body by death.⁵

footnotes:
⁵ A second explanation is indicated by I. E. in the additional words או טעמו or its meaning is; the explanation itself is missing in the Hebrew text, or it is the same which is mentioned below (ver. 3.), and is likewise introduced by the words או טעם; the two words have therefore been omitted in the translation.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:1)


**הטו.** ולכו ממקומכם אלי, כמו סור' אלי אל תירא [שופטים ד, יח]:


ולכו אלי *And come unto me*. Lit., Go away from your place toward me; comp. סורה אלי turn in to me (Jud. 4:18).⁶

footnotes:
⁶ הלך to go signifies removal from the place of him that speaks, בוא to come, approach to it. The preposition אלי demands the verb ובואו, while the verb ולכו demands ממני; I. E. therefore explains the words ולכו אלי as an elliptical phrase, meaning, and go from your place and come unto me. Comp. I. E. on 31:1, Note 2.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:2)


**ותחי נפשכם.** הטעם עמידת הנשמה במות הגוף או טעם, שיחיים המשיח, אחרי ששבו לדת השם:


*And your soul shall live*. That is, your soul shall live for ever after the death of the body, or you will receive new life through Messiah, when you will return to the Divine Law.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:3:3)


**ואכרתה לכם ברית עולם.** שלא תמוט, כברית וחסד שכרתי עם דוד, וכתוב לעולם אשמור לו חסדי [תהילים פט, כט] ויתכן היות חסדי דוד רמז על המשיח שהוא ממשפחתו כאשר נקרא הנביא ישראל, וכאלו הוא, כי חסדי דוד נאמני' הם והעד על זה, הפסוק הבא אחריו:


*An everlasting covenant*, that will never expire. *The sure mercy of David*, that is, like the covenant which I made with David and the kindness which I showed to him, promising him my mercy will I keep for him for evermore, etc. (Ps. 89:29). It is also possible, that by David in this verse Messiah is meant, who will be of the family of David; as the prophet is sometimes called Israel for the same reason;⁷ and the meaning of הנאמנים חסדי דוד is in that case: for the kindness of Messiah is sure.⁸ This explanation is supported by the next verse.

footnotes:
⁷ See I. E. on 49:3.
⁸ That is, is everlasting, and therefore the covenant which will be made with you through him, will likewise be ברית עולם an everlasting covenant. According to the first explanation the everlasting covenant promised here, is compared with the everlasting covenant which God made with King David.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:1)


**הן עד.** זהו המשיח:


*Behold, I have given him*, namely, Messiah.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:2)


**למ"ד לאומים שורש.** ויתכן היות לטעם [והטעם] כי המשיח לעד כי אין מלך אחר נגיד על העולם:


לאמים The people, the ל being radical; or to the people, the ל being a preposition.⁹ *For a witness*. Messiah will testify, that there is no other king, no other ruler of the world, than God.

footnotes:
⁹ There are in Hebrew two words which signify nation, namely: אֹם and לאֹם; pl. אֻמִּים (Ps. 117:1) and לאֻמִּים (49:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:4:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:4:3)


**ומצוה.** אשר יצוה מה שיצוה (יעשו):


ומצוה And one that issues commands.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ This remark appears to be quite superfluous, since מְצַוֵּה can hardly mean anything else; it is perhaps intended to indicate that it is not an irregular participle instead of מְצַוֶּה, but the construct state of the noun מְצַוֶּה commander. See Kimchi ad locum.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:1)


**הן גוי לא תדע.** גוי לא היית יודעו תקרא, שיבוא אליך, כטעם לעבדי קראתי (איוב י"ט ט"ז):


*A nation, that thou knowest not*, which thou hast not known hitherto, *thou shalt call* to come unto thee; comp. I called my servant, etc. (Job 19:16).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:2)


**אליך ירוצו.** והנה התברר מה שפירשתי:


*And nations that knew not thee shall run unto thee*. This proves my explanation¹¹ to be correct.

footnotes:
¹¹ This refers to the opinion of I. E. that the prophecies contained in this part of the book, describe the time of Messiah yet to come; the verse before us supports that opinion, since the promise contained in it, has not yet been fulfilled.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:5:3)


**פארך.** מלה זרה בדקדוק, כי אין כמוה בפעלים השלמים, רק בנחים כמו כשמעתו ענך (ישעיהו ל' י"ט):


פארך *He hath glorified thee*. It is irregular;¹² there is no other instance of a perfect verb having this form; but there is one of the weak verb: עׇנׇךְ He hath answered thee (30:19)

footnotes:
¹² The regular form of the two verbs is: עׇנְךָ ,פְּאֵרְךָ.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:6:1)


**דרשו וגו'.** לפי דעתי כי זאת הפרשה תוכחה על אנשי דורו, הטעם אחר שתדעו כי תגאלו מבבל וגם מכל הגוים פעם שנית דרשו השם:


*Seek ye the Lord*. This appeal is made to the contemporaries of the prophet,¹³ telling them to seek the Lord, since they knew that they would be redeemed from Babylon, and after that again from all other nations.

footnotes:
¹³ That were, together with the prophet, captives in Babylon. See I. E. on 40:1.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:6:2)


וטעם **בהמצאו** לדורשים, כי ידוע שהשם נמצא בכל מקום ובכל עת, הנה הטעם קודם חתום הגזרות, וכן טעם בהיותו קרוב, רמז לשכינה שהיא במקדש:


*While He may be found* by those that seek Him. God is certainly everywhere at all times; but the meaning of this phrase is, while the decree is not yet resolved upon: in a similar way the phrase, while He is near is to be explained, namely, while He permits His glory to rest upon the temple.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ The words רמז לשכינה שהיא במקדש seem to be a new explanation, which is quite different from the preceding one while the decree is not yet resolved upon. In the commentary Michlal Jofi the latter is assigned to the Talmud, the former to Don Isaak Abravanel. We conjecture therefore that the word או or before רמז has been dropped; and have restored it in the translation.



### Verse 7

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:7:1)


**יעזוב וגו'.** פירוש דרשו השם:


*Let the wicked forsake*, etc. This is the explanation of Seek ye the Lord, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:7:2)


**דרכו.** שהוא נהוג ללכת בה, ויעזוב איש און מחשבותיו, והנה העקר המחשבה והמעשה:


*His way*. The way which he is accustomed to go. ואיש און מחשבתיו *And the unrighteous man his thoughts*. Supply יעזב let him forsake. The principal points, the thought and the deed are mentioned by the prophet.¹⁵

footnotes:
¹⁵ According to I. E. דרך signifies the way of action, the practice, contrasted with מחשבה thought, plan.

**כי ירבה לסלוח.** העונות:


*He will abundantly pardon* the iniquities.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:8:1)


**כי וגו'.** טעמו כי חשבתם שאגמול לכם רע אע"פ שתשובו אלי, על כן לא מחשבותי כמחשבותיכם, כי במחשבותי להטיב לכם, וככה לא דרככם דרכי, כי דרכי הם ישרי', גם מפורש בספר יחזקאל הדרכי לא יתכנו (יחזקאל י"ח כ"ט):


*For my thoughts are not yours*. You thought that I should punish you even after your return to me; but your thoughts are not mine; my intention is to do good to you. *Neither are your ways my ways*. My ways are righteous; comp., Are not my ways equal? are not your ways unequal ? (Ez. 18:19)



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:9:1)


**כי וגו'.** דרך משל:


*For as the heavens*, etc., *so are my ways higher*, etc. This is a figurative expression.¹⁶

¹⁶ In the Hebrew text there is no proper distinction between this verse and the succeeding. משל should be separated from the succeeding words by a full stop. The conjunction כי, which follows, is not part of the commentary but of ver. 10, the text which is to be explained.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:10:1)


**כי הגשם.** ברדתו מן השמים, ירוה את הארץ, על כן הורדתיה לתת זרע לזורע ולחם לאוכל:


*For as the rain cometh down*, etc. The rain watereth the earth, in coming down from heaven; for that purpose God sends it down, in order that seed may be given to the sower and bread to the eater.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:11:1

**כן יהיה דברי.** לא ישוב אלי ריקם, והטעם כי אמלא כל אשר דברתי אל נביאי, וזהו:


*So shall my word*, etc. I shall fulfil all I spake to the prophets.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:12:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:12:2)


**תובלון.** אל ארצכם על סוסים ופרדים, [אם] על גלות בבל, כן היה ואם לעתיד מפורש בסוף הספר (ישעיהו ס"ו כ'), י"א על שתי גליות דיבר:


*And be led forth with peace* to your land on horses and mules. If this passage be referred to the Babylonian exile, it was indeed literally fulfilled.¹⁷ But if it is understood to allude to a future redemption, in that case comp. And they shall bring all your brethren upon horses, etc. (66:20). Some refer it to both.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁷ Comp. Ezr. 1:3, sqq.
¹⁸ To the Babylonian exile and the Roman exile.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:12:3)


**ימחאו.** כטעם יכו, וזאת הלשון ידועה בארמית, ומגזרת ומחה אל כתף ים כנרת (במדבר ל"ד י"א):


ימחאו *Shall clap*. This verb is frequently met with in the Chaldee.¹⁹ ומחה and shall reach (Num. 34:11) is of the same root.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ Comp. Dan. 2:35, 5:19.
²⁰ The two verbs compared by I. E. are not the same, the one is ל״ה, the other ל״א; but א and ה interchange. The word מגזרת before ומחה seems to be a corruption of ומגזרתו; since ימחאו is not derived from מחה, but the latter is, in the one passage quoted here, exceptionally used in the sense of מחא, to join, to clap, or to strike.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:13:1)


**תחת הנעצוץ.** כמו הנעצוצים (ישעיהו ז' י"ט), ואין ספק כי הברוש טוב ממנו:


הנעצוץ *The thorn*. Comp. הנעצוצים the thorns (7:19). The fir is undoubtedly better than the thorn.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 55:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/55:13:2)


**הסרפד.** מין ממיני צמחי החוחים, הנה יחדש פלא, לשום נהרות במדבר, בשובם אל ציון, וזהו והיה ליי לשם לאות עולם, וזהו פלא עומד:


סרפד *The brier*. A kind of thorn. *And it shall be to the Lord for a name*, etc. He will perform wonders, in providing the wilderness with rivers, when Israel will return to Zion, and this will be to the Lord *An everlasting sign*, a miracle that will remain for ever.²¹

footnotes:
²¹ I. E. means either that the rivers and fountains produced in the wilderness by a miracle will remain for ever, and thus continually testify the glory of God, or that the miracle will be of such an extraordinary character, that it will for ever remain in the memory of mankind.



## Chapter 56


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:1:1)


**כה.** אחר שתדעון כי השם יגאלכם [ויעשה] לכם כל אלה הטובות, שמרו משפטיו כי קרובה הישועה, והנה לעד כי העונות מעכב [צ"ל מעכבות] ביאת משיח:


*Keep ye judgment*, etc. You know that God will redeem you, and that He will bless you with all these benefits; keep, therefore, His judgments, for, if you do this, salvation is near to come. We may learn from this verse that the coming of Messiah is delayed because of our sins.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:2:1)


**יעשה זאת.** המצוה שאמר והיא שמור שבת מחללו, וידוע כי שבת סימן התיו לנקבה, אולי זה בא כאילו אמר יום שבת, או יהיה וי"ו מחללו חלול השמור, כי עם כל פועל שם הוא בכח הלשון ואם לא נכתב, כאשר פירש רבי משה הכהן ז"ל במלת ותצפנו (יהושע ב' ד') שהוא שב ללקח, וכמוהו וברב יועצים תקום (משלי ט"ו כ"ב), והטעם עצה ואם לא נכתב:


*Blessed is the man that does this*, that keeps the following precepts, to observe the Sabbath, etc. מחללו *From polluting it*. It is certain that the ת in שבת indicates the feminine gender;¹ the masculine pronoun וֹ refers to the masculine noun יום day, which may be supplied before שבת, or to the verbal noun שִׁמּוּר implied in the verb שֹׁמֵר; for every verb implies a verbal noun, if that is not directly expressed;² compare the remark of R. Moses Hakkohen on וַתִּצְפְּנוֹ (Jos. 2:7), that the suffix refers to the verbal noun the taking;³ compare also ברב יעצים עצה תקום ═ ברב יעצים תקום, in the multitude of counsellors it is established⁴ (Prov. 15:22), the word עצה being supplied.

footnotes:
¹ It is generally believed that the ת in שבת is radical and that it is formed from שבת, like גַּנׇּב thief from גׇּנַב to steal. I. E. either derives the word from שוב to return, to rest, or believes that one ת has been dropped.
² I. E. repeatedly mentions the rule that every form of the verb contains the verbal noun, which may be supplied, whenever required, either in the form of a masculine noun, or of a feminine one, according to circumstances. The suffix singular וֹ in ותצפנו (Jos. 2:4.) does not agree with the plural שני האנשים the two men; it is therefore explained to refer to the noun לקח the taking contained in the verb ותקח and she took, and the sense of the passage is accordingly: She took the two men and hid that fact. The subject to תקום (Prov. 15:22) is עצה counsel, which is contained in the participle יועצים they that give counsel. The masculine suffix וֹ in מחללו is in the same way explained to refer to the masculine noun שמור the keeping, contained in the participle שמר who keepeth.
³ A. V., And hid them.
⁴ A. V., But in multitude of counsellors they (the purposes מחשבות) are established.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:1)


**בן הנכר.** אלה הגרים גרי הצדק:


*The son of the stranger*. The true proselytes.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:2)


**הנלוה.** פועל עבר והה"א תחת אשר, כה"א ההלכוא אתו (יהושע י' כ"ד):


הַנִּלְוׇה *That hath joined himself*. It is the past tense with a prefixed ה, which is here equivalent to the relative אשר that; comp. ההלכוא who went (Jos. 10:24)⁵.

footnotes:
⁵ The past of the Niphal of לוה is נִלְוׇה, the participle נִלְוֶה m., נִלְוׇה f. Because of the preceding בן הנכר the masculine is here required, and נִלְוׇה is consequently the past, third person masculine; the ה, which before nouns and participles has a demonstrative character, has before the past or future of a verb the power of a relative pronoun. This latter case is, however, very rare.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:3)


**יבדילני.** פתח גדול תחת קמץ קטן, וכמוהו כי עתה יאהבני אישי (בראשית כ"ט ל"ב):


יבדילֵנִי═יבדילַני The Lord will separate me. Comp. יאהבַני (my husband) will love me (Gen. 29:32).⁶

footnotes:
⁶ The vowel, which connects the suffix with the verb, is Kamez or Pathah for the forms of the past tense, Zere or Segol for the other forms. This rule, however, is not without exceptions, of which יַבְדִילַנִי instead of יַבְדִּילֵנִי is one.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:3:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:3:4)


**הן אני עץ יבש.** בעבור שלא יוליד:


*I am a dry tree*, because I cannot have children.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:4:1)


**כי כה אמר יי.** הזכיר השבתו', כי אות היא בינו ובין שומרימו בעבור ששבת השם, הנה כל שומר שבת הוא לשם:


*That keep my sabbath*, etc. The sabbath is mentioned, because it is a sign of the covenant between Him and those that keep it, on account of God having rested on it;⁷ he who keeps the Sabbath is, therefore, a worshipper of the Lord.

footnotes:
⁷ The words on account of God having rested on that day are part of the condition of the covenant; the Sabbath is to be kept, because God declared it holy when He created the universe in six days and rested on the seventh.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:5:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:6:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:7:1)

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:8:1)


**נאם. מקבץ נדחי ישראל.** כי אם עלו מבבל ומעילם ואשור:


*The outcasts of Israel*, that came from Babylon, Elam, and Assyria.⁸

footnotes:
⁸ The words of the Hebrew text are: כי אם עלו מבבל ומעילם ומאשור. It is impossible to make sense of these words; אם is probably the cause of the confusion, and if we replace it by הם, they, we get a tolerable sense; this emendation has been adopted for the translation. But the whole remark of I. E. seems to be superfluous, for the meaning of the outcasts of Israel is well known. Another emendation suggests itself to the reader, namely, to alter אם into עמהם with them; and to translate the phrase thus: For people of Babylon, Elam, Assyria went up with them (the Israelites). The remark would in that case not explain the expression outcasts of Israel, but the word לנקבציו; its proper place would then be at the end of the verse.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:8:2)


וטעם **לנקבציו** על הגרים, והנה עוד אקבץ גרים על נקבצי ישראל, וי"ו לנקבציו שב אל ישראל:


*Beside those that are gathered unto him*, that is, besides the proselytes. The meaning of the whole phrase is, *Yet* will I gather others to him, besides those that have already joined Israel. The suffix in ¹לנקבציו, that are gathered unto him, refers to Israel.

footnotes:
¹ ולנקבציו of the Hebrew text is probably a corruption of ו״״ו לנקבציו.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:9:1)


**כל וגו'.** הטעם שהצדיקים גם הגרים ישובו, רק המקטרים לע"ז לא ישובו, והנה אתיו לשון ציווי, כמו אם תבעיון בעיו שובו אתיו (ישעיהו כ"א י"ב) כמו בואו, מגזרת אתא מרבבות קודש (דברים ל"ג ב'), והטעם, כי השם צוה לאומות העולם הרשעים, להרוג רשעי ישראל, כמו החיות שתהרוגנ' אלה את אלה:


*All ye beasts of the field*, etc. The idea connecting the following with the preceding verses is, that the righteous Israelites and the proselytes will return, but those that persevere in the worship of idols will not return. אתיו *Come*. It is imperative (comp. 21:12) of אתה to come; comp. ואתה, and He came (Deut. 33:2). God summons the idolatrous wicked nations, to come and devour the wicked of Israel, like wild beasts that devour each other.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:1)


**צופיו.** יאמר אל נביאי השקר שהיו בישראל, והיו כצופים עורים, והנה דרך משל, על היום או על כלבים אלמים בלילה כי לא ישמרו הבית ותועלת אין בהם:


*His watchmen are blind*, etc. The false prophets in Israel are meant, who were like blind watchmen during the day, and like dumb dogs during the night, that cannot guard the house and are of no use whatever.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:2)


**לנבוח.** זעקת הכלב, וכן בלשון קדר:


לנבח *To bark*. The word has in Arabic the same meaning.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:10:3)


**הזים.** כמו כלבים, ואין ריע לו, כי הה"א עיקר כה"א הורים והוגים (ישעיהו נ"ט י"ג), כי לא יבא הפועל מבנין הפעיל כי אם במ"ם, פירש רבי יונה אמר המתרגם ניימין שכבין, לפי שהכלבים הם אדוקים בתנומה יותר משאר כל בעלי חיים, והנה הטעם כפול:


הזים *Dogs*.⁹ It is hap. leg.; the ה is radical as in הורו והנו conceiving and uttering (59:13).¹⁰ The participle Hiphil has always מ at the beginning.—R. Jonah says that the Targum renders הזים by ניימין slumbering, because dogs are more addicted to slumber than all other animals.¹¹ *Loving the slumber*. Repetition of the same idea.

footnotes:
⁹ A. V., Sleeping.
¹⁰ The Hebrew text has הורים והוגים; but since those words do not occur in the Bible, the words הרו והגו have been substituted for them. I. E. read perhaps הרים והגים instead of הרו והגו.
¹¹ Dogs are employed as the guardians of the house, because their sleep is not very deep, but rather like slumbering which is interrupted by the least noise; they are, therefore, according to R. Jonah, called the slumberers.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:1)


**והכלבים עזי נפש.** רוב הנפש הנמצא במקרא על הכח המתאוה לאכל, כמו ונפשו מאכל תאוה (איוב ל"ג כ'), והטעם, כי על [צ"ל כל] אלה הכלבים אין בהם תועלת רק יזיקו, כי הם חזקי התאוה, וזאת היא עזות נפש, ולא ישבעו לעולם, והנה הנמשל:


עזי נפש *Greedy*. The word נפש is mostly used in Scripture to express the appetitive soul;¹² comp. ונפשו מאכל תאוה and his soul (abhorreth) dainty meat (Job 33:20). All these dogs are useless; they do only harm, because of their strong, insatiable appetite, called עזות נפש greediness;¹ they can never have enough. The words which follow contain the explanation of the figure used here.

footnotes:
¹² Comp. I. E. on 26:9, Note 9, and Eccles. 7:3. Three kinds of נפש, soul, are mentioned there; one of them, which is mostly understood by נפש, is נפש הצומחת or נפש המתאוה, the vegetative or appetitive soul.
¹ Lit., Strength of appetite.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:2)


**והמה.** הטעם הכלבים הנזכרים, הם רועי ישראל שלא ידעו הבין, שם הפועל:


*And they*, the dogs mentioned here, *Are the shepherds* of Israel, that cannot understand. הבין *Understand*. It is infinitive.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:3)


**איש לבצעו.** מה יועיל לו מאומה כמו מה בצע בדמי (תהלים ל' י'):


לבצעו *For his gain*, for that which brings him profit; comp. מה בצע what profit is there (Ps. 30:10).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:11:4)


**[מקצהו].** כל אחד מקצהו:


מקצהו *From his quarter*. Every one from his quarter.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ This remark, which is usually made by I. E. to explain the use of the singular instead of the plural, is here superfluous; since the singular איש, and also לבצעו are preceding. The similar phrase, כל העם מקצה (Gen. 19:4) was perhaps intended as an explanation of מקצהו, everyone, from whatever quarter he might come.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:1)


**אתיו וגו'.** ובממון שיקחו חמס יתענגו בו לשתות, ואומר הרועה לחבירו בא ונקחה יין:


*Come ye*, etc. The money which they acquire unjustly, they spend in feasting, and one shepherd says to his fellow- shepherd, Come, let us buy wine.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:2)


**ונסבאה שכר.** משכר, כמו אל תהי בסובאי יין (משלי כ"ג כ'), ולא יעשו יום אחד לבדו, רק יום אחר יום:


ונסבאה שכר *And let us fill ourselves with strong drink*. Let us make ourselves drunk.¹⁴ Comp. סבאי יין wine-bibbers (Prov. 23:20). *And to-morrow shall be as this day*. They do this not one day alone but day after day.

footnotes:
¹⁴ משכר in the Hebrew text is probably a corruption of נשתכר; and the quotation from the Book of Proverbs is to prove that the verb סבא means to drink too much. Comp. I. E. on Deut. 21:20.—To explain שכר by משכר of strong drink would be wrong, since סבא does not govern the preposition מן of; and would not be supported by the phrase quoted.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 56:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/56:12:3)


**יתר מאד.** תאר השם, שיהיה ליום מחר יתרון על היום בעונג ובמשתה:


יתר *More abundant*. It is an adjective. The morrow shall excel to-day in pleasure and feasting.



## Chapter 57


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:1:1)


**הצדיק.** אלה מעשה הרועים, הצדיקים אבדו, ואין איש שם על לב לאמר, מדוע יאבדו הצדיקים ויחיו אלה הרשעים, והנה זה פי' הנביא, נאסף הצדיק עד שלא יראה הרע הבא על ישראל, ועל עיר הקודש:


*The righteous perisheth*, etc. There is nothing but the deeds of these evil shepherds; the righteous are gone, *And no man layeth it to heart* to consider, why do the righteous perish, and those wicked people remain alive; but the prophet gives the answer to this question: *The righteous is taken away from the evil to come*, that he should not see the evil that is coming over Israel and the holy city.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:2:1)


**יבא וגו'.** [יבואו] הצדיקים בשלום על קברם, כטעם בשלום תמות (ירמיה ל"ד ה') ואתה תבא אל אבותיך בשלום (בראשית ט"ו ט"ו):


יבא שלום *He shall enter into peace*, etc. The righteous shall come in peace to his grave; comp. Thou shalt die in peace (Jer. 34:5); And thou shalt go to thy fathers in peace (Gen. 15:15).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:2:2)


**ינוחו על משכבותם.** כל מי שהולך נוכח השם, כטעם אחרי יי אלהיכם תלכו (דברים י"ג ה'), וי"א השלום יבא עם ההשקט וינוחו על משכבותם:


ינוחו על משכבותם הלך נכחו *They that walk before Him, shall rest in their beds*.¹ Comp. אחרי יי אלהיכם תלכו ye shall walk after the Lord your God (Deut. 13:5). Some explain the verse thus: Peace and tranquillity shall come to them, and they that walk, etc.²

footnotes:
¹ A. V., They shall rest in their beds, each one walking in his uprightness.
² According to the first explanation בשלום ═ שלום in peace, and the subject הצדיק the righteous must be supplied, which is the subject to יבא as well as to ינוחו; to the latter in a collective sense. According to the second explanation שלום is the subject to יבוא, and שלום together with השקט tranquillity (which must be supplied), the subject to the plural form ינוחו, they shall rest. But whence we have to get the supplementary השקט is not explained.

**הולך נכוחו.** [והנה נכוחו] תחת נכחו, כי משקלי השמות משתנים:


נִכְחוֹ ═ נְכֹחוֹ *Before Him*. The form of nouns varies.³

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:5:1)


**הנחמים.** הטוב בפירושים, שידבר על ע"ז, ויהיה הנחמים על משקל הנצבים (בראשית מ"ה א'), מבנין נפעל, מגזרת בכל יחם הצאן [שם ל' מ"א], והנה הוא דבק עם ילדי פשע והנה כתוב, ובחטא יחמתני אמי (תהלים נ"א ז'):


הנחמים באלים The best of the various explanations of this phrase is that it refers to idolatry;⁴ הנחמים Who are conceived, similar in form to הנצבים that stood (Gen. 45:1), is the Niphal of יחם to conceive; comp. בכלּ יַחֵם whensoever (the stronger cattle) did conceive (Gen. 30:41). This expression is the description of children of transgression (ver. 4); comp., And in sin did my mother conceive me (Ps. 51:7).

footnotes:
⁴ The noun אלים signifies here trees under which idols were worshipped. See Rashi and Targum ad locum.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:8:8](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:8:8)


**[יד חזית].** בכל מקום שראית, (כמו בכל מקום אשר תראה דברים י"ב י"ג):


יד חזית *In every place which thou sawest*.¹¹ It has the same meaning as בכל מקום אשר תראה in every place, which thou seest (Deut. 12:13)

footnotes:
¹¹ A. V., Where thou sawest it.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:1)


**ותשורי וגו'.** והנה עוד רעה אחרת, לא די שעבדת לע"ז, עד ששגרת דורון למלך אשור או למצרים להשען עליו, והנה ותשורי כמו אשורנו, הלכת לראות:


ותשרי וגו׳ *And thou gavest*,¹² etc. There is yet another evil, says the Lord, to Israel; thou hast not only worshipped idols, thou hast also sent presents to the kings of Assyria or Egypt, and hast relied on them.¹³ As to the meaning of ותשרי and thou gavest a present, comp. ותשורה and a present (1 Sam. 9:7); R. Moses Hannagid¹⁴ derives תשורה from שור to see, and explains it to signify the fees for the vision and prophecy; according to this explanation ותשרי may be compared with אשורנו I shall see him (Num. 24:17), and explained thou didst go to see him.

footnotes:
¹² A. V., And thou wentest.
¹³ Comp. c. xxx. and xxxi.; Hos. 14:4; 2 Kings 16:8, 17:4.
¹⁴ R. Moses Hannagid is probably identical with R. Moses Hakkohen. Hannagid means the prince, and is a title given to men of distinction.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:2)


**בשמן.** כי מארץ ישראל יוליכו השמן:


*With oil*. Oil was exported from Palestine.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:3)


**ציריך.** הם השלוחים:


ציריך Thy messengers.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:9:4)


**ותשפילי.** נפשך, עד שאול:


זתשפילי *And didst debase* thyself.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:10:1)


**ברוב דרכך יגעת.** מרוב דרכים ששנית, והנה יגעת, ולא אמרת נואש לבי, כמו ונואש ממנו שאול (שמואל א' כ"ז ב'), רק אמרת אולי תועיל יגיעתי:


*In the greatness of thy ways*, which thou didst frequent, and in which thou hast wearied thyself, without saying: נואש *there is no hope*, my heart is despairing;¹⁵ (comp. שאול ונואש ממני and Saul shall despair of me (1 Sam. 27:2)); thou thoughtest that thy exertion might still be of some use.

footnotes:
¹⁵ I. E. supplies the masculine noun לבי, my heart, as the subject to נואש.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:10:2)


**חית.** כמו כח, והטעם דבק עם יגעת, על כן לא חלית:


חית *The life*, that is, the strength. *Thou hast found the life of thine hand*, when thou hadst wearied thyself; therefore thou wast not grieved.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:11:1)


**ואת וגו'.** למה הוצרכת לדאוג מאויב ולירא מאויב עד שהוצרכת לכזב, ולא זכרת אותי:


*And of whom hast thou been afraid*, etc. What hadst thou to fear from an enemy and to be afraid of him for, so as to lie, and not to think of me.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:11:2)


**הלא אני מחשה.** לפי דעתי שהוא פועל יוצא לשנים פעולים, והטעם כי אני משתיק באמת מי שיכזב, כן אני וכן הייתי, ויתכן היות את מי דאגת, מתי יראת ממני, והראשון הוא הנכון, ויש אומרים שטעם מחשה כטעם החשיתי (מ"ב י"ד) שאסבול, כאדם שישתוק:


מחשה is a causative verb, and means silencing. אני מחשה ומעולם *I silence, even of old*,¹⁶ those that lie; this I am doing now, and have always done. It is, however, possible to explain the words ואת מי דאגת ונו׳ when hast thou feared me, etc.;¹⁷ but I prefer the first explanation. Some compare אני מחשה with החשתי I have holden my peace (42:14), and explain it I held my peace, I forbore; it is in that case an anthropomorphism.

footnotes:
¹⁶ A. V., Have not I held my peace even of old.
¹⁷ One can hardly see how the meaning when can be found in the words מתי ;ואת מי is perhaps a corruption of את מי, and the meaning of I. E.’s remark would in that case be, for whom hast thou been afraid of me ?



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:12:1)


**אני אגיד צדקתך.** בפה:


צדקתך *Thy righteousness* in words.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:12:2)


**ואת מעשיך ולא יועילוך.** בעבור שמעשיך רעי', שבטחת על זולתי יי:


*And thy works they shall not profit thee*, because they are bad; thou hast trusted to others beside me.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:1)


**בזעקך יצילוך קבוציך.** אלה שקבצת להושיעך, והנה קבוציך תאר השם, כמו למודי יי (ישעיהו נ"ד י"ג):


קבוציך *Thy companies*, which thou hast brought together for thy assistance. קבוציך lit., those gathered by thee, is an adjective, in form like למודי taught of (54:13).¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁸ That is, the pupils of. Comp. c. iii. Note 5.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:2)


**ואת כולם ישא רוח יקח הבל.** (אותם) דרך משל שיאבדו ולא יראו ישועת השם:


*But the wind shall carry them all away*, etc. This is a figurative expression for they will perish and not see the salvation which is coming from the Lord.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:13:3)


**והחוסה בי ינחל ארץ ויירש הר קדשי.** והנה הוא דבק עם הפרשה הנכתבת למעלה כל שומר שבת (ישעיהו נ"ו ו'):


*And he that putteth his trust*, etc. We see here how this chapter is connected with the preceding; comp. whosoever keepeth the Sabbath etc. (56:6).¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁹ I. E. seems to consider the keeping of the Sabbath as a sign of our trust in the Lord, since he finds in the words and he that putteth a trust in me a reference to the words that keepeth the Sabbath from polluting it.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:1)


**ואמר.** האומר או הקורא או הכרוז:


ואמר *And it will be said*. Lit., and shall say the subject, האומר he who will say, הקורא he who will call, or הכרוז the proclamation is to be supplied.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ Comp. I. E. on 2:4, Note 5.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:2)


**סולו סולו.** המסילה סקלו מאבן, וטעם פעמים שהקורא יקרא כן פעם אחר פעם:


סלו Remove the stones from the path. The repetition of סלו indicates, that this proclamation is to be made repeatedly.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:14:3)


**מדרך עמי.** שהיו עובדי השם, על כן בסוף הפרשה אין שלום אמר יי לרשעים:


*My people*, that is, those that worship the Lord; comp., there is no peace to the wicked (ver. 21).²¹
