²¹ The expression עמי my people must, therefore, be limited to the good of the people of God; only for them are all these happy events predicted.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:1)


**רם ונשא.** שמו:


רם ונשא *The high and lofty*. He whose name is high and lofty.²²

footnotes:
²² Instead of attributing the properties high and lofty directly to God, I. E. connects them with the name of God, in order to attenuate the anthropomorphism.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:2)


**שוכן עד.** עד עולמי עד, עד שלא יוכל אדם לספור, והטעם נצח, וטעם שוכן כי כל הנבראים יש להם תנועה גם לכוכבים תנועה כנשמה:


עולמי עד═עד Innumerable worlds; עד signifies that which cannot be counted; eternity.²³ *That resteth for ever*. This is a distinctive attribute of God, since all creatures move, the stars also change their places, and even the soul.²⁴

footnotes:
²³ I. E. repeatedly gives this paraphrase of עד, but does not explain how it is drawn from the word עד. It would be equally strange to suppose that עד is the beginning of a sentence which is to be supplied, namely, עד שלא יוכלו לספור; a similar ellipsis is suggested by I. E., for the phrase עולם ועד עולם═עולם ועד Comp. I. E. on Ex. 15:18; Ps. 9:6.
²⁴ The Hebrew text has the words גם לכוכבים יש תנועה כנשמה also the stars move like the soul; but it can hardly be found what I. E. meant by these words. We have, perhaps, to read גם לנשמה instead of כנשמה, as has been emended for the translation, or בשמים in the heavens. In the latter case, the meaning of the phrase would be, that even the stars, which are, according to the opinion of I. E., more stationary and durable than the earth and the creatures below, move about in their exalted places.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:15:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:15:3)


**מרום וקדוש אשכון וגו'.** והטעם כי אשכון עם המלאכים למעלה, ועם דכא שהוא בארץ, (וטעם אשכון) להחיות רוח שפלים, או אשכון מרום להחיות אלה השפלים:


*I dwell in the high and holy place*, with the angels above. ואת דכא ושפל רוח *And with him that is of a contrite and humble spirit* on earth, I dwell, to revive the spirit, etc.; or, I dwell in the high and holy place above with the angels in order to give life to those humble people on earth.²⁵

footnotes:
²⁵ According to the first explanation we have to repeat the verb אשכון after ואת דכא ושפל רוח; according to the second the verb להחיות must be supplied.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:16:1)

*Neither will I be always wroth;* for I have created the spirits, and the spirit that comes from me should be humble.²⁶

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:16:3)

### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:1)


**בעון. ואכהו.** שב אל עמי הנזכר למעלה, או אל דכא ושפל רוח, ואכהו פועל יורה על זמן עומד, כי אין סימן לו בלשון הקדש:


ואכהו *And smote him*, namely, my people (ver. 14), or him that is of a contrite and humble spirit (ver. 15). It is the imperfect, for which the Hebrew language has no special form.²⁸

footnotes:
²⁸ Comp. I. E. on 1:21, and Note 43.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:2)


**הסתר.** הסתרתי פני והכיתיהו ביד, דרך משל, עד שלא ארחם עליו, והנה הסתר שם הפועל:


*I hid me*. I hid my face when I smote him with my hand. It is a figurative expression for I smote him without pity. הסתר lit., to hide is infinitive.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:17:3)


**[וילך שובב].** הוא הלך שובב מתנצח ומתגבר ושב אל דרכו הרעה, ומלת שובב לגנאי:


וילך שובב *He went on returning*,²⁹ with frowardness and obstinacy, *in the way of his heart*, that is, in his evil ways. שובב is used in a bad sense.¹

footnotes:
²⁹ A. V., He went on frowardly.
¹ שובב is derived from שוב to return, to repeat, and means repeating perseveringly, but is always used in the Bible in a bad sense, while the verb שוב is chiefly used in a good sense: to cause to return to God or to the good way.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:1)


**דרכיו ראיתי.** הנה זאת לאות על יושר פירוש הספר, כאשר ראיתי דרכיו, או שעשה תשובה, או טעמו כמו כי יצר לב האדם רע (בראשית ח' כ"א):


*I have seen his ways*, etc. This verse proves that my opinion concerning this book is right.³⁰ *His ways*, that is, his repentance, or his innate evil inclination; comp. for the imagination of man’s heart is evil from his youth (Gen. 8:21).³¹

footnotes:
³⁰ The punishment of the Israelites, which consisted, according to I. E., in the Babylonian exile and their slow improvement, are described here in the past tense: Was I wroth, he went on frowardly in the way of his heart, I have seen his ways, but the promised deliverance in the future tense: and will heal them, etc.; I. E. infers from this that at the time when the prophet uttered this prophecy, the Babylonian exile was already expiring, and that the prophet consequently did not live in the time of King Hezekiah, but was a contemporary of the Persian King Cyrus, and of Zerubbabel.
³¹ According to both explanations the expression דרכיו his ways is different from the preceding ררך לבו the way of his heart, which refers to his evil doings. By his ways the prophet means, according to I. E., either his proper ways, the ways which he should go, that is, the way of repentance, or his natural character, his natural weakness in resisting temptation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:2)


**וארפאהו.** כי כחולה היה, כי אין כח לחולה שילך:


*And I will heal him*, *and I will lead him also*. He is like an invalid, that has no strength to go by himself.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:3)


**ואשלם נחומים לו.** שאנחמהו על החולי שעבר עליו:


*And I will restore comforts unto him* for the calamity that had befallen him.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:18:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:18:4)


**ולאבליו.** הם אוהביו כדרך האבלים על החולה במותו:


*And to his mourners*, that is, to his friends; people usually begin to mourn when they see their sick friend dying.³²

footnotes:
³² That is, before he is actually dead. Israel was in exile, and was considered by his friends as already entirely lost, without hope of recovery. I. E. explains by this comparison the expression ולאבליו and to his mourners, which is only used in case of death.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:19:1)


**בורא.** כל המפרשים אמרו כי השם הוא בורא, ותחסר מלת אמר, לולי שאין ראוי לחדש, כי הייתי אומר שהוא לשון בריאה מגזרת ובורא חושך (ישעיהו מ"ה ז'):


בורא *The Creator*. It is generally explained to refer to God, and the verb אמר said is supplied. Were it allowed to depart from the common explanation, I should suggest to take בורא in the sense of decreeing; comp. ובורא חשך (45:7).³³

footnotes:
³³ Comp. I. E. on 45:7, 40:28, Note 61, and on Gen. 1:1.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:19:2)


**ומלת ניב כמו פרי.** כמו תנובות שדי (דברים ל"ב י"ג), והטעם הדיבור, וכן פירושו אמרו שלום לרחוק ולקרוב, הודיעו שכבר רפא השם את ישראל, והטעם ורפאתיו:


ניב *Fruit* Comp. תנובות fruits (Deut. 32:13). By fruit of the lips the speech is meant. The meaning of the whole verse is: Proclaim, Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near; announce, that the Lord has already saved Israel, because ורפאתיו I have indeed healed him.³⁴

footnotes:
³⁴ ורפאתיו admits of two explanations; it can be past with ו conjunctive, and I have healed him, or past with ו conversive, I will heal him. I. E. seems to be in favour of the first explanation.



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:1)


**והרשעים וגו'.** והטעם שהשם ירפא צדיקי ישראל ולא הרשעים, כי הם כים שהוא נגרש תמיד, כמו ויגרשו מימיו, וקרוב מגזרת הנני גורש מפניך (שמות ל"ד א'):


*But the wicked are*, etc. God heals the righteous of Israel, but not the wicked, because the latter are troubled, like the sea that is continually troubled. נגרש *Troubled*. It has the same meaning as ויגרשו and they moved, and is probably of the same root as גורש driving out (Ex. 34:11);


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:2)


**כי השקט לא יוכל.** פירוש כים נגרש, הנה תחסר מלת שהוא (נגרש), כי נגרש תאר השם:


it is explained by the words which follow: when it cannot rest. Before נגרש the relative (אשר═) שהוא is to be supplied;³⁵ for נגרש is an adjective.¹

footnotes:
³⁵ Or the definite article בַּיָם הַנִּגְרָשׁ
¹ Comp. I. E. on 13:15, and Note 18.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:20:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:20:3)


**ויגרשו מימיו.** כמו ינועו:


ויגרשו And they moved.³⁶

³⁶ A. V., Whose waters cast up.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 57:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/57:21:1)


**אין.** על כן לא יהיה להם שלום, כי הם לא יוכלו השקט:


*There is no peace*, etc. No peace shall be to them, because they cannot rest.



## Chapter 58


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:1:1)


**קרא.** דבר השם אל נביאו קרא בגרון אל תחשוך הקריאה, כי חשך פועל יוצא:


*Cry aloud*. The prophet is addressed by God. אל תחשך *Spare not* the crying; the objective case must be supplied, because חשך is a transitive verb.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:1:2)


**כשופר.** שישמעו כולם:


*Like a trumpet*, etc. That all may hear.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:2:1)


**ואותי יום יום ידרושון.** בפה (ובדעת):


*Yet they seek me daily* with their words and thoughts.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:2:2)


**ודעת דרכי יחפצון.** בדבור שישאלון אליהם משפטי צדק, והם חפצים להיותם קרובים אלי:


*They wish to know my ways*. They express their wish in words, namely, *They ask of me* for themselves the ordinance of justice, and are desirous to be near me.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:1)


**למה.** הם מתענים ואומרים לשם למה צמנו ולא ראית, כאילו לא תראה ולא תדע, והטעם לא תושיענו, והתשובה הן ביום צומכם ימצא כל איש חפצו, מי שיש לו מריבה עם אדם אחר:


*Wherefore have we fasted*, etc. They fast, and then they say, Wherefore have we fasted. *And thou seest not*, etc. It is as if thou didst not see, nor take any knowledge of it; for thou dost not help us. The reply to these questions is: *Behold in the day of your fast*, etc. On the very day of the fast every one that has a dispute with his neighbour proceeds with his lawsuit.¹

footnotes:
¹ חפץ means desire, the object of the desire, business. מצא חפץ to find the object of his desire, to seek to find the object of his desire, to go after his business. This latter, general meaning of the expression is given also by Rashi and Targum Jonathan; I. E. explains it to seek the object of his desire, viz., of his neighbour, that is to seek to obtain what he demands from his neighbour, to proceed with his quarrel, and considers the beginning of the next verse הן לריב ומצה תצומו behold, ye fast for strife and debate, as the explanation of the words הן ביום צמכם תמצאו תפץ.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:2)


**וכל עצביכם.** ממון כמו ועצביך בבית נכרי (משלי ה' ו'), וקרוב מגזרת עצבון (בראשית ג' י"ז) כמו יגיע כפיך (תהלים קכ"ח ב'):


עצביכם *Your debtors*.² עצבים means money. Comp. ועצביך and thy wealth (Prov. 5:10); it is probably connected with עצבון labour2a (Gen. 3:17); comp. יגיע בפיך the labour of thine hands (Ps. 128:2); יגיע מצרים the labour of Egypt (45:14).

footnotes:
² A. V., Your labours. And thy labours. Sorrow.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:3:3)


**תנגושו.** הנה הנו"ן כנו"ן כהנדוף עשן [שם ס"ח ג'], ויחסר בעל כאילו אמר בעל עצבים וכמוהו אשה יראת יי (משלי ל"א ל') ורבים כך:


תנגשו *You press*.³ It is written in full with נ, like כהנדוף as is driven, תנדף drive (Ps. ixviii. 3).¹ וכל בעל עצביכם תנגשו═וכל עצביכם תננשו And you press all your debtors. Comp. אשה בעלת יראת יי═אשה יראת יי a woman that feareth the Lord⁴ (Prov. 31:30); there are many other instances of this kind of ellipsis.

footnotes:
³ A. V., You exact.
¹ The verbs פ״נ usually assimilate the נ to the next consonant and replace it by Dagesh whenever it concludes a syllable, e.g., תִּנְדֹּף═תִּדֹּף ,תִּנְגשֹׁוּ═תִּנּשֹׁוּ; in some cases the radical נ has been left; as e.g., in the examples given here by I. E.
⁴ Lit., A woman of the fear of the Lord; but אשה being in the absolute state, I. E. supplies a word in the construct state. Comp. I. E. on 30:20 42:25.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:4:1)


**באגרוף רשע.** דבר קשה שיוכה בו, ובדברי הקדמונים ז"ל בעלי אגרופין [פסחים נ"ג], וכמוהו באבן או באגרוף (שמות כ"א י"ח), וי"א חתיכת עפר קשה, כמו מגרפותיהם (יואל א' י"ז):


אגרף Some hard thing to strike with.⁵ In this sense it is used in Rabbinical literature. Comp. בעלי אגרפין men with force (Pesachim 53); compare besides באגרף (Ex. 21:18).⁶ Others⁷ render it a piece of hard earth, and connect it with מגרפותיהם their clods (Joel 1:17).

footnotes:
⁵ A. V., First.
⁶ In his commentary on Ex. 21:18, I. E. mentions this comparison in the name of Saadiah, while the other explanation, introduced here by the words, Others render it, is given, in his abridged commentary on Ex. 21:18, as his own, introduced by the word ויתכן, It is also right to say.
⁷ Very probably R. Jonah is meant, whose explanation is quoted in the commentary of I. E. on Ex. 21:18; he derived the word from the root גרף to sweep.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:4:2)


**לא תצומו כיום.** טעמו כיום הזה:


כיום הזה═כיום As ye do this day.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:1)


**הכזה.** יום ענות אדם נפשו, כפול, כי הוא הצום:


*A day for a man to afflict his soul*. Repetition of the same idea (a fast) in other words.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:2)


**הלכוף.** מפעלי הכפל במשקל לקב אויבי (במדבר כ"ג י"א):


לכוף *To bow down*. It is a verb ע״ע similar in form to לקב to curse (Num. 23:11).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:3)


**כאגמון.** צמח רך שישח את ראשו, והוא ידוע:


אנמן *Bulrush*. A tender plant, that bends its top; it is well known.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:5:4)


**יציע.** דגשות הצד"י לחסרון יו"ד השרש, כמלת אצרך (ירמיה א' ה') והשלם ייציע, והטעם ישים מצע [כמו] ושק ואפר יציע (אסתר ד' ג'):


יַצִּיעַ *To spread*. The Dagesh in צ compensates for the omission of the radical ;⁸י comp. אצרך I form thee (Jer. 1:5); the full form is יַיְצִיעַ, and its meaning is to place as a couch; comp. יצע was spread (Est. 4:3)

footnotes:
⁸ יצע is one of those verbs פ״י, that compensate for the omission of the י by the reduplication of the second radical.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:1)


**הלא.** פתח, כמו התר:


פתח *To loose*.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:2)


**חרצובות.** כמו קשרים, וכמוהו כי אין חרצובות למותם (תהלים ע"ג ד'):


חרצבות *The bands*. Comp. Ps. 73:4.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:6:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:3)


**מוטה.** כמו מטת עלכם (ויקרא כ"ו י"ג), והנה הטעם להחפיש העבדים, ככתוב בספר ירמיהו [ל"ד]:


מוטה *Yoke*. Comp. מוטות עלכם the bands of your yoke (Lev. 26:13). *To loose the bands*, etc. To make the slaves free. Comp. Jer. 1:34.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:6:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:6:4)


(העשוקים משפט). **רצוצים.** (כמו רצוצים) הם העבדים העשוקים, כמו רצוץ משפט (הושע ה' י"א), כמו ואת מי רצותי (שמואל א' י"ב ג'), ויש אומרים כי חרצובות רשע על המחשבות, והראשון נכון בעיני:


רצוצים⁹ *The oppressed*. The slaves that are oppressed; comp. רצוץ oppressed (Hos. 5:11); רצתי have I oppressed (l Sam. 12:3). Some understand to loose the bands, etc., to refer to the thoughts of man; but I prefer the first explanation.

footnotes:
⁹ The Hebrew text has before רצוצים the words העשוקים משפט, which are in no connection with the preceding remark; they are either the explanation of רצוצים, and should be placed after that word, or they are the result of the carelessness of some copyist, who had erroneously repeated them here from the succeeding remark, and forgot afterwards to strike them out; the latter suggestion is probable, since the explanation of רצוצים is complete without these two words.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:1)


**הלא פרוש.** כמו פורש אין להם (איכה ד' ד') וכמוהו פריסת מלכותך (דניאל ה' כ"ח), והטעם פריסת ככר לחם:


פרוס *Break*. Comp. פרש אין להם no man breaketh it unto them (Lam. 4:4); פריסת is divided (Dan. 5:28). It means here to break a loaf of bread, in order to give a part of it to the poor.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:2)


**מרודים.** המ"ם שורש, והנה הוא כמו מעונים (דברי הימים א' ד' מ"א), וכמוהו זכור עניי ומרודי (איכה ג' י"ט):


מְרוּדִים *That are cast out*. The מ is radical, as in מְעוּנִים habitations (1 Chr. 4:41); comp. מרודי my exile¹⁰ (Lam. 3:19).

footnotes:
¹⁰ A. V., My misery.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:3)


**תביא בית.** בית שלך:


*To the house*. To thy house.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:7:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:7:4)


**ומבשרך לא תתעלם.** כמו קרוב, כמו אחינו בשרנו הוא (בראשית ל"ז כ"ז):


*From thine own flesh*. From thy relative. Comp. He is our brother and our flesh (Gen. 37:27)



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:1)


**אז יבקע אורך כשחר.** שכל רגע יוסף האור:


*Then shall thy light break forth as the morning*, gradually increasing.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:2)


**וארוכתך.** רפואתך, והוא שם, כמו אעלה ארוכה לך, ויש אומרים כי ארוכתך ימי גבול החולי, על כן מלת מהרה:


וארוכתך *And thine health*. ארוכה is a noun; comp. Jer. 30:17. Some say that ארוכה, lit. length refers here to the time during which the illness is to last; the word מהרה speedily, which follows, agrees well with this explanation.¹¹

footnotes:
¹¹ The meaning of the phrase ארוכתך מהרה תצמח accordingly is: The time of thy suffering will quickly run out.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:8:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:8:3)


**והלך לפניך צדקך.** יאספך, כמו מאסף לכל המחנות (במדבר י' כ"ה), והנה יהיה שמור:


יאספך *Shall be thy rereward*. Comp. מאסף rereward (Num. 10:25). *And thy righteousness shall go*, etc. Thus, there will be protection from all sides.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:9:1)


**מתוכך.** מקרבך, והטעם על המחשבה, או מתוכך מתוך ישראל, וטעם מוטה העבדים:


*From thy midst*. From thy heart, or from the midst of Israel. מוטה *Yoke*. Slavery.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:9:2)


**שלח אצבע.** שם הפעל על משקל כשכב אדוני המלך (מלכים א' א' כ"ה), כאילו אמר לשלוח יד להכות רעו, או לקחת הונו, גם ודבר און שם הפעל:


שׁלַח *The putting forth*. It is a verbal noun similar in form to the infinitive שְׁכַב to lie (1 Kgs. 1:21). *The putting forth of thy finger*, that is, the stretching out of the hand to smite the neighbour or to take away his property. ודבר *And to speak*. דבר is a verbal noun.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:1)


**ותפק.** כטעם ויפק רצון מיי (משלי ח' ל"ה), והנה נפשך כדרך פעול:


ותפק *And if thou draw out*. Comp. ויפק and obtaineth (Prov. 8:35.) נפשך *Thy soul*. It is, as it were,¹² in the objective case.

footnotes:
¹² Grammatically נפשך thy soul is in the objective case governed by ותפק, and if thou draw out. I. E., however does not consider it as the true object, since in reality the soul is not drawn out; but the food is given to the hungry with the soul, that is, willingly and gladly. But נפשך meaning, according to I. E., thy desire (see 56:11), admits also of the meaning: the object of thy desire, and the whole phrase may be explained thus: And if thou givest the hungry that which thou desirest for thyself; in that case נפשך would be the true object.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:2)


**ונפש נענה תשביע.** לעולם ענוי דבק עם נפש הוא צום, ומלת תשביע לעדה:


נענה *Afflicted*. ענה נפש means always to fast, as may in this case be inferred from the expression תשביע thou wilt satisfy, which follows.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ שבע full is the opposite of רעב hungry; תשביע thou wilt fill, requires for its object רעב the hungry; נפש נענה signifies, therefore, a person that is hungry, that is fasting, and not in a figurative sense, a person that afflicts his soul, that humbles himself by repentance. This remark of I. E. seems to be directed against those who explain the commandment נפשתיכם תענו את (Lev. 16:29) figuratively. Comp. I. E. on Lev. 16:29.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:10:3)


**וזרח בחשך.** אפי' בחשך לילה יזרח אורך, והטעם כאשר תבוא רעה לעולם אתה תנצל:


*Then shall thy light*, etc. Thy light shall shine even in darkness; when evil afflicts mankind, thou wilt be delivered.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:1)


**ונחך יי תמיד.** והטעם שהוא יהיה עמך בכל מקום שתלך:


*And the Lord shall guide thee continually*. He will be with thee, wherever thou goest.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:2)


**בצחצחות.** כמו צחה צמא (ישעיהו ה' י"ג), הפך הריווי:


בצחצחות *In drought*. Comp. צחא is dry (5:13). It is the opposite of fulness.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:3)


**ועצמותיך יחליץ.** יש אומר כמו ידשן בלי חבר, ואחרי' אמרו יחזק, כמו חלוצי צבא (במדבר ל"א ה'), ויש אומרים שיחליץ כמו יחלץ, (איוב ל"ו ט"ו) כאשר מצאנו ישליח (שמות ח' י"ז) ישלח (תהלים ע"ח מ"ה), ישמיח [שם פ"ט מ"ג] ישמח (איכה ב' י"ז), וזהו הנכון, כי הנה הוא כמו שומר כל עצמותיו (תהלים ל"ד כ"א), והנה יחלצם משבר:


יחליץ Some declare it to be hap. leg., and explain it he will make fat; others render it he will strengthen, comparing it with חלוצי armed (Num. 31:5); others still think that יַחֲלִיץ and יְחַלֵּץ he delivereth (Job 36:15) are the same in meaning;¹ as is the case with יַשְׁלִיחַ (Ex. 8:17) and יְשַׁלַּח he sendeth (Ps. 78:45), with יַשְֹמִיחַ (Ps. 89:43), and יְשַֹמַּח he gladdeneth (Lam. 2:17). This latter explanation is right; comp. He keepeth all his bones, not one of them is broken (Ps. 34:21);

footnotes:
¹ The Hebrew text has the Kal יחלוץ; but from the other instances quoted, which are Piёl and Hiphil, it may be inferred that the Piёl יְחַלֵּץ was here intended by I. E.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:11:4)


**לא יכזבו.** כמו יכרתו, וכזב [שם ד' ג'] מגזרתו, כי הוא דבר שאינו עומד, כי מקרה הוא:


ועצמתיו יחליץ means, therefore, He delivereth his bones from the danger of being broken. לא יכזבו *Fail not*, are not cut off; comp. כזב leasing (Ps. 4:3), a thing that cannot last but by chance.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ The word מקרה chance can not be taken literally here; this would be against the theory of I. E.; it is opposed to עומד everlasting, and signifies exposed to unexpected dangers.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:12:3)


**תקומם.** כמו [תשובב תהלים ס' ג'] משובב נתיבות לשבת, אחר שאינם הולכים עליהם בני אדם, לשבת תשובבם:


תקומם *Thou shalt raise up*. It is Polel like תשובב (Ps. 60:3).¹⁵ *The restorer of paths to dwell in*. After people had ceased to tread them, thou wilt restore them, that people will dwell therein.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁵ The Hebrew text has משובב, but this word is the beginning of the phrase which is next to be explained; the word with which תקומם is compared is missing, and תשובב, the word given in the translation, is probably the intended parallel.
¹⁶ The roads had been desolate for a long time, they were not in a good condition, nor safe from the usual dangers of a lonely way; but now they will be restored, they will be in a good condition and well protected; they will not only be frequented by travellers, but people will settle along the roads.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:1)


**אם וגו'.** יי ינחך תמיד אם תשיב משבת רגלך, או הוא דבק עם משובב נתיבות, גם הוא נכון, וטעם משבת מלכת בשבת (רגלך):


*If thou turn away*, etc. The Lord will lead thee continually (ver. 11), if thou keep back thy foot from the sabbath; or, thou shalt be called the restorer, etc. (ver. 12), if thou turn, etc., both explanations are equally admissible.¹⁷ משבת From walking on sabbath.

footnotes:
¹⁷ The difference between the two explanations can hardly be seen, for if the sentence, If thou turn away, etc., is the protasis to And the Lord shall guide thee, etc., (ver. 11), the words Thou shalt be called, etc., are part of the apodosis, which includes verses 11 and 12. The following conjecture suggests itself as probable: The words או הוא דבק עם משובב נתיבות are the product of some careless copyist, who omitted the word אז after עם, and erroneously repeated, perhaps, from the preceding line the words נתיבות משובב, which must therefore be struck out. The remark of I. E., thus emended, would tell us that the conditional sentence, If thou turn, etc., may be connected with the preceding verses as well as with the succeeding.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:2)


**עשות חפציך.** הטעם כפול:


*From doing thy pleasure*. Repetition of the same idea.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:3)


**וקראת לשבת עונג.** שלא תעשה בו מלאכה, ושתתענג הנפש בשמוע דברי תורה:


*And thou wilt call the sabbath a delight*, that thou wilt do no work on it, and thy soul will rejoice in reading the words of the Law.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:13:4)


**לקדוש יי מכובד.** הוא יום שבת, והנה פירוש מה טעם מכובד, והוא וכבדתו מעשות דרכיך, שאתה רגיל לעשות בחול, וכן (מצאנו) ממצא חפצך ודבר דבר עתיד, או בדברי העולם, כי אם בדברי תורה, והכלל שאנחנו צריכין לקבלה:


*The holy of the Lord*. The sabbath. *Honourable*. The words which follow explain its meaning. *And thou shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways*, which thou art accustomed to do in week days; the same idea is contained in the words from finding thine own pleasure. ודבר דבר *Nor speaking a word*,¹⁸ concerning any future act, or concerning worldly affairs; thou shalt only speak of the words of the Law. As a general rule observe, that we require tradition for understanding this.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁸ A. V., Nor speaking thine own words.
¹⁹ Tradition explains in detail what kind of work, according to the words of the prophet, is prohibited to be done on the Sabbath, and what is allowed. Comp. Tract. Shabbath, and Erubin. In everything that concerns the religious practice, I. E., refers to tradition contained in the Talmud, that is, to the Oral Law.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:14:1)


**אז תתענג.** אם תקרא יום שבת עונג אז תתענג על יי, כבן שמתענג על האב, והרכבתיך על במותי ארץ, על גבהי הארץ והיא ארץ ישראל:


*Then shalt thou delight*, etc. If thou call the sabbath a delight,²⁰ then thou shalt find delight in the Lord, as a child does in his father. במתי ארץ *The high places of the earth*. The holy land.²¹

footnotes:
²⁰ I. E. seems to cite intentionally the second part of vers. 13, in order to leave the question concerning the conditional sentence, If thou wilt turn, etc., still open. The question accordingly touches only the first part of the verse.
²¹ Comp. I. E. on Deut. 32:13. Palestine was believed to be the middle of the inhabited part of the earth, and, therefore, the highest part of it.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 58:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/58:14:2)


**והאכלתיך נחלת יעקב.** הטעם, הנה ידבר עם בני הגולה, על כן והרכבתיך, גם משובב נתיבות:


*And feed thee with the heritage*, etc. The prophet speaks to those that are in exile;²² therefore he uses the expressions, And I will cause thee to ride and Restorer of paths.

footnotes:
²² That are not in possession of their inheritance, that do not yet occupy the high places of the earth, and for whom the paths are not yet restored; all this is promised in this prophecy; I. E. therefore concludes that these words are addressed to those in exile.



## Chapter 59


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:1:1)


**הן.** הנה שב הנביא להוכיח עוד בני הגולה, ובאחרונה אמר, ואני זאת בריתי, והנה כל הפרשיות דבקות:


The prophet continues to reprove those who are in exile, and concludes with the words, As for me, this is my covenant, etc. (ver. 21). Thus all these chapters are well connected together in one whole.¹

footnotes:
¹ The leading idea in all these chapters from c. xl., according to I. E., is to prove that the Israelites are wrong in disbelieving the prophet, and manifesting want of confidence in the Divine promise of a perfect and lasting salvatior. I. E. points out, therefore, how this chapter begins with, Behold, the Lord’s hand is not shortened, etc., and concludes with the declaration that the truth of the words which God commanded the prophet to proclaim, will be established for ever.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:1:2

וטעם **הן לא קצרה**, דעו כי לא קצרה יד השם מהושיעכם:


*Behold the Lord’s hand*, etc. Know that the Lord is not unable to help you.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:2:2

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:1)


**ביצי.** והנה המשילם שהם כביצי צפעוני כאשר יבקעו:


*They hatch*, etc. They are compared with the cockatrice’s eggs, when they open themselves.⁵

footnotes:
⁵ A. V., They hatch cockatrice’s eggs. I. E. supplies the relative כאשר when. The Hebrew text has the words: המשילם שהם כביצי צפעוני. Lit., he compared them, (saying) that they are like the eggs of the cockatrice. This passage seems to be corrupt, because, in the first place, if I. E. intended only to say that the prophet compared them with the eggs of the cockatrice, he would have said המשילם לביצי צפעוני, or אמר שהם כביצי צפעוני; secondly, the whole remark would, in that case, be superfluous; thirdly, from the preceding remark of I. E., in which thoughts and words are pointed at as meant by the prophet, it may be inferred, that the commentator will show in this remark that the prophet speaks of the deeds of the people. It is, therefore, probable that the words in question are a corruption of the original מעשיהם לביצי צפעוני המשיל, he compares their deeds with the eggs, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:2)


**וקורי [עכביש].** ידוע ממעשה העכביש:


וקורי עכביש The web⁶ of the work of a spider.

footnotes:
⁶ The Hebrew text has ידוע well-known; but יריעה, a web, a curtain, is meant. The same expression is used by Kimchi in explaining the word קורי.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:3)

*Of their eggs*. Of the eggs of the cockatrice.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:5:4)


**והזורה.** היה ראוי להיות תחת הרי"ש קמץ גדול, ובאה מלה זרה כמו ולנה בתוך ביתו (זכריה ' ד'), והנה הזורה פעולה, כמו כי מולים היו (יהושע ה' ד') סוגה בשושנים (שיר השירים ז' ג'), היא מגזרת ויזר את הגזה (שופטים ו' ל"ח), כי מי שיזרנה אז תבקע הצפעוני ויצא אפעה, כמו אפעה ושרף (ישעיהו ל' ו'):


וְהַזּוּרֶה *And that which is crushed*. It is an irregular form; the Segol under ר is substituted for Kamez, as in ולנה and it shall remain (Zec. 5:4.) זורה is participle passive; comp. מולים circumcised (Jos. 5:5); סוגה set about (Songs 7:2). As to its meaning comp. ויזר and he pressed⁷ (Jud. 6:38). If one presses the egg, the cockatrice breaks through and comes out. אפעה *Viper*. Comp. 30:6

footnotes:
⁷ A.V., And thrust together.

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:7:1)


**רגליהם וגו'.** כי מחשבותם שוד ושבר במסילות שידרכו בם והנה טעם רגליהם כפול:


*Their thoughts are thoughts of iniquity, of wasting and destruction in their paths*, that is, in the paths which they go. The second half of the verse contains the same idea as the first half.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:8:1)


**נתיבותיהם.** שהיו ידועות, עקשי', ומי ילך בנתיבותיהם וילמד מהם:


*Their paths* that were well known before (as straight), are now crooked. *Whosoever goeth therein*, that is, he who walks in their ways, and learns from them.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:9:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:9:2

### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:1)


**נגששה.** כמו נמשש, ואין רע לו, וי"א מגזרת וגוש עפר (איוב ז' ה'):


נגששה *We grope*. It is hap. leg. Some connect it with גוש a clod (Job 7:5).⁸

footnotes:
⁸ Or rather the reverse, connect גוש with גשש. The fundamental meaning seems to be to touch, to feel; from this is derived גוש clod, that is, some substantial thing that is felt. Comp. Ges. Lex., sub voce גוש.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:2)


**בצהרים.** שהוא חצי היום, כאילו היינו בנשף, וזה דרך משל:


*At noon day as in the night*, that is, as if it were in the evening. It is a figurative expression.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:10:3)


**באשמנים.** יש אומרים קברים, ויתכן שהוא כמו צהרים, או כמו בחיים, והטעם בינות החיים, ויתכן היות האל"ף נוסף והטעם בינות השמנים, והם הגוים:


באשמנים. Some say that it means in graves;¹ but it is equally admissible to explain it, at noon,⁹ or, amongst the living.² or, considering the א to be prosthetic, among the fat ones, that is, the heathen people.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹ Comp. Targ. Jonathan: מתיא אתאחד באפנא כמה דאחידין קבריא באפי The door closes before us, as the graves close to the dead.—R. Joseph Kimchi explains likewise באשמנים in graves; he derives the word from the root שמם═אשם to be desolate, with a paragogic נ.
⁹ The opposite is said by some commentators, namely, that באשמנים means the same as במחשכים in darkness; this explanation is probably based on a comparison of this phrase with the verse He hath set me in dark places (במחשכים), as they that be dead of old (Lam. 3:6). צהרים in the Hebrew text is perhaps a corruption of חשכים.
² באשמנים being considered to be the opposite of כמתים as dead men, as in the preceding phrase בצהרים at noonday is the opposite of כנשף in the night.
¹⁰ The Israelites, while in exile, and deprived of liberty and independence, among successful and prospering people, compare themselves to dead persons among the living.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:11:1)


**נהמה כדובים וגו'.** והטעם, נצעק ואין מושיע, ואין מי שיעשה לנו משפט:


*We roar*, etc. We cry, but nobody comes to our assistance, nobody comes to do us justice.



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:1)


**כי וגו'.** אלה דברי הנביא על לשון ישראל שיודו לשם עונותם:


*For our transgressions*, etc. The repenting Israelites are now represented by the prophet as speaking.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:2)


**ענתה בנו.** כמו לא תענה ברעך (שמות כ' י"ג):


ענתה בנו *Hath testified against us*. Comp. לא תענה ברעך, thou shalt not testify against thy neighbour (Ex. 20:13).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:12:3)


**כי פשעינו אתנו.** הם עוד:


*For our iniquities are with us*. Our iniquities are yet with us.¹

footnotes:
¹ They have not yet been removed by repentance on the one side, and pardon on the other.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:1)


**פשוע וכחש.** שמות הפעלי', והנה פשוע לצאת מתחת הרשות:


פׇּשֹׁעַ וְכַחֵשׁ *In transgressing and lying*. These are infinitives; the meaning of פשע is to renounce obedience.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:2)


**ונסוג.** שם הפועל מבניין נפעל על דרך ונשלוח (אסתר ג' י"ג):


נסג *Departing*. It is infinitive Niphal, similar in form to ונשלח and being sent (Est. 3:13).¹¹

footnotes:
¹¹ The forms of the infinitive Niphal are נִפְעול and נׇסוג ;הִפׇּעְל and נשלוח are formed after נִפְעוֹל.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:13:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:3)


**סרה.** מגזרת סורר ומור' (דברים כ"א י"ח):


סרה *Revolt*. Comp. סורר rebellious (Deut. 21:18).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:13:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:4)


**הורו כמו עושו (איוב מ' י"ג).** והורו מגזרת על ברכת הורי (בראשית מ"ט כ"ו), ותהר את מרים (דברי הימים א' ד' י"ז), והנה הוא על משקל הוגו והוי"ו שב אל שקר, ויש אומרים כי היה ראוי להיותו על משקל בנה בניתי (מלכים א' ח' י"ח), ובאו זרות:


הורו *Conceiving it*,¹ that is, forming it; comp. הורי my progenitors (Gen. 49:26); ותהר and she conceived (1 Chr. 4:17).¹² Its form is the same as that of the succeeding והגו and uttering it; the possessive pronoun (וֹ) refers to שקר falsehood. Some say that הֹרוֹ and הֹגוֹ are irregular forms of the infinitive; the regular infinitive would be הׇגֹה ,הׇרֹה, comp. בׇּנֹה to build (1 Kings 8:13.)

footnotes:
¹ A.V., Conceiving, Uttering.
¹² The instances quoted are intended to prove that the verb הרה to conceive, which is mostly used as a neuter verb, expressing a certain state and condition, is sometimes used as a transitive verb, and governs in that case the accusative.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:13:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:13:5)


וטעם **מלב.** מלבם יוציאו דברי שקר:


מלב *From the heart*. They bring forth words of falsehood out of their hearts.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:1)


**והסג.** מבנין שלא נזכר שם פועלו:


והסג *And is turned away*. It is Hophal


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:2)


**וצדקה מרחוק תעמד.** דרך משל, כי אין צדקתו [אמת], אמת לשון נקבה, והוא חסר נו"ן וימצא מבולע במלת אמתך (ישעיהו ל"ח י"ח):


*And justice standeth afar off*. It is figurative expression for "they evince no justice". אמת *Truth*. It is a feminine noun; the third radical (נ) is dropped and expressed implicitly by Dagesh in אמתך "thy truth" (38:18).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:14:3)


**ונכוחו.** דברים שיאמר אדם לנכח חבירו, ראה דבריך טובי' ונכוחים (שמואל ב' ט"ו י"ג):


נכחה *Equity*. Things which one says straightforwardly to his neighbour; comp. נכוחים right (Sam II 15:3).



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:15:1)


**משתולל.** יש אומרים משוגע, כמו אלכה ערום ושולל [מיכה א' ח'], אשתוללו אבירי לב (תהלים ע"ו ו'), ויתכן היות הכל מגזרת שלל, להסיר הון, הנה משתולל שם הפועל מבנין התפעל:


משתולל According to some it means "mad;" comp. שולל "mad"¹³ (Mic. 1:8); אשתללו "they are mad" (Ps. 76::6); perhaps all these words are serived from שלל "to deprive of property;"¹⁴ משתולל is the participle Hitpael of שלל.

footnotes:
¹³ A.  V., "stripped."
¹⁴ The meaning of משתולל accordingly is "maketh himself a prey (A. V.).



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:1)


**וישתומם.** מגזרת שממה (ישעיהו א' ז'), ורבי מנחם שהוציאו מגזרת שתום העין (במדבר כ"ד ג') לא אמר אמת, כי לא יכול אדם לאמור מן וישבור וישבורר, כפול הלמ"ד:


וישתומם *And wondered*. Comp. שממה desolation (1:7).¹⁵ Rabbi Menahem connects it with ¹⁶שתום (Num. 24:3); but he is wrong; it is improper to form וישבורר from שבר, with reduplication of the third radical.

footnotes:
¹⁵ שמם to be desolate, so that no word is heard; so he that wonders cannot utter a word in the first moment.
¹⁶ וישתומם is, according to the opinion of R. Menahem, formed from שתם with reduplication of the third radical. I. E. properly rejects this explanation, because the ת is not a radical, but a formative letter, the characteristic of the Hithpael, being placed after the first radical, in accordance with the rule concerning the verbs, whose first radical is a sibilant. R. Menahem is a famous grammarian of the 11th century.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:2)


**ותושע לו.** כלשון בני אדם, כי השם הוא המושיע ואיננו נושע, והנה הטעם על כבודו להראות גבורתו:


ותשע לו זרעו *Therefore His arm helped him*.¹⁷ This is an anthropomorphism, for, in fact, God helps, but does not require the assistance of others. The meaning of the phrase is, His glory helped Him to show His power.¹

footnotes:
¹⁷ A. V., Brought salvation.
¹ The words of the Hebrew text are זרעו .והטעם על כבודו להראות גבורתו His arm, seems hero to be explained by His glory; and ותשע לו helped Him, to be complemented by to show His power. I. E. intends to remove the anthropomorphism by this explanation, but in reality he replaced it only by another one. The most striking expression in the anthropomorphism, the verb helped, as correctly pointed out by I. E., is not replaced by another verb. It is, however, possible that the whole phrase גבורתו והטעם, על כבודו להראות is the explanation of the expression זרעו his arm: his glory, in displaying his power, is meant.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:16:3)


**מפגיע.** כמו ולפושעים יפגיע (ישעיהו נ"ג י"ב):


מפגיע *Intercessor*. Comp. יפגיע made intercession (53:12)



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:1)


**וילבש.** דרך משל לגבור שהוא לובש התחרא, הוא השריון:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:2)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:17:3)

ויעט כמעיל קנאה *And was clad with zeal as a cloke*, that is, as if he were clad with a cloke.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁸ I. E. seems to point out by this remark, that קנאה is not a genitive governed by מעיל, and that the whole phrase does not mean and was clad as it were with a cloke of zeal (similar to בגדי נקם garments of vengeance), but that both מעיל and קנאה are in the accusative case governed by the verb ויעט.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:18:1)

E. whether this remark refers also to כעל ישלם, and explains it to mean like a man (who is zealous) for revenge, or is limited to כעל גמלות; in that case the whole phrase is to be translated, Like a man (who is zealous) for repaying, so he (is clad with zeal) for revenge. ###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:18:2)


**[לאיים].** לכל האיים **גמול ישלם.** והנה צריו ואויביו ביבשה, גם הזכיר לאיי הים:

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:1)


**ויראו.** י"א שהוא מלשון יראה והוא חסר יו"ד, וי"א כמשמעו:


ויראו Some explain it, And they will fear; one י being omitted (וייראו═ויראו); others, paying strict regard to its orthography, render it, and they shall see.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:2)


וטעם **שם יי.** מעשהו והעד את כבודו:


*The name of the Lord.* His deeds, as proved by the parallelism of the verse; His glory in the second part corresponds to the name of the Lord, in the first part.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ If יראו means they will see, the expression the name of the Lord must refer to the works of the Lord, since the name cannot be seen. His glory is identical with his glorious works, or the glory displayed in his works.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:19:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:19:3)


**כי יבא כנהר צר.** כמו צר ומצוק מצאוני (תהלים קי"ט קמ"ג) והנה הוא שם, רוח יי נוססה בו מגזרת נס, וזה הטעם קרוב מדברי דניאל והיתה עת צרה לכל העולם אשר לא נהייתה כמוה (דניאל י"ב א'), וישראל לבדם ינצלו על כן אחרי זאת, ובא לציון גואל:


צר *Distress*.²¹ Comp. צר ומצק trouble and anguish (Ps. 119:143). It is a noun.²² In such a degree רוח יי נוססה בו the spirit of the Lord will wonderfully act therein.²³ נוססה is derived from נס miracle. This verse is in perfect harmony with the prophecy, And there shall be a time of trouble such as never was, etc. (Dan. 12:1). At that time Israel alone will be saved; therefore this verse is followed by the words, And the Redeemer shall come to Zion.

footnotes:
²¹ A. V., The enemy.
²² It can hardly be anything else. I. E. means, perhaps, to say that צר is an abstract noun (שם) signifying distress, and not a common noun (שם התואר) signifying enemy. (Comp. c. iii., Note 5).
²³ A. V., The spirit of the Lord shall lift up a standard against him. Standard.

### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:21:1)


**ואני זאת בריתי.** הנה אכרו' ברית עמה' ומה היא רוחי אשר עליך, וכ"ף לישראל ידבר, וטעם רוחי נבואתי, כאשר כתוב, והיה אחרי כן אשפך את רוחי (יואל ג' א'):


*As for me*, *this is my covenant*. I shall make a covenant with them, namely, that my spirit which is upon thee, etc. *Upon thee*. Israel is addressed. *My spirit.* My prophecy; comp. And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh, etc. (Joel 3:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 59:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/59:21:2)


**ודברי אשר שמתי בפיך.** והטעם כפול, כי התנבאו ולא תפסק להם הנבואה מזרעם לעולם:


*And my words which I have put in thy mouth.* Repetition of the same idea. God has revealed Himself to His people through prophets, whose divine words shall never depart from the hearts of the Israelites.



## Chapter 60


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:1:1)


**קומי אורי.** לשון ציווי כמו בואי (שמואל ב' י"ג י"א), בא בחולם בעבור האל"ף:


אורי *Shine.* It is the imperative; comp. בואי come (2 Sam. 13:11); these two have Holem instead of Shurek on account of the א.¹, קוּם, to rise. Generally the vowel is affected by the consonant which follows, but not by the preceding, as is the case in אוֹדִי, according to the opinion of I. E.

footnotes:
¹ The infinitive Kal of the verb ע״ו has, according to the rule, the vowel וּ; e.g.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:1:2)


**כי בא אורך.** לשבח, ולפי דעתי שביאת האור הוא חשך, כמו בא ערב ונפסק האור שהיה לך, **וזרח עליך כבוד יי.** והעד לא יהיה לך עוד אור השמש לאור יומם [להלן י"ט], וטעם אורי על מלכות או הנבואה:


בא אורך Thy light is come, if taken in a good sense; but I think that it means thy light has set, and it has become dark; that is,² the evening is come, and the light which has shone for thee hitherto, is gone, but in its stead the glory of the Lord will henceforth shine over thee; comp. The sun shall be no more thy light by day, etc. (ver. 19). By the words Shine, etc., the restoration of the kingdom of Israel, or of the prophecy is meant.

footnotes:
² The Hebrew text has the word במו, which can be translated as if to say, or that is, but usually it introduces some quotation from the Bible; very probably it was originally followed by the words בי בא השמש because the sun was set (Gen. 28:11).



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:1)


**כי הנה החשך.** זהו כטעם כי יבא כנהר צר (ישעיהו נ"ט י"ט):


*For behold, the darkness will cover the earth.* Comp. For distress shall come in like a flood (59:19).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:2)


**וערפל [לאמים].** תכסה לאומים:


וערפל לאמים *And gross darkness*—supply יכסה shall cover—*the people*.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:2:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:2:3)


**ועליך יזרח יי.** והטעם עליך לבדך:


*But upon thee*. Upon thee alone.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:3:1)


**והלכו גוים לאורך.** כי מנהג מי שהוא בחשך לראות היושבים באור:


*And nations shall come to thy light.* He who is in darkness usually sees those that are dwelling in light.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:4:1)


**כולם.** רמז על בניך ובנותיך שיזכירם, ויתכן להיות כלם סימן המלכים:


*All they.* All thy sons and daughters, whom the prophet is going to mention; it may also refer to kings (ver. 3).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:4:2)


**תאמנה.** מגזרת ויהי אומן את הדסה (אסתר ב' ז'):


תאמנה *Shall be nursed.* Comp. ויהי אמן and he brought up (Est. 2:7)



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:1)


**אז תיראי.** והטעם כאשר יבאו המלכים אליך ויביאו בניך, אז תיראי כאדם שיפחד בבא לו תשועה ודבר שלא עלה על לב, כאשר יקרא למצא אבדה:


*Then.* When kings come unto thee and bring thee thy children. תראי *Thou shalt fear,*³ like a man that trembles when help comes to him suddenly, or anything he did not anticipate; this is usually the case with a person who finds something.

footnotes:
³ A. V., Thou shalt see. I. E. seems to have read תִּֽרְאִי or תִּרְאִי (root ירא), instead of תִּרְאִי.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:2)


**ונהרת.** תרוצי פה ופה:


ונהרת And thou wilt run hither and thither.⁴

footnotes:
⁴ A. V., And flow together.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:3)


**ופחד.** והנה יהיה פחד מעורב עם שמחה, וזאת רחב לבבך, הפך הצרה:


*And thine heart shall fear and be enlarged.* Anxiety will be mixed with the rejoicing, which is indicated by the words: *And thine heart shall be enlarged.* This is the opposite of צרה straits, distress.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:5:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:4)


**כי יהפך עליך המון ים.** או טעם תיראי מרוב המון שיהפך עליך:


The reason of the joy will be *Because the abundance of the sea,* etc. The verse may also be explained thus: Thou shalt fear because of the great multitude that will flow unto thee.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:5:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:5:5)


**חיל גוים.** ביבשה:


חיל גוים *The forces of the nations.*⁵ The land armies.⁶

footnotes:
⁵ A. V., Of the Gentiles.
⁶ According to this explanation המון ים is not the abundance of the sea, but the multitude or the armies that will come by sea.



### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:6:1)


**שפעת.** חבורה, כמו שפעת (מים) אני רואה (מלכים ב' ט' י"ז):


שפעת *A company*. Comp. 2 Kgs. 9:17.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:6:2)


**בכרי.** הבי"ת משרת, מגזרת שלחו כר (ישעיהו ט"ז א'), ישאו דורון:


בכרי *With dromedairies*.⁷ The ב is a preposition; comp. בר the swift (16:1). *They shall bring* for a present.

footnotes:
⁷ A. V., The dromedaries.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:7:1)


**ישרתונך.** הטעם יהיו לצרכך, וכמוהו את בגדי השרד לשרת בקדש (שמות ל"ה י"ט), הם בגדי הנסיעה:


ישרתונך *Shall minister unto thee*, that is, shall be at thy service; comp. לשרת to do service (Ex. 35:19), which is used of the cloth for covering the holy vessels during the journey.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:7:2)


**יעלו על רצון מזבחי.** והנה על ימשוך אחר עמו וכן הוא על מזבחי:


על רצון על מזבחי═על רצון מזבחי With acceptance on my altar.⁸

footnotes:
⁸ Usually one preposition is connected with several nouns, but in one and the same meaning; here this is not the case. על רצון means with acceptance, or for acceptance; על מזבחי upon my altar. But, in fact, the repetition of the preposition is not required here at all, since עלה governs also the accusative; comp. Gen. 49:4; Num. 13:17.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:8:1)


**מי אלה.** הטעם על הבנים, והנה קומי אורי [לעיל א'] ידבר עם ציון:


*Who are these*, etc. This question refers to the children (ver. 4). The words Arise, shine, etc. (ver. 1) are addressed by God to Zion.⁹

footnotes:
⁹ It seems as if I. E. explained this chapter to be a dialogue between God and Zion. Ver. 1 to ver. 7 is assigned to God; ver. 8 contains a question asked by Zion, the verses which follow contain the answer of God. Otherwise the remark is here superfluous, or at least out of place. (Comp. ver. 14).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:8:2)


**אל ארובותיהם.** הם החלונות ששם קנם:


ארבתיחם *Their windows.* The holes, where their nests are.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:1)


**כי לי איים יקוו.** שאתן להם שכר טוב:


*Shall wait for me,* that I shall give them a good reward.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:2)


**ואניות תרשיש כבראשונה.** והזכיר תרשיש כי היא קרובה לארץ:


*Tarshish.* This place is mentioned because it is near Palestine.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ Comp. I. E. on Jonah 1:3. He mentions there the opinion of Saadiah, that Tarshish is the same as Tarsus, Tartessus in Hispania Bætica; and also the opinion of another commentator, who believes it to be Tunis in Africa.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:3)


**כספם וזהבם.** והנה הטעם כי לי איים יקוו, כי לא יתנון להם ישראל שכר, והנה הוא מפורש לשם יי אלהיך:


*Their silver and their gold with them.* These words contain the reason why the islands shall wait for the Lord; the Israelites will not give them wages. It is distinctly said unto the name of the Lord thy God.¹¹

footnotes:
¹¹ They will do all this work for the Israelites without expecting any pay for it except from the Lord, whose will they carry out.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:9:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:9:4)


והנה **פארך.** בא בקמץ גדול תחת קטן בעבור היותו סוף פסוק:


פארך *He hath glorified thee.* The Kamez under ר instead of Zeré, is caused by the pause.¹²

footnotes:
¹² The feminine suffix –ֵ is here to be expected, because it refers to Zion, which is, in this whole chapter, addressed as a woman. I. E. attributes the cause of this change to the pause; but it must be considered as very exceptional, since the pause changes the masculine suffix –ְ into –ָ, but not so the feminine suffix –ֵ.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:10:1)


**ובנו וגו'.** אפילו בני ישראל לא יבנו חומות ירושלם כאשר לא בנו הבית, כי אם הגוים:


*And the sons of strangers shall build*, etc. The Israelites will not build the walls of Jerusalem, as they did not build even the temple; other nations will do it.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:11:1)


**ופתחו.** יש אומרים החירק תחת שורק, ויש אומרים כי ופתחו שב אל בני נכר, ואיננו רחוק, והנה הטעם ידוע, להביא אליך חיל גוים ביום גם בלילה:


ופתּחו Some say that וּפִחְּחוּ is the same as וּפֻתְּחוּ and they will be opened. According to others, And they will open, that is, the sons of strangers will open, etc.; this explanation is not improbable.—The sense of the whole verse is: the gates will be opened continually, day and night, by those that will bring in the abundance of nations.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:11:2)


**ומלכיהם.** שהיו נוהגים יובאו נהוגים, כטעם לאסור מלכיה' בזקי' (תהלים קמ"ט ח'):


*Their kings*, that is, those who had been their kings. *And that their kings may be brought.* Comp. To bind their kings with chains (Ps. 149:8)



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:12:1)


**חרוב יחרבו.** מגזרת חרב, החרב נחרבו המלכים (מלכים ב' ג' כ"ג), ויש אומרים מלשון חרבן, והראשון הוא נכון:


חרב יחרבו *They will be slain.* This verb is derived from חרב sword; comp. החרב נחרבו they are surely slain. (2 Kgs. 3:23). Some explain it they shall be utterly wasted, and compare it with חרבן destruction. I prefer the first explanation.



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:13:1)


**כבוד הלבנון.** והנה פי' האילנים הנכבדים בלבנון, ברוש תדהר ותאשור יחדו:


*The glory of Lebanon.* The best trees of Lebanon; the fir tree, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:13:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:13:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:13:2)


**לפאר.** לבנות בית השם:


*To beautify the place of my sanctuary.* To build the house of the Lord.



### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:1)


**והלכו.** שחוח, שם:


שחח *Bending.* It is a noun.¹³

footnotes:
¹³ I. E. uses the expression שם a noun; he means perhaps שם הפועל infinitive or verbal noun, as contrasted with פועל participle, and שם התואר common noun; in the latter cases the plural form would be used. Comp. c. iii., Note 5.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:14:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:2)


**וקראו לך עיר יי.** והנה לעד [כי] קומי אורי אמר על ציון:


*And they shall call thee the city of the Lord.* This proves that the exclamation Arise, etc. is addressed to Zion.¹⁴

footnotes:
¹⁴ Another opinion is mentioned, Midrash Yalkut ad locum: R. Johanan compares these words (קומי אורי) to those uttered by one who is about to travel at night a little before dawn; he gets a candle lit, but the flame is blown out; he gets another candle, but it meets with the same fate; he then resigns himself and says: I shall not trouble myself any longer with those candles, I shall wait for the light of the morning. The same was the case with the Israelites: they said: We have lit the candle in the time of Moses; it has been put out; under king Solomon we lit another candle, this also was extinguished; we must now resign ourselves and wait, till the Lord himself will renew for us the light. Therefore God said: Arise, my light (אורי), etc. I. E. thought, perhaps, of this or similar passages in the Midrash, when he considered it necessary to remind us repeatedly that the words קומי אורי are addressed to Zion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:14:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:14:3)


**עיר.** ימשך עצמו ואחר עמו וכן הוא ציון עיר קדוש ישראל. כמו אל באפך תוכיחני (תהלים ו' א'):


עיר קדש ישראל═קדש ישראל The city of the holy One of Israel. Comp. Ps. 6:1.¹⁵ here, the word עיר city.

footnotes:
¹⁵ קדוש ישראל is the genitive; but it cannot be governed by ציון, because the latter is a proper noun, and proper nouns do not govern a genitive; wherever, therefore, this seems to be the case, another noun in apposition to it is supplied, as e. g.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:15:1)

*Thou hast been forsaken.* When in a state of ruin.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:15:2)
