### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:16:1)


**וינקת חלב גוים.** הטעם ממון שיתנו מס:


*The milk of nations*. Their money; they will pay tribute.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:16:2)


**ושוד מלכים.** מגזרת שדים (ישעיהו ל"ב י"ב), כי משקלי השמות משתנים:


שד *Breast.* It is the same as שָׁדַיִם. The form of the nouns is not constant.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ The two forms referred to are שֹׁד and שֵׁד. Comp. I. E. on c. 9:3, and Note 4.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:1)


**תחת הנחשת אביא זהב.** אשים בלב הגוים שיביאו הזהב, והנכון שאביא לך שכר זהב, והנה הנחשת נכבד מהברזל על [כן] תחתיו זהב כנגדו:


*I will bring gold.* That is, I shall induce the nations to bring the gold, or, and that is perhaps better—I shall bring thee the value of gold;¹⁷ (or,¹⁸ the value of the gold of nations.) Copper is better than iron, it is therefore contrasted with gold.

footnotes:
¹⁷ That is, for the copper that has been taken away from thee, thou wilt get a compensation of such a value, as if gold had been taken away.
¹⁸ זהב גוים the gold of nations seems to be another reading for the preceding זהב gold, but not a new explanation. Comp. נ״א another reading of the M.S. of the British Museum.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:2)


**ושמתי פקודתך.** אנשי פקודתך, כמו פקיד, והם החולקים המס:


פקודתך *Thy officers.* Lit., the men of thy office (אנשי פקודתך). Comp. פקיד officer. The men, who distribute the taxes.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:17:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:3)


**[שלום].** שיקחוהו בשלום:


*I will make thine officers peace*. They will collect the taxes in peace.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:17:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:17:4)


**ונוגשיך [צדקה].** בצדקה:


*And thine exactors righteousness*. They will exact the money with righteousness.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:18:1)


**לא ישמע עוד חמס בארצך שוד ושבר.** הטעם כפול:


*Violence shall not,* etc. Repetition of the same idea.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:18:2)


**וקראת.** יש אומר' כמו וקראת אתכם הרעה (דברים ל"א כ"ט), ויש אומרים מלשון קריאה, כי הישועה תקרא אל חומותיך, והנכון שמלת וקראת לנכח ציון, כי חומותיך תקראם ישועה, והעד ושעריך תהלה, והנה וקראת ימשוך אחר עמו כמשפט:


וקראת ישועה חומתיך Some explain it: And salvation will meet thy walls; comp. וֹקראת אתכם הרעה and evil will befall you (Deut. 31:29); others: And salvation shall call unto thy walls; but it is more correct to take וקראת as the second person feminine, and to render it, And thou, Zion, wilt call thy walls salvation. The correctness of this explanation is proved by the words which follow: ושעריך תהלה and thy gates praise. וקראת is to be repeated before ושעריך, according to the rule of ellipsis.



### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:19:1)


**לא וגו'.** לא תצטרכי לאור השמש בעבור אור השכינה:


*The sun shall be no more,* etc. Thou wilt not want the light of the sun, because of the light of God.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:19:2)


**לאור עולם.** יומם ולילה:


*An everlasting light,* that shines day and night.



### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:20:1)


**לא וגו'.** זה השמש לא יבוא וירח אשר לא יאסף, והטעם כי בהתחברו עם השמש אז יעדר אור מהארץ:


*Thy sun shall no more go down*, etc. That sun¹⁹ will not set, and that moon לא יאסף *Shall not withdraw itself.* Lit., shall not be gathered; the moon appears dark to the earth, when in conjunction with the sun.²⁰

footnotes:
¹⁹ The glory of the Lord mentioned in the preceding verse as a substitute for the light of sun and moon.
²⁰ The phrase the moon is gathered means, according to I. E., the moon comes together with the sun, in one straight line from the earth, so that the part of the moon illuminated by the sun is not seen by the inhabitants of the earth, and she is, therefore, not seen at all: this is the case at every new moon.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:20:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:20:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:20:2)


**ושלמו ימי אבלך.** כי האבל ישב בחשך:


*And the days of thy mourning shall be ended.* The mourner sits, as it were, in darkness.



### Verse 21

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:21:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:21:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:21:1)


**נצר.** כמו ונצר משרשיו יפרה (ישעיהו י"א א'):


*The branch.* Comp. And a branch shall grow out of his roots (11:1).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:21:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:21:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:21:2)


**מעשה ידי להתפאר.** כדרך בן אדם שישמח במעשיו בהיותם מתוקנים:


*The work of my hands, that I may be glorified.* It is a figure taken from the joy which a man feels when his work proves to be successful.²¹

footnotes:
²¹ God rejoices that Israel have proved themselves, by repentance and by faithfulness to the word of God, deserving of the promised distinction, and worthy of the position assigned to them among the nations.



### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:22:1)


**הקטן.** המשפחה הקטנה שמספרם מעט תהיה לאלף:


*The little one,* etc. The small family, that numbers a few, shall become a thousand.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 60:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/60:22:2)


**בעתה.** בגעת עת הישועה, והנכון שהוא דבק עם הקטן יהיה לאלף, והנה אחיש לעשות לשום מצעיר לגוי עצום, כדרך ואעשך לגוי גדול (בראשית י"ב ב'):


*In his time,* that is, when the time of salvation will come, *I will hasten it,* that is, the salvation; or, I shall hasten to make the little one a strong nation; לגוי עצום *A strong nation*. Comp. And I shall make thee a great nation (Gen. 12:2)



## Chapter 61


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:1)


**רוח וגו'.** אלה דברי הנביא, והם נבואה כמו ויאצל מן הרוח (במדבר י"א כ"ה):


*Upon me.* The first person refers to the prophet. *The spirit.* The prophecy. Comp. And took of the spirit, that was upon him (Num. 11:25).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:2)


**יען משח יי אותי.** כי הנביאי' יקראו משיחי', וכמוהו אל תגעו במשיחי (תהלים ק"ה ט"ו), והם האבות ויאמר רבי משה הכהן, כי תשובת יען משח יי אותי, שוש אשיש ביי [לקמן פסוק י'], ואין צורך, כי יען טעמו השם משחני בעבור שאבשר ענוי':


*Because the Lord hath anointed me.* The prophets are called anointed; comp. Touch not mine anointed (Ps. 105:15).¹ R. Moses Hakkohen says that the protasis beginning Because the Lord is continued till ver. 9, and the apodosis commences I will greatly rejoice (ver. 10); but it is not at all necessary to make this explanation; because יען means² the reason of, and the whole phrase can be rendered thus: The reason why God has anointed me is, that I shall bring good tidings, etc.

footnotes:
¹ The second part of this verse, And do my prophets no harm, shows that the expressions anointed (משיחי) and prophets (נביאי) signify here the same persons.
² The Hebrew text has the words כי יען טעמו השם משחני, lit., for יען has the meaning ‘ God has anointed me,’ etc., but יען has not this meaning; after טעמו the word טעם the reason why has been omitted, which has been restored in the translation.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:1:3)


**פקח קוח.** מל' אחת ועי"ן ולמ"ד הם כפולי', כמו סחרחר (תהלים ל"ח י"א) או ירקרק (ויקרא י"ג מ"ט) אדמדם [שם] והוא שם:


פקחקח *The opening of the prison.* It is one word, with the reduplication of the second and third radical; it is similar in form to סחרחר panteth (Ps. 38:11), אדמדם red (Lev. 13:49), ירקרק green (Lev. ibid).



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:2:1)


**לקרא שנת רצון.** היא שנת כל הגאול':


*The acceptable year.* The year of redemption.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:2:2)


**לנחם כל אבלי'.** והנה פרש אחר כן כי הם אבלי ציון:


*All that mourn* for Zion, as is said in the next verse.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:1)


**לשום לאבלי ציון.** הוא שפרש פאר תחת אפר שמן ששון תחת אבל, כי האבל לא יסוך שמן, והתקועית לעדה (שמואל ב' י"ד ב'):


*To appoint unto them that mourn for Zion* that which the text is going to enumerate¹. *Beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning.* The mourner does not anoint with oil, as may be gathered from the story of the woman of Tekoa. (2 Sam. 14:2).

footnotes:
¹ The words לתת להם to give unto them, are accordingly a mere repetition of the phrase לשום לאבלי ציון to appoint unto them that mourn for Zion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:2)


**רוח כהה.** שם התאר מגזרת כהה הנגע (ויקרא י"ג ו'), יש אומרים כטעם חשך, והנכון בעיני שהוא הפך פשה:


כהה *Weak.*³ It is an adjective of the same root as the verb בהה (Lev. 13:6) which is rendered by some is become dark, but by me hath decreased, as it is contrasted with פׁשהֹ spread.⁴

footnotes:
³ A. V., Heaviness.
⁴ Comp. I. E. on 42:3, and on Levit. 13:6.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:3:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:3:3)


**אילי הצדק.** מגזרת אילנים, כמו מאילים אשר חמדתם (ישעיהו א' כ"ט), והעד מטע השם:


אילי *Trees*. Comp. אילים oaks (1:29);⁵ the words which follow, the planting of the Lord, support this explanation.

footnotes:
⁵ The same explanation is given by Rashi; but the Chaldæan translation renders it רברבי the great.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:4:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:4:2

### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:5:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:5:2)

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:6:1)


**ואתם.** כבר אמרתי כי כל כהן לעולם הוא משרת, והעד משרתי אלהינו, והנה יהיו הגוים כנגד ישראל וישראל כנגד בני אהרן, על כן חיל גוים כנגד המעשר:


כהני *The priests*. I said already that the meaning of כהן is, one that ministers; it is therefore qualified here by the genitive of our God. The other nations will resemble the Israelites, and the Israelites will be like the Aaronites; the Israelites will therefore receive the abundance of nations as their tithes.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:6:2)

תתאמרו═תתימרו *Shall ye boast yourselves.* Comp. האמרת thou hast boasted (Deut. 26:17).⁹

⁹ I. E. connects with the same root the word אמיר (17:6). In his commentary on Deuteronomy he explains likewise the verb האמרת to mean thou hast praised, but at the same time approves of the explanation of R. Jehudah Hallevi, that האמרת means thou hast caused to declare.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:7:1)

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:7:2)

### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:8:1)


**כי וגו'.** הטעם אשלם להם גמול, כי אני אוהב צדק שונא גזל אפי' בעולה שהיא קרבה לפני, על כן ונתתי פעולתם כמו שכרם, כמו ולא תלין פעולת שכיר (ויקרא י"ט י"ח):


*For I, the Lord, love judgment*, etc. I shall give them their reward, for I love righteousness; I hate robbing even in the burnt offering that is brought to me; therefore ונתתי פעלתם וגו׳ *I will give them their reward*, etc. As to פעלתם their reward comp. פעלת the wages (Lev. 19:13).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:8:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:8:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:8:2)

By these words the expression I hate robbing is explained; as if God said, I shall not rob them; for if I gave them not their reward, I should rob them of their wages.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:9:1)


**ונודע בגוים.** לא יורה זה הכתו' שישראל יהיו עוד מפוזרים, רק יודעו בינות הגוים הבאים לחוג את חג הסכות, ככתוב בספר זכריה (זכריה י"ד ט"ז), והנותנים מס:


*And their seed shall be known.* This prediction does not imply that Israel will again be scattered among the nations, but that they will be known among the nations, who will come up to the holy land to celebrate the feast of Tabernacles (comp. Zec. 14:16), and among them that will bring the tribute.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:1)


**שוש וגו'.** אז יאמר ישראל שוש אשיש:


*I will greatly rejoice.* These are the words which Israel will then proclaim.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:2)


**יעטני.** פועל עבר מגזרת עוטה אור כשלמה (תהלים ק"ד ב'), והם שני בניינים [צ"ל שרשים]:


יעטני *He hath covered me*. It is past of עוטה ; יעט covering (Ps. 104:2) is of the same root, though of a different form.¹⁰

footnotes:
¹⁰ The Hebrew text has the words מגזרת עוטה והם שני בנינים, of the same root as עוטה, but of a different conjugation. This is not the case; both are of the Kal, but their roots are different; the one is to be derived from עטה, the other from יעט. The reverse would be correct, namely, מבנין עוטה והם ב׳ שרשים פעל עבר it is the past tense of the same conjugation as עוטה, but the two verbs have different roots. This is perhaps the right reading.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:10:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:3)


**כחתן יכהן פאר.** הוא פועל יוצא, שהוא מצטרך לפאר נפש כאשר פירשתי במלת ישרתונך (ישעיהו ס' ז'):


יכהן *Serveth*.¹¹ It is a transitive verb, and פאר ornament is the object; it is attended to by the bridegroom; compare my remark on ישרתונך shall minister unto thee (60:7).

footnotes:
¹¹ A. V., Decketh himself with.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:10:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:10:4)


**תעדה כליה.** הם הקשורים על גרגרותיה:


*And as a bride adorneth herself with her jewels,* with the chain round her neck.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 61:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/61:11:1)


**כי כארץ [אשר תוציא צמחה וכגנה], אשר זרועיה תצמיח, יצמיח צדקה.** הטעם שיגדל הצדק כאילו הוא צמח:


כארץ תוציא *Like the earth which bringeth forth*.¹² *So the Lord will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth*. Righteousness and praise will increase, as though they grew.

footnotes:
¹² A. V., As the earth bringeth forth, etc.13 I. E. explains the expression צמח, to grow, used here of righteousness, in a figurative sense. Righteousness will, as it were, grow in the estimation of man, so that all will endeavour to become righteous, and to perform righteous deeds.



## Chapter 62


### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:1:1)


**למען.**אלה דברי השם, ורבים אמרו שגם אלה דברי ישראל בגלות:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:1:2)


**כלפיד יבער.** היו"ד שב אל לפיד, ותחסר מת אשר, (בגלות):


יבער *That burneth.* The relative אשר that must be supplied; for the verb agrees with לפיד lamp.¹

footnotes:
¹ יבער being the third person masculine cannot be connected as predicate with the feminine noun יבער; וישועתה is therefore connected with the masculine noun לפיד, by supplying the relative אשר; and the whole phrase is to be translated: And the salvation thereof as a lamp that burneth.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:2:1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:2:2

### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:3:1)


**והיית עטרת.** ביד יי, כי יש מקומות שיתקנו העטרות בידים:


*In the hand of the Lord.* In some countries people wear crowns on their hands.², here, of the hand. But it is, in fact, not necessary to join ביד with עטרת; we may join it with והיית and explain the phrase thus: Thou shalt be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord—that is, well protected and guarded by the Lord. Comp. Kimchi ad locum.

footnotes:
² This is equivalent to saying that the word עטרת, mostly used in the meaning of crown, that is, an ornament of the head, has sometimes the general meaning ornament, referring to ornaments of other parts of the body, as e.g.

*Thou shalt no more be termed forsaken*, etc. This verse shows that the words For Zion’s sake, etc. are spoken by the Lord; the expression I will not rest, etc. must be taken in a figurative sense.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:5:1)

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:6:1)


**על וגו'.** אלה השומרים כנוי על אבלי ציון, שאין להם עסק כי אם בכי, ולא ישנו בלילה, כשומרי החומות:


*Watchmen.* By this name those that mourn for Zion are meant, who do nothing else but cry, who do not sleep during the night, but are like watchmen upon the walls,


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:6:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:6:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:6:2)


והוסיף **כל היום**, כי מנהג השומרים לישן ביום וכן כתוב משמרים לבוקר (תהלים ק"ל ו') (משמרים הבלי שוא יונה ב' ט'), והנה פירש הנביא דבריו, שהם מזכירים הוא פועל יוצא לשנים פעולים, כמו הזכירני נשפטה יחד (ישעיהו מ"ג כ"ו):


nor do they sleep during the day, while watchmen may at least sleep during the day; comp. They that cause to watch for lying vanities, forsake their idol (Jon. 2:9).⁴ The prophet himself explains the expression watchmen by the words המזכירים את יי that remind the Lord. מזכירים is a causative verb; lit., that cause the Lord to remember; comp. הזכירני put me in remembrance (43:26)

footnotes:
⁴ A. V., They that observe lying vanities.—I. E. proves by this quotation that the expression to watch signifies sometimes to wait for help, to pray; because משמרים means they that cause to pray, and refers to the people in the ship that stirred each other up to prayer; so here also the word שמרים watchmen refers to those that feel themselves continually stirred up to pray to the Almighty for the restoration of Jerusalem and the temple.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:8:1)


**נשבע.** גם זה יורה לאות כי זאת הנבואה לעתיד, כי הנה נשבע השם, שהיא גזר' בלא תנאי, וטעם בימינו כמו גבורתו שהיא עומדת לעד, וטעם להזכיר במקום הזה בימינו, שאדם לא יוכל לקחת דגנך בחזקה:


*The Lord hath sworn*, etc. This verse also proves⁵ clearly, that this prophecy refers to the time yet to come; for the Lord hath sworn, that is, has made an unconditional decree.⁶ *By His right hand.* By His might, which is everlasting. The right hand is mentioned here to indicate His power of preventing enemies despoiling the Israelites of their corn, etc.

footnotes:
⁵ The Hebrew text has the words גם נשבע גם זה לאות וגו׳. The first גם connects this verse with the preceding verse in this way: Till He make Jerusalem a praise in the earth. Yea, he has sworn to do it. But it is also possible that it is an erroneous repetition of the second גם.—The Lord here promised to establish Jerusalem in such a way that it should no more be spoiled. This cannot refer to the deliverance from the Babylonian exile, because Jerusalem was repeatedly spoiled after that event; and since the word that cometh out of the mouth of the Lord, does not return void, these predictions are explained to refer to the deliverance yet to come.
⁶ The predictions of good or evil events are generally connected with the condition pronounced or understood, if you hearken unto me or if you hearken not unto me. But a prediction introduced by a phrase like He hath sworn will be accomplished unconditionally.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:9:1)


**כי וגו'.** יאכלוהו שב אל דגנך ומקבציו ישתוהו שב אל התירוש:


*Shall eat it.* Shall eat thy corn. *And they that have brought it together*, that have brought the wine together.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 62:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/62:10:1)


**עברו וגו'.** טעם, להזכיר טוב לארץ, בעבור אבלי ציון שיתענגו בלא פחד, והנה שב לבאר שתהיה יציאת ישראל מגלותם ושובם אל ארצם בכבוד, וכן יאמרו פקידי הגוים. וטעם **עברו בשערים** להכריז בכל שער ושער לאמר, פנו דרך העם, סקלו אותה מאבן, הרימו נס בעולם:


*Go through,* etc. Having mentioned the prosperity of the land for the sake of the mourners for Zion, who will enjoy it without anxiety, the prophet continues to describe, how the deliverance of Israel from his exile, and his return to his own land will be with honour; the princes of the nations will say Go through, etc. that is, go through the gates to proclaim in every place Prepare the way of the people, clear it of stones, lift up a standard throughout the whole world.

### Verse 1

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:1:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:1:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:1:1)


**מי וגו'.** יש אומרים כי זה הבא הוא המשיח, ויש אומרים שהוא מיכאל, והנכון שהוא רמז לשם הנכבד והטעם על הגזרה שגזר על אדום, וזאת היא מלכות רומא וקוסטנטינא, ונקראו אדומים בעבור שנכנסו בתורת אדום, וזאת התורה נקראה על שם אדום, שהאדומיים האמינו בתחלה בתורת האיש הידוע:


*Who is this that cometh.* Some refer this to Messiah, others to the angel Michael;¹ but more correctly it may be referred to God.² This prophecy contains the decree made against Edom, that is, against the empire of Rome and Constantinople, who are called Edomites, because they adopted the Edomite religion—that is, the Christian religion—which was first established among the Edomites.¹

footnotes:
¹ Comp. And there is none that holdeth with me in these things, but Michael, your prince Dan. 10:21.
² The words השםִ הנכבד the honoured name of the Hebrew text are used instead of יי the Lord, by I. E., in order not to connect the description with dyed garments, etc., directly with God. Comp. I. E. on 42:8.
¹ The words This prophecy, etc., till among the Edomites, are omitted in some editions; they were either struck out by the censors, or left out by the printers from fear of the censorship.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:4)


**ויז נצחם.** הנה יז כמו ויט משה (שמות ט' כ"ג):


וְיֵז *And sprinkled*. It is similar in form to וַיֵט and he stretched forth (Ex. 9:23).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:3:5

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:5](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:5)


**נצחם** הוא הדם שבו יחיה האד' נצחו, והוא מגזרת נצח (ישעיהו ל"ד י'):


נצחם *Their blood*. The blood is called נֶצַח lit. time, because t¹¹hrough the blood man lives his time; it is of the same root as נצח for ever (34:10).

footnotes:
¹¹ The phrase לנצח נצחים (34:10) is explained by I. E., להם זמנים אין קץ periods of time without end. Others compare נצחם their blood with נצח strength (1 Sam. 15:29), the purity and proper circulation of the blood being the essential condition of the health and strength of man; others, again, derive it from a root נזה═נצח to sprinkle. (Ges. Lex. Hebr. Chald.)


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:3:6

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:6](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:3:6)


**אגאלתי.** האל"ף תחת ה"א הבנין, ולפי דעתי שהיא מלה מורכבת מפועל עבר ועתיד, ופי' אגאלתי כמו טנוף, כמו יגאלוהו חשך וצלמות (איוב ג' ה'):


אגאלתי *I stained*. The א is here substituted for ה, the characteristic of the Hiphil, or the word is a compound of the past and future; I prefer the latter explanation. As to its meaning I stained, comp. יגאלהו shall stain it (Job 3:5)



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:4:1)


**כי וגו'.** אעשה נקמה באויבי ואגאל אוהבי, והנה גאולי פעולים והיו"ד סימן המדבר והוא השם:


*For the day of vengeance*, etc. For I will wreak vengeance against my enemies, and I will redeem my friends. גאולי *My redeemed.* It is participle passive plural with the suffix, first person, referring to God.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:5:1

**ואביט.** דרך משל, כי אין צורך לשם:

### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:1)


**חסדי.** אז יודו משכילי ישראל על רוב החסדים שעשה השם עם ישראל בצאתם ממצרים, גם בגלות, ושהושיעם והשיבם אל ארצם:


*I will mention*, etc. The wise of Israel will then acknowledge the great number of benefits bestowed upon them by God at the departure from Egypt, during the exile, and in their deliverance and restoration to their own country.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:7:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:2)


וטעם **תהלות יי.** כי מזכיר חסדי השם זאת היא תהלתו:


*The praises of the Lord.* The mention of the kindness of the Lord, is His praise.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:7:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:7:3)


**ורב טוב.** תואר השם, שהוא רב טוב:


ורב טוב *And great in goodness.*¹² This is an attribute of the Lord.¹³

footnotes:
¹² A. V., And the great goodness.
¹³ By this remark I. E. reminds us not to confound the attribute of God רַב מוב Great in goodness, with רב מוּב the abundance of goodness ═ the great goodness. רַב is an adjective, רֹב an abstract noun.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:8:1)


**ויאמר.** הטעם כי אמר, כדרך בן אדם שחשב שיהיו בנים נאמנים, על כן הושיעם:


*For he said.* This is an anthropomorphism.¹⁴ He thought they would become faithful children, and therefore he helped them.

footnotes:
¹⁴ In reality, such a miscalculation cannot be attributed to the Omniscient; but the prophet means to say that God favoured the Israelites to such a degree that they ought to have been faithful servants of the Lord at all times.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:1)


**לא צר.** האמת שהוא בוי"ו, כטעם ותקצר נפשו (שופטים י' ט"ו), דרך משל להבין [השומעים], כאלו גם הוא הוה [צ"ל היה] בצרה על כן מהר להושיעם:


לא The true meaning of the word is to Him;¹⁵ and לא צר (lit., Unto Him was trouble), he was afflicted, has the same meaning as And His soul was grieved (Jud. 10:16). It is a figurative expression. He was, as it were, in distress, therefore He hastened to deliver them.

footnotes:
¹⁵ I. E. usually follows the Keri, that is, the reading recommended by the Massorah; לו to him is here the Keri, לׂא not, the Ketib.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:9:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:2)


**ומלאך פניו הושיעם.** וכן כתיב וישלח מלאך ויוציאנו ממצרים (במדבר כ"א י"ט), ואיננו משה כלל:


*And the angel of His presence*. Comp. And sent an angel, and hath brought us forth out of Egypt (Num. 20:16); this does by no means refer to Moses.¹

footnotes:
¹ Although I. E. admits that the word מלאך angel or messenger is sometimes used of prophets (Comp. I. E. on 42:19), he refers it in this case to the angel in the usual sense of the word. Comp. I. E. on Num. 20:16.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:9:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:9:3)


**וינטלם.** כמו ונטל החול (משלי כ"ז ג'), והנה הטעם שגאלם ממצרים וינשאם בארצם, על כן אמר כל ימי עולם כל הימים שהיו בארצם:


וינטלם *And he bare them*. Comp. ונטל and the weight (Prov. 27:3). It refers to the deliverance of Israel from Egypt. *And he carried them* in their land. כל ימי עולם *All the days of the long period* of their stay in their own land.¹⁶

footnotes:
¹⁶ עולם is, according to I. E., a long period, but its nature and limits must be gathered from the context; ימות עולם (Deut. 32:7) refers to the past; עד עולם (Ps. 90:2) for ever to the future; עד עולם (1 Sam. 1:22), the whole lifetime, etc., here I. E. infers from the preceding, And he carried them in their land, that it refers to the period during which they had possession of their land.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:10:1)


והמה **מרו ועצבו.** מגזרת אל תעצבו (בראשית מ"ה ה') דרך משל, ויש אומרים כי רוח קדשו הוא מלאך הכבוד, הוא נלחם בם, עד שיצאו מארצו:


ועצבו *And vexed*. Comp. אל תעצבו be not grieved (Gen. 45:5). *And vexed His holy spirit*. This is a figurative expression. Some understand by the holy spirit the angel of the Lord.¹⁷ *He fought against them* till they left His land.

footnotes:
¹⁷ In order to remove the anthropomorphism. Comp. Targ. Jonathan וארגיזו על מימר נביאי קודשיה they acted provokingly against the words of His holy prophets.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:1)


**ויזכור ימי עולם.** שעבר:


*Then he remembered the days of old*, the days that have passed.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:2)


**[משה עמו].** ימי משה ועמו, כמו שמש ירח עמד (חבקוק ג' י"א), ויתכן היות משה פועל, כי הוא מושה את ישראל, והראשון הוא הנכון:


משה עמו *The days of Moses and his people.*¹⁸ As to the asyndeton משה עמוּ comp. שמש ירח the sun and moon (Hab. 3:11). The word משה, however, may also be taken as a participle, meaning he who brought out, who delivered Israel; but the first explanation is preferable.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁸ A. V., Moses and His people.
¹⁹ In his excursus on Ex. 3:15, he says that the tetragrammaton is generally used as a proper noun, but sometimes as a common noun, and thus find it analogous to the proper noun משה, which is once used as a common noun, namely, in this passage משה עמו. The words but the first explanation is preferable are, perhaps, spurious.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:3)


**איה המעלם.** הטעם עתה יאמרו הגוים, איה המעלה אותם מים סוף:


*Where is he that*, etc. Where is he, that brought them up, out of the Red Sea?


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:11:4)


**את רעה צאנו.** עם משה שהוא רועה את ישראל:


את רעה צאנו *With the shepherd of his flock.* With Moses who was the shepherd of Israel.²⁰

footnotes:
²⁰ The words of the Hebrew text are על משקל משה, which seem to have been written by mistake instead of עם with, the explanation of אֵת. Firstly, it is not correct to say that רֹעֵה is formed after משֶֹה; secondly, if the discrepancy with regard to the vowels be not taken into account, it is unnecessary to make any remarks concerning the formation of the regular construct state רֹעֵה from רֹעֶה. The words על משקל are probably the product of some ingenious copyist, who took עם for the initials of על משקל.

**איה השם.** בקרב משה, ויש אומרים על הכבוד שהיה בקרב ישראל:


*That put within him,* that put within Moses, the angel of the Lord, or, that put in the midst of Israel.

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:14:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:14:2

**מזבול**, כמו דירה, וכמוהו יזבלני אישי (בראשית ל' כ"א), והנה הטעם כפול:

### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:16:1)

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:16:2)


והזכיר אברהם שהוא היה הראשון שכרת השם ברית עמו להיות לו לאלהים ובניו, והזכיר גם יעקב שהוא סוף האבות, והוא עקרנו לבדו:


*Though Abraham be ignorant of us,* etc. Abraham is mentioned, as having been the first with whom God made a covenant to be a God unto him and his children; Jacob is also mentioned as the last of the patriarchs, and the founder of our nation exclusively.

### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:17:1)


**למה וגו'.** בעבור היות השם הסבה העליונה, היא הראשונה, אמר למה תתענו, ויש משיבים כי זה כטעם מה שאמרו קדמונינו ז"ל אין מספיקין בידו לעשות תשובה, ואחרים אמרו כי הכתוב דבר כנגד המחשבות, ויש אומרים בעבור שאנחנו בגלות לא נוכל לעשות כל המצות שהם תלויות בארץ:


למה תתענו *Why dost thou make us to err*.²³ Because God is the highest, first cause of everything, therefore He is mentioned as the cause of this erring. Others take it in a sense similar to that of the Rabbinical phrase לעשות תשובה אין מספיקין בידו he is not permitted to repent (Mishnah Aboth, 5:18).¹ Some are of opinion that this is only the imagination of man;²⁴ others, again, say that this refers to those duties only which we cannot perform during our exile.² the commandments introduced by a formula like When ye be come into the land; the commandments concerning the temple and the service therein.

footnotes:
²³ A. V., Why hast Thou made us to err? It is considered a blasphemy to say of God, that He causes men to sin; the object of the various explanations mentioned by I. E. is, to free the expression from this charge.
¹ This is said of him, who misleads others to sin; he is not permitted to repent, he cannot completely remedy the evil which he has produced. It is easy to mislead, but not so easy to make people, when once misled, understand their error, and return to the right way. The question, Why doest Thou make us to err? is to be explained in a similar way, namely, Why do we find it so difficult to repent, to undo our acts of wickedness? Why doest Thou not make the way of our return unto Thee smooth and easy?
²⁴ People that feel some strong inclination to sin, are easily misled to imagine that God Himself prevents them from improving, and that it is no more in their power to master themselves. According to this explanation, the question Why dost Thou cause us to err? is to be taken literally, and to be considered as the expression of a false opinion widely spread among the people.
² As e.g.,

למצער ידשו עם קדשך *The people of thy holiness have possessed* the holy land *but for a little while*, and now *the enemies have trodden down*, etc. Some explain the verse thus: The people of Thy holiness has been dispossessed (by the enemy) for a small thing, or for a short time,²⁷ and this latter explanation is right.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 63:19:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:19:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/63:19:2)


**לוא קרעת שמים.** יש אומרים על מתן תורה, כאילו לא קרעת שמים, והאמת שהוא כמשמעו, כמו לו עמי שומע לי (תהלים פ"א י"ד), וזה הטעם, אילו היית קורע שמים ותרד, והטעם על הגזרות, אז יהיו ההרים נוטפים מפניך, הטעם המלכים היושבים בטח:


לוא קרעת שמים Some refer this phrase to the revelation on Mount Sinai, and render it As if Thou hadst not rent the heavens;¹ but it is more correct to take לוּ═לוּא in its usual meaning if; (comp. Ps. 84:13), and to explain the sentence thus: If Thou wouldst rend the heavens and come down, that is, if Thou wouldst send forth Thy decrees, then, the mountains, that is, the kings² who sit in safety, would flow down at Thy presence. נָזֹלּוּ *Would flow down*. The Dagesh in the ל is caused by the pause;³

¹ To give us Thy commandments. לוּא is, according to this explanation, the same as לא not. Comp. Targum Jonathan: לא להון ארבנת שמיא not for them (for the heathen people) hast thou descended from heaven.
² Kingdoms (מלכות) or nations (גוים) would better correspond with the phrase מפניך גוים ירגזו thus the nations would tremble at Thy presence (64:1), which seems to be the explanation of מפניך הרים נזלו.
³ This Dagesh is called by the Grammarians: euphonic (לתפארת הקריאה); comp. חָדְלֽוּ ═ חָדֵלּֽוּ (Jud. 5:7).

ונדגש למ"ד **נזולו** בעבור שהוא סוף פסוק, על משקל ולא יכלו (שמות ח' י"ד):


נָזֹלּוּ is in form similar to יָכֹלוּ they could (Ex. 8:14).⁴

footnotes:
¹⁵ A. V., In those is continuance.—The words לעולם הספירות הקצף are corrupt; they must contain the explanation of עולם, since that of בהם is given before in the words בעבור הצדיקים through the righteous. E. renders עולם disappearance from עלם to conceal; and the Hebrew text is to be altered into עולם י הפרת הקצף or עולם.עולם י סתירת הקצף means the disappearance of the wrath.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:1:1

*I was*¹ *sought*, etc. This is the reply of God to the prayer of the Israelites; He says: Your fathers have provoked me, but ‘ I was sought,’ that is, I offered myself to be found whenever they were in trouble, to them that asked me not, that I should be accessible to them.

¹ A. V., I am sought.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:1:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:1:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:1:2)


**אמרתי הנני הנני.** פעם אחר פעם על יד הנביאים:


*I said*, ‘ *Behold me*, *behold me*,’ repeatedly through the prophets.²

footnotes:
² I. E. adds through the prophets, because the Lord revealed Himself directly to the whole nation only once, namely, on Mount Sinai.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:1:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:1:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:1:3)


**לא קורא.** לא היה נקרא בשמי בימים ההם, כי אם בשם הבעל:


*That was not called by my name* in those days, but by the name of Baal.



### Verse 2

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:2:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:2:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:2:1)


**נדרשתי [צ"ל פרשתי].** אמר רבי משה הכהן כי הכתוב הראשון על אומות העולם, והטעם כי אפילו לגוים שלא נקראו בשמי נדרשתי, ולעמי פרשתי ידי, והטעם שאקבל אותם:


*I have spread out my hands,* etc. According to R. Moses Hakkohen, the preceding verse refers to all nations, as if God said, Even to nations that are not called by my name, I was accessible, but as regards my people I have spread my hands to receive them.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:2:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:2:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:2:2)


**הדרך.** ימשך עצמו ואחר עמו, וכן הוא הדרך דרך לא טוב כמו ועץ הדעת טוב ורע (בראשית ב' ט'):


הדרך לא טוב *In a way that is not good.* Supply דרך way before לא טוב not good;³ comp. טוב ורע עץ הדעת דעת═עץ הדעת טוב ורע the tree of knowledge of good and evil (Gen. 2:9)

footnotes:
³ לא טוב is the genitive governed by דרך, which must be supplied; because הדרך cannot govern the genitive on account of the definite article. Comp. I. E. on 30:20.



### Verse 3

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:3:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:3:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:3:1)


**העם המכעיסים אותי על פני.** כעבד שיכעיס אדוניו והוא רואהו בעיניו:


*To my face*. Like a servant that provokes his master while in his presence.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:3:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:3:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:3:2)


**זבחים בגנות.** לע"ז:


*In gardens* of idolatry.



### Verse 4

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:4:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:1)


**היושבים.** לדרוש אל המתים ודברי השדים:


*That sit among the graves*, to inquire of the dead, and to listen to the spirits.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:4:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:2)


**ובנצורים.** חרבות, כעיר נצורה (ישעיהו א' ח'):


ובנצורים *And in ruins.*⁴. Comp. נצורה waste (1:8).

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:4:3

**האוכלי' בשר החזי'.** להכעיסני:

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:4:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:4:4)


**ומרק.** ידוע, ואת מרק שפוך (שופטים ו' כ') וכתיב ופרק והם שני שמות לטעם אחד:


וטרק *And broth.* Its meaning is well known; comp. Judg. 6:20. The Ketib⁵ is ופרק; the two words, however, are the same in meaning.

⁵ See ix. Note 2.



### Verse 5

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:5:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:1)


**האומרים.** הם טמאים, והם אומרים לאחרים שלא אכלו בשר החזיר:


*Which say.* They, the unclean, say to the others, that have never eaten swine’s meat, etc.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:2)


**קרב אליך.** כמו גשה אליך:


גשה אליך═קרב אליך *Stand by thyself.* Lit. Go nearer to thyself.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:5:3)


**כי קדשתיך.** פעל עומד כמו בני יצאוני (ירמיה י' כ'), וכן הוא כי קדשתי ממך, אני קדוש ממך:


קדשתיך *I am holier than thou.* It is an intransitive verb; as to the suffix,⁶ קרשתיך I am holier than thou. comp. יצאוני have gone out of me (Jer. x 20); similarly קדשתיך has the same meaning as קדשתי ממך I am holy, more than thou.

footnotes:
⁶ The suffix of the verb is generally the same as the corresponding pronoun in the accusative, and should therefore be joined only to transitive verbs; but exceptionally it is a substitute for a pronoun and a preposition, and can in that case be joined to a neuter verb, as e.g.,

**אלה.** שמו עשן באפי:


אלה עשן באפי These put⁷ smoke in my nose.

### Verse 6

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:6:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:6:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:6:1)


**הנה וגו'.** זאת הרעה שעשו כתוב' היתה לפני לא שכחתיה:


*Behold it is written before me*. This evil which they have done, is, as it were, written before me; I have not forgotten it.



### Verse 7

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:7:1)


**עונותיכם וגו'.** והנה אתם הוספתם עונות על עונות אבותיכם, וטעם ראשונה שהלכו בגלות אבותיכם, בעבור עבודה זרה:


*Your iniquities*, etc. You have added sins to the sins of your forefathers. *I measured their former work into their bosom*. Your fathers went into exile for their idolatry.



### Verse 8

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:8:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:8:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:8:1)


**כה.** אף על פי כן יהיה בימים ההם כאשר ימצ' התירוש באשכול לאמר אדם לחברו אל תשחיתהו ויאמר כי ברכה בו כן אעשה למען עבדי הם צדיקי ישראל בגלות לבלתי השחית הכל:


*Thus saith the Lord, As the new wine,* etc. Although they have sinned, it will, nevertheless, be in those days as when *the new wine is found in the cluster and one saith* to the other *do not destroy it*, *for a blessing is in it.* I shall do the same for the sake of my servants, the righteous men of Israel, during their exile; namely, I shall not utterly destroy them.



### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:9:1)


**והוצאתי וגו'.** שיצאו בגלות, והם הצדיקים, והעד שאמר בחירי:


*And I will bring forth out of Jacob*, of those that had gone into exile, of the righteous among them: who deserve to be called mine elect.



### Verse 10

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:10:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:10:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:10:1)


**והיה.** עמק עכור סביב ירושלם, וכתוב את עמק עכור לפת' תקוה (הושע ב' י"ז), ורבים אמרו כטעם עוכר ישראל (מלכים א' י"ח י"ז), ואין צורך:


עמק עכור *The valley of Achor.* This valley is near Jerusalem; comp. And the valley of Achor for a door of hope (Hos. 2:15). Others render it, Valley of trouble,⁸ comparing it with עכר that troublest (1 Kings 18:17). The latter is a forced explanation.

footnotes:
⁸ That is, the valley, in which the Israelites have brought trouble upon themselves through their bad actions. I. E., justly rejects this explanation, because the words עמק עכור are probably like השרון in the first part of the verse, a proper name, without any reference to trouble or sin.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:10:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:10:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:10:2)


**אשר דרשוני.** כי יזכור אשר דרשו זולתי:


*For my people that sought me.* For He will remember those that seek another besides Him.



### Verse 11

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:11:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:1)


**ואתם.** השכחים, שם תאר על משקל יראים (שמואל א' כ"ג ג'):


הַשְׁכֵחִים *That forget*, (lit., that are forgetful). It is an adjective,⁹ similar in form to יְרֵאִים afraid (1 Sam. 23:3).

footnotes:
⁹ I. E. explains שְׁכֵהִים to be an adjective, although it governs an accusative, since the participle is שֹׁכְחִים; or he means by שם תאר the participle, and שְׁכֵחִים would in that case be another form of the participle, that could be compared with יראים, the only form of the participle Kal of ירא, to fear.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:11:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:2)


**לגד.** גדוד השמים, ויאמר רבי משה הכהן כי לגד הוא כוכב צדק שיורה על כל דבר טוב, כי כן לשון קדר, ואמר כי אין כמוהו בא גד (בראשית ל' י"א):


לגד *For the host of the heavens*.¹⁰ R. Moses Hakkohen says, that גד means the planet Jupiter which forebodes only good things;¹¹ that in Arabic the word has the same meaning;¹² but that בגל (Gen. 30:11) is different from it.¹³

footnotes:
¹⁰ A. V., That troop.
¹¹ According to the belief of Eastern people; In Arabic, Jupiter is called السعد الاكبر the greatest fortune.
¹² جَدٌ Felicitas.
¹³ I. E. renders בגד a troop comes, and refers it to the troop of five children, which Leah then had.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:11:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:3)


**למני.** יש אומרים לצורת הגלגל, שכל צורה וצורה יש לה מניין ידוע מכוכבים, ור' משה הכהן אמר שהוא שם כוכב:


למני *For Meni*.¹⁴ According to some מני (lit., number) is the name of the Zodiac, because each of its constellations has a certain number of stars. R. Moses Hakkohen says that מני is the name of one star.¹⁵ the moon.

footnotes:
¹⁴ A. V., That number.
¹⁵ R. Moses Hakkohen mentions no name of that star. Gesenius is of opinion that מני is Venus; others compare it with μήvη


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:11:4

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:4](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:11:4)


**ממסך.** מגזרת מסכה יינה (משלי ט' ב'):


ממסך *Drink offering.* Comp., מסכה she hath mingled (Prov. 9:2)



### Verse 12

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:12:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:12:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:12:1)


**ומניתי.** דרך צחות בלשון הקודש לאמר גד גדוד יגודנו (בראשית מ"ט י"ט) דן ידין עמו [שם ט"ז] ובעבור שאמר למני אמר אחריו ומניתי, ממספר כמו ע"י מונה (ירמיה ל"ג י"ג):


ומניתי *And I will number*. The repetition of the same root is considered as an elegance in Hebrew. Comp. גד גדוד עודנו Gad, a troop shall overcome him (Gen. 49:19); דן ידין Dan shall judge (ibid. 16). Thus the verb ומניתי is used because of מני at the end of the preceding verse; it means I shall number; comp. מונה that telleth (Jer. 33:13)



### Verse 13

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:13:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:13:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:13:1)


**לכן וגו'.** עבדי, הם השבים אל ציון:


*My servants,* that return to Zion.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:13:2

### Verse 14

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:14:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:14:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:14:1)


**תיילילו.** ראוי להיות תחת התי"ו פתח, על דרך יישירו נגדך (משלי ד' כ"ה), וכמוהו ממרחק יידע (תהלים קל"ח ט' ו'), ואלמנה לא ייטיב (איוב כ"ד כ"א):


תְּיֵילִילוּ *Ye shall howl.* The regular form of the word would be ¹⁶תַּיְלִילוּ; comp., יַיְשִׁירוּ they look straight (Prov. 4:25). It is similar in form to יְיֵדָע he knoweth; (Ps. 138:6), and יְיֵטִיב he doth good (Job 24:21)

footnotes:
¹⁶ Or תֵּילִילוּ after the form הֵילִילוּ (23:1); the root is ילל.



### Verse 15

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:15:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:15:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:15:1)


**והנחתם שמכם לשבוע'.** ואלה כמו ישימך כצדקיהו וכאחאב (ירמיה כ"ט כ"ב), ויאמר אדם לחבירו והמיתך יי:


*And ye shall leave your name for a curse.* Comp.¹⁷ The Lord make thee a curse and an oath (Num. 5:21); The Lord make thee like Zedekiah and like Ahab (Jer. 29:22). *The Lord God shall slay thee.* Thus they will say to each other.¹⁸

footnotes:
¹⁷ The Hebrew text has the words ואלה כמו; and a curse, comp. ואלה is either the explanation of לשבועה and must be altered into לאלה, or it is the remnant of a quotation, and must in that case be preceded by כמו.
¹⁸ This explanation is given on account of the change of the number; the suffix in שמכם is plural, while that of והמיתך is singular. In Targum Jonathan it is rendered, וימיתכון and shall kill you.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:15:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:15:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:15:2)


**יקרא שם אחר.** נכבד:


*Another name.* That is, a better name.



### Verse 16

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:16:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:1)


**אשר וגו'.** אין מלת מתברך כמו ונברכו בו (בראשית י"ח י"ח) כי הפרש יש ביניהם:


המתברך *He who blesseth himself.* This word is not like ונברכו and shall be blessed (Gen. 18:18); there is a difference between the two words.¹⁹

footnotes:
¹⁹ ונברכו is the passive (Niphal), they shall be blessed; that is, they shall receive the blessing from the Almighty; מתברך is reflective (Hithpael): he who blesses himself; that is, he who believes himself blessed or wishes himself to be blessed, as I. E. himself explains below.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:16:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:2)


וטעם **באלהי אמן** שיכיר כל העולם כי אין אלוה אמת זולתו, כי אמן מגזרת אמונה (ישעיהו כ"ה א') והוא תאר השם, והטעם שיודה שזהו אמת או מתפלל שיתאוה להיותו אמת:


באלהי אמן In the God whom all the world will acknowledge to be the true God, and that there is none besides Him.²⁰ אמן is an adjective ¹ of the same root as אמונה truth (25:1); יתברך ונו׳ *Shall bless himself,* etc. He shall thankfully acknowledge that this²¹ is true, or wish and pray that it may become true.

footnotes:
²⁰ A. V., In the God of truth.
¹ I. E. seems to overlook that the adjective אמן demands the absolute state before it, not the construct. If, however, אמן is referred by him to the, people, to the faithful, and not to God, the construct state would be explained hereby, but the use of the singular אמן instead of the plural, would still require some explanation.
²¹ That God is recognised by all people as the Lord of the universe.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:16:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:16:3)


וטעם **כי [נשכחו]**, נסתרו הצרות שעברו על הצדיקים עובדי השם, כי בראות הרשעים שהצרות באות עליהם, היו מלעיגים בם ובעבודתם:


*Because the former troubles*, etc., *are hid from mine eyes*. The troubles which have befallen the righteous, the servants of the Lord, have been intensified by the circumstance that the wicked used to mock at the pious and their piety, when the latter were afflicted with calamities¹

footnotes:
¹ I. E. perhaps explains here the expression from mine eyes to mean from the eyes of my pious people who perceive all the insults and mocking of the wicked.



### Verse 17

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:17:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:17:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:17:1)


**כי וגו'.** יש אומרים כי הטעם כאילו, ורבי יהודה המדקדק נ"ע אמר כי טעם בריאת שמים והארץ על הפרטים, והנכון כי השמים הם הרקיע, והשם יחדש אויר טוב שיהיו בני האדם בריאי' בגופם, ויחיו שנים רבות, וגם יוסיף בכח הארץ, והנה היא חדשה, והאומר כי זה רמז לעולם הבא, איננו דבק בפרשה, כי אין לעולם הבא אכילה, וכן הורו קדמונינו ז"ל [ברכות י"ז], והוא אמת לבדו:


בי הנני בורא שמים חדשים וגו׳ *For behold, I create new heavens*, etc. Some explain this verse thus: Behold, it will be as if I created, etc.²² The grammarian, R. Jehudah, says, that by the new heavens the creatures in heaven and earth are meant.²³ The right explanation, however, is, that by heavens the atmosphere over the earth is meant, and the meaning of the whole sentence is: God will create a new good atmosphere, that people will be healthy and enjoy a long life; He will likewise increase the productive power of the earth, that it will be as though it were new. Those that refer the passage to the future life of man, are wrong; for it cannot thus agree with the context of the chapter, since in the future life there is neither eating nor drinking, as our sages have taught us,¹ and this idea concerning the future life is the only true one.

footnotes:
²² The heavens are considered as not subject to a material change; it was therefore found necessary to explain the seeming contradiction of this opinion, contained in the prediction of the creation of new heavens. Some explain that there will not be a real, but only an apparent creation of new heavens.
²³ According to this opinion, the totality of the heavens is unchangeable, and that will not be renewed, but the individual creatures in them do not share the same privilege; the new creation refers to them.
¹ Comp. Talmud Babli, Berachoth p. 17.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:17:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:17:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:17:2)


**הראשונות.** יש או' על הצרות, והוא הנכון, ואחרים אמרו על השמים והארץ, ואין טועם לפירוש זה, והעד הפסוק הבא אחריו:


*The former*. The former troubles, as some quite correctly explain; others supply heaven and earth; but there is no sense in their explanation, as may be proved from the next verse.²⁴

footnotes:
²⁴ The opposite of the former things, which shall not be remembered, is described in the next verse by גילה, rejoicing, and משוש,joy. The former things are therefore the former troubles and sufferings.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:18:1)


**עדי עד.** שנים ארוכות, כי הנה אחריו ימות, והנה בורא את ירושלם יוכיח, כי אין הבריא' להוציא יש מאין כאשר אמרו כל המפרשים, רק הוא מגזרת חדש':


עדי עד *Long years*.²⁵ For at last man dies ¹ (comp. vers. 20). הנני בורא את ירושלים *Behold*, *I make*²⁶ *Jerusalem.* From this passage it can be proved that the word ברא does not mean to create (to produce from non-existence into existence) but to form, to renew.

footnotes:
²⁵ A. V., For ever.
¹ And therefore he cannot rejoice for ever, and עדי עד in this verse signifies only a long space of time.
²⁶ A. V., I create.

### Verse 20

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:20:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:20:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/65:20:1)


**לא וגו'.** הנה תורה זאת הפרשה כי השבים אל ציון בימות המשיח יחיו שנים רבות, והנה הזקן ימלא את ימיו שהוא בתולדת לחיות, כמו הקדמונים מאדם ועד נח, וכן עול ימים שהוא העולל, והמת מת והוא בן מאה שנה, ואם מת יקולל, כי אם חיה פחות מאלה השנים, אז יאמרו עליו עדיין לא שלמה דעתו, וזה אמר שמת והוא נער והחוטא אם יהיה בן מאה. הכתוב לעד כי סוף העולם ישוב כראשיתו:


*There shall be no more*, etc. This verse shows, that those who will return to Zion will enjoy a long life. The old man will complete his days, that is, the days which the natural constitution of man permits him to live; he will live as long as the former generations from Adam to Noah lived; the same is the case with עולל═עול ימים infant of days.²⁷ ימות וגו׳ כי הנער בן טאה שנה.²⁸ *For the young man*²⁹ *shall die one hundred years old*, etc. The sinner who dies a hundred years old, will be cursed; for if he lived less than that, his infancy will plead for him, his mental faculties not yet being fully developed; but being a hundred years old he is a young man, and being then a sinner, he is cursed.³⁰ We learn from this verse that the world will at last be again as it was at the beginning.³¹

footnotes:
²⁷ The infant will likewise complete his days; the time of infancy will be prolonged in the same proportion.
²⁸ The Hebrew text has the words והמת מת, which do not seem to harmonise with the context; from the words which follow, והוא בן מאה שנה, it may be inferred that the word נער, or the whole phrase כי הנער בן מאה שנה, is to be explained, and that the words והמת מת have to be replaced by הנער, or by the whole phrase נער .כי הנער בן מאה שנה is the period of life next to עול ימים.
²⁹ A. V., The child.
³⁰ According to Jewish law the age of responsibility of man for his actions begins with the completion of the thirteenth year. Comp. בן שלש עשרה למצות (Aboth. 5:24).
³¹ That the life of man will equal in length that of the first generations from Adam to Noah, that is, the length of about a thousand years.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 65:21:1

**ובנו וגו'.** הטעם שיהיו לבטח כי אין אויב, והפסו' הבא אחריו לעד, או טעמו שיבנו בית וישבו בה שנים רבות, ולא כמתי מלחמה:


*And they shall build houses*, etc. That is, they will be in safety, for there will be no enemy, as explained in the next verse; or, they will build houses, and dwell therein for a long time, while those that die in war are not so happy.

וטעם **ומעשה ידיהם יבלו בחירי**, כי יש מעשים שיעשה האדם ויזקין, והם יראו חדשים כבניין והמכתב. (והם) **בחירי.** הם פועלים:


*And mine elect shall outlive the work of their hands*. Many works of man retain still their new appearance, while man has already become old, as *e.g.* a building, a book. The pronoun their refers to mine elect, the subject of the sentence.

**זאב וגו'.** הטעם השלום, ולפי דעת רבים שהשם יסיר תולדת הזאב, והעד כבקר יאכל תבן:


*The wolf and the lamb shall feed together*. This is a figurative expression for peace will be established. Many imagine this to be done in such a way, that God will deprive the wolf of its natural voracity, as indicated by the words, And the lion shall eat straw like the bullock.

**השמים כסאי.** ידענו כי כבוד השם מלא השמים והארץ, והטעם כי מן השמים תבאנה הגזרות על כל העולם כולו, כאשר תצאנה מלפני המלך בשבתו על כסאו:


*The heaven is my throne*. We know that the glory of the Lord filleth heaven and earth; but by the words the heaven is my throne the prophet indicates, that the destinies of the whole world come from above, as it were by decrees, which the king, sitting on his throne, sends forth.¹

*But to this man will I look,* etc. Although heaven is my throne, yet will I look to the poor and to him that is of a contrite spirit. *I will look,* I will direct my eye, my attention to him; it is the opposite of I will hide my face from you (1:15)

**שוחט וגו'.** הטעם כי אביט אל חרד אל דברי, לא אל המקריבים עולה, ומעשיהם רעים, והנה שוחט השור כאילו יכה איש, הטעם דם יחשב, כי אין העולה קרבן כהוגן, או יהיה מכה איש לא מכת מות רק מכת פצע וחבורה:


*He that killeth an ox,* etc. I look to him that trembleth at my word, not to those that sacrifice burnt offerings, and at the same time act badly; for he that killeth an ox, מכה איש is as guilty as if he slew a man; it is considered as murder on his part, because the offering is not brought properly; or is guilty as if he struck a man, not killing, but hurting and wounding him;²

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:5:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:5:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:5:2)


וטעם **אחיכם.** שהוא יותר קשה:


Your brethren is added, because this circumstance, that they are brethren, gives greater force to the offence.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:5:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:5:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:5:3)


**יכבד יי.** אמר רבי משה הכהן כי הוא מלשון כבדות, והטעם כי הוא כבד עליו לזכרו ולשמר חוקיו, וראייתו כי לא ימצא מלשון כבוד כי אם מבנין נפעל, כמו נכבדת (ישעיהו נ"ו ט"ו), והנה שכח יכבדו בניו (איוב י"ד כ "א) והעד יצערו [שם], והנה על פירושו הטעם ידוע, ותחס' מלת זמן, כאילו אמר עוד אביא זמן שנראה בשמחתכם והם יבושו, דברי המנדים, וכן פירוש הפסוק, אמרו אחיכם למען שמי יכבד השם מי יתן ויכבד השם מגזרת כבוד ונראה בשמחתכם ונבוש אנחנו, וזה הוא טעם והם יבושו, והטעם שיאמרו שהשם לא יוכל להראות כבודו, והנה יהיה זה הכתוב דבק עם הבא אחריו, והמפרשים אמרו שאיננו לשון המנדים, ואמרו כי הוא דבר השם, כדרך נעשה אדם (בראשית א' כ"ו) ואחיכם אמרו השם והנביא:


יכבד יי R. Moses Hakkohen says, that it means, the Lord is heavy; that is, it is difficult to them to remember Him and to keep His commandments; as a proof of the correctness of this explanation he adds, that only the Niphal of כבד is found in the meaning of to be honoured, as *e.g.* נכבדת Thou art glorified (26:15); but he did not think of יִבְבְּדוּ they are honoured, which is the opposite of יצערו they are little (Job 14:21). According to this explanation the sense of the verse is clear.¹⁰ After יכבד יי the Lord is heavy the word yet must be supplied¹ once, yet, or are the corruption of ותחסר מלת עוד, as adopted for the translation., as if the prophet said, yet a time will come, when we shall see your¹¹ rejoicing, while they, that cast you out, will be confounded. But I think that¹² these are the words of your brethren that cast you out, and that the whole verse must be explained thus: Your brethren say, For my name’s sake let the Lord be honoured [יכבד being derived from כבוד honour (11:10)], we wish it that the Lord be honoured, then we shall see your rejoicing and be ashamed; this is the meaning of the words והם יבשו and they shall be ashamed.¹³ They say it ironically and mean to indicate, that God will not be able to show His glory. In this way there is a connection between this verse and the next. Those that take these words, not as uttered by your brethren etc., but spoken by God, understand the plural in נראה as pluralis majestatis, like the plural in נעשה let us make (Gen. 1:26), or² refer it to both, to God and the prophet together.

footnotes:
¹⁰ Comp. Kimchi ad locum: The wicked say to those that are anxious to fulfil the word of the Lord, ‘Certainly, the Lord is too hard for us with His commandments,’ but, says the prophet to the good, He will appear in the midst of your rejoicings, and they will be ashamed. This is probably also the explanation of R. Moses Hakkohen, partly quoted by I. E.
¹ The Hebrew text has the words ותחסר מלת זמן, which either mean, and an adverb of time is wanting, as, e. g.,
¹¹ The good, that tremble at His word, are addressed by the prophet.
¹² These words are added in the translation; the corresponding Hebrew phrase, ולפי דעתי is missing. That he approves of the explanation that follows is clear from the words, In this way there is a connection between this verse and the next.
¹³ According to this explanation this would be one of the very rare instances of the oratio indirecta in Hebrew; the oratio directa would be ואנחנו נבוש, and we shall be ashamed.
² ואחיכם of the Hebrew text gives no sense, and must be corrected into ואחרים, and others.

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:7:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:7:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:7:1)


**בטרם תחיל.** מגזרת חיל כיולדה (תהלים מ"ח ז'), הטעם שיבואו בני ציון בלא טורח, כיולדה שילדה בנים בלי טורח:


תחיל *She travailed.* Comp. חיל trembling (Ps. 45:7). *Before she travailed she brought forth*. This is a figurative expression, indicating, that the Israelites will return to Zion, without any difficulty, like a woman, that bears children without troubles.

**והמליטה.** כטעם ילדה, וכמוהו שמה קננה קפוד ותמלט (ישעיהו ל"ד ט"ו), ואם הם שנים בנינים, והטעם שיבואו בני ציון בלי טורח מארבע רוחות פתאום, כאילו חלה וילדה בנים ביום אחד, והוא דבר פלא:


והמליטה זכר *She was delivered of a man child.* Comp. תְּמַלֵּט she will lay eggs (34:15), though of a different conjugation.¹⁴—The Israelites will suddenly come together, without much exertion, from all quarters; it will be as though Zion had conceived and born her children in one day, and that is wonderful.¹⁵

### Verse 9

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:9:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:9:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:9:1)


**האני אשביר.** מגזרת במשבר בנים (הושע י"ג י"ג), הטעם שיש לי כח לעשות כאלה, כאילו אני אגיע היולדה על המשבר ולא אוכל להוליד, או אני שהייתי מוליד כל העולם, ועצרתי:


האני אשביר *Shall I bring to birth*. Comp. משבר בנים "birth of children" (Hos. 13:13). *Shall I bring to birth* etc. I have the power to do all this,¹⁶ to bring the woman, as it were, near the birth, and should I not be able to bring force? or should I could cause the whole world to bring forth a children, shut the womb of Zion?

footnotes:
¹⁶ The Hebrew text has באלה which seems to be nothing but the כאלה "such things," of preceding verse, and refers to the wonderful events (restoration of Zion) described by the prophet; the reading באלה "with those," can, however, to be defended, and explained to refer to the enemies mentioned ver. 6. The punishment of the enemies would thus be described as the first step towards the restoration of Zion, and the prophet asks, Should be, that has the power to preform the first pat, not be able to do the rest?

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:12:1

**כי וגו'.** כנהר אטה אל ציון שלום, וכנחל שוטף יבוא חיל גוים, כמו עשה לי את החיל הזה (דברים ח' י"ז):


*I shall extend to Zion peace like a river,* etc. ²⁰חיל means property; comp. החיל הזה this wealth (Deut. 8:17).

footnotes:
²⁰ I. E. read חיל גוים instead of כבוד הגוים of our editions of the Bible; both mean the same. Comp. Hebr. Bib. cum varietate lect., ed. Doederlein.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:12:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:12:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:12:2)

*Ye shall be borne on her sides,* when returning from exile.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:12:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:12:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:12:3)


**תשעשעו.** כמו ושעשע יונק (ישעיהו י"א ח'), ובא העין בקמץ חטף בעבור היותו סוף פסוק:


תשעשעו *Ye will play.* Comp. ושעשע and shall play (11:8). The ע has a short Kamez because of the pause.²¹

footnotes:
²¹ The regular form would be ע ,תְּשָׁעְשְׁעוּ being a guttural, it should receive the compound Sheva (ֳ) instead of the simple; but for the Sheva of the next letter it changes the compound Sheva into the short Kamez; the pause changes the Sheva of the ש into a vowel (ָ), and restores, therefore, the compound Sheva under ע. It would be more correct to say that the compound Sheva owes its origin to the guttural character of the letter, and that the Kamez under ש is the proper sign of the pause. The absence of any remark concerning the difference between וְשִׁעֲשַׁע and תְּשָׁעֳשָׁעוּ (the one being Piel, the other Pual), is rather suspicious, and leads to the suggestion that I. E. identified תְּשָׁעֳשָׁעוּ with תְּשַׁעֲשָׁעוּ, and explains, but wrongly, the change of ֲ into ֳ, as caused by the pause.

*Eating swine’s meat.* They sanctify themselves, but their bodies are full of uncleanliness.



### Verse 18

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:18:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:1)


**ואנכי.** כטעם על יי ועל משיחו (תהלים ב' ב'):


ואנכי מעשיהם ומחשבתיהם *And I am their works and their thoughts*.³² It has the same meaning as the rulers take counsel together against the Lord, and against His anointed (Ps. 2:2),

footnotes:
³² A. V., For I know their works and their thoughts.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:18:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:2)


**באה.** תחסר מלת עם [צ"ל עת] והטעם, כאשר יחשבו שיוסדו עלי, אז תבא עת לקבץ כל הגוים סביב ירושלם:


באה *The time hath come.*³³ Supply עת time. The meaning of the whole verse is, When they intend to rebel against me, then the time is come to assemble all nations round Jerusalem, etc.

footnotes:
³³ A. V., It shall come.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:18:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:18:3)


**וראו את כבודי.** שאעשה בהן דין עד שיראו כבודי בכל העולם, וזה מלחמת גוג ומגוג:


*And see my glory.* I shall punish them till they will declare my glory to all people. This passage refers to the war of Gog and Magog.³⁴

### Verse 19

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:19:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:19:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:19:1)


**ושמתי בהם אות.** זה האות לגנאי בחסרון עין, והאות חדוש שלא נראה כמוהו:


אות *A sign* of reproach, as *e.g.,* the loss of one eye;³⁵ it will be some new thing, the like of which has never appeared before.

³⁵ The Hebrew text has בחסרון עי״ן, with omission of ע, instead of כחסרון עין. Comp. 1 Sam. 11:2.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:19:2

וטעם **פלטים** שימותו רובם, כאשר הוא מפורש בספר יחזקאל (יחזקאל ל"ח, כ"א כ"ב, ל"ט, י"א וכולי) ובספר זכריה (זכריה י"ד י"ב י"ח):


*Those that escape.* The greater part will die, as is stated distinctly. Comp. Ez. 38:21, 22; 39:11 sqq.; and Zec. 14:12, 13
