### Verse 22

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:22:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:1)


**החדשים.** פירשתיו (ישעיהו ס"ה י"ז):


*The new heavens*. I have already explained this expression (65:17).


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:22:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:2)


**עומדים לפני.** שלא יבלו כקדמונים, וטעם לפני בעבור כי השם עיקר כל עמידה:


עמדים *Shall remain,* shall not be destroyed, as their predecessors have been. *Before me.* Before God, who is the first, cause of all existing things.⁴⁰

footnotes:
⁴⁰ All things are kept in existence by the will of God, they are therefore said to stand before the Lord, as if to receive from Him the power of existence.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:22:3

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:22:3)


**כן יעמד זרעכם ושמכם.** שלא ימחה, או שמכם (שלא ימחה) כמו זרעכם, והטעם כפול והטעם [צ"ל וכמוהו] כעת יאמר ליעקב ולישראל (במדבר כ"ג כ"ג):


*And your name* shall remain, so that it will not be blotted out; or,⁴¹ it has the same meaning as your seed, and is a mere repetition of the same idea. Comp. To Jacob and to Israel (Num. 23:23)

footnotes:
⁴¹ The words שלא ימחה after שמכם are superfluous. According to the second explanation שם has here the meaning substance; comp. I. E. on Ruth 3:16.



### Verse 23

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:23:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:23:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:23:1)


**והיה מדי.** קרוב מטעם כל עת שיהיה החדש, וכמוהו, מדי עברו (מלכים ב' ד' ח'):


מדי חדש *Whenever new moon will be*.⁴² מדי has nearly the same meaning as בכל עת whenever (Est. 5:13). Comp. מדי עברו whenever he passed (2 Kings 4:8).

footnotes:
⁴² A. V., From one new moon to another. Your daily tasks.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:23:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:23:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:23:2)


ו**חדש בחדשו** כמו דבר יום ביומו (שמות ה' י"ג), והטעם, כל יום ויום בעתו, ומזה הכתוב למדו הקדמונים ז"ל שמשפט רשעים בגיהנם י"ב חדש, וטעם מדי שנה (זכריה י"ד ט"ז), [וטעם מדי שבת בשבתו] בפרשת ז' שבתות (ויקרא כ"ג, ט' כ"ב, כ"ה, א' י"ג):


חדש בחדשו a new moon on the day appointed for it. Comp. דבר יום ביומו the task of every day on the day appointed for it (Ex. 5:13). From this verse the ancients derived that the wicked had to suffer the future punishment for twelve months;¹ they explain the word מדי to signify one year.⁴³ The meaning of מדי שבת בשבתו I have explained in my commentary on the chapter concerning the seven weeks.² 25:1-13. The words מדי שבת בשבתו are explained in neither of the two passages. I. E. is perhaps of opinion that the expression שבת, used here by the prophet, includes also the festivals, and he refers therefore to his remark on Lev. 23:11, in which he proves that the word שבת in the phrase ממחרת השבת refers to the first day of Passover.

footnotes:
¹ See Midrash Yalkut ad locum.
⁴³ This seems to be I. E.’s interpretation of the passage quoted from the Midrash; but this explanation of מרי is not found there.
² Lev. 23:9-22, or ib.



### Verse 24

###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:24:1

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:1](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:1)


**ויצאו וגו'.** סביב ירושלם כי שם תופת, וזה הכתוב למדו כל החכמים שיהיה יום דין בירושלם, ורבים אמרו כי ואשם לא תכבה רמז לנשמה בהפרדה מעל גוויתה, אם לא היתה זוכה לעלות אל מלאכי השם, תשאר אצל גלגל האש, והקדמונים אמרו כי זה אחר תחיית המתים, וראייתם שאמר דניאל על הרשעים אחר שיקיצו, שיהיו לדראון עולם, והכל אמת אמרו:


*And look* round Jerusalem, where Topheth is; from this verse all the learned⁴⁴ gather that there will be a day of judgment in Jerusalem. *Neither shall their fire be quenched*. Many discover here an allusion to the fact, that the soul, when it leaves the body, remains within the sphere of fire, if it does not deserve to join the angels of the Lord. The ancients said, that this would take place after the resurrection of the dead, and supported this opinion by a reference to Daniel (12:12), who asserts, that all the wicked, when called to life again, will be to an everlasting abhorring. All this is quite true.⁴⁵

footnotes:
⁴⁴ See Rashi, Kimchi, and Midrash Yalkut ad locum.
⁴⁵ By this remark I. E. indicates that he does not think that the prophet intended to express these opinions in this verse, but that he has nothing to say against them. Comp. I. E. on 51:6.


###### Ibn Ezra on Isaiah 66:24:2

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:2](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:2)


ומלת**לדראון** כמו גדוף, ויש אומרים שהם שתי מלות, ויפרשו ראון מגזרת הוי מראה ונגאלה [צפניה ג' א'], ומלת לדראון עולם (דניאל י"ב ב') יכחישם:


דראון *Abhorring*. According to some, it is composed of two words, די דאון much abhorring; as to דאון, comp. מוראה filthy (Zeph. 3:1); but this explanation is not admissible because of לדראון (Dan. 12:2).⁴⁶

footnotes:
⁴⁶ I. E. fails to prove why it should be more difficult to explain דראון in Daniel as equivalent to די ראון, than the same word used here by Isaiah. In his commentary on Daniel he only states that the word is not a compound, but the statement is not supported by any argument. The remark is perhaps based on the change of the Zere in דֵּרָאוֹן into Hirek in the construct state ,דִּרְאוֹן, since דֵּי═דֵ is the form of the construct state, and is not affected any further by the construct state of the succeeding word.

[https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:3](https://torahapp.org/share/book/Ibn%20Ezra%20on%20Isaiah/r/66:24:3)


נשלם ספר ישעיה הנביא / והודות לאין מספר לאלהי אבי / שלמדני ספר נביאו והחכים לבבי / יתמך ימיני להשלים מכתבי / באייר שנת ת'ת'ק'ה' לעולם בלוקא עיר מושבי:


END OF THE BOOK OF ISAIAH THE PROPHET.
